body.text: maṅgalācaraṇam
body.translated_text: Auspicious invocation

children.text: siddhiḥ sādhye satām astu prasādāt tasya dhūrjaṭeḥ |
children.translated_text: May success attend the worthy in their endeavors, by the grace of that <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (Śiva),

children.text: jāhnavī-phena-lekheva yan-mūrdhni śaśinaḥ kalā // Hit_0.1 //
children.translated_text: on whose head rests the crescent moon like a streak of foam on the <s>Jāhnavī</s> (Gaṅgā). // Hit_0.1 //

children.text: śruto hitopadeśo 'yaṃ pāṭavaṃ saṃskṛtoktiṣu |
children.translated_text: This <s>Hitopadeśa</s> (Beneficial Instruction), when heard, bestows eloquence in Sanskrit expression,

children.text: vācāṃ sarvatra vaicitryaṃ nīti-vidyāṃ dadāti ca // Hit_0.2 //
children.translated_text: variety in speech everywhere, and knowledge of <s>nīti</s> (statecraft and ethics). // Hit_0.2 //

body.text: vidyā-praśaṃsā
body.translated_text: Praise of learning

children.text: ajarāmaravat prājño vidyāmarthaṃ ca cintayet |
children.translated_text: The wise man should pursue learning and wealth as if he were ageless and immortal,

children.text: gṛhīta iva keśeṣu mṛtyunā dharmamācaret // Hit_0.3 //
children.translated_text: but should practice <s>dharma</s> as if seized by the hair by Death. // Hit_0.3 //

children.text: sarva-dravyeṣu vidyaiva dravyam āhur anuttamam |
children.translated_text: Among all possessions, they say learning is the supreme possession,

children.text: ahāryatvād anarghatvād akṣayatvāc ca sarvadā // Hit_0.4 //
children.translated_text: because it cannot be stolen, is priceless, and is imperishable at all times. // Hit_0.4 //

children.text: saṃyojayati vidyaiva nīcagāpi naraṃ sarit |
children.translated_text: Learning alone unites a man — even a lowly-flowing river

children.text: samudram iva durgharṣaṃ nṛpaṃ bhāgyam ataḥ param // Hit_0.5 //
children.translated_text: reaches the ocean, so formidable — with a king; fortune is beyond even that. // Hit_0.5 //

children.text: vidyā dadāti vinayaṃ vinayād yāti pātratām |
children.translated_text: Learning gives humility; from humility comes worthiness;

children.text: pātratvāt dhanam āpnoti dhanād dharmaṃ tataḥ sukham // Hit_0.6 //
children.translated_text: from worthiness one obtains wealth; from wealth, <s>dharma</s>; and from that, happiness. // Hit_0.6 //

children.text: vidyā śastraṃ ca śāstraṃ ca dve vidye pratipattaye |
children.translated_text: Weaponry and scholarship are two kinds of knowledge, both for practical application;

children.text: ādyā hāsyaya vṛddhatve dvitīyādriyate sadā // Hit_0.7 //
children.translated_text: the first becomes laughable in old age, but the second is always honored. // Hit_0.7 //

children.text: yan nave bhājane lagnaḥ saṃskāro nānyathā bhavet |
children.translated_text: The impression made on a new vessel cannot be changed later;

children.text: kathā-cchalena bālānāṃ nītis tad iha kathyate // Hit_0.8 //
children.translated_text: therefore, <s>nīti</s> (practical wisdom) is here taught to children through the device of stories. // Hit_0.8 //

children.text: mitra-lābhaḥ suhṛd-bhedo vigrahaḥ sandhir eva ca |
children.translated_text: The Winning of Friends, the Separation of Friends, War, and Peace —

children.text: pañca-tantrāt tathānyasmād granthād ākṛṣya likhyate // Hit_0.9 //
children.translated_text: these are drawn and compiled from the <s>Pañcatantra</s> and from other works. // Hit_0.9 //

body.text: atha kathā-mukham
body.translated_text: Now, the introduction to the story

body.text: asti bhāgīrathī-tīre pāṭaliputra-nāmadheyaṃ nagaram | tatra sarva-svāmi-guṇopetaḥ sudarśano nāma narapatir āsīt | sa bhūpatir ekadā kenāpi pāṭhyamānaṃ śloka-dvayaṃ śuśrāva-
body.translated_text: On the banks of the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> (Gaṅgā) there was a city named <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>. There lived a king named <s>Sudarśana</s>, endowed with all the virtues of a sovereign. That king once heard someone reciting a pair of verses —

children.text: aneka-saṃśayocchedi parokṣārthasya darśakam |
children.translated_text: The <s>śāstra</s> (scripture) resolves manifold doubts, reveals what is beyond perception,

children.text: sarvasya locanaṃ śāstraṃ yasya nāsty andha eva saḥ // Hit_0.10 //
children.translated_text: and is the eye of all — he who lacks it is truly blind. // Hit_0.10 //

children.text: yauvanaṃ dhana-sampattiḥ prabhutvam avivekitā |
children.translated_text: Youth, abundance of wealth, lordship, and lack of discrimination —

children.text: ekaikam apy anarthāya kim u yatra catuṣṭayam // Hit_0.11 //
children.translated_text: each one alone leads to ruin; how much more so when all four combine! // Hit_0.11 //

body.text: ity ākarṇyātmanaḥ putrāṇām anadhigata-śāstrāṇāṃ nityam unmārga-gāmināṃ śāstrānanuṣṭhānenodvigna-manāḥ sa rājā cintayāmāsa |
body.translated_text: Having heard this, the king, distressed in mind because his sons had not mastered the <s>śāstras</s> and were always straying from the right path due to their disregard for scripture, reflected:

children.text: ko 'rthaḥ putreṇa jātena yo na vidvān na dhārmikaḥ |
children.translated_text: What use is a son who is born if he is neither learned nor righteous?

children.text: kāṇena cakṣuṣā kiṃ vā cakṣuḥ pīḍaiva kevalam // Hit_0.12 //
children.translated_text: What use is a blind eye? It only causes pain to the eye. // Hit_0.12 //

children.text: ajāta-mṛta-mūrkhāṇāṃ varam ādyau na cāntimaḥ |
children.translated_text: Of the unborn, the stillborn, and the fool — the first two are preferable, not the last;

children.text: sakṛd duḥkha-karāv ādyāv antimas tu pade pade // Hit_0.13 //
children.translated_text: the first two cause grief only once, but the last causes it at every step. // Hit_0.13 //

body.text: kiṃ ca-

children.text: varaṃ garbha-srāvo varam api ca naivābhigamanaṃ
children.translated_text: Better a miscarriage, better even to have no union at all,

children.text: varaṃ jātaḥ preto varam api ca kanyāvajanitā |
children.translated_text: better the child be born dead, better even a daughter be born,

children.text: varaṃ bandhyā bhāryā varam api ca garbheṣu vasatir
children.translated_text: better the wife be barren, better even to remain in the womb,

children.text: na vāvidvān rūpa-draviṇa-guṇa-yukto 'pi tanayaḥ // Hit_0.14 //
children.translated_text: than a son who, though endowed with beauty, wealth, and virtues, is unlearned. // Hit_0.14 //

body.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: sa jāto yena jātena yāti vaṃśaḥ samunnatim |
children.translated_text: He alone is truly born by whose birth the family rises to eminence;

children.text: parivartini saṃsāre mṛtaḥ ko vā na jāyate // Hit_0.15 //
children.translated_text: in this revolving <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of existence), who that has died is not born again? // Hit_0.15 //

body.text: anyac ca-

children.text: guṇi-gaṇa-gaṇanā'rambhe
children.translated_text: When one begins to count the assemblage of virtuous men,

children.text: na patati kaṭhinī sa-sambhramād yasya |
children.translated_text: if the counting-stone does not fall eagerly for someone,

children.text: tenāmbā yadi sutinī
children.translated_text: then if his mother is called a fruitful woman,

children.text: vada bandhyā kīdṛśī bhavati ? // Hit_0.16 //
children.translated_text: tell me, what would a barren woman be like? // Hit_0.16 //

body.translated_text: And also —

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: Furthermore —

children.text: dāne tapasi śaurye ca yasya na prathitaṃ manaḥ |
children.translated_text: He whose mind is not inclined toward giving, austerity, valor,

children.text: vidyāyām artha-lābhe ca mātur uccāra eva saḥ // Hit_0.17 //
children.translated_text: learning, or acquisition of wealth — he is but his mother's excrement. // Hit_0.17 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: varam eko guṇī putro na ca mūrkha-śatair api |
children.translated_text: Better one son endowed with virtues than a hundred fools;

children.text: ekaś candramas tamo hanti na ca tārā-gaṇair api // Hit_0.18 //
children.translated_text: a single moon dispels darkness, which a multitude of stars cannot. // Hit_0.18 //

children.text: puṇya-tīrthe kṛtaṃ yena tapaḥ kvāpy atiduṣkaram |
children.translated_text: He who has performed extremely difficult <s>tapas</s> (austerities) at a sacred pilgrimage site,

children.text: tasya putro bhaved vaśyaḥ samṛddho dhārmikaḥ sudhīḥ // Hit_0.19 //
children.translated_text: his son will be obedient, prosperous, righteous, and wise. // Hit_0.19 //

children.text: tathā coktaṃ-
children.translated_text: And thus it is said —

children.text: arthāgamo nityam arogitā ca priyā ca bhāryā priya-vādinī ca |
children.translated_text: Constant income, freedom from disease, a beloved wife who speaks sweetly,

children.text: vaśyaś ca putro 'rtha-karī ca vidyā ṣaḍ jīva-lokasya sukhāni rājan // Hit_0.20 //
children.translated_text: an obedient son, and learning that brings wealth — these are the six pleasures of the living world, O king. // Hit_0.20 //

children.text: ko dhanyo bahubhiḥ putraiḥ kuśūlāpūraṇāḍhakaiḥ |
children.translated_text: What glory is there in many sons who are like bushels merely filling the granary?

children.text: varam ekaḥ kulālambī yatra viśrūyate pitā // Hit_0.21 //
children.translated_text: Better is one who upholds the family, through whom the father becomes renowned. // Hit_0.21 //

children.text: ṛṇa-kartā pitā śatrur mātā ca vyabhicāriṇī |
children.translated_text: A father who incurs debts is an enemy; an unchaste mother is an enemy;

children.text: bhāryā rūpavatī śatruḥ putraḥ śatrur apaṇḍitaḥ // Hit_0.22 //
children.translated_text: a beautiful wife is an enemy; an unlearned son is an enemy. // Hit_0.22 //

children.text: yasya kasya prasūto 'pi guṇavān pūjyate naraḥ |
children.translated_text: No matter whose son he may be, a man of virtues is honored;

children.text: dhanur vaṃśa-viśuddho 'pi nirguṇaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati // Hit_0.23 //
children.translated_text: what can a bow, though made of pure bamboo, accomplish if it lacks quality? // Hit_0.23 //

children.text: hā hā putraka nādhītaṃ gatāsv etāsu rātriṣu |
children.translated_text: Alas, alas, my child, you did not study during those nights that have now passed!

children.text: tena tvaṃ viduṣāṃ madhye paṅke gaur iva sīdasi // Hit_0.24 //
children.translated_text: Therefore you sink in the midst of the learned like a cow in the mud. // Hit_0.24 //

body.text: tat katham idānīm ete mama putrā guṇavantaḥ kriyantām ? yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Then how can these sons of mine now be made virtuous? For —

children.text: āhāra-nidrā-bhaya-maithunāni sāmānyam etat paśubhir narāṇām |
children.translated_text: Eating, sleeping, fearing, and mating — these are common to both animals and men;

children.text: jñānaṃ narāṇām adhiko viśeṣo jñānena hīnāḥ paśubhiḥ samānāḥ // Hit_0.25 //
children.translated_text: <s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge) is the distinguishing quality of men; those devoid of knowledge are equal to animals. // Hit_0.25 //

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Because —

children.text: dharmārtha-kāma-mokṣāṇāṃ yasyaiko 'pi na vidyate |
children.translated_text: He who possesses not even one among <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s> (wealth), <s>kāma</s> (pleasure), and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) —

children.text: ajāgala-stanasyeva tasya janma nirarthakam // Hit_0.26 //
children.translated_text: his birth is as useless as the teats on a goat's neck. // Hit_0.26 //

children.text: yac cocyate-
children.translated_text: And as it is said —

children.text: āyuḥ karma ca vittaṃ ca vidyā nidhanam eva ca |
children.translated_text: Lifespan, <s>karma</s>, wealth, learning, and death —

children.text: pañcaitāni hi sṛjyante garbhasthasyaiva dehinaḥ // Hit_0.27 //
children.translated_text: these five are determined for the embodied being while still in the womb. // Hit_0.27 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: avaśyaṃ bhāvino bhāvā bhavanti mahatām api |
children.translated_text: Events that are destined to occur do occur, even for the great;

children.text: nagnatvaṃ nīlakaṇṭhasya mahāhi-śayanaṃ hareḥ // Hit_0.28 //
children.translated_text: nakedness befell <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s> (Śiva), and the great serpent became the bed of <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu). // Hit_0.28 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: yad abhāvi na tad bhāvi bhāvi cen na tad anyathā |
children.translated_text: What was not to be will not be; what was to be will not be otherwise;

children.text: iti cintā-viṣa-ghno 'yam agadaḥ kiṃ na pīyate // Hit_0.29 //
children.translated_text: this antidote that destroys the poison of anxiety — why is it not drunk? // Hit_0.29 //

body.text: etat kāryākṣamāṇāṃ keṣāṃcid ālasya-vacanam | puruṣakārautkārṣyam āha-

children.text: yathā hy ekena cakreṇa na rathasya gatir bhavet |
children.translated_text: Just as a chariot cannot move with a single wheel,

children.text: tathā puruṣakāreṇa vinā daivaṃ na siddhyati // Hit_0.30 //
children.translated_text: so too fate does not succeed without human effort. // Hit_0.30 //

body.translated_text: This is the speech of the lazy who are incapable of action. Now he speaks of the excellence of human effort —

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And so —

children.text: pūrva-janma-kṛtaṃ karma tad daivam iti kathyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> performed in a previous birth — that is called fate;

children.text: tasmāt puruṣakāreṇa yatnaṃ kuryād atandritaḥ // Hit_0.31 //
children.translated_text: therefore one should exert oneself through human effort without laziness. // Hit_0.31 //

children.text: na daivam api saṃcintya tyajed udyogam ātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: One should not abandon one's own enterprise merely by thinking of fate;

children.text: anudyogena tailāni tilebhyo nāptum arhati // Hit_0.32 //
children.translated_text: without effort, one cannot extract oil from sesame seeds. // Hit_0.32 //

body.text: anyac ca-

children.text: udyoginaṃ puruṣa-siṃham upaiti lakṣmīr
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s> (Fortune) approaches the industrious man, a lion among men;

children.text: daivena deyam iti kāpuruṣā vadanti |
children.translated_text: "fate must give" — so say the cowards;

children.text: daivaṃ nihatya kuru pauruṣam ātma-śaktyā
children.translated_text: cast fate aside and exert your own prowess with your own strength;

children.text: yatne kṛte yadi na sidhyati ko 'tra doṣaḥ // Hit_0.33 //
children.translated_text: if the goal is not achieved despite effort, what fault lies therein? // Hit_0.33 //

body.translated_text: And also —

children.text: yathā mṛt-piṇḍataḥ kartā kurute yad yad icchati |
children.translated_text: Just as a potter makes whatever he wishes from a lump of clay,

children.text: evam ātma-kṛtaṃ karma mānavaḥ pratipadyate // Hit_0.34 //
children.translated_text: so a man obtains the fruits of <s>karma</s> made by himself. // Hit_0.34 //

children.text: kākatālīyavat prāptaṃ dṛṣṭvāpi nidhim agrataḥ |
children.translated_text: Even upon seeing a treasure before him, obtained by chance like a crow and a palm fruit,

children.text: na svayaṃ daivam ādatte puruṣārtham apekṣate // Hit_0.
children.translated_text: fate does not seize it by itself — it requires human effort. // Hit_0.

children.text: udyamena hi sidhyanti kāryāṇi na manorathaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Tasks are accomplished through exertion, not through mere wishes;

children.text: nahi suptasya siṃhasya praviśanti mukhe mṛgāḥ // Hit_0.36 //
children.translated_text: deer do not enter the mouth of a sleeping lion. // Hit_0.36 //

children.text: tathā coktaṃ-
children.translated_text: And thus it is said —

children.text: mātā śatruḥ pitā vairī yena bālo na pāṭhitaḥ |
children.translated_text: A mother is an enemy and a father a foe by whom a child is not educated;

children.text: na śobhate sabhā-madhye haṃsa-madhye bako yathā // Hit_0.37 //
children.translated_text: he does not shine in the assembly, like a crane among swans. // Hit_0.37 //

children.text: rūpa-yauvana-sampannā viśāla-kula-sambhavāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those endowed with beauty and youth, born of illustrious families,

children.text: vidyā-hīnā na śobhante nirgandhā iva kiṃśukāḥ // Hit_0.38 //
children.translated_text: without learning do not shine, like <s>kiṃśuka</s> (flame-of-the-forest) flowers without fragrance. // Hit_0.38 //

children.text: aparac ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: pustakeṣu ca nādhītaṃ nādhītaṃ guru-sannidhau |
children.translated_text: What has not been studied in books, what has not been studied in the presence of a teacher,

children.text: na śobhate sambhā-madhye jāra-garbha iva striyāḥ // Hit_0.39 //
children.translated_text: does not shine in the assembly — like the illegitimate child of a woman. // Hit_0.39 //

body.text: etac cintayitvā rājā paṇḍita-sabhāṃ kāritavān | rājovāca-bho bhoḥ paṇḍitāḥ ! śrūyatāṃ mama vacanam | asti kaścid evambhūto vidvān yo mama putrāṇāṃ nityam unmārga-gāminām anadhigata-śāstrāṇām idānīṃ nīti-śāstropadeśena punar janma kārayituṃ samarthaḥ ? yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Having thought thus, the king convened an assembly of scholars. The king said: "O learned ones! Hear my words. Is there any scholar of such caliber who is capable of giving my sons — who always stray from the right path and have not mastered the <s>śāstras</s> — a new birth, as it were, through instruction in <s>nītiśāstra</s> (the science of statecraft)? For —

children.text: kācaḥ kāñcana-saṃsargād dhatte mārakatīr dyutīḥ |
children.translated_text: Glass, through association with gold, assumes the brilliance of an emerald;

children.text: tathā sat-sannidhānena mūrkho yāti pravīṇatām // Hit_0.40 //
children.translated_text: similarly, through the company of the good, even a fool attains proficiency. // Hit_0.40 //

children.text: uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And it is said —

children.text: hīyate hi matis tāta hīnaiḥ saha samāgamāt |
children.translated_text: The intellect deteriorates, dear one, through association with the inferior;

children.text: samaiś ca samatām eti viśiṣṭaiś ca viśiṣṭatām // Hit_0.41 //
children.translated_text: it reaches equality with equals, and distinction with the distinguished. // Hit_0.41 //

body.text: atrāntare viṣṇu-śarma-nāmā mahā-paṇḍitaḥ sakala-nīiti-śāstra-tattva-jño bṛhaspatir ivābravīt-deva mahākula-sambhūtā ete rājaputrāḥ | tat mayā nītiṃ grāhayituṃ śakyante | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: At that point, a great scholar named <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s>, a knower of the essence of all <s>nītiśāstras</s>, spoke like <s>Bṛhaspati</s> himself: "O king, these princes are born of a great family. Therefore I am able to make them learn <s>nīti</s>. For —

children.text: nādravye nihitā kācit kriyā phalavatī bhavet |
children.translated_text: No action applied to an unworthy object can bear fruit;

children.text: na vyāpāra-śatenāpi śukavat pāṭhyate bakaḥ // Hit_0.42 //
children.translated_text: not even by a hundred efforts can a crane be taught to speak like a parrot. // Hit_0.42 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: asmiṃs tu nirguṇaṃ gotre nāpatyam upajāyate |
children.translated_text: In this noble lineage, no unworthy offspring is born;

children.text: ākare padya-rāgānāṃ janma kāca-maṇeḥ kutaḥ // Hit_0.43 //
children.translated_text: in a mine of rubies, how can a mere glass gem be born? // Hit_0.43 //

body.text: ato 'haṃ ṣaṇ-māsābhyantare bhavat-putrān nīti-śāstrābhijñān kariṣyāmi | rājā sa-vinayaṃ punar uvāca |
body.translated_text: Therefore I shall make your sons proficient in <s>nītiśāstra</s> within six months." The king spoke again with humility:

children.text: kīṭo 'pi sumanaḥ-saṅgād ārohati satāṃ śiraḥ |
children.translated_text: "Even an insect, through association with flowers, ascends to the heads of the virtuous;

children.text: aśmāpi yāti devatvaṃ mahadbhiḥ supratiṣṭhitaḥ // Hit_0.44 //
children.translated_text: even a stone attains divinity when properly installed by the great. // Hit_0.44 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: yathodaya-girer dravyaṃ sannikarṣeṇa dīpyate |
children.translated_text: Just as the substance of the eastern mountain (Mount <s>Udaya</s>) shines through proximity,

children.text: tathā sat-sannidhānena hīna-varṇo 'pi dīpyate // Hit_0.45 //
children.translated_text: so even one of low status shines through the company of the good. // Hit_0.45 //

children.text: guṇā guṇajñeṣu guṇā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Virtues are virtues only among those who appreciate virtues;

children.text: te nirguṇaṃ prāpya bhavanti doṣāḥ |
children.translated_text: when they reach one devoid of virtues, they become faults;

children.text: āsvādya-toyāḥ pravahanti nadyaḥ
children.translated_text: rivers flow with sweet waters,

children.text: samudram āsādya bhavanty upeyāḥ // Hit_0.46 //
children.translated_text: but upon reaching the ocean, they become undrinkable. // Hit_0.46 //

body.text: tad eteṣām asmat-putrāṇāṃ nīti-śāstropadeśāya bhavantaḥ pramāṇam ity uktvā tasya viṣṇu-śarmaṇo kare bahumāna-puraḥsaraṃ putrān samarpitavān //
body.translated_text: Therefore you are the authority for instructing these sons of ours in <s>nītiśāstra</s>." Having said this, he respectfully entrusted his sons into the hands of <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s>.

body.text:
i.
mitra-lābhaḥ
body.translated_text: I. The Winning of Friends

body.text: atha prāsāda-pṛṣṭhe sukhopaviṣṭānāṃ rājaputrāṇāṃ purastāt prastāva-krameṇa paṇḍito 'bravīt-bho rāja-putrāḥ śṛṇuta-
body.translated_text: Then, with the princes comfortably seated on the terrace, the scholar spoke to them as the occasion arose: "O princes, listen —

children.text: kāvya-śāstra-vinodena kālo gacchati dhīmatām |
children.translated_text: The time of the wise passes in the enjoyment of poetry and learning,

children.text: vyasanena tu mūrkhāṇāṃ nidrayā kalahena vā // Hit_1.1 //
children.translated_text: while that of fools passes in vice, sleep, or quarrels. // Hit_1.1 //

body.text: tad bhavatāṃ vinodāya kāka-kūrmādīnāṃ vicitrāṃ kathāṃ kathayiṣyāmi | rāja-putrair uktam-ārya ! kathyatāṃ | viṣṇu-śarmovāca-śṛṇuta yūyam | samprati mitra-lābhaḥ prastūyate | yasyāyam ādyaḥ ślokaḥ-
body.translated_text: For your entertainment, I shall tell a wonderful tale of a crow, a tortoise, and others." The princes said: "Sir, please tell it." <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s> said: "Listen, all of you. Now begins the Winning of Friends, whose opening verse is —

children.text: asādhanā vitta-hīnā buddhimantaḥ suhṛn-matāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who are without resources and devoid of wealth, yet wise and possessed of friends,

children.text: sādhayanty āśu kāryāṇi kāka-kūrma-mṛgākhuvat // Hit_1.2 //
children.translated_text: accomplish their tasks quickly — like the crow, the tortoise, the deer, and the mouse. // Hit_1.2 //

body.text: rājaputrā ūcuḥ-katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The princes asked: "How is that?"

body.text: so 'bravīt-asti godāvarī-tīre viśālaḥ śālmalī-taruḥ | tatra nānā-dig-deśād āgatya rātrau pakṣiṇo nivasanti | atha kadācid avasannāyāṃ rātrau astācala-cūḍāvalambini bhagavati kumudinī-nāyake candramasi | laghupatana-nāmā vāyasaḥ prabuddhaḥ kṛtāntam iva dvitīyam aṭantaṃ pāśa-hastaṃ vyāgham apaśyat | tam ālokyācintayat-adya prātar evāniṣṭa-darśanaṃ jātam | na jāne kim anabhimataṃ darśayiṣyati | ity uktvā tad anusaraṇa-krameṇa vyākulaś calati | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: He said: "On the banks of the <s>Godāvarī</s> there stands a great <s>śālmalī</s> (silk-cotton) tree. There, birds coming from various directions and countries roost at night. Now one night, when the night was far spent, when the lord of the water-lilies, the blessed moon, was resting on the peak of the western mountain, a crow named <s>Laghupatanaka</s> (Light-wing), having awakened, saw a hunter prowling about with a net in hand, like a second <s>Kṛtānta</s> (Death). Seeing him, he thought: 'Today, at the very break of dawn, an inauspicious sight has appeared. I do not know what misfortune it will reveal.' Having said this, troubled, he followed the hunter. For —

children.text: śoka-sthāna-sahasrāṇi bhaya-sthāna-śatāni ca |
children.translated_text: Thousands of occasions for grief and hundreds of occasions for fear

children.text: divase divase mūḍham āviśanti na paṇḍitam // Hit_1.3 //
children.translated_text: beset the foolish day after day, but not the wise. // Hit_1.3 //

children.text: anyac ca-viṣayiṇām idam avaśyaṃ kartavyam |
children.translated_text: And also — this must certainly be done by those who are worldly-wise:

children.text: utthāyotthāya boddhavyaṃ kim adya sukṛtaṃ kṛtam |
children.translated_text: "Having risen again and again, one should reflect: what meritorious deed have I done today?

children.text: āyuṣaḥ khaṇḍam ādāya ravir astaṃ gamiṣyati // Hit_1.4 //
children.translated_text: The sun is about to set, carrying away a portion of one's life." // Hit_1.4 //

body.text: atha tena vyādhena taṇḍula-kaṇān vikīrya jālaṃ vistīrṇam | sa ca tatra pracchanno bhūtvā sthitaḥ | asminn eva kāle citragrīva-nāmā kapota-rājaḥ sa-parivāro viyati visarpaṃs taṇḍula-kaṇān avalokayāmāsa | tataḥ kapota-rājas taṇḍula-kaṇa-lubdhān kapotān prāha-kuto 'tra nirjane vane taṇḍula-kaṇānāṃ sambhavaḥ | tan nirūpyatāṃ tāvat | bhadram idaṃ na paśyāmi prāyeṇānena taṇḍula-kaṇa-lobhenāsmābhir api tathā bhavitavyam |
body.translated_text: Now that hunter scattered rice-grains and spread a net. He then remained there, hidden. At that very time, the pigeon-king named <s>Citragrīva</s> (Speckle-neck), flying through the sky with his retinue, caught sight of the rice-grains. Then the pigeon-king said to the pigeons, who were greedy for the rice-grains: 'Whence could rice-grains appear here in this uninhabited forest? Let it be examined first. I see no good in this — most likely, through greed for these rice-grains, the same [fate] shall befall us too.'

children.text: kaṅkaṇasya tu lobhena magnaḥ paṅke sudustare |
children.translated_text: Through greed for a bracelet,

children.text: vṛddha-vyāghreṇa samprāptaḥ pathikaḥ sammṛtaḥ // Hit_1.5 //
children.translated_text: a traveler sank in impassable mud and, seized by an old tiger, was killed.

body.text:
kapotā ūcuḥ-katham etat ?
kathā 1
body.translated_text: The pigeons said: 'How was that?' Story 1:

body.text: so 'bravīt-aham ekadā dakṣiṇāraṇye carann apaśyam eko vṛddho vyāghraḥ snātaḥ kuśa-hastaḥ saras-tīre brūte-bho bho panthāḥ ! idaṃ suvarṇa-kaṅkaṇaṃ gṛhyatām | tato lobhākṛṣṭena kenacit pānthena ālocitam-bhāgyena etat sambhavati | kintu asmin ātma-sandehe pravṛttir na vidheyā | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: He said: 'Once, while wandering in the southern forest, I saw an old tiger, freshly bathed, with <s>kuśa</s> grass in hand, standing on the bank of a lake, calling out: "O travelers! Take this golden bracelet!" Then a certain traveler, drawn by greed, thought: "This comes about by fortune. But in a matter of such danger to oneself, one should not proceed. For —"'

children.text: aniṣṭād iṣṭa-lābhe'pi na gatir jāyate śubhā |
children.translated_text: 'Even when a desired gain comes from an undesirable [source],

children.text: yatrāste viṣa-saṃsargo 'mṛtaṃ tad api mṛtyave // Hit_1.6 //
children.translated_text: a wholesome course does not arise; where there is contact with poison, even nectar leads to death.'

body.text: kintu sarvatrārthārjana-pravṛttau sandeha eva | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: 'But in every endeavor to acquire wealth, there is indeed doubt. And as it is said —'

children.text: na saṃśayam anāruhya naro bhadrāṇi paśyati |
children.translated_text: 'Without venturing into doubt, a man does not see good fortune;

children.text: saṃśayaṃ punar āruhya yadi jīvati paśyati // Hit_1.7 //
children.translated_text: but having ventured into doubt, if he survives, he sees [it].'

body.text: tan nirūpayāmi tāvat | prakāśaṃ brūte | kutra tava kaṅkaṇam ? vyāghro hastaṃ prasārya darśayati | pāntho 'vadat-kathaṃ mārātmake tvayi viśvāsaḥ ?
body.translated_text: '"So let me examine." He said aloud: "Where is your bracelet?" The tiger stretched out his hand and showed [it]. The traveler said: "How can there be trust in you, who are murderous by nature?"'

body.text: vyāghra uvāca-śṛṇu re pāntha ! prāg eva yauvana-daśāyām aham atīva durvṛtta āsam | aneka-go-mānuṣāṇāṃ vadhād me putrā mṛtā dārāś ca | vaṃśa-hīnaś cāham | tataḥ kenacid dhārmikeṇāham upadiṣṭaḥ | dāna-dharmādikaṃ caratu bhavān iti | tad-upadeśādi-dānīm ahaṃ snāna-śīlo dātā vṛddho galita-nakha-dantaḥ na kathaṃ viśvāsa-bhūmiḥ ? uktaṃ ca-
body.translated_text: 'The tiger said: "Listen, O traveler! In my youth I was exceedingly wicked. From killing many cows and humans, my sons died and my wife too. And I am without lineage. Then I was instructed by a certain righteous person: 'Sir, you should practice charity, <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), and the like.' Following that instruction, I am now devoted to bathing, a giver, old, with claws and teeth fallen — how am I not worthy of trust? And it is said —"'

children.text: ijyā'dhyayana-dānāni tapaḥ satyaṃ dhṛtiḥ kṣamā |
children.translated_text: 'Sacrifice, study, charity,

children.text: alobha iti mārgo 'yaṃ dharmasyāṣṭa-vidhaḥ smṛtaḥ // Hit_1.8 //
children.translated_text: austerity, truth, steadfastness, forbearance,

children.text: tatra pūrvaś caturvargo dambhārtham api sevyate |
children.translated_text: and non-covetousness — this eightfold path of <s>dharma</s> is declared.

children.text: uttaras tu caturvargo mahātmany eva tiṣṭhati // Hit_1.9 //
children.translated_text: Of these, the first four may be practiced even for the sake of ostentation, but the latter four exist only in the great-souled.'

body.text: mama caitāvān lobha-virahaḥ | yena sva-hasta-stham api suvarṇa-kaṅkaṇaṃ yasmai kasmaicid dātum icchāmi tathāpi vyāghro mānuṣaṃ khādatīti lokāpavādo durnivāraḥ | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: '"Such is my freedom from greed that I wish to give this golden bracelet, though in my own hand, to anyone at all. Yet the popular slander that a tiger devours humans is hard to overcome. For —"'

children.text: gatānugatiko lokaḥ kuṭṭanīm upadeśinīm |
children.translated_text: 'The world follows convention and takes a procuress as its teacher;

children.text: pramāṇayati no dharme yathā goghnam api dvijam // Hit_1.10 //
children.translated_text: it does not accept as authority in <s>dharma</s> even a twice-born who has killed a cow.'

body.text: mayā ca dharma-śāstrāṇi adhītāni | śṛṇu-
body.translated_text: '"And I have studied the <s>dharma-śāstras</s> (treatises on law). Listen —"'

children.text: maru-sthalyāṃ yathā vṛṣṭiḥ kṣudhārte bhojanaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: 'As rain [falls] upon the desert, as food [is given] to the hungry,

children.text: daridre dīyate dānaṃ saphalaṃ pāṇḍu-nandana // Hit_1.11 //
children.translated_text: so charity given to the poor is fruitful, O son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>.'

children.text: prāṇā yathātmano 'bhīṣṭā bhūtānām api te tathā |
children.translated_text: 'Just as one's own life-breaths are dear to oneself, so are they to [all] beings;

children.text: ātmaupamyena bhūtānāṃ dayāṃ kurvanti sādhavaḥ // Hit_1.12 //
children.translated_text: the virtuous show compassion to beings by likening [them] to themselves.'

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'And furthermore —'

children.text: pratyākhyāne ca dāne ca sukha-duḥkhe priyāpriye |
children.translated_text: 'In refusal and in giving, in pleasure and in pain, in what is agreeable and disagreeable,

children.text: ātmaupamyena puruṣaḥ pramāṇam adhigacchati // Hit_1.13 //
children.translated_text: a person arrives at the standard [of conduct] by likening [others] to himself.'

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: 'And moreover —'

children.text: mātṛvat para-dāreṣu para-dravyeṣu loṣṭravat |
children.translated_text: '[Regarding] the wives of others as [one's own] mother, the wealth of others as a clod of earth,

children.text: ātmavat sarva-bhūteṣu yaḥ paśyati sa paṇḍitaḥ // Hit_1.14 //
children.translated_text: and all beings as oneself — he who sees thus is a wise man.'

body.text: tvaṃ ca atīva-durgataḥ | tena tat tubhyaṃ dātuṃ sa-yatno 'ham | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: '"And you are exceedingly destitute. Therefore I am making an effort to give this to you. And as it is said —"'

children.text: daridrān bhara kaunteya mā prayaccheśvare dhanam |
children.translated_text: '"Sustain the poor, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>; do not give wealth to the rich;

children.text: vyādhitasyauṣadhaṃ pathyaṃ nīrujasya kim auṣadhaiḥ // Hit_1.15 //
children.translated_text: medicine and wholesome [diet] are for the sick — what use has the healthy person for medicine?"'

children.text: anyat ca-
children.translated_text: 'And also —'

children.text: dātavyam iti yad dānaṃ dīyate'nupakāriṇi |
children.translated_text: 'That gift which is given with the thought "it should be given," to one who does no favor in return,

children.text: deśe kāle ca pātre ca tad dānaṃ sāttvikaṃ viduḥ // Hit_1.16 //
children.translated_text: at the right place, time, and to a worthy recipient — that gift is known as <s>sāttvika</s> (of the nature of goodness).'

body.text: tad atra sarasi snātvā suvarṇa-kaṅkaṇam idaṃ gṛhāṇa | tato yāvad asau tad-vacaḥ-pratīto lobhāt saraḥ snātuṃ praviṣṭaḥ, tāvan mahā-paṅke nimagnaḥ palāyitum akṣamaḥ | taṃ paṅke patitaṃ dṛṣṭvā vyāghro 'vadat-ahaha mahā-paṅke patito 'si | atas tvām aham utthāpayāmi | ity uktvā śanaiḥ śanair upagamya tena vyāghreṇa dhṛtaḥ sa pāntho 'cintayat-
body.translated_text: '"So bathe in this lake and take this golden bracelet." Thereupon, trusting those words, that person entered the lake to bathe out of greed, but he sank in deep mud and was unable to escape. Seeing him fallen in the mud, the tiger said: "Alas! You have fallen in deep mud. So I shall lift you out." Having said this, he slowly, slowly approached, and the traveler, seized by that tiger, thought —'

children.text: na dharma-śāstraṃ paṭhatīti kāraṇaṃ
children.translated_text: 'It is not the reading of <s>dharma-śāstras</s> that is the [determining] cause,

children.text: na cāpi vedādhyayanaṃ durātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: nor is it the study of the <s>Vedas</s> [that makes] an evil-natured [person good];

children.text: svabhāva evātra tathātiricyate
children.translated_text: innate nature here predominates indeed,

children.text: yathā prakṛtyā madhuraṃ gavāṃ payaḥ // Hit_1.17 //
children.translated_text: just as the milk of cows is naturally sweet.'

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'Moreover —'

children.text: avaśendriya-cittānāṃ hasti-snānam iva kriyā |
children.translated_text: 'For those whose senses and minds are uncontrolled, action is like an elephant's bath;

children.text: durbhagābharaṇa-prāyo jñānaṃ bhāraḥ kriyāṃ vinā // Hit_1.18 //
children.translated_text: knowledge without practice is a burden, like ornaments on an ugly woman.'

body.text: tan mayā bhadraṃ na kṛtam | yad atra mārātmake viśvāsaḥ kṛtaḥ | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: '"So I have not acted wisely in placing trust in this murderous [creature]. And as it is said —"'

children.text: nadīnāṃ śastra-pāṇīnāṃ nakhināṃ śṛṅgiṇāṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: 'In rivers, in those armed with weapons, in those with claws, and in those with horns,

children.text: viśvāso naiva kartavyaḥ strīṣu rāja-kuleṣu ca // Hit_1.19 //
children.translated_text: trust should never be placed — nor in women and royal families.'

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'And furthermore —'

children.text: sarvasya hi parīkṣyante svabhāvā netare guṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Of everyone, the innate nature is to be examined, not other qualities;

children.text: atītya hi guṇān sarvān svabhāvo mūrdhni vartate // Hit_1.20 //
children.translated_text: for, surpassing all [acquired] qualities, innate nature stands supreme.'

body.text: anyac ca-

children.text: sa hi gagana-vihārī kalmaṣa-dhvaṃsa-kārī
children.translated_text: 'He who travels in the sky, who destroys sins,

children.text: daśa-śata-kara-dhārī jyotiṣāṃ madhya-cārī |
children.translated_text: who bears a thousand rays, who moves in the midst of luminaries —

children.text: vidhur api vidhi-yogād grasyate rāhuṇāsau
children.translated_text: even the moon, by the decree of fate, is swallowed by <s>Rāhu</s>;

children.text: likhitam api lalāṭe projjhitaṃ kaḥ samarthaḥ // Hit_1.21 //
children.translated_text: what is written on the forehead, who is able to efface?'

body.translated_text: 'And also —'

body.text: iti cintayann evāsau vyāghreṇa dhṛtvā vyāpāditaḥ khāditaś ca | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-kaṅkaṇasya tu lobhenety ādi | ata eva sarvathāvicāritaṃ karma na kartavyam iti | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: 'Thus thinking, he was seized by the tiger, killed, and eaten. Therefore I say: "Through greed for a bracelet..." and so forth. Hence, one should never perform an action without deliberation. For —'

children.text: sujīrṇam annaṃ suvicakṣaṇaḥ sutaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Well-digested food, a well-discerning son,

children.text: suśāsitā strī nṛpatiḥ susevitaḥ |
children.translated_text: a well-governed wife, a well-served king,

children.text: sucintya coktaṃ suvicārya yat kṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: a word spoken after due reflection, a deed done after due deliberation —

children.text: sudīrgha-kāle'pi na yāti vikriyām // Hit_1.22 //
children.translated_text: even after a very long time, does not undergo change.'

body.text: etad vacanaṃ śrutvā kaścit kapotaḥ sa-darpam āha-āḥ ! kim evam ucyate ?
body.translated_text: Having heard this speech, a certain pigeon said proudly: 'Ah! Why is this said?'

children.text: vṛddhasya vacanaṃ grāhyam āpat-kāle hy upasthite |
children.translated_text: 'The word of an elder should be heeded when a time of calamity has arrived;

children.text: sarvatraivaṃ vicāre ca bhojane'pi pravartatām // Hit_1.23 //
children.translated_text: let such deliberation prevail everywhere — even in the matter of food.'

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: 'For —'

children.text: śaṅkābhiḥ sarvam ākrāntam annaṃ pānaṃ ca bhūtale |
children.translated_text: 'Everything on earth — food and drink — is beset by apprehensions;

children.text: pravṛttiḥ kutra kartavyā jīvitavyaṃ kathaṃ na vā ? // Hit_1.24 //
children.translated_text: where should one undertake action? How else is one to live?'

children.text: yathā coktam-
children.translated_text: 'As it is said —'

children.text: īrṣyī ghṛṇī tv asantuṣṭaḥ krodhano nitya-śaṅkitaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The envious, the squeamish, the discontented, the wrathful, the ever-suspicious,

children.text: para-bhāgyopajīvī ca ṣaḍ ete nitya-duḥkhitāḥ // Hit_1.25 //
children.translated_text: and one who lives off others' fortune — these six are always miserable.'

body.text: etac chrutvā taṇḍul-kaṇa-lobhena nabho-maṇḍalād avatīryas arve kapotās tatropaviṣṭāḥ | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Having heard this, all the pigeons, driven by greed for rice-grains, descended from the sky and alighted there. For —

children.text: sumahānty api śāstrāṇi dhārayanto bahu-śrutāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Even those who retain great scriptures, who are learned,

children.text: chettāḥ saṃayānāṃ ca kliśyante lobha-mohitāḥ // Hit_1.26 //
children.translated_text: and who resolve doubts are tormented when deluded by greed.'

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: 'And also —'

children.text: lobhāt krodhaḥ prabhavati lobhāt kāmaḥ prajāyate |
children.translated_text: 'From greed anger arises, from greed desire is born,

children.text: lobhān mohaś ca nāśaś ca lobhaḥ pāpasya kāraṇam // Hit_1.27 //
children.translated_text: from greed [come] delusion and ruin — greed is the cause of sin.'

body.text: anyac ca-

children.text: asaṃbhavaṃ hema-mṛgasya janma
children.translated_text: 'The birth of a golden deer is impossible,

children.text: tathāpi rāmo lulubhe mṛgāya |
children.translated_text: yet <s>Rāma</s> was enticed by the deer;

children.text: prāyaḥ samāpanna-vipatti-kāle
children.translated_text: generally, when the time of calamity has arrived,

children.text: dhiyo 'pi puṃsāṃ malinā bhavanti // Hit_1.28 //
children.translated_text: the minds of men become clouded.'

body.translated_text: 'And also —'

body.text: anantaraṃ te sarve jāla-nibaddhā babhūvuḥ, tato yasya vacanāt tatrāvalambitās taṃ sarve tiraskurvanti sma | yataḥ,
body.translated_text: Thereupon they were all caught in the net. Then they all reproached the one on whose advice they had alighted there. For —

children.text: na gaṇasyāgrato gacchet siddhe kārye samaṃ phalam |
children.translated_text: 'One should not walk ahead of the group; if the task succeeds, the fruit is shared equally,

children.text: yadi kārya-vipattiḥ syān mukharas tatra hanyate // Hit_1.29 //
children.translated_text: but if the task goes awry, the spokesman is killed.'

body.text: tasya tiraskāraṃ śrutvā citragrīva uvāca-nāyam asya doṣaḥ, yataḥ
body.translated_text: Hearing their reproach, <s>Citragrīva</s> said: 'This is not his fault. For —'

children.text: āpadām āpatantīnāṃ hito 'py āyāti hetutām |
children.translated_text: 'When calamities come rushing, even a well-wisher becomes a cause [of trouble];

children.text: mātṛ-jaṅghā hi vatsasya stambhī-bhavati bandhane // Hit_1.30 //
children.translated_text: the mother's leg itself becomes a fetter for the calf when binding [it].'

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: 'And also —'

children.text: sa bandhur yo vipannānām āpad-uddharaṇa-kṣamaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'A friend is one who is capable of rescuing the distressed from calamity,

children.text: na tu bhīta-paritrāṇa-vastūpālambha-paṇḍitaḥ // Hit_1.31 //
children.translated_text: not one who is clever [only] at finding fault with the means of saving the frightened.'

body.text: vipat-kāle vismaya eva kāpuruṣa-lakṣaṇam | tad atra dhairyam avalambya pratīkāraś cintyatām, yataḥ-
body.translated_text: 'Astonishment in time of adversity is the mark of a coward. So here, taking courage, let a remedy be considered. For —'

children.text: vipadi dhairyam athābhyudaye kṣamā
children.translated_text: 'Steadfastness in adversity, patience in prosperity,

children.text: sadasi vākya-paṭutā yudhi vikramaḥ |
children.translated_text: eloquence in the assembly, valor in battle,

children.text: yaśasi cābhirucir vyasanaṃ śrutau
children.translated_text: delight in fame, and devotion to learning —

children.text: prakṛti-siddham idaṃ hi mahātmanām // Hit_1.32 //
children.translated_text: this is the naturally accomplished [character] of great souls.'

children.text: sampadi yasya na harṣo vipadi viṣādo raṇe ca bhīrutvam |
children.translated_text: 'He at whose prosperity there is no elation, in whose adversity there is no dejection, and in battle no cowardice —

children.text: taṃ bhuvana-traya-tilakaṃ janayati jananī sutaṃ viralam // Hit_1.33 //
children.translated_text: rarely does a mother give birth to such a son, who is the ornament of the three worlds.'

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: 'And also —'

children.text: ṣaḍ-doṣāḥ puruṣeṇeha hātavyā bhūtim icchatā |
children.translated_text: 'Six faults are to be abandoned here by a man desiring prosperity:',

children.text: nidrā tandrā bhayaṃ krodha ālasyaṃ dīrgha-sūtratā // Hit_1.34 //
children.translated_text: sleep, drowsiness, fear, anger, laziness, and procrastination.'

body.text: idānīm api evaṃ kriyatām-sarvair ekacittībhūya jālam ādāya uḍḍīyatām | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: 'Now let this be done: let all of us, united in one purpose, take up the net and fly away. For —'

children.text: alpānām api vastūnāṃ saṃhatiḥ kārya-sādhikā |
children.translated_text: 'The union of even small things accomplishes the task;

children.text: tṛṇair guṇatvam āpannair badhyante matta-dantinaḥ // Hit_1.35 //
children.translated_text: by blades of grass woven into a rope, mad elephants are bound.'

children.text: saṃhatiḥ śreyasī puṃsāṃ svakulair alpakair api |
children.translated_text: 'Unity is better for men, even with their own kind who are few;

children.text: tuṣeṇāpi parityaktā na prarohanti taṇḍulāḥ // Hit_1.36 //
children.translated_text: rice-grains, when deprived of their husks, do not sprout.'

body.text: iti vicitya pakṣiṇaḥ sarve jālam ādāya utpatitāḥ | anantaraṃ ca vyādhaḥ sudūrāj jālāpahārakāṃs tān avalokya paścād dhāvito 'cintayat-
body.translated_text: Having deliberated thus, all the birds took up the net and flew away. Thereupon the hunter, seeing from far off those who had carried away his net, ran after [them] and thought:

children.text: saṃhatās tu haranty ete mama jālaṃ vihaṅgamāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'United, these birds carry away my net;

children.text: yadā tu nipatiṣyanti vaśam eṣyanti me tadā // Hit_1.37 //
children.translated_text: but when they fall [apart], they will come into my power.'

body.text: tatas teṣu cakṣur viṣayam atikrānteṣu pakṣiṣu sa vyādho nivṛttaḥ | atha lubdhakaṃ nivṛttaṃ dṛṣṭvā kapotā ūcuḥ-svāmin ! kim idānīṃ kartum ucitam ?
body.translated_text: Then, when those birds had passed beyond the range of his sight, the hunter turned back. Now, seeing the hunter turn back, the pigeons said: 'Master, what is appropriate to do now?'

body.text:
citragrīva uvāca-
mātā mitraṃ pitā ceti svabhāvāt tritayaṃ hitam | kārya-kāraṇataś cānye bhavanti hita-buddhayaḥ // Hit_1.38 //
body.translated_text: <s>Citragrīva</s> said: 'Mother, friend, and father — these three are naturally well-wishers; others become well-intentioned through cause and purpose.'

body.text: tan me mitraṃ hiraṇyako nāma mūṣika-rājo gaṇḍakī-tīre citra-vane nivasati | so 'smākaṃ pāśāṃś chetsyati ity ālocya sarve hiraṇyaka-vivara-samīpaṃ gatāḥ | hiraṇyakaś ca sarvadā apāya-śaṅkayā śata-dvāraṃ vivaraṃ kṛtvā nivasati | tato hiraṇyakaḥ kapotāvapāta-bhayāc cakitaḥ tūṣṇīṃ sthitaḥ | citragrīva uvāca-sakhe hiraṇyaka ! katham asmān na sambhāṣase ?
body.translated_text: 'I have a friend, a mouse-king named <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>, who lives in <s>Citravana</s> on the bank of the <s>Gaṇḍakī</s> [river]. He will cut our bonds.' Having thus deliberated, they all went near the burrow of <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>. And <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>, always fearing danger, lived in a burrow with a hundred openings. Then <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>, frightened by the sound of the pigeons landing, remained silent. <s>Citragrīva</s> said: 'Friend <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>! Why do you not speak to us?'

body.text: tato hiraṇyakas tad-vacanaṃ pratyabhijñāya sa-sambhramaṃ bahir niḥsṛtya abravīt-āḥ ! puṇyavān asmi priya-suhṛn me citragrīvaḥ samāyātaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>, recognizing that voice, rushed out in excitement and said: 'Ah! I am fortunate — my dear friend <s>Citragrīva</s> has arrived!'

children.text: yasya mitreṇa sambhāṣo yasya mitreṇa saṃsthitiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'He who converses with a friend, he who stays with a friend,

children.text: yasya mitreṇa saṃlāpas tato nāstīha puṇyavān // Hit_1.39 //
children.translated_text: he who talks with a friend — there is no one more fortunate than he in this world.'

body.text: atha pāśa-baddhāṃś caitān dṛṣṭvā sa-vismayaḥ kṣaṇaṃ sthitvā uvāca-sakhe ! kim etat ?
body.translated_text: Then, seeing them bound in snares, he stood for a moment in astonishment and said: 'Friend, what is this?'

body.text: citragrīva uvāca-sakhe ! asmākaṃ prāktana-janma-karmaṇaḥ phalam etat |
body.translated_text: <s>Citragrīva</s> said: 'Friend, this is the fruit of our <s>karma</s> (actions) from previous births.'

children.text: yasmāc ca yena ca yathā ca yadā ca yac ca
children.translated_text: 'From whatever cause, by whomever, in whatever manner, whenever, and whatever,

children.text: yāvac ca yatra ca śubhāśubham ātma-karma |
children.translated_text: to whatever extent, and wherever — the good and bad <s>karma</s> of the self —

children.text: tasmāc ca tena ca tathā ca tadā ca tac ca
children.translated_text: from that very cause, by that very [agent], in that very manner, at that very time, and that very [result],

children.text: tāvac ca tatra ca vidhātṛ-vaśād upaiti // Hit_1.40 //
children.translated_text: to that very extent, and in that very place — it comes about by the will of the Creator.'

body.text: rāga-śoka-parītāpa-bandhana-vyasanāni ca | ātmāparādha-vṛkṣāṇāṃ phalāny etāni dehinām // Hit_1.41 //
body.translated_text: 'Attachment, grief, torment, bondage, and calamity — these are the fruits, for embodied beings, of the trees of one's own transgressions.'

body.text: etac chrutvā hiraṇyakaś citragrīvasya bandhanaṃ chettuṃ satvaram upasarpati | tatra citragrīva uvāca-mitra ! mā maivaṃ kuru | prathamam asmad-āśritānām eteṣāṃ tāvat pāśāṃś chindhi | mama pāśaṃ paścāc chetsyasi |
body.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> quickly approached to cut <s>Citragrīva</s>'s bonds. Thereupon <s>Citragrīva</s> said — Friend! Do not do this! First cut the snares of these my dependents; you shall cut my snare afterwards.

body.text: hiraṇyako 'py āha-aham alpa-śaktiḥ | dantāś ca me komalāḥ | tad eteṣāṃ pāśāṃś chettuṃ kathaṃ samartho bhavāmi ? tat yāvan me dantā na truṭyanti, tāvat tava pāśaṃ chinadmi | tad-anantaram apy eteṣāṃ bandhanaṃ yāvat śakyaṃ chetsyāmi |
body.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> also said — I am of little strength, and my teeth are soft. How then shall I be able to cut through the snares of all these? Therefore, while my teeth have not yet broken, let me cut your snare first. After that, I shall cut the bonds of the others as far as I am able.

body.text: citragrīva uvāca-astv evam | tathāpi yathā-śakti bandhanam eteṣāṃ khaṇḍaya |
body.translated_text: <s>Citragrīva</s> said — Let it be so. Nevertheless, break their bonds as far as you can.

body.text: hiraṇyakenoktam-ātma-parityāgena yadāśritānāṃ parirakṣaṇaṃ tan na nīti-vedināṃ sammatam | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said — The protection of dependents at the cost of sacrificing oneself is not approved by those versed in <s>nīti</s> (statecraft). For —

children.text: āpad-arthe dhanaṃ rakṣed dārān rakṣed dhanair api |
children.translated_text: One should protect wealth for times of adversity; one should protect one's wife even at the cost of wealth;

children.text: ātmānaṃ satataṃ rakṣed dārair api dhanair api // Hit_1.42 //
children.translated_text: One should always protect oneself, even at the cost of wife and wealth. // Hit_1.42 //

children.text: anyac ca--
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: dharmārtha-kāma-mokṣāṇāṃ prāṇāḥ saṃsthita-hetavaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇas</s> (vital breaths) are the foundation for <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>artha</s> (wealth), <s>kāma</s> (desire), and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation);

children.text: tān nighnatā kiṃ na hataṃ rakṣatā kiṃ na rakṣitam // Hit_1.43 //
children.translated_text: By one who destroys them, what is not destroyed? By one who protects them, what is not protected? // Hit_1.43 //

body.text: citragrīva uvāca-sakhe ! nītis tāvad īdṛśy eva, kintv aham asmad-āśritānāṃ duḥkhaṃ soḍhuṃ sarvathāsamarthas tenedaṃ bravīmi | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: <s>Citragrīva</s> said — Friend! Such indeed is the rule of <s>nīti</s> (statecraft), but I am utterly unable to endure the suffering of those who depend upon me; therefore I say this. For —

children.text: dhanāni jīvitaṃ caiva parārthe prājña utsṛjet |
children.translated_text: A wise person should sacrifice wealth and even life for the sake of others;

children.text: sannimitte varaṃ tyāgo vināśe niyate sati // Hit_1.44 //
children.translated_text: When destruction is certain, it is better to give up for a worthy cause. // Hit_1.44 //

body.text: ayam aparaś cāsādhāraṇo hetuḥ |
body.translated_text: And here is another extraordinary reason:

children.text: jāti-dravya-balānāṃ ca sāmyam eṣāṃ mayā saha |
children.translated_text: These are equal to me in birth, substance, and strength;

children.text: mat-prabhutva-phalaṃ brūhi kadā kiṃ tad bhaviṣyati // Hit_1.45 //
children.translated_text: Tell me, what fruit of my lordship will ever come to be, and when? // Hit_1.45 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: vinā vartanam evaite na tyajanti mamāntikam |
children.translated_text: Even without sustenance, these do not leave my side;

children.text: tan me prāṇa-vyayenāpi jīvayaitān mamāśritān // Hit_1.46 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, even at the cost of my life, keep alive these dependents of mine. // Hit_1.46 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: māṃsa-mūtra-purīṣāsthi-pūrite'tra kalevare |
children.translated_text: In this body filled with flesh, urine, excrement, and bones,

children.text: vinaśvare vihāyāsthāṃ yaśaḥ pālaya mitra me // Hit_1.47 //
children.translated_text: Which is perishable — abandoning attachment to it, protect my honor, O friend. // Hit_1.47 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca paśya-
children.translated_text: And consider this —

children.text: yadi nityam anityena nirmalaṃ mala-vāhinā |
children.translated_text: If by the impermanent, impurity-bearing body

children.text: yaśaḥ kāyena labhyeta tan na labdhaṃ bhaven nu kim // Hit_1.48 //
children.translated_text: Eternal fame can be obtained, would that not be a worthy gain? // Hit_1.48 //

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: For —

children.text: śarīrasya guṇānāṃ ca dūram atyantam antaram |
children.translated_text: Between the body and virtues, the distance is immeasurable;

children.text: śarīraṃ kṣaṇa-vidhvaṃsi kalpānta-sthāyino guṇāḥ // Hit_1.49 //
children.translated_text: The body perishes in a moment, but virtues endure until the end of a <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age). // Hit_1.49 //

body.text: ity ākarṇya hiraṇyakaḥ prahṛṣṭa-manāḥ pulakitaḥ san abravīt-sādhu mitra ! sādhu | anenāśrita-vātsalyena trailokyasyāpi prabhutvaṃ tvayi yujyate | evam uktvā tena sarveṣāṃ kapotānāṃ bandhanāni chinnāni | tato hiraṇyakaḥ sarvān sādaraṃ sampūjya āha-sakhe citragrīva ! sarvathātra jāla-bandhana-vidhau sati doṣam āśaṅkya ātmani avajñā na kartavyā | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>, delighted in heart and thrilled with joy, said — Well done, friend! Well done! By this affection for your dependents, sovereignty over the three worlds would be fitting for you. Having said this, he cut the bonds of all the pigeons. Then <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>, having respectfully honored them all, said — Friend <s>Citragrīva</s>! In any such event of being caught in a net, you should not hold yourself in contempt, apprehending fault in yourself. For —

children.text: yo 'dhikād yojana-śatān paśyatīhāmiṣaṃ khagaḥ |
children.translated_text: The bird that sees food from over a hundred <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) away,

children.text: sa eva prāpta-kālas tu pāśa-bandhaṃ na paśyati // Hit_1.50 //
children.translated_text: That very same one, when its time has come, does not see the snare. // Hit_1.50 //

body.text: aparaṃ ca-

children.text: śaśi-divākarayor graha-pīḍanaṃ
children.translated_text: The eclipsing of the moon and the sun,

children.text: gaja-bhujaṅgamayor api bandhanam |
children.translated_text: The binding of elephants and serpents,

children.text: matimatāṃ ca vilokya daridratāṃ
children.translated_text: And seeing the poverty of the wise —

children.text: vidhir aho balavān iti me matiḥ // Hit_1.51 //
children.translated_text: Fate is indeed powerful, such is my conviction. // Hit_1.51 //

body.translated_text: And moreover —

body.text: anyac ca-

children.text: vyomaikānta-vihāriṇo 'pi vihagāḥ samprāpnuvanty āpadaṃ
children.translated_text: Even birds that soar exclusively in the sky meet with calamity;

children.text: badhyante nipuṇair agādha-salilān matsyāḥ samudrād api |
children.translated_text: Even fish are caught by the skillful from the fathomless ocean.

children.text: durnītaṃ kim ihāsti kiṃ sucaritaṃ kaḥ sthāna-lābhe guṇaḥ
children.translated_text: What here is misconduct? What is good conduct? What use is gaining position?

children.text: kālo hi vyasana-prasārita-karo gṛhṇāti dūrād api // Hit_1.52 //
children.translated_text: For Time, with its hand outstretched in calamity, seizes even from afar. // Hit_1.52 //

body.translated_text: And further —

body.text: iti prabodhya ātithyaṃ kṛtvā āliṅgya ca tena sampreṣitaś citragrīvo 'pi saparivāro yatheṣṭa-deśān yayau, hiraṇyako 'pi sva-vivaraṃ praviṣṭaḥ |
body.translated_text: Having thus consoled him, offered hospitality, and embraced him, <s>Citragrīva</s>, sent off by him, departed with his retinue to whatever land he wished, and <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> also entered his hole.

children.text: yāni kāni ca mitrāṇi kartavyāni śatāni ca |
children.translated_text: Whatever friendships one may form, let them be a hundred;

children.text: paśya mūṣika-mitreṇa kapotā mukta-bandhanāḥ // Hit_1.53 //
children.translated_text: See how through the friendship of a mouse, the pigeons were freed from their bonds. // Hit_1.53 //

body.text: atha laghu-patanaka-nāmā kākaḥ sarva-vṛttānta-darśī sāścaryam idam āha-aho hiraṇyaka ! ślāghyo 'si, ato 'ham api tvayā saha maitrīṃ kartum icchāmi | atas tvaṃ māṃ maitryeṇānugrahītum arhasi | etac chrutvā hiraṇyako 'pi vivarābhyantarād āha-kas tvam ?
body.translated_text: Now, the crow named <s>Laghupatanaka</s>, having witnessed the entire affair, said with wonder — O <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>! You are praiseworthy; therefore I too wish to form a friendship with you. So please favor me with your friendship. Hearing this, <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> spoke from inside his hole — Who are you?

body.text: sa brūte-laghupatanaka-nāmā vāyaso 'ham | hiraṇyako vihasyāha-kā tvayā saha maitrī ? yataḥ-
body.translated_text: He said — I am a crow named <s>Laghupatanaka</s>. <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> laughed and said — What friendship can there be with you? For —

children.text: yad yena yujyate loke budhas tat tena yojayet |
children.translated_text: Whatever is fitting for one in the world, a wise person should connect with that;

children.text: aham annaṃ bhavān bhoktā kathaṃ prītir bhaviṣyati // Hit_1.54 //
children.translated_text: I am the food and you are the eater — how can there be affection? // Hit_1.54 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: bhakṣya-bhakṣayoḥ prītir vipatteḥ kāraṇaṃ matam |
children.translated_text: Affection between the eatable and the eater is considered a cause of misfortune;

children.text: śṛgālāt pāśabaddho 'sau mṛgaḥ kākena rakṣitaḥ // Hit_1.55 //
children.translated_text: By the jackal's fault, the deer was caught in a snare, but was saved by the crow. // Hit_1.55 //

body.text: vāyaso 'bravīt--katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The crow asked — How is that?

body.text: hiraṇyakaḥ kathayati-
body.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> narrates —

body.text: kathā 2
body.translated_text: Story 2

body.text: asti magadha-deśe campakavatī nāma araṇyānī | tasyāṃ cirāt mahatā snehena mṛga-kākau nivasataḥ | sa ca mṛgaḥ svecchayā bhrāmyan hṛṣṭa-puṣṭāṅgaḥ kenacit śṛgālenāvalokitaḥ | taṃ dṛṣṭvā śṛgālo 'cintayat-āḥ ! katham etan-māṃsaṃ sulalitaṃ bhakṣayāmi ? bhavatu, viśvāsaṃ tāvad utpādayāmi ity ālocya upasṛtyābravīt-mitra ! kuśalaṃ te ?
body.translated_text: In the land of <s>Magadha</s>, there is a forest named <s>Campakavatī</s>. In it, a deer and a crow had long lived together in great affection. That deer, roaming freely, plump and well-nourished, was spotted by a certain jackal. Seeing him, the jackal thought — Ah! How can I eat this delicious flesh? Well then, let me first win his trust. Having so decided, he approached and said — Friend! Are you well?

body.text: mṛgeṇoktam-kas tvam ?
body.translated_text: The deer said — Who are you?

body.text: sa brūte-kṣudra-buddhi-nāmā jambuko 'ham | atrāraṇye bandhu-hīno mṛtavat ekākī nivasāmi | idānīṃ tvāṃ mitram āsādya punaḥ sa-bandhur jīva-lokaṃ praviṣṭo 'smi | adhunā tavānucareṇa mayā sarvathā bhavitavyam iti |
body.translated_text: He replied — I am a jackal named <s>Kṣudrabuddhi</s> (Small-wit). In this forest, bereft of kinsmen, I live alone like a dead man. Now, having found you as a friend, I have entered the world of the living again with a kinsman. Henceforth, I shall be your companion in every way.

body.text: mṛgeṇoktam-evam astu |
body.translated_text: The deer said — So be it.

body.text:
tataḥ paścād astaṃ gate savitari bhagavati marīci-mālini tau mṛgasya vāsa-bhūmiṃ gatau | tatra campaka-vṛkṣa-śākhāyāṃ subuddhi-nāmā kāko mṛgasya cira-mitraṃ nivasati | tau dṛṣṭvā kāko 'vadat-sakhe citrāṅga ! ko 'yaṃ dvitīyaḥ ?
mṛgo brūte-mitra ! akasmād āgantunā saha maitrī na yuktā | tan na bhadram ācaritam | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: Then, after the blessed sun with his garland of rays had set, the two went to the deer's dwelling place. There, on a branch of a <s>campaka</s> tree, lived a crow named <s>Subuddhi</s> (Good-wit), a long-time friend of the deer. Seeing the two, the crow said — Friend <s>Citrāṅga</s>! Who is this second one? The deer said — Friend! Friendship with a stranger who comes unannounced is not proper; you have not acted wisely. And so it is said —

children.text: ajñāta-kula-śīlasya vāso deyo na kasyacit |
children.translated_text: One whose family and character are unknown should not be given shelter by anyone;

children.text: mārjārasya hi doṣeṇa hato gṛdhro jarad-gavaḥ // Hit_1.56 //
children.translated_text: Through the fault of the cat, the vulture <s>Jaradgava</s> was killed. // Hit_1.56 //

body.text: tau āhatuḥ--katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The two asked — How is that?

body.text:
kākaḥ kathayati-
kathā 3
body.translated_text: The crow narrates — Story 3

body.text: asti bhāgīrathī-tīre gṛdhrakūṭa-nāmni parvate mahān parkaṭī-vṛkṣaḥ tasya koṭare daiva-durvipākāt galita-nakha-nayano jaradgava-nāmā gṛdhraḥ prativasati | atha kṛpayā taj-jīvanāya tad-vṛkṣa-vāsinaḥ pakṣiṇaḥ svāhārāt kiṃcit kiṃcid uddhṛtya tasmai dadati, tenāsau jīvati, teṣāṃ śāvaka-rakṣāṃ ca karoti | atha kadācit dīrghakarṇa-nāmā mārjāraḥ pakṣi-śāvakān bhakṣayituṃ tatrāgataḥ | tatas tam āyāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā pakṣi-śāvakair bhayārtaiḥ kolāhalaḥ kṛtaḥ | tac chrutvā jaradgavena uktam-ko 'yam āyāti ? dīrghakarṇo gṛdhram avalokya sa-bhayam āha-hā hato 'smi yato 'yaṃ māṃ vyāpādayiṣyati | athavā-
body.translated_text: On the bank of the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> (Ganges), on a mountain named <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak), there stands a great fig tree. In its hollow, by cruel turn of fate, there lived a vulture named <s>Jaradgava</s> (Old Cow), whose claws and eyes had deteriorated. Out of compassion, the birds dwelling in that tree would each set aside a little from their own food and give it to him; thus he lived, and in return he protected their young ones. Now once, a cat named <s>Dīrghakarṇa</s> (Long-ear) came there to devour the bird-chicks. Seeing him approach, the frightened bird-chicks raised a clamor. Hearing that, <s>Jaradgava</s> said — Who comes there? <s>Dīrghakarṇa</s>, seeing the vulture, said in fear — Alas, I am doomed, for he will kill me! But then again —

children.text: tāvad bhayasya bhetavyaṃ yāvad bhayam anāgatam |
children.translated_text: One should fear danger only as long as it has not yet arrived;

children.text: āgataṃ tu bhayaṃ vīkṣya naraḥ kuryād yathocitam // Hit_1.57 //
children.translated_text: But seeing danger that has come, one should act as is appropriate. // Hit_1.57 //

body.text: adhunātisannidhāne palāyitum akṣamaḥ | tad yathā bhavitavyaṃ tathā bhavatu, tāvat viśvāsam utpādyāsya samīpam upagacchāmīty ālocya tam upasṛtyābravīt-ārya ! tvām abhivande |
body.translated_text: Now, being too close to flee, let whatever will be, be. Let me win his trust and approach him — so deciding, he approached and said — Venerable sir! I salute you.

body.text: gṛdhro 'vadat-kas tvam ?
body.translated_text: The vulture said — Who are you?

body.text: so 'vadat-mārjāro 'ham |
body.translated_text: He said — I am a cat.

body.text: gṛdhro brūte-dūram apasara no cet hantavyo 'si mayā |
body.translated_text: The vulture said — Go far away, or you shall be killed by me!

body.text: mārjāro 'vadat-śrūyatāṃ tāvat mad-vacanam | tato yady ahaṃ vadhyas tadā hantavyaḥ | yataḥ -
body.translated_text: The cat said — Hear my words first. Then, if I deserve to be killed, kill me. For —

children.text: jāti-mātreṇa kiṃ kaścid vadhyate pūjyate kvacit |
children.translated_text: Is anyone killed or honored merely on account of their species?

children.text: vyavahāraṃ parijñāya vadhyaḥ pūjyo 'thavā bhavet // Hit_1.58 //
children.translated_text: Having ascertained one's conduct, one should determine whether they are to be punished or honored. // Hit_1.58 //

body.text: gṛdhro brūte-brūhi kim artham āgato 'si ?
body.translated_text: The vulture said — Tell me, for what purpose have you come?

body.text: so 'vadat-aham atra gaṅgā-tīre nitya-snāyī nirāmiṣāśī brahmacārī cāndrāyaṇa-vratam ācaraṃs tiṣṭhāmi | yuṣmān dharma-jñāna-ratāḥ prema-viśvāsa-bhūmayaḥ iti pakṣiṇaḥ sarve sarvadā mamāgre prastuvanti, ato bhavadbhyo vidyāvayo-vṛddhebhyo dharmaṃ śrotum ihāgataḥ | bhavantaś caitādṛśā dharmajñāḥ, yan mām atithiṃ hantum udyatāḥ ? gṛhastha-dharmaś ca eṣaḥ -
body.translated_text: He said — I dwell here on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, bathing daily, abstaining from meat, observing celibacy, and practicing the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar) vow. All the birds constantly praise you before me as devoted to righteous knowledge and as the very ground of love and trust; therefore I have come here to learn <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) from you, who are advanced in learning and age. And you, being such knowers of <s>dharma</s>, are prepared to kill me, a guest? The duty of a householder is this —

children.text: arāv apy ucitaṃ kāryam ātithyaṃ gṛham āgate |
children.translated_text: Even to an enemy, proper hospitality should be shown when he comes to one's house;

children.text: chettum apy āgate chāyāṃ nopasaṃharate drumaḥ // Hit_1.59 //
children.translated_text: Even when someone comes to cut it, a tree does not withdraw its shade. // Hit_1.59 //

body.text: kiṃ ca-yadi annaṃ nāsti, tadā suprītenāpi vacasā tāvad atithiḥ pūjya eva |
body.translated_text: Moreover — if there is no food, even so, a guest should be honored with kind words at the very least.

children.text: tṛṇāni bhūmir udakaṃ vāk caturthī ca sūnṛtā |
children.translated_text: Grass, ground, water, and a fourth — kind speech;

children.text: etāny api satāṃ gehe nocchidyante kadācana // Hit_1.60 //
children.translated_text: These are never lacking in the house of the good. // Hit_1.60 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: bālo vā yadi vā vṛddho yuvā vā gṛham āgataḥ |
children.translated_text: Whether a child, an old man, or a youth comes to one's house,

children.text: tasya pūjā vidhātavyā sarvasyābhyāgato guruḥ // Hit_1.61 //
children.translated_text: He should be honored, for a guest is the guru of all. // Hit_1.61 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: nirguṇeṣv api sattveṣu dayāṃ kurvanti sādhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: The good show compassion even toward beings without merit;

children.text: na hi saṃharate jyotsnāṃ candraś cāṇḍāla-veśmanaḥ // Hit_1.62 //
children.translated_text: The moon does not withhold its light from the house of a <s>caṇḍāla</s> (outcast). // Hit_1.62 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: atithir yasya bhagnāśo gṛhāt pratinivartate |
children.translated_text: The guest who turns away from a house with his hopes dashed,

children.text: sa dattvā duṣkṛtaṃ tasmai puṇyam ādāya gacchati // Hit_1.63 //
children.translated_text: Having given his sins to the host, departs taking the host's merit. // Hit_1.63 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: uttamasyāpi varṇasya nīco 'pi gṛham āgataḥ |
children.translated_text: Even a lowly person who comes to the house of one of the highest <s>varṇa</s> (caste)

children.text: pūjanīyo yathā-yogyaṃ sarva-deva-mayo 'tithiḥ // Hit_1.64 //
children.translated_text: Should be honored appropriately, for a guest embodies all the gods. // Hit_1.64 //

body.text: gṛdhro 'vadat-mārjāro hi māṃsa-ruciḥ | pakṣi-śāvakāś cātra nivasanti | tenāham eva bravīmi | tac chrutvā mārjāro bhūmiṃ spṛṣṭvā karṇau spṛśati, brūte ca-mayā dharma-śāstraṃ śrutvā vīta-rāgenedaṃ duṣkaraṃ vrataṃ cāndrāyaṇam adhyavasitam | yataḥ parasparaṃ vivadamānānām api dharma-śāstrāṇām ahiṃsā paramo dharmaḥ ity atraikamatyam | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: The vulture said — A cat is fond of meat, and bird-chicks dwell here; that is why I spoke thus. Hearing this, the cat touched the ground and then his ears, and said — Having heard the <s>dharmaśāstra</s> (law scriptures), I, now free from passion, have undertaken this difficult <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar) vow. For even the <s>dharmaśāstras</s>, though they disagree with one another on many points, are unanimous on this: <s>ahiṃsā</s> (non-violence) is the highest <s>dharma</s>. For —

children.text: sarva-hiṃsā-nivṛttā ye narāḥ sarva-sahāś ca ye |
children.translated_text: Those men who have renounced all violence, who endure all things,

children.text: sarvasyāśraya-bhūtāś ca te narāḥ svarga-gāminaḥ // Hit_1.65 //
children.translated_text: And who are the refuge of all — those men go to heaven. // Hit_1.65 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: eka eva suhṛd dharmo nidhane'py anuyāti yaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness) alone is the one true friend that follows even in death;

children.text: śarīreṇa samaṃ nāśaṃ sarvam anyad hi gacchati // Hit_1.66 //
children.translated_text: Everything else perishes along with the body. // Hit_1.66 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: yo 'tti yasya yadā māṃsam ubhayoḥ paśyatāntaram |
children.translated_text: Consider the difference between the one who eats another's flesh and the other;

children.text: ekasya kṣaṇikā prītir anyaḥ prāṇair vimucyate // Hit_1.67 //
children.translated_text: For one there is momentary pleasure, while the other is deprived of life. // Hit_1.67 //

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: martavyam iti yad duḥkhaṃ puruṣasyopajāyate |
children.translated_text: The suffering that arises in a person from the thought 'I must die' —

children.text: śakyas tenānumānena paro 'pi parirakṣitum // Hit_1.68 //
children.translated_text: By that reasoning, one can protect others as well. // Hit_1.68 //

children.text: śṛṇu punaḥ-
children.translated_text: Listen further —

children.text: svacchanda-vana-jātena śākenāpi prapūryate |
children.translated_text: Even with vegetables grown wild in the forest, one can fill oneself;

children.text: asya dagdhodarasyārthe kaḥ kuryāt pātakaṃ mahat // Hit_1.69 //
children.translated_text: For the sake of this burning stomach, who would commit a great sin? // Hit_1.69 //

body.text: evaṃ viśvāsya sa mārjāras taru-koṭare sthitaḥ | tato dineṣu gacchatsu asau pakṣi-śāvakān ākramya sva-koṭaram ānīya pratyahaṃ khādati | atha yeṣām apatyāni khāditāni | taiḥ śokārtair vilapadbhir itas tato jijñāsā samārabdhā | tat parijñāya mārjāraḥ koṭarān niḥsṛtya bahiḥ palāyitaḥ | paścāt pakṣibhir itas tato nirūpayadbhis tatra taru-koṭare śāvakāḥ khāditā iti sarvaiḥ pakṣibhir niścitya ca gṛdhro vyāpāditaḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-ajñāta-kula-śīlasya ity ādi |
body.translated_text: Having thus gained [the deer's] trust, the cat stayed in the hollow of the tree. Then, as the days passed, that [cat] would seize the chicks of the birds, bring them to his own hollow, and eat them every day. Then those whose offspring had been eaten, grieving and lamenting, began searching here and there. Realizing this, the cat slipped out of the hollow and fled. Afterwards, the birds, looking here and there, determined that the chicks had been eaten right there in that tree-hollow; and all the birds, having concluded [this], killed the vulture. Therefore I say — 'Of one whose family and character are unknown' and so forth.

body.text: ity ākarṇya sa jambukaḥ sa-kopam āha-mṛgasya prathama-darśana-dine bhavān api ajñāta-kula-śīla eva āsīt | tat kathaṃ bhavatā saha etasya snehānuvṛttir uttarottaraṃ vardhate ? athavā-
body.translated_text: Hearing this, the jackal said angrily: 'On the day of first meeting the deer, you too were of unknown family and character! So how is it that your affectionate intimacy with him keeps growing more and more? Or rather —'

children.text: yatra vidvaj-jano nāsti ślāghyas tatrālpadhīr api |
children.translated_text: Where there is no learned person, even one of small intellect is praised;

children.text: nirasta-pādape deśe eraṇḍo 'pi drumāyate // Hit_1.70 //
children.translated_text: in a land devoid of trees, even the castor-oil plant passes for a tree. // Hit 1.70 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: ayaṃ nijaḥ paro veti gaṇanā laghu-cetasām |
children.translated_text: 'This one is mine, that one is a stranger' — such is the reckoning of the small-minded;

children.text: udāra-caritānāṃ tu vasudhaiva kuṭumbakam // Hit_1.71 //
children.translated_text: for the noble-hearted, however, the entire earth is [their] family. // Hit 1.71 //

body.text: yathā cāyaṃ mṛgo mama bandhus tathā bhavān api | mṛgo 'bravīt kamanena uttarottareṇa ? sarvair ekatra viśrambhālāpaiḥ sukham anubhavadbhiḥ sthīyatām | yataḥ-

children.text: na kaścit kasyacin mitraṃ na kaścit kasyacid ripuḥ |
children.translated_text: No one is anyone's friend, no one is anyone's enemy;

children.text: vyavahāreṇa mitrāṇi jāyante ripavas tathā // Hit_1.72 //
children.translated_text: friends and foes alike are born through [actual] dealings. // Hit 1.72 //

body.translated_text: Just as this deer is my friend, so are you also.' The deer said: 'By what [means], progressively?' 'Let all of us stay together, enjoying happiness through confidential conversations. For —'

body.text: kākena uktam-evam astu | atha prātaḥ sarve yathābhimata-deśaṃ gatāḥ | ekadā nibhṛtaṃ śṛgālo brūte-sakhe mṛga ! etasminn eva vanaika-deśe sasya-pūrṇaṃ kṣetram asti | tad ahaṃ tvāṃ tatra nītvā darśayāmi | tathā kṛte sati mṛgaḥ pratyahaṃ tatra gatvā sasyaṃ khādati | tato dina-katipayena kṣetra-patinā tad dṛṣṭvā pāśās tatra yojitāḥ | anantaraṃ punar āgato mṛgaḥ tatra caran pāśair baddho 'cintayat-ko mām itaḥ kāla-pāśād iva vyādha-pāśāt trātuṃ mitrād anyaḥ samarthaḥ ?
body.translated_text: The crow said: 'So be it.' Then, in the morning, all went to their respective desired places. One day, the jackal said privately: 'Friend deer! In a certain part of this very forest there is a field full of crops. I shall take you there and show it.' When that was done, the deer went there every day and ate the crops. Then, after some days, the field-owner saw this and set snares there. Subsequently, the deer, coming again and grazing there, was caught in the snares and thought: 'Who other than a friend is able to rescue me from this snare of the hunter, which is like the snare of Death?'

body.text: atrāntare jambukas tatrāgatya upasthito 'cintayat-phalitas tāvad asmākaṃ kapaṭa-prabandhaḥ | manoratha-siddhir api bāhulyān me bhaviṣyati | yataḥ etasya uktṛtyamānasya māṃsāsṛg-liptāni asthīni mayā avaśyaṃ prāptavyāni | tāni ca bāhulyena mama bhojanāni bhaviṣyanti | sa ca mṛgas taṃ dṛṣṭvā ullāsito brūte-sakhe ! chindhi tāvan mama bandhanam | satvaraṃ trāyasva mām | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the jackal arrived there and stood nearby, thinking: 'Our deceitful scheme has indeed borne fruit! My heart's desire will also be abundantly fulfilled. For when this [deer] is cut up, I shall certainly obtain the bones smeared with flesh and blood, and those will provide me with abundant food.' The deer, seeing him, said hopefully: 'Friend! Cut my bonds at once! Save me quickly! For —'

children.text: āpatsu mitraṃ jānīyād raṇe śūraṃ ṛṇe śucim |
children.translated_text: One should know a friend in adversity, a hero in battle, an honest man in debt,

children.text: bhāryāṃ kṣīṇeṣu vitteṣu vyasaneṣu ca bāndhavān // Hit_1.73 //
children.translated_text: a wife when wealth is exhausted, and kinsmen in times of calamity. // Hit 1.73 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: utsave vyasane prāpte durbhikṣe śatru-saṅkaṭe |
children.translated_text: In a festival, in a calamity that has befallen, in famine, in danger from an enemy,

children.text: rāja-dvāre śmaśāne ca yas tiṣṭhati sa bāndhavaḥ // Hit_1.74 //
children.translated_text: at the king's gate, and at the cremation ground — he who stands [by you] is a [true] kinsman. // Hit 1.74 //

body.text: jambukaḥ pāśaṃ muhur muhur vilokyācintayat-dṛḍhas tāvad ayaṃ bandhaḥ | brūte ca-sakhe ! snāyu-nirmitāḥ pāśāḥ, tad adya bhaṭṭāraka-vāre katham etān dantaiḥ spṛśāmi ? mitra ! yadi citte na anyathā manyase, tadā prabhāte yat tvayā vaktavyaṃ tat kartavyam iti | anantaraṃ sa kākaḥ pradoṣakā mṛgamanāgatam avalokya itas tato 'nviṣyan tathāvidhaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā uvāca-sakhe ! kim etat ? mṛgeṇoktam-avadhīrita-suhṛd-vākyasya phalam etat tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: The jackal, looking at the snare again and again, thought: 'This bond is indeed strong.' And he said: 'Friend! The snares are made of sinew; how then can I touch them with my teeth on this holy day of the Sun (<s>Bhaṭṭāraka-vāra</s>)? Dear friend! If you do not think otherwise in your mind, then at dawn whatever you say shall be done.' Subsequently, the crow, not seeing the deer return by evening, went searching here and there, and seeing him in that condition, said: 'Friend! What is this?' The deer said: 'This is the fruit of one who disregarded the words of a well-wishing friend. And so it is said —'

children.text: suhṛdāṃ hita-kāmānāṃ yaḥ śṛṇoti na bhāṣitam |
children.translated_text: He who does not heed the words of friends who desire his welfare —

children.text: vipat sannihitā tasya sa naraḥ śatrunandanaḥ // Hit_1.75 //
children.translated_text: calamity is near at hand for that man; he is a delighter of enemies. // Hit 1.75 //

body.text: kāko brūte-sa vañcakaḥ kvāste ?
body.translated_text: The crow said: 'Where is that deceiver?'

body.text: mṛgeṇoktaṃ-man-māṃsārthī tiṣṭhaty atraiva |
body.translated_text: The deer said: 'Desiring my flesh, he stands right here.'

body.text: kāko brūte-mitra ! uktam eva mayā pūrvam |
body.translated_text: The crow said: 'Friend! I told you so before!'

children.text: aparādho na me'stīti naitad viśvāsa-kāraṇam |
children.translated_text: 'I have committed no offense' — this alone is not a cause for trust;

children.text: vidyate hi nṛśaṃsebhyo bhayaṃ guṇavatām api // Hit_1.76 //
children.translated_text: for even the virtuous have reason to fear from the cruel. // Hit 1.76 //

children.text: dīpa-nirvāṇa-gandhaṃ ca suhṛd-vākyam arundhatīm |
children.translated_text: The smell of an extinguished lamp, the words of a well-wisher, [the star] <s>Arundhatī</s> —

children.text: na jighranti na śṛṇvanti na pśyanti gatāyuṣaḥ // Hit_1.77 //
children.translated_text: those whose life is spent do not smell, do not hear, do not see [these]. // Hit 1.77 //

children.text: parokṣe kārya-hantāraṃ pratyakṣe priya-vādinam |
children.translated_text: One who ruins your affairs behind your back yet speaks sweetly to your face —

children.text: varjayet tādṛśaṃ mitraṃ viṣa-kumbhaṃ payomukham // Hit_1.78 //
children.translated_text: such a friend should be avoided, [for he is] a pot of poison with milk on top. // Hit 1.78 //
