body.text: tataḥ kāko dīrghaṃ niḥśvasya uvāca-are vañcaka ! kiṃ tvayā pāpa-karmaṇā kṛtam | yataḥ-

children.text: saṃlāpitānāṃ madhurair vacobhir
children.translated_text: Of those who have been engaged in conversation with sweet words

children.text: mithyopacāraiś ca vaśīkṛtānām |
children.translated_text: and won over by false courtesies,

children.text: āśāvatāṃ śraddadhatāṃ ca loke
children.translated_text: of those full of hope and trusting in this world —

children.text: kim arthināṃ vañcayitavyam asti // Hit_1.79 //
children.translated_text: what need is there to deceive such supplicants? // Hit 1.79 //

body.translated_text: Then the crow, heaving a long sigh, said: 'O deceiver! What have you done, evil-doer? For —'

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: upakāriṇi viśrabdhe śuddha-matau yaḥ samācarati pāpam |
children.translated_text: He who does evil to one who is helpful, trusting, and pure of mind —

children.text: taṃ janam asatya-sandhaṃ bhagavati vasudhe kathaṃ vahasi // Hit_1.80 //
children.translated_text: O divine Earth, how do you bear such a person of broken faith? // Hit 1.80 //

children.text: durjanena samaṃ sakhyaṃ vairaṃ cāpi na kārayet |
children.translated_text: One should make neither friendship nor enmity with a wicked person;

children.text: uṣṇo dahati cāṅgāraḥ śītaḥ kṛṣṇāyate karam // Hit_1.81 //
children.translated_text: a hot coal burns, and a cold one blackens the hand. // Hit 1.81 //

body.text: athavā sthitir iyaṃ durjanānām-
body.translated_text: Or rather, this is the nature of the wicked —

children.text: prāk pādayoḥ patati khādati pṛṣṭha-māṃsaṃ
children.translated_text: First he falls at [your] feet, then he devours the flesh of [your] back,

children.text: karṇe phalaṃ kim api rauti śanair vicitram |
children.translated_text: he buzzes something strange softly in [your] ear,

children.text: chidraṃ nirūpya sahasā praviśaty aśaṅkaḥ
children.translated_text: finding a gap, he enters suddenly without hesitation —

children.text: sarvaṃ khalasya caritaṃ maśakaḥ karoti // Hit_1.82 //
children.translated_text: a mosquito performs the entire conduct of a villain! // Hit 1.82 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And so too —

children.text: durjanaḥ priya-vādī ca naitad viśvāsa-kāraṇam |
children.translated_text: A wicked person speaks sweetly — that alone is not a cause for trust;

children.text: madhu tiṣṭhati jihvāgre hṛdi hālāhalaṃ viṣam // Hit_1.83 //
children.translated_text: honey sits on the tip of his tongue, but in his heart is <s>hālāhala</s> poison. // Hit 1.83 //

body.text: atha prabhāte sa kṣetra-patir laguḍa-hastas taṃ pradeśam āgacchan kākenāvalokitaḥ | tam avalokya kākenoktam-sakhe mṛga ! tvam ātmānaṃ mṛtavat sandarśya vātenodaraṃ pūrayitvā pādān stabdhīkṛtya tiṣṭha | ahaṃ tava cakṣuṣī cañcvā kim api vilikhāmi, yadāhaṃ śabdaṃ karomi, tadā tvam utthāya satvaraṃ palāyiṣyase |
body.translated_text: Then at dawn, the field-owner, stick in hand, was seen by the crow coming toward that spot. Seeing him, the crow said: 'Friend deer! Make yourself appear dead — fill your belly with air, stiffen your legs, and lie still. I shall scratch at your eyes with my beak; when I make a sound, then you shall rise quickly and flee.'

body.text: mṛgas tathaiva kāka-vacanena sthitaḥ | tataḥ kṣetra-patinā harṣotphulla-locanena tathāvidho mṛga ālokitaḥ | athāsau-āḥ ! svayaṃ mṛto 'si ? ity uktvā mṛgaṃ bandhanāt mocayitvā pāśān saṃvarītuṃ satvaro babhūva | tataḥ kiyad dūre antarite kṣetra-patau sa mṛgaḥ kākasya śabdaṃ śrutvā satvaram utthāya palāyitaḥ | tam uddiśya tena kṣetra-patinā prakopāt kṣiptena laguḍena śṛgālo vyāpāditaḥ | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: The deer lay just so, as the crow had instructed. Then the field-owner, his eyes wide with delight, saw the deer in that state. Then he exclaimed: 'Ah! You have died on your own?' and saying so, released the deer from its bonds and hastened to gather up the snares. Then, when the field-owner had gone some distance away, the deer, hearing the crow's signal, quickly rose and fled. The stick hurled by the field-owner in anger, aimed at the [fleeing] deer, killed the jackal [instead]. And so it is said —

children.text: tribhir varṣais tribhir māsais tribhiḥ pakṣais tribhir dinaiḥ |
children.translated_text: In three years, in three months, in three fortnights, in three days —

children.text: atyutkaṭaiḥ pāpa-puṇyair ihaiva phalam aśnute // Hit_1.84 //
children.translated_text: the fruits of exceedingly intense sin and merit are experienced in this very life. // Hit 1.84 //

body.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-bhakṣya-bhakṣyakayoḥ prītir ity ādi |
body.translated_text: Therefore I say — 'Between the eater and the eaten, [there can be no true] affection' and so forth.

body.text: iti mṛga-vāyasa-śṛgāla-kathā
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the story of the deer, the crow, and the jackal.

body.text: kākaḥ punar āha-
body.translated_text: The crow further said:

children.text: bhakṣitenāpi bhavatā nāhāro mama puṣkalaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Even though you have eaten, my nourishment is not abundant;

children.text: tvayi jīvati jīvāmi citragrīva ivānagha // Hit_1.85 //
children.translated_text: as long as you live, I live — like <s>Citragrīva</s>, O sinless one. // Hit 1.85 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: tiraścām api viśvāso dṛṣṭaḥ puṇyaika-karmaṇām |
children.translated_text: Trust has been observed even among animals, [when they are] of exclusively meritorious deeds;

children.text: satāṃ hi sādhu-śīlatvāt svabhāvo na nivartate // Hit_1.86 //
children.translated_text: for the nature of the good, being virtuous by disposition, does not turn away. // Hit 1.86 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Furthermore —

children.text: sādhoḥ prakopitasyāpi mano nāyāti vikriyām |
children.translated_text: Even when provoked, the mind of a good person does not undergo corruption;

children.text: na hi tāpayituṃ śakyaṃ sāgarāmbhas tṛṇolkayā // Hit_1.87 //
children.translated_text: for it is not possible to heat the ocean's water with a torch of straw. // Hit 1.87 //

body.text: hiraṇyako brūte-capalas tvam | capalena saha snehaḥ sarvathā na kartavyaḥ | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said: 'You are fickle. With a fickle one, friendship should never be formed. And so it is said —'

children.text: mārjāro mahiṣo meṣaḥ kākaḥ kāpuruṣas tathā |
children.translated_text: A cat, a buffalo, a ram, a crow, and a base man —

children.text: viśvāsāt prabhavanty ete viśvāsas tatra no hitaḥ // Hit_1.88 //
children.translated_text: these gain power through trust; trust in them is not beneficial. // Hit 1.88 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat-śatru-pakṣo bhavān asmākam | śatruṇā sandhir na vidheyam | uktaṃ caitat-

children.text: śatruṇā na hi sandadhyāt saṃśliṣṭenāpi sandhinā |
children.translated_text: One should not make a treaty with an enemy, even with an intimate treaty;

children.text: sutaptam api pānīyaṃ śamayaty eva pāvakam // Hit_1.89 //
children.translated_text: for even thoroughly heated water extinguishes fire. // Hit 1.89 //

body.translated_text: 'And what is more — you belong to the camp of our enemies. One should not make an alliance with an enemy. And this has been said —'

children.text: durjanaḥ parihartavyo vidyayālaṅkṛto 'pi san |
children.translated_text: A wicked person should be avoided, even if adorned with learning;

children.text: maṇinā bhūṣitaḥ sarpaḥ kim asau na bhayaṅkaraḥ // Hit_1.90 //
children.translated_text: is a serpent adorned with a jewel not [still] fearsome? // Hit 1.90 //

children.text: yad aśakyaṃ na tac chaktyaṃ yac chaktyaṃ śakyam eva tat |
children.translated_text: What is impossible cannot be achieved; what is achievable can indeed be achieved;

children.text: nodake śakaṭaṃ yāti na ca naur gacchati sthale // Hit_1.91 //
children.translated_text: a cart does not move on water, nor does a boat travel on land. // Hit 1.91 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: mahatāpy artha-sāreṇa yo viśvasiti śatruṣu |
children.translated_text: He who trusts enemies, even with great wealth [at stake],

children.text: bhāryāsu ca viraktāsu tad-antaṃ tasya jīvanam // Hit_1.92 //
children.translated_text: and wives who are disaffected — his life [lasts only] until that [trust is betrayed]. // Hit 1.92 //

body.text: laghu-patanako brūte-śrutaṃ mayā sarvaṃ, tathāpi mamaitāvan eva saṅkalpaḥ | yat tvayā saha sauhṛdyam avaśyaṃ karaṇīyam iti | anyathā anāhāreṇātmānaṃ tava dvāri vyāpādayiṣyāmīti | tathā hi-
body.translated_text: <s>Laghupatanaka</s> said: 'I have heard everything; still, my resolve is precisely this — that friendship with you must be formed, no matter what. Otherwise, I shall starve myself to death at your door! For —'

children.text: mṛd-ghaṭavat sukha-bhedyo duḥsandhānaś ca durjano bhavati |
children.translated_text: A wicked person, like an earthen pot, is easily broken and hard to mend;

children.text: sujanas tu kanaka-ghaṭavad durbhedyaś cāśu sandheyaḥ // Hit_1.93 //
children.translated_text: but a good person, like a golden vessel, is hard to break and quickly joined again. // Hit 1.93 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Furthermore —

children.text: dravatvāt sarva-lohānāṃ nimittād mṛga-pakṣiṇām |
children.translated_text: Metals [are drawn together] by melting, deer and birds by a [common] cause,

children.text: bhayāl lobhāc ca mūrkhāṇāṃ saṅgataḥ darśanāt satām // Hit_1.94 //
children.translated_text: fools by fear and greed, and the good by mere sight [of one another]. // Hit 1.94 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Furthermore —

children.text: nārikela-samākārā dṛśyante hi suhṛjjanāḥ |
children.translated_text: Some good people are seen to be like coconuts —

children.text: anye badarikākārā bahir eva manoharāḥ // Hit_1.95 //
children.translated_text: [while] others are like jujube fruits, pleasing only on the outside. // Hit 1.95 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: sneha-cchede'pi sādhūnāṃ guṇā nāyānti vikriyām |
children.translated_text: Even when affection is broken, the virtues of the good do not undergo change;

children.text: bhaṅge'pi hi mṛṇālānām anubadhnanti tantavaḥ // Hit_1.96 //
children.translated_text: for even when lotus stalks are snapped, the fibers still cling [together]. // Hit 1.96 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: śucitvam tyāgitā śauryaṃ sāmānyaṃ sukha-duḥkhayoḥ |
children.translated_text: Purity, generosity, valor, equanimity in happiness and sorrow,

children.text: dākṣiṇyaṃ cānuraktiś ca satyatā ca suhṛd-guṇāḥ // Hit_1.97 //
children.translated_text: courtesy, devotion, and truthfulness — these are the qualities of a [true] friend. // Hit 1.97 //

body.text: etair guṇair upeto bhavad=anyo mayā kaḥ suhṛt prāptavyaḥ ? ity ādi tad-vacanam ākarṇya hiraṇyako bahiḥ niḥsṛtyāha-āpyāyito 'haṃ bhavatām etena vacanāmṛtena | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: 'Endowed with these qualities, what other friend besides you could I find?' and so forth. Hearing those words, <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> came out [of his hole] and said: 'I am nourished by this nectar of your words. And so it is said —'

children.text: gharmārtaṃ na tathā suśītala-jalaiḥ snānaṃ na muktāvalī
children.translated_text: Not a bath with cool water for one scorched by heat, not a string of pearls,

children.text: na śrīkhaṇḍa-vilepanam sukhayati pratyaṅgam apy arpitam |
children.translated_text: not an anointing with sandalwood applied to every limb —

children.text: prītyai sajjana-bhāṣitaṃ prabhavati prāyo yathā cetasaḥ
children.translated_text: [none of these] delight the mind as the speech of a good person generally does,

children.text: sad-yuktyā ca pariṣkṛtaṃ sukṛtinām ākṛṣṭi-mantropamam // Hit_1.98 //
children.translated_text: refined by sound reasoning — [it is] like a charm that attracts the meritorious. // Hit 1.98 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: rahasya-bhedo yācñā ca naiṣṭhuryaṃ cala-cittayā |
children.translated_text: Betrayal of secrets, begging, harshness, fickleness,

children.text: krodho niḥsatyatā dyūtam etan mitrasya dūṣaṇam // Hit_1.99 //
children.translated_text: anger, dishonesty, and gambling — these are the defects of a friend. // Hit 1.99 //

body.text: anena vacana-krameṇa tat ekam api dūṣaṇaṃ tvayi na lakṣyate | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: 'By this sequence of [your] words, not even one of these defects is observed in you. For —'

children.text: paṭutvaṃ satyavāditvaṃ kathā-yogena buddhyate |
children.translated_text: Eloquence and truthfulness are discerned through the course of conversation;

children.text: astabdhatvam acāpalyaṃ pratyakṣenāvagamyate // Hit_1.100 //
children.translated_text: absence of arrogance and absence of fickleness are perceived directly. // Hit 1.100 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: anyathaiva hi sauhārdaṃ bhavet svacchāntarātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: The affection of one whose inner self is transparent manifests in one way;

children.text: pravartate'nyathā vāṇī śāṭhyopahata-cetasaḥ // Hit_1.101 //
children.translated_text: the speech of one whose mind is corrupted by duplicity proceeds in another way. // Hit 1.101 //

children.text: manasy anyad vacasy anyat karmaṇy anyad durātmanām |
children.translated_text: The wicked have one thing in mind, another in speech, and another in action;

children.text: manasy ekaṃ vacasy ekaṃ karmaṇy ekaṃ mahātmanām // Hit_1.102 //
children.translated_text: the great-souled have the same thing in mind, in speech, and in action. // Hit 1.102 //

body.text: tad bhavatu bhavataḥ abhimatam eva ity uktvā hiraṇyako maitryaṃ vidhāya bhojana-viśeṣair vāyasaṃ santoṣya vivaraṃ praviṣṭaḥ | vāyaso 'pi sva-sthānaṃ gataḥ tataḥ-prabhṛti tayoḥ anyo 'nyāhāra-pradānena kuśala-praśnaiḥ viśrambhālāpaiś ca kiyat-kālo 'tivartane | ekadā laghu-patanako hiraṇyakam āha-sakhe ! vāyasasya kaṣṭataralabhyāhāram idaṃ sthānam | tad etat parityajya sthānāntaraṃ gantum icchāmi |
body.translated_text: 'Then let it be as you wish,' said <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>, and having established friendship, he satisfied the crow with special foods and entered his burrow. The crow too went to his own place. From then on, some time passed with the two exchanging food, asking after each other's welfare, and engaging in intimate conversation. One day <s>Laghupatanaka</s> said to <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>: 'Friend! This is a place where food is obtained with great difficulty for a crow. So I wish to leave this place and go to another.'

children.text: hiraṇyako brūte-
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said:

children.text: sthāna-bhraṣṭā na śobhante dantāḥ keśā nakhā narāḥ |
children.translated_text: Teeth, hair, nails, and men — displaced from their position, they do not shine;

children.text: iti vijñāya matimān sva-sthānaṃ na parityajet // Hit_1.103 //
children.translated_text: knowing this, a wise person should not abandon his own place. // Hit_1.103 //

body.text: kāko brūte-mitra ! kāpuruṣasya vacanam etat | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: The crow said: 'Friend! That is the speech of a coward. For —'

children.text: sthānam utsṛjya gacchanti siṃhāḥ sat-puruṣā gajāḥ |
children.translated_text: Lions, noble men, and elephants leave their place and go;

children.text: tatraiva nidhanaṃ yānti kākāḥ kāpuruṣā mṛgāḥ // Hit_1.104 //
children.translated_text: but crows, cowards, and deer die in the very same spot. // Hit_1.104 //

body.text: anyac ca-

children.text: ko vīrasya manasvinaḥ sva-viṣayaḥ ko vā videśaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: For the brave and spirited person, what is his own territory and what is called a foreign land?

children.text: yaṃ deśaṃ śrayate tam eva kurute bāhu-pratāpārjitam |
children.translated_text: Whatever land he resorts to, he makes it his own, won by the might of his arms.

children.text: yad daṃṣṭrānakha-lāṅgula-praharaṇaḥ siṃho vanaṃ gāhate
children.translated_text: When the lion, whose weapons are his fangs, claws, and tail, plunges into the forest,

children.text: tasminn eva hata-dvipendra-rudhirais tṛṣṇāṃ chinnatty ātmanaḥ // Hit_1.105 //
children.translated_text: in that very forest he quenches his thirst with the blood of slain lordly elephants. // Hit_1.105 //

body.translated_text: And furthermore —

body.text: hiraṇyako brūte-mitra kva gantavyam ? tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said: 'Friend, where shall we go? As it has been said —'

children.text: calaty ekena pādena tiṣṭhaty ekena buddhimān |
children.translated_text: The wise person moves with one foot and stands with the other;

children.text: nāsamīkṣya paraṃ sthānaṃ pūrvam āyatanaṃ tyajet // Hit_1.106 //
children.translated_text: one should not abandon one's former abode without examining the next place. // Hit_1.106 //

body.text: vāyaso brūte-mitra ! asti sunirūpitaṃ sthānam |
body.translated_text: The crow said: 'Friend! There is a well-examined place.'

body.text: hiraṇyako 'vadat-kiṃ tat ?
body.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> asked: 'What is it?'

body.text: vāyasaḥ kathayati-asti daṇḍakāraṇye karpūragaurābhidhānaṃ saraḥ | tatra cira-kālopārjitaḥ priya-suhṛn me mantharābhidhānaḥ kūrmaḥ sahaja-dhārmikaḥ prativasati | paśya mitra !
body.translated_text: The crow said: 'There is a lake named <s>Karpūragaurā</s> in the <s>Daṇḍakāraṇya</s> forest. There dwells my dear friend acquired over a long time, a tortoise named <s>Manthara</s>, righteous by nature. See, friend!

children.text: paropadeśe pāṇḍityaṃ sarveṣāṃ sukaraṃ nṛṇām |
children.translated_text: To give advice to others — this cleverness is easy for all men;

children.text: dharme svīyam anuṣṭhānaṃ kasyacit tu mahātmanaḥ // Hit_1.107 //
children.translated_text: but to practice <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) oneself belongs only to some great soul. // Hit_1.107 //'

body.text: sa ca bhojana-viśeṣair māṃ saṃvardhayiṣyati | hiraṇyako 'py āha-tat kim atrāvasthāya mayā kartavyam ? yataḥ-
body.translated_text: 'He will nourish me with special foods.' <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> also said: 'Then what should I do staying here? For —'

children.text: yasmin deśe na sammāno na vṛttir na ca bāndhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: A land where there is no honor, no livelihood, no kinsmen,

children.text: na ca vidyāgamaḥ kaścit taṃ deśaṃ parivarjayet // Hit_1.108 //
children.translated_text: and no acquisition of knowledge — that land one should avoid. // Hit_1.108 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca---
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: dhanikaḥ śrotriyo rājā nadī vaidyas tu pañcamaḥ |
children.translated_text: A wealthy person, a learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a king, a river, and fifth a physician —

children.text: pañca yatra na vidyante tatra vāsaṃ na kārayet // Hit_1.109 //
children.translated_text: where these five are not found, one should not make one's dwelling. // Hit_1.109 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca---
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: loka-yātrā bhayaṃ lajjā dākṣiṇyaṃ tyāga-śīlatā |
children.translated_text: Social intercourse, security, modesty, courtesy, and a disposition for generosity —

children.text: pañca yatra na vidyante na kuryāt tatra saṃsthitim // Hit_1.110 //
children.translated_text: where these five are not found, one should not settle there. // Hit_1.110 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And furthermore —

children.text: tatra mitra ! na vastavyaṃ yatra nāsti catuṣṭayam |
children.translated_text: One should not dwell there, friend, where these four are absent:

children.text: ṛṇa-dātā ca vaidyaś ca śrotriyaḥ sajalā nadī // Hit_1.111 //
children.translated_text: a money-lender, a physician, a learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, and a river with water. // Hit_1.111 //

body.text: ato mām api tatra naya |
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, take me there too.'

body.text: vāyaso 'vadat-evam astu |
body.translated_text: The crow said: 'So be it.'

body.text: atha vāyasas tena mitreṇa saha vicitrālāpa-sukhena tasya sarasaḥ samīpaṃ yayau | tato mantharo dūrād eva laghu-patanakam avalokya utthāya yathocitam ātithyaṃ vidhāya mūṣikasyāpy atithi-satkāraṃ cakāra | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Then the crow, together with that friend, went near that lake, enjoying pleasant conversation along the way. <s>Manthara</s>, seeing <s>Laghupatanaka</s> from afar, rose and performed appropriate hospitality, and extended the courtesy of a guest to the mouse as well. For —

children.text: bālo vā yadi vā vṛddho yuvā vā gṛham āgataḥ |
children.translated_text: Whether a child, an old man, or a youth has come to one's house,

children.text: tasya pūjā vidhātavyā sarvatrābhyāgato guruḥ // Hit_1.112 //
children.translated_text: he should be honored; a guest who has arrived is always venerable. // Hit_1.112 //

children.text: tathā-
children.translated_text: Likewise —

children.text: gurur agnir dvijātīnāṃ varṇānāṃ brāhmaṇo guruḥ |
children.translated_text: Fire is the guru of the twice-born; the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is the guru of the <s>varṇas</s> (social classes);

children.text: patir eko guruḥ strīṇāṃ sarvatrābhyāgato guruḥ // Hit_1.113 //
children.translated_text: the husband alone is the guru of women; and everywhere, a guest who has arrived is the guru. // Hit_1.113 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: uttamasyāpi varṇasya nīco 'pi gṛham āgataḥ |
children.translated_text: Even if one of the lowest [class] has come to the house of one of the highest <s>varṇa</s>,

children.text: pūjanīyo yathā-yogyaṃ sarva-deva-mayo 'tithiḥ // Hit_1.114 //
children.translated_text: a guest should be honored as befitting, for the guest is the embodiment of all gods. // Hit_1.114 //

body.text: vāyaso 'vadat-sakhe ! manthara ! sa-viśeṣa-pūjām asami vidhehi, yato 'yaṃ puṇya-karmaṇāṃ dhurīṇaḥ kāruṇya-ratnākaro hiraṇyaka-nāmā mūṣika-rājaḥ | etasya guṇa-stutiṃ jihvā-sahasra-dvayenāpi yadi sarpa-rājaḥ kadācit kartuṃ samarthaḥ syāt ity uktvā citragrīvopākhyānaṃ varṇitavān | tato mantharaḥ sādaraṃ hiraṇyakaṃ sampūjyāha-bhadra ! ātmano nirjana-vanāgamana-kāraṇam ākhyātum arhasi ?
body.translated_text: The crow said: 'Friend <s>Manthara</s>! Give this one special honors, for he is the foremost among those of meritorious deeds, an ocean of compassion, the mouse-king named <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>. Even if the serpent-king, with his two thousand tongues, could ever suffice to sing his virtues —' and so saying, he narrated the story of <s>Citragrīva</s>. Then <s>Manthara</s>, having honored <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> with respect, said: 'Good sir! Please tell me the reason for your coming to this desolate forest.'

body.text:
hiraṇyako 'vadat-kathayāmi, śrūyatām |
kathā 4
body.translated_text:
<s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said: 'I shall tell you — listen.
Story 4'

body.text: asti campakābhidhānāyāṃ nagaryāṃ parivrājakāvasathaḥ | tatra cūḍākarṇo nāma parivrājakaḥ prativasati | sa ca bhojanāvaśiṣṭa-bhikṣānna-sahitaṃ bhikṣāpātraṃ nāgadantake'vasthāpya svapiti | ahaṃ ca tad annam utplutya utplutya pratyahaṃ bhakṣayāmi | anantaraṃ tasya priya-suhṛd vīṇākarṇo nāma parivrājakaḥ samāyātaḥ, tena saha nānā-kathā-prasaṅgāvasthito mama trāsārthaṃ jarjara-vaṃśa-khaṇḍena cūḍākarṇo bhūmim atāḍayat | taṃ tathāvidhaṃ dṛṣṭvā vīṇākarṇa uvāca-sakhe ! kim iti mama kathā-virakto 'nyāsakto bhavān ? yataḥ-
body.translated_text: In a city called <s>Campakā</s> there is a lodging house for mendicants. There lived a mendicant named <s>Cūḍākarṇa</s>. He would place his alms-bowl, containing food left over from his meal, on a peg and sleep. And I, jumping up again and again, would eat that food every day. Then his dear friend, a mendicant named <s>Vīṇākarṇa</s>, arrived. While engaged in various conversations with him, <s>Cūḍākarṇa</s> struck the ground with a worn bamboo stick to frighten me. Seeing him thus, <s>Vīṇākarṇa</s> said: 'Friend! Why are you distracted from my story and attending to something else? For —'

children.text: mukhaṃ prasannaṃ vimalā ca dṛṣṭiḥ
children.translated_text: A cheerful face, a clear gaze,

children.text: kathānurāgo madhurā ca vāṇī |
children.translated_text: delight in conversation, and sweet speech,

children.text: sneho 'dhikaḥ sambhrama-darśanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: great affection and a display of respect —

children.text: sadānuraktasya janasya lakṣma // Hit_1.115 //
children.translated_text: these are the marks of a person who is always attached [to one]. // Hit_1.115 //

children.text: adṛṣṭi-dānaṃ kṛta-pūrva-nāśanam
children.translated_text: Not giving one's gaze, destroying what was previously done,

children.text: ānanaṃ duścaritānukīrtanam |
children.translated_text: a frowning face, recounting [others'] misdeeds,

children.text: kathā-prasaṅgena ca nāma-vismṛtir
children.translated_text: and forgetting the name during conversation —

children.text: virakta-bhāvasya janasya lakṣaṇam // Hit_1.116 //
children.translated_text: these are the marks of a person who is disaffected. // Hit_1.116 //

body.text: cūḍākarṇenoktam-bhadra ! nāhaṃ viraktaḥ, kintu paśya ayaṃ mūṣiko mamāpakārī sadā pātrasthaṃ bhikṣānnam utplutya bhakṣayati | vīṇākarṇo nāgadantam avalokyāha-katham ayaṃ mūṣikaḥ svalpa-balo 'py etāvad dūram utpatati ? tad atra kenāpi kāraṇena bhavitavyam |
body.translated_text: <s>Cūḍākarṇa</s> said: 'Good sir! I am not disaffected. But look — this mouse, my tormentor, always jumps up and eats the alms-food from my bowl.' <s>Vīṇākarṇa</s>, looking at the peg, said: 'How does this mouse, though of little strength, jump so far? There must be some reason for this.'

body.text: kṣaṇaṃ vicintya parivrājakenoktam-kāraṇaṃ cātra dhana-bāhulyam eva pratibhāti | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: After pondering for a moment, the mendicant said: 'The reason here appears to be an abundance of wealth. For —'

children.text: dhanavān balavān loke sarvaḥ sarvatra sarvadā |
children.translated_text: In the world, the wealthy person is strong — everywhere, always, in all things;

children.text: prabhutvaṃ dhana-mūlaṃ hi rājñām apy upajāyate // Hit_1.117 //
children.translated_text: sovereignty itself arises from wealth as its root, even for kings. // Hit_1.117 //

body.text: tataḥ khanitram ādāya tena parivrājakena vivaraṃ khanitvā cira-sañcitaṃ mama dhanaṃ gṛhītam | tataḥ prabhṛti pratyahaṃ nija-śakti-hīnaḥ sattvotsāha-rahitaḥ svāhāram apy utpādayitum akṣamaḥ sann āsaṃ mandaṃ mandam upasarpan cūḍākarṇenāvalokitaḥ | tatas tenoktam-
body.translated_text: Then, taking a spade, that mendicant dug up the burrow and took the wealth I had accumulated over a long time. From then on, bereft of my own power day after day, devoid of spirit and energy, unable even to procure my own food, I crept along slowly and was noticed by <s>Cūḍākarṇa</s>. Then he said:

children.text: dhanena balavān loko dhanād bhavati paṇḍitaḥ |
children.translated_text: The world is strong through wealth; through wealth one becomes learned;

children.text: paśyainaṃ mūṣikaṃ pāpaṃ svajāti-samatāṃ gatam // Hit_1.118 //
children.translated_text: behold this wicked mouse, reduced to the level of his own kind! // Hit_1.118 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: arthena tu vihīnasya puruṣasyālpa-medhasaḥ |
children.translated_text: For a person deprived of wealth, of meager intellect,

children.text: kriyā sarvā vinaśyanti grīṣme kusarito yathā // Hit_1.119 //
children.translated_text: all undertakings perish, as small streams [dry up] in summer. // Hit_1.119 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: yasyārthās tasya mitrāṇi yasyārthās tasya bāndhavāḥ |
children.translated_text: He who has wealth has friends; he who has wealth has kinsmen;

children.text: yasyārthāḥ sa pumān loke yasyārthāḥ sa hi paṇḍitaḥ // Hit_1.120 //
children.translated_text: he who has wealth is a [real] person in the world; he who has wealth is truly learned. // Hit_1.120 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: aputrasya gṛhaṃ śūnyaṃ san-mitra-rahitasya ca |
children.translated_text: The house of one without sons is empty, as is [the life] of one without a good friend;

children.text: mūrkhasya ca diśaḥ śūnyāḥ sarva-śūnyā daridratā // Hit_1.121 //
children.translated_text: the directions are empty for a fool, but everything is empty for the destitute. // Hit_1.121 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: dāridryān maraṇād vāpi dāridryam avaraṃ smṛtam |
children.translated_text: Between poverty and death, poverty is considered worse;

children.text: alpa-kleśena maraṇaṃ dāridryam atiduḥsaham // Hit_1.122 //
children.translated_text: death involves little suffering, but poverty is utterly unbearable. // Hit_1.122 //

body.text: anyac ca-

children.text: tānīndriyāṇy avikalāni tad eva nāma
children.translated_text: The same unimpaired senses, the same name,

children.text: sā buddhir apratihatā vacanaṃ tad eva |
children.translated_text: the same unobstructed intellect, the same speech —

children.text: arthoṣmaṇā virahitaḥ puruṣaḥ sa eva
children.translated_text: yet the same person, deprived of the warmth of wealth,

children.text: anyaḥ kṣaṇena bhavatīti vicitram etat // Hit_1.123 //
children.translated_text: becomes another in an instant — how wondrous this is! // Hit_1.123 //

body.translated_text: And furthermore —

body.text: etat sarvam ākarṇya mayālocitaṃ-mamānnāvasthānam ayuktam idānīm | tathā coktam-

children.text: atyanta-vimukhe daive vyarthe yatne ca pauruṣe |
children.translated_text: When fate is utterly hostile and effort and human endeavor are futile,

children.text: manasvino daridrasya vanād anyat kutaḥ sukham // Hit_1.124 //
children.translated_text: for the self-respecting but poor person, what happiness is there other than the forest? // Hit_1.124 //

body.translated_text: Hearing all this, I reflected: my remaining here for food is no longer fitting. As has been said —

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And furthermore —

children.text: manasvī miryate kāmaṃ kārpaṇyaṃ na tu gacchati |
children.translated_text: The self-respecting person may well die, but does not descend to wretchedness;

children.text: api nirvāṇam āyāti nānalo yāti śītatām // Hit_1.125 //
children.translated_text: even fire may be extinguished, but it never becomes cold. // Hit_1.125 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: kusuma-stavakasyeva dve vṛttī tu manasvinaḥ |
children.translated_text: Like a cluster of flowers, two are the modes of life for the self-respecting person:

children.text: sarveṣāṃ mūrdhni vā tiṣṭhed viśīryeta vane'thavā // Hit_1.126 //
children.translated_text: either he stands upon the head of all, or withers in the forest. // Hit_1.126 //

body.text: yac cānyasmai etad vṛttānta-kathanaṃ tad apy anucitam | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: And the telling of this story to another is also improper. For —

children.text: artha-nāśaṃ manas-tāpaṃ gṛhe duścaritāni ca |
children.translated_text: Loss of wealth, mental anguish, misconduct in the household,

children.text: vañcanaṃ cāpamānaṃ ca matimān na prakāśayet // Hit_1.127 //
children.translated_text: being deceived, and being dishonored — an intelligent person does not reveal these. // Hit_1.127 //

body.text: yac cātraiva yācñayā jīvanaṃ tad apy atīva-garhitam | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: And living here by begging is also extremely contemptible. For —

children.text: varaṃ vibhava-hīnena prāṇaiḥ santarpito 'nalaḥ |
children.translated_text: Better that one deprived of fortune should satisfy the fire with his life-breaths,

children.text: nopacāra-paribhraṣṭaḥ kṛpaṇaḥ prārthyate janaḥ // Hit_1.128 //
children.translated_text: than that the wretched one, fallen from propriety, should beseech people. // Hit_1.128 //

body.text: anyac ca-

children.text: dāridryād dhriyam eti hrī-parigataḥ sattvāt paribhraśyate
children.translated_text: From poverty, one loses modesty; possessed by loss of modesty, one falls from virtue;

children.text: niḥsattvaṃ paribhūyate paribhavān nirvedam āpadyate |
children.translated_text: devoid of virtue, one is despised; from contempt, one becomes despondent;

children.text: nirviṇṇaḥ śucam eti śoka-phihito buddhyā parityajyate
children.translated_text: despondent, one is overcome by grief; afflicted by grief, one's intellect is abandoned;

children.text: nirbuddhiḥ kṣayam ety aho nidhanatā sarvāpadām āspadam // Hit_1.129 //
children.translated_text: without intellect, one goes to ruin — alas, destitution is the abode of all calamities! // Hit_1.129 //

body.translated_text: And furthermore —

body.text: kiṃ ca-

children.text: varaṃ maunaṃ kāryaṃ na ca vacanam uktaṃ yad anṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: Better silence than speaking what is false;

children.text: varaṃ klaibyaṃ puṃsāṃ na ca para-kalatrābhigamanam |
children.translated_text: better impotence for men than approaching another's wife;

children.text: varaṃ prāṇa-tyāgo na ca piśuna-vākyeṣv abhirucir
children.translated_text: better to abandon life than to delight in slanderous words;

children.text: varaṃ bhikṣāśitvaṃ na ca para-dhanāsvādana-sukham // Hit_1.130 //
children.translated_text: better to live on alms than the pleasure of tasting another's wealth. // Hit_1.130 //

body.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: varaṃ śūnyā śālā na ca khalu varo duṣṭa-vṛṣabho
children.translated_text: Better an empty barn than a vicious bull;

children.text: varaṃ veśyā patnī na punar avinītā kula-vadhūḥ |
children.translated_text: better a courtesan as wife than an ill-bred woman of good family;

children.text: varaṃ vāso 'raṇye na punar avivekādhipa-pure
children.translated_text: better to dwell in the forest than in the city of an undiscerning lord;

children.text: varaṃ prāṇa-tyāgo na punar adhamānām upagamaḥ // Hit_1.131 //
children.translated_text: better to abandon life than to associate with the base. // Hit_1.131 //

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: seveva mānam akhilaṃ jyotsneva tamo jareva lāvaṇyam |
children.translated_text: As service [destroys] all honor, as moonlight [destroys] darkness, as old age [destroys] beauty,

children.text: hari-hara-katheva duritaṃ guṇa-śatam apy arthitā harati // Hit_1.132 //
children.translated_text: as the tale of <s>Hari</s> and <s>Hara</s> [destroys] sin — even a hundred virtues are destroyed by begging. // Hit_1.132 //

body.text: tat kim ahaṃ para-piṇḍena ātmānaṃ poṣayāmi ? kaṣṭaṃ bhoḥ ! tad api dvitīyaṃ mṛtyu-dvāram | anyac ca-
body.translated_text: 'So shall I sustain myself by another's morsel? Alas! That too is a second door to death. And furthermore —'

children.text: rogī cira-pravāsī parānna-bhojī parāvasatha-śāyī |
children.translated_text: One who is sick, one on a long journey, one who eats another's food, one who sleeps in another's dwelling —

children.text: yaj jīvati tan maraṇaṃ yan maraṇaṃ so 'sya viśrāmaḥ // Hit_1.133 //
children.translated_text: his living is death, and his death is his rest. // Hit_1.133 //

body.text: ity ālocyāpi lobhāt punar api tadīyam annaṃ grahītuṃ graham akaravam | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: 'Having reflected thus, yet out of greed I again attempted to take his food. As has been said —'

children.text: lobhena buddhiś calati lobho janayate tṛṣām |
children.translated_text: Greed causes the mind to waver; greed gives rise to craving;

children.text: tṛṣārto duḥkham āpnoti paratreha ca mānavaḥ // Hit_1.134 //
children.translated_text: a person afflicted by craving suffers misery, in this world and the next. // Hit_1.134 //

body.text: tato 'haṃ mandaṃ mandam upasarpaṃs tena vīṇākarṇena jarjara-vaṃśa-khaṇḍena tāḍitaś cācintayam-lubdho hy asantuṣṭo niyatam ātma-drohī bhavati | tathā ca-
body.translated_text: 'Then, as I crept along slowly, I was struck by that <s>Vīṇākarṇa</s> with the worn bamboo stick, and I thought: the greedy and discontented person inevitably becomes a self-betrayer. And so —'

children.text: dhana-lubdho hy asantuṣṭo 'niyatātmājitendriyaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who is greedy for wealth, discontented, uncontrolled, and with unmastered senses —

children.text: sarvā evāpadas tasya yasya tuṣṭaṃ na mānasam // Hit_1.135 //
children.translated_text: all misfortunes belong to him whose mind is not at peace. // Hit_1.135 //

children.text: sarvāḥ sampattasyas tasya santuṣṭaṃ yasya mānasam |
children.translated_text: All fortunes belong to him whose mind is at peace;

children.text: upānad-gūḍha-pādasya nanu carmāvṛteva bhūḥ // Hit_1.136 //
children.translated_text: for one whose feet are covered by shoes, the earth is as if covered with leather. // Hit_1.136 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: santoṣāmṛta-tṛptānāṃ yat sukhaṃ śānta-cetasām |
children.translated_text: The happiness of those who are satisfied by the nectar of contentment, whose minds are tranquil —

children.text: kutas tad-dhana-lubdhānām itaś cetaś ca dhāvatām // Hit_1.137 //
children.translated_text: how can that [happiness] belong to those greedy for wealth, running hither and thither? // Hit_1.137 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: tenādhītaṃ śrutaṃ tena tena sarvam anuṣṭhitam |
children.translated_text: He has truly studied, he has truly heard, he has truly accomplished everything,

children.text: yenāśāḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā nairāśyam avalambitam // Hit_1.138 //
children.translated_text: who, having cast hopes behind, has embraced desirelessness. // Hit_1.138 //

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: aseviteśvara-dvāram adṛṣṭa-viraha-vyatham |
children.translated_text: One who has not frequented the doors of lords, who has not seen the pain of separation,

children.text: anukta-klība-vacanaṃ dhanyaṃ kasyāpi jīvanam // Hit_1.139 //
children.translated_text: who has not spoken craven words — blessed is the life of such a one! // Hit_1.139 //

children.text: na yojana-śataṃ dūraṃ vāhyamānasya tṛṣṇayā |
children.translated_text: Even a hundred <s>yojanas</s> is not far for one who is driven by desire;

children.text: santuṣṭasya kara-prāpte'py arthe bhavati nādaraḥ // Hit_1.140 //
children.translated_text: but the contented one has no regard even for wealth within reach. // Hit 1.140 //

body.text: tad atra avasthocita-kārya-paricchedaḥ śreyān |
body.translated_text: Therefore, here, the discernment of action appropriate to one's circumstances is best.

children.text: ko dharmo bhūta-dayā kiṃ saukhyaṃ nityam aroginā jagati |
children.translated_text: What is <s>dharma</s>? Compassion for beings. What is happiness? Being perpetually healthy in the world.

children.text: kaḥ snehaḥ sad-bhāvaḥ kiṃ pāṇḍityaṃ paricchedaḥ // Hit_1.141 //
children.translated_text: What is affection? Goodwill. What is learning? Discernment. // Hit 1.141 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And so —

children.text: paricchedo hi pāṇḍityaṃ yadāpannā vipattayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Discernment is indeed wisdom when calamities have befallen;

children.text: apariccheda-kartṝṇāṃ vipadaḥ syuḥ pade pade // Hit_1.142 //
children.translated_text: for those who lack discernment, misfortunes arise at every step. // Hit 1.142 //

children.text: tathā hi-
children.translated_text: For instance —

children.text: tyajed ekaṃ kulasyārthe grāmasyārthe kulaṃ tyajet |
children.translated_text: One should sacrifice one person for the sake of the family; sacrifice the family for the sake of the village;

children.text: grāmaṃ janapadasyārthe ātmārthe pṛthivīṃ tyajet // Hit_1.143 //
children.translated_text: sacrifice the village for the sake of the country; and sacrifice the earth for the sake of the self. // Hit 1.143 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And another —

children.text: pānīyaṃ vā nirāyāsaṃ svādvannaṃ vā bhayottaram |
children.translated_text: Water obtained without effort, or delicious food accompanied by fear —

children.text: vicāryaṃ khalu paśyāmi tat sukhaṃ yatra nirvṛtiḥ // Hit_1.144 //
children.translated_text: upon reflection, I see that happiness is where there is contentment. // Hit 1.144 //

body.text: ity ālocyāhaṃ nirjana-vanam āgataḥ | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Having reflected thus, I have come to this uninhabited forest. For —

children.text: varaṃ vanaṃ vyāghra-gajendra-sevitaṃ
children.translated_text: Better the forest frequented by tigers and great elephants,

children.text: drumālayaḥ patra-phalāmbu-bhakṣitam |
children.translated_text: a tree for one's dwelling, fruits, leaves, and water for food,

children.text: tṛṇāni śayyā vasanaṃ ca valkalaṃ
children.translated_text: grass for a bed and bark for clothing,

children.text: na bandhu-madhye dhana-hīna-jīvanam // Hit_1.145 //
children.translated_text: than a life destitute of wealth among kinsmen. // Hit 1.145 //

children.text: ataḥ-
children.translated_text: Therefore —

children.text: saṃsāra-viṣaya-vṛkṣasya dve eva rasavat phale |
children.translated_text: Of the tree of worldly existence, there are only two savory fruits:

children.text: kāvyāmṛta-rasāsvādaḥ saṅgamaḥ sajjanaiḥ saha // Hit_1.146 //
children.translated_text: the tasting of the nectar of poetry, and the company of good people. // Hit 1.146 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And another —

children.text: sat-saṅgaḥ keśave bhaktir gaṅgāmbhasi nimajjanam |
children.translated_text: The company of the good, devotion to <s>Keśava</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), and bathing in the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> —

children.text: asāre khalu saṃsāre trīṇi sārāṇi bhāvayet // Hit_1.147 //
children.translated_text: in this truly worthless <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), one should cultivate these three essentials. // Hit 1.147 //

body.text: manthara uvāca-

children.text: arthāḥ pāda-rajopamā giri-nadī-vegopamaṃ yauvanam
children.translated_text: Wealth is like the dust on one's feet; youth is like the rush of a mountain torrent;

children.text: āyuṣyaṃ jala-bindu-lola-capalaṃ phenopamaṃ jīvanam |
children.translated_text: life-span is as fickle as a drop of water; life is like foam.

children.text: dharmaṃ yo na karoti niścala-matiḥ svargārgalodghāṭanaṃ
children.translated_text: He who, with a steadfast mind, does not perform <s>dharma</s> — which is the bolt that opens the gate of heaven —

children.text: paścāt-tāpa-hato jarā-pariṇataḥ śokāgninā dahyate // Hit_1.148 //
children.translated_text: stricken by remorse afterwards, worn out by old age, is burned by the fire of grief. // Hit 1.148 //

body.translated_text: <s>Manthara</s> (the tortoise) said:

body.text: yuṣmābhir atisañcayaḥ kṛtaḥ | tasyāyaṃ doṣaḥ | śṛṇu-

children.text: upārjitānāṃ vittānāṃ tyāga eva hi rakṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: The protection of accumulated wealth lies indeed in giving it away,

children.text: taḍāgodara-saṃsthānāṃ parīvāhaivāmbhasām // Hit_1.149 //
children.translated_text: just as the (protection) of water stored in a reservoir is through an outlet channel. // Hit 1.149 //

body.translated_text: You have accumulated excessively. This is its fault. Listen —

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And furthermore —

children.text: yad adho 'dhaḥ kṣitau vittaṃ nicakhāna mitampacaḥ |
children.translated_text: Whatever wealth the miser buried deeper and deeper in the ground,

children.text: tad-adho nilayaṃ gantuṃ cakre panthānam agrataḥ // Hit_1.150 //
children.translated_text: he made a path in advance to go to a dwelling below (i.e., to hell). // Hit 1.150 //

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: For —

children.text: nija-saukhyaṃ nirundhāno yo dhanārjanam icchati |
children.translated_text: He who suppresses his own comfort and desires to accumulate wealth

children.text: parārtha-bhāra-vāhīva sa kleśasyaiva bhājanam // Hit_1.151 //
children.translated_text: is merely a vessel of suffering, like a beast of burden carrying another's load. // Hit 1.151 //

children.text: tathā coktaṃ-
children.translated_text: And as it is said —

children.text: dānopabhoga-hīnena dhanena dhanino yadi |
children.translated_text: If the wealthy are (called) wealthy because of wealth devoid of charity and enjoyment,

children.text: bhavāmaḥ kiṃ na tenaiva dhanena dhanino vayam // Hit_1.152 //
children.translated_text: then are we not wealthy too with that very same (unused) wealth? // Hit 1.152 //

body.text: yataḥ-

children.text: dhanena kiṃ yo na dadāti nāśnute
children.translated_text: What use is wealth to one who neither gives nor enjoys?

children.text: balena kiṃ yaś ca ripūn na yādhatte |
children.translated_text: What use is strength to one who does not subdue enemies?

children.text: śrutena kiṃ yo na ca dharmam ācaret
children.translated_text: What use is learning to one who does not practice <s>dharma</s>?

children.text: kim ātmanā yo na jitendriyo bhavet // Hit_1.153 //
children.translated_text: What use is the self to one who has not conquered the senses? // Hit 1.153 //

body.translated_text: For —

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And another —

children.text: asambhogena sāmānyaṃ kṛpaṇasya dhanaṃ paraiḥ |
children.translated_text: The wealth of a miser, unused, is common with others (who also don't use it);

children.text: asyedam iti sambandho hānau duḥkhena gamyate // Hit_1.154 //
children.translated_text: the connection 'this is his' is understood through sorrow only at the time of its loss. // Hit 1.154 //

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: na devāya na viprāya na bandhubhyo na cātmane |
children.translated_text: The wealth of a miser goes neither to the gods, nor to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, nor to kinsmen, nor to oneself;

children.text: kṛpaṇasya dhanaṃ yāti vahni-taskara-pārthivaiḥ // Hit_1.155 //
children.translated_text: it goes to fire, thieves, and kings. // Hit 1.155 //

body.text: tathā coktam-

children.text: dānaṃ priya-vāk-sahitaṃ
children.translated_text: Giving accompanied by kind words,

children.text: jñānam agarvaṃ kṣamānvitaṃ sauryam |
children.translated_text: knowledge without pride, valor endowed with patience,

children.text: tyāgaṃ sahitaṃ ca vittaṃ
children.translated_text: and wealth accompanied by renunciation —

children.text: durlabham etac catur bhadram // Hit_1.156 //
children.translated_text: this fourfold excellence is rare. // Hit 1.156 //

body.translated_text: And as it is said —

children.text: uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And it is said —

children.text: kartavyaḥ sañcayo nityaṃ na tu kāryo 'tisañcayaḥ |
children.translated_text: One should always accumulate, but one should not hoard excessively;

children.text: atisañcaya-śīlo 'yaṃ dhanuṣā jambuko hataḥ // Hit_1.157 //
children.translated_text: this jackal, given to excessive hoarding, was killed by a bow. // Hit 1.157 //

body.text: tāv āhatuḥ-katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The two asked: 'How is that?'

body.text: mantharaḥ kathayati-
body.translated_text: <s>Manthara</s> tells the story:

body.text: kathā 5
body.translated_text: Story 5:

body.text: āsīt kalyāṇa-kaṭaka-vāstavyo bhairavo nāma vyādhaḥ | sa caikadā māṃsa-lubdho dhanur ādāya mṛgam anviṣyan vindhyāṭavī-madhyaṃ gataḥ | tatra tena mṛga eko vyāpāditaḥ | tato mṛgam ādāya gacchatā tena ghorākṛtiḥ śūkaro dṛṣṭaḥ | tatas tena mṛgaṃ bhūmau nidhāya śūkaraḥ śareṇa hataḥ | śūkareṇāpy āgatya pralaya-ghana-ghora-garjanaṃ kurvāṇena sa vyādho muṣka-deśe hataḥ chinna-druma iva papāta | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: There was a hunter named <s>Bhairava</s>, a resident of <s>Kalyāṇakaṭaka</s>. Once, greedy for meat, taking his bow and seeking deer, he went into the midst of the <s>Vindhya</s> forest. There he killed a deer. Then, while carrying the deer, he saw a boar of fearsome form. He set the deer down on the ground and struck the boar with an arrow. The boar too, approaching and making a roar as terrible as a thundercloud at the time of dissolution, struck the hunter in the groin — he fell like a felled tree. And as it is said —

children.text: jalam agnir viṣaṃ śastaṃ kṣud vyādhiḥ patanaṃ gireḥ |
children.translated_text: Water, fire, poison, a weapon, hunger, disease, or a fall from a mountain —

children.text: nimittaṃ kiñcid āsādya dehī prāṇair vimucyate // Hit_1.158 //
children.translated_text: encountering some cause, an embodied being is separated from its life-breaths. // Hit 1.158 //

body.text: atha tayoḥ pādāsphālanena ekaḥ sarpo 'pi mṛtaḥ | atrāntare dīrgharāvo nāma jambukaḥ paribhramanāhārārthā tān mṛtān mṛga-vyādha-sarpa-śūkarān apaśyat | ālokyācintayac ca-aho bhāgyam ! adya mahad bhojyaṃ me samupasthitam |
body.translated_text: Then, from the thrashing of their feet, a snake also died. Meanwhile, a jackal named <s>Dīrgharāva</s>, roaming about in search of food, saw those dead ones — the deer, the hunter, the snake, and the boar. Having observed them, he thought: 'Oh, what fortune! Today a great feast has come to me!'

children.text: athavā-
children.translated_text: Or rather —

children.text: acintitāni duḥkhāni yathaivāyānti dehinām |
children.translated_text: Just as unthought-of sorrows come to embodied beings,

children.text: sukhāny api tathā manye daivam atrātiricyate // Hit_1.159 //
children.translated_text: so too do joys, I think — fate is supreme in this. // Hit 1.159 //

children.text: māsam ekaṃ naro yāti dvau māsau mṛga-śūkarau |
children.translated_text: The man will last one month; the deer and boar, two months;

children.text: ahir ekaṃ dinaṃ yāti adya bhakṣyo dhanurguṇaḥ // Hit_1.160 //
children.translated_text: the snake, one day — today I shall eat the bowstring. // Hit 1.160 //

body.text: tataḥ prathama-bubhukṣāyām idaṃ niḥsvādu kodaṇḍa-lagnaṃ snāyu-bandhanaṃ khādāmi, ity uktvā tathākarot | tataś chinne snāyu-bandhane drutam utpatitena dhanuṣā hṛdi nirbhinnaḥ sa dīrgharāvaḥ pañcatvaṃ gataḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi kartavyaḥ sañcayo nityam ity ādi | tathā ca-
body.translated_text: Then, in his initial hunger, (he thought) 'I shall chew this tasteless sinew-binding attached to the bow,' and did so. When the sinew-binding was severed, the bow sprang up swiftly, pierced his heart, and that <s>Dīrgharāva</s> died. Therefore I say: 'One should always accumulate,' and so on. And also —

children.text: yad dadāti yad aśnāti tad eva dhanino dhanam |
children.translated_text: Whatever one gives and whatever one enjoys — that alone is the wealth of the wealthy;

children.text: anye mṛtasya krīḍanti dārair api dhanair api // Hit_1.161 //
children.translated_text: others make sport with a dead man's wives and wealth. // Hit 1.161 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Furthermore —

children.text: yad dadāsi viśiṣṭebhyo yac cāśnāsi dine dine |
children.translated_text: Whatever you give to the distinguished and whatever you eat day by day,

children.text: tat te vittam ahaṃ manye śeṣaṃ kasyāpi rakṣasi // Hit_1.162 //
children.translated_text: that alone I consider your wealth — the rest you are guarding for someone else. // Hit 1.162 //

body.text: yātu, kim idānīm atikrāntopavarṇanena | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: But enough — what is the use of dwelling on what is past? For —

children.text: nāprāyam abhivāñchanti naṣṭaṃ necchanti śocitum |
children.translated_text: The wise do not long for what has not arrived, nor do they wish to grieve over what is lost;

children.text: āpatsv api na muhyanti narāḥ paṇḍita-buddhayaḥ // Hit_1.163 //
children.translated_text: even in calamities they are not bewildered — men of learned intellect. // Hit 1.163 //

body.text: tat sakhe ! sarvadā tvayā sotsāhena bhavitavyam, yataḥ-
body.translated_text: So, friend! You must always be full of enthusiasm. For —

children.text: śāstrāṇy adhītyāpi bhavanti mūrkhā
children.translated_text: Even after studying the scriptures, some remain fools;

children.text: yas tu kriyāvān puruṣaḥ sa vidvān |
children.translated_text: but the man of action — he is the learned one.

children.text: sucintitaṃ cauṣadham āturāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: A well-prescribed medicine for the sick

children.text: na nāma-mātreṇa karoty arogam // Hit_1.164 //
children.translated_text: does not restore health by its name alone. // Hit 1.164 //

body.text: anyac ca-

children.text: na svalpam apy adhyavasāya-bhīroḥ
children.translated_text: Not even a little good does the method of knowledge do

children.text: karoti vijñāna-vidhir guṇaṃ hi |
children.translated_text: for one who is timid about resolution.

children.text: andhasya kiṃ hasta-tala-sthito 'pi
children.translated_text: Does a lamp placed in the palm of the hand

children.text: prakāśayaty artham iha pradīpaḥ // Hit_1.165 //
children.translated_text: illumine an object here for a blind man? // Hit 1.165 //

body.translated_text: And another —

body.text: tad atra sakhe daśātiśeṣEṇa śāntiḥ karaṇīyā | etad apy atikaṣṭaṃ tvayā na mantavyam |
body.translated_text: So, friend, here a peace-rite should be performed according to the remainder of one's fortune. And you should not regard even this as too difficult —

children.text: sukham āpatitaṃ sevyaṃ duḥkham āpatitaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: One should accept happiness when it comes, and likewise suffering when it comes;

children.text: cakravat parivartante duḥkhāni ca sukhāni ca // Hit_1.166 //
children.translated_text: sorrows and joys revolve like a wheel. // Hit 1.166 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And another —

children.text: nipānam iva maṇḍūkāḥ saraḥ pūrṇam ivāṇḍajāḥ |
children.translated_text: Like frogs to a watering-hole, like birds to a full lake,

children.text: sodyogaṃ naram āyānti vivaśāḥ sarva-sampadaḥ // Hit_1.167 //
children.translated_text: all fortunes come of their own accord to the man who exerts himself. // Hit 1.167 //

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: utsāha-saṃpannam adīrgha-sūtraṃ kriyā-vidhijñaṃ vyasaneṣv asaktam |
children.translated_text: One who is endowed with enthusiasm, who does not procrastinate, who knows the method of action, who is unattached in adversities,

children.text: śūraṃ kṛtajñaṃ dṛḍha-sauhṛdaṃ ca- lakṣmīḥ svayaṃ vāñchati vāsa-hetoḥ // Hit_1.168 //
children.translated_text: who is brave, grateful, and firm in friendship — <s>Lakṣmī</s> (Fortune) herself desires such a one for her dwelling. // Hit 1.168 //

body.text: viśeṣataś ca-

children.text: vināpy arthair dhīraḥ spṛśati bahumānonnati-padaṃ
children.translated_text: The courageous one attains the position of high honor even without wealth;

children.text: samāyukto 'py arthaiḥ paribhava-padaṃ yāti kṛpaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: even when endowed with wealth, the wretched one goes to a position of contempt.

children.text: svabhāvād udbhūtāṃ guṇa-samudayāvāpti-viṣayāṃ
children.translated_text: The splendor of a lion, arising from its nature, pertaining to the attainment of an assemblage of qualities —

children.text: dyutiṃ saiṃhīṃ śvā kiṃ dhṛta-kanaka-mālo 'pi labhate // Hit_1.169 //
children.translated_text: can a dog obtain it, even if adorned with a golden necklace? // Hit 1.169 //

body.translated_text: And especially —

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Furthermore —

children.text: dhanavān iti hi madas te kiṃ gata-vibhavo viṣādam upayāsi |
children.translated_text: 'I am wealthy' — why this pride? 'I have lost my fortune' — why do you succumb to despair?

children.text: kara-nihata-kanduka-samāḥ pātotpātā manuṣyāṇām // Hit_1.170 //
children.translated_text: The falls and rises of men are like a ball struck by the hand. // Hit 1.170 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And another —

children.text: vṛtty-arthaṃ nāticeṣṭate sā hi dhātraiva nirmitā |
children.translated_text: One need not strive excessively for livelihood, for that is created by the Creator himself;

children.text: garbhād utpatite jantau mātuḥ prasravataḥ stanau // Hit_1.171 //
children.translated_text: when the child emerges from the womb, the mother's breasts overflow. // Hit 1.171 //

children.text: api ca sakhe śṛṇu-
children.translated_text: Also, friend, listen —

children.text: yena śuklī-kṛtā haṃsāḥ śukāś ca haritīkṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: He who made swans white and parrots green,

children.text: mayūrāś citritā yena sa te vṛttiṃ vidhāsyati // Hit_1.172 //
children.translated_text: He who painted the peacocks — He will provide for your livelihood. // Hit 1.172 //

body.text: aparaṃ ca satāṃ rahasyaṃ śṛṇu, mitra !
body.translated_text: And hear another secret of the good, O friend —

children.text: janayanty arjane duḥkhaṃ tāpayanti vipattiṣu |
children.translated_text: They (riches) cause pain in their acquisition, they torment in misfortune,

children.text: mohayanti ca sampattau katham arthāḥ sukhāvahāḥ // Hit_1.173 //
children.translated_text: they delude in prosperity — how can riches bring happiness? // Hit 1.173 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And another —

children.text: dharmārdhaṃ yasya vittehā varaṃ tasya nirīhatā |
children.translated_text: For one whose desire for wealth is (only) for the sake of <s>dharma</s>, better is the absence of desire altogether;

children.text: prakṣālanād dhi paṅkasya dūrād asparśanaṃ varam // Hit_1.174 //
children.translated_text: for rather than washing mud, it is better not to touch it from a distance. // Hit 1.174 //

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: For —

children.text: yathāāmiṣam ākāśe pakṣibhiḥ śvāpadair bhuvi |
children.translated_text: Just as meat is devoured in the sky by birds and on earth by wild beasts,

children.text: bhakṣyate salile matsyais tathā sarvatra vittavān // Hit_1.175 //
children.translated_text: and in water by fish — so is the man of wealth (devoured) everywhere. // Hit 1.175 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And another —

children.text: rājataḥ salilād agneś corataḥ svajanād api |
children.translated_text: From the king, from water, from fire, from thieves, and even from one's own people —

children.text: bhayam arthavatāṃ nityaṃ mṛtyoḥ prāṇa-bhṛtām iva // Hit_1.176 //
children.translated_text: the wealthy always have fear, just as living beings (have fear) of death. // Hit 1.176 //

children.text: tathā hi-
children.translated_text: For instance —

children.text: janmani kleśa-bahule kiṃ nu duḥkham ataḥ param |
children.translated_text: In this birth, so full of troubles, what greater sorrow is there than this:

children.text: icchā-sampad yato nāsti yac cecchā na nivartate // Hit_1.177 //
children.translated_text: that the desired prosperity is not (there), and that desire does not cease? // Hit 1.177 //

children.text: anyac ca bhrātaḥ śṛṇu-
children.translated_text: And brother, listen to another —

children.text: dhanaṃ tāvad asulabhaṃ labdhaṃ kṛcchreṇa pālyate |
children.translated_text: Wealth is first hard to obtain; once obtained, it is guarded with difficulty;

children.text: labdha-nāśo yathā mṛtyus tasmād etan na cintayet // Hit_1.178 //
children.translated_text: the loss of what was gained is like death — therefore one should not worry about it. // Hit 1.178 //

children.text: sā tṛṣṇā cet parityaktā ko daridraḥ ka īśvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: If that craving is abandoned, who is poor, who is wealthy?

children.text: tasyāś cet prasaro datto dāsyaṃ ca śirasi sthitam // Hit_1.179 //
children.translated_text: But if its advance is permitted, servitude is established upon one's head. // Hit 1.179 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And another —

children.text: yad yad eva hi vāñcheta tato vāñchā pravartate |
children.translated_text: Whatever one desires, from that more desire arises;

children.text: prāpta evārthataḥ so 'rtho yato vāñchā nivartate // Hit_1.180 //
children.translated_text: that goal is truly attained from which desire ceases. // Hit 1.180 //

body.text: kiṃ bahunā, viśrambhālāpair mayaiva sahātra kālo nīyatām | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: In short, let time be passed here with me in intimate conversation. For —

children.text: āmraṇāntāḥ praṇayāḥ kopāś ca kṣaṇa-bhaṅgurāḥ |
children.translated_text: Affections last until death, while angers are momentary;

children.text: parityāgāś ca niḥsaṅgā na bhavanti mahātmanām // Hit_1.181 //
children.translated_text: renunciations of great souls are not free from attachment. // Hit 1.181 //

body.text: iti śrutvā laghupatanako brūte-dhanyo 'si manthara ! sarvathā āśrayaṇīyo 'si | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Laghupatanaka</s> (the crow) says: 'You are blessed, <s>Manthara</s>! In every way, you are one to be taken refuge in. For —

children.text: santa eva satāṃ nityam āpad-uddharaṇa-kṣamāḥ |
children.translated_text: The good alone are always capable of rescuing the good from calamity;

children.text: gajānāṃ paṅka-magnānāṃ gajā eva dhurandharāḥ // Hit_1.182 //
children.translated_text: only elephants can bear the burden of elephants stuck in the mud. // Hit 1.182 //

body.text: aparaṃ ca-

children.text: ślāghyaḥ sa eko bhuvi mānavānāṃ
children.translated_text: Praiseworthy is he alone among men on earth,

children.text: sa uttamaḥ sat-puruṣaḥ sa dhanyaḥ |
children.translated_text: he is the best, the excellent man, he is blessed,

children.text: yasyārthino vā śaraṇāgatā vā
children.translated_text: from whom the supplicants or those who have come for refuge

children.text: nāśāvibhaṅgā vimukhāḥ prayānti // Hit_1.183 //
children.translated_text: do not depart with disappointed hopes, turning away. // Hit 1.183 //

body.translated_text: And another —

body.text: tad evaṃ te svecchāhāra-vihāraṃ kurvāṇāḥ santuṣṭāḥ sukhaṃ nivasanti sma | atha kadācit citrāṅga-nāmā mṛgaḥ kenāpi trāsitas tatrāgatya militaḥ | tat-paścād āyāntaṃ bhaya-hetuṃ sambhāvya mantharo jalaṃ praviṣṭaḥ | mūṣikaś ca vivaraṃ gataḥ, kāko 'pi uḍḍīya vṛkṣāgram ārūḍhaḥ | tato laghupatanakena sudūraṃ nirūpya bhaya-hetur na ko 'py avalambitaḥ | paścāt tad-vacanād āgatya punaḥ sarve militvā tatraivopaviṣṭāḥ | manthareṇoktaṃ-bhadra mṛga ! kuśalaṃ te ? svecchayā udakādyāhāro 'nubhūyatām | atrāvasthānena vanam idaṃ sanāthīkriyatām |
body.translated_text: Thus, living contentedly with food and recreation as they pleased, they dwelt happily. Now once, a deer named <s>Citrāṅga</s>, frightened by someone, came there and joined them. Suspecting that a cause of danger was following behind him, <s>Manthara</s> entered the water, the mouse went into his hole, and the crow flew up to the top of a tree. Then <s>Laghupatanaka</s>, having surveyed from afar, found no cause of danger present. Afterwards, at his word, all came back and sat down together at that very place. <s>Manthara</s> said: 'Dear deer! Are you well? Enjoy food such as water and the rest as you please; by residing here, grace this forest with your presence.'

body.text: citrāṅgo brūte-lubdhaka-trāsito 'haṃ bhavatāṃ śaraṇam āgataḥ | tataś ca, bhavadbhiḥ saha mitratvam icchāmi | bhavantaś ca anukampayantu maitryeṇa | yataḥ-

children.text: lobhād vātha bhayād vāpi yas tyajec charaṇāgatam |
children.translated_text: He who, out of greed or fear, abandons one who has come for refuge —

children.text: brahma-hatyā-samaṃ tasya pāpam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ // Hit_1.184 //
children.translated_text: the wise say that his sin is equal to <s>Brahma</s>-cide. // Hit 1.184 //

body.translated_text: <s>Citrāṅga</s> says: 'Frightened by a hunter, I have come to you for refuge. Therefore, I desire friendship with you. And may you show me compassion with friendship. For —

body.text: hiraṇyako 'py avadat-mitratvaṃ tāvad asmābhiḥ saha, ayatnena niṣpannaṃ bhavataḥ | yataḥ-

children.text: aurasaṃ kṛta-sambandhaṃ tathā vaṃśa-kramāgatam |
children.translated_text: Whether born in the family, made through formal bond, or inherited through lineage,

children.text: rakṣakaṃ vyasanebhyaś ca mitraṃ jñeyaṃ catur-vidham // Hit_1.185 //
children.translated_text: A friend should be known as fourfold: one who protects from calamities. // Hit 1.185 //

body.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> (the mouse) also said: 'Friendship with us has been accomplished by you effortlessly. For —

body.text: tad atra bhavatā sva-gṛha-nirviśeṣeṇa sthīyatām | tac chrutvā mṛgaḥ sānando bhūtvā kṛta-svecchāhāraḥ pānīyaṃ pītvā jalāsanna-vaṭa-taru-cchāyāyām upaviṣṭaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therefore, let Your Honor stay here, treating [this place] as no different from your own home.' Hearing that, the deer, having become joyful, having eaten food at will and drunk water, sat down in the shade of a banyan tree near the water.

body.text: atha mantharo brūte-sakhe mṛga ! kena trāsito 'si ? asmin nirjane vane kadācit kiṃ vyādhāḥ sañcaranti ?
body.translated_text: Then <s>Manthara</s> (the tortoise) said: 'Friend deer! By whom were you frightened? In this desolate forest, do hunters ever roam about?'

body.text: mṛgeṇoktam-asti kaliṅga-viṣaye rukmāṅgado nāma nṛpatiḥ | sa ca digvijaya-vyāpāra-krameṇa āgatya candrabhāgā-nadī-tīre samāveśita-kaṭako vartate, prātaś ca tenātrāgatya karpūra-saraḥ samīpe bhavitavyam iti vyādhānāṃ mukhāt kiṃvadantī śrūyate | tad atrāpi prātar-avasthānaṃ bhaya-hetukam ity ālocya yathā kāryaṃ tathā ārabhyatām |
body.translated_text: The deer said: 'There is in the <s>Kaliṅga</s> country a king named <s>Rukmāṅgada</s>. He, in the course of his campaign of conquest, has arrived and encamped his army on the bank of the river <s>Candrabhāgā</s>. And I have heard a rumor from the mouths of hunters that he is to come here tomorrow morning near the <s>Karpūra</s> lake. Therefore, having considered that staying here in the morning would be a cause for fear, let appropriate action be undertaken.'

body.text: tac chrutvā kūrmaḥ sa-bhayam āha-mitra ! jalāśayāntaraṃ gacchāmi |
body.translated_text: Hearing that, the tortoise said fearfully: 'Friend! I shall go to another body of water.'

body.text: kāka-mṛgāv api uktavantau-mitra ! evam astu !
body.translated_text: The crow and the deer also said: 'Friend! So be it!'

body.text: hiraṇyako vimṛśyābravīt-punar jalāśaye prāpte mantharasya kuśalam | sthale gacchato 'sya kā vidhā ?
body.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> (the mouse), having reflected, said: 'Once <s>Manthara</s> reaches another lake, all will be well. But what provision is there for him traveling on land?'

children.text: ambhāṃsi jala-jantūnāṃ durgaṃ durga-nivāsinām |
children.translated_text: Waters are the fortress of aquatic creatures; the stronghold [is the fortress] of those dwelling in fortresses;

children.text: sva-bhūmiḥ śvāpadādīnāṃ rājñāṃ sainyaṃ paraṃ balam // Hit_1.186 //
children.translated_text: their own terrain [is the fortress] of wild animals and the like; the army is the supreme strength of kings. // Hit 1.186 //

children.text: upāyena hi yac chakyaṃ na tac chakyaṃ parākramaiḥ |
children.translated_text: What can be accomplished by stratagem cannot be accomplished by valor;

children.text: kākī kanaka-sūtreṇa kṛṣṇa-sarpam aghātayat // Hit_1.187 //
children.translated_text: a female crow, by means of a golden thread, caused a black serpent to be killed. // Hit 1.187 //

body.text:
tad yathā-
kathā 6
body.translated_text:
That is as follows —
Story 6

body.text: asti brahmāraṇye karpā̆ūratilako nāma hastī | tam avalokya sarve śṛgālāś cintayanti sma | yady ayaṃ kenāpy upāyena miryate, tadāsmākam etena dehena māsa-catuṣṭayasya svecchā-bhojanaṃ bhavet | tatas tan-madhyād ekena vṛddha-śṛgālena pratijñā kṛtā | mayā buddhi-prabhāvād asya maraṇaṃ sādhayitavyam | anantaraṃ sa vañcakaḥ karpūratilaka-samīpaṃ gatvā sāṣṭāṅga-pātaṃ praṇamyovāca-deva ! dṛṣṭi-prasādaṃ kuru |
body.translated_text: There is in the <s>Brahmāraṇya</s> forest an elephant named <s>Karpūratilaka</s>. Seeing him, all the jackals thought: 'If this one were to die by some stratagem, then with his body we would have food at our pleasure for four months.' Then one old jackal among them made a pledge: 'I shall accomplish his death through the power of intellect.' Thereupon that deceiver went near <s>Karpūratilaka</s> and, prostrating himself with all eight limbs, said: 'Lord! Bestow the grace of your glance.'

body.text: hastī brūte-kas tvam ? kutaḥ samāyātaḥ ?
body.translated_text: The elephant said: 'Who are you? Whence have you come?'

body.text: so 'vadat-jambuko 'haṃ sarvair vana-vāsibhiḥ paśubhir militvā bhavat-sakāśaṃ prasthāpitaḥ | yad vinā rājñā sthātuṃ na yuktam | tad atrāṭavī-rājye'bhiṣektuṃ bhavān sarva-svāmi-guṇopeto nirūpitaḥ | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: He said: 'I am a jackal. Having assembled together, all the forest-dwelling animals have sent me to your presence. For it is not proper to remain without a king. Therefore, you have been chosen to be consecrated as king of this forest realm, being endowed with all the qualities of a sovereign. For —'

children.text: kulācāra-janācārair atiśuddhaḥ pratāpavān |
children.translated_text: One who is exceedingly pure through family custom and popular custom, possessed of valor,

children.text: dhārmiko nīti-kuśalaḥ sa svāmī yujyate bhuvi // Hit_1.188 //
children.translated_text: righteous, and skilled in statecraft — he is fit to be a sovereign on earth. // Hit 1.188 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca paśya-
children.translated_text: Moreover, consider this —

children.text: rājānaṃ prathamaṃ vindet tato bhāryāṃ tato dhanam |
children.translated_text: One should first seek a king, then a wife, then wealth;

children.text: rājany asati loke'smin kuto bhāryā kuto dhanam // Hit_1.189 //
children.translated_text: when there is no king in this world, whence a wife, whence wealth? // Hit 1.189 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: parjanya iva bhūtānām ādhāraḥ pṛthivī-patiḥ |
children.translated_text: The lord of the earth is the support of beings, like the rain-cloud;

children.text: vikale'pi hi parjanye jīvyate na tu bhūpatau // Hit_1.190 //
children.translated_text: even when the rain-cloud fails, one may live; but not when the king [fails]. // Hit 1.190 //

body.text: kiṃ ca-

children.text: niyata-viṣaya-vartī prāyaśo daṇḍa-yogāj
children.translated_text: Confined to regulated objects, generally through the application of the rod [of punishment],

children.text: jagati para-vaśe'smin durlabhaḥ sādhu-vṛtteḥ |
children.translated_text: in this world subject to another's control, rare is [one of] virtuous conduct;

children.text: kṛśam api vikalaṃ vā vyādhitaṃ vādhanaṃ vā
children.translated_text: even [a husband who is] emaciated, impaired, diseased, or poor —

children.text: patim api kula-nārī daṇḍa-bhītyābhyupaiti // Hit_1.191 //
children.translated_text: a woman of good family submits [to him] out of fear of the rod [of punishment]. // Hit 1.191 //

body.translated_text: Moreover —

body.text: tad yathā lagna-velā na calati tathā kṛtvā satvaram āgamyatāṃ devena | ity uktvā utthāya calitaḥ | tato 'sau rājya-lābhākṛṣṭaḥ karpūratilakaḥ śṛgāla-darśita-vartmanā dhāvan mahā-paṅke nimagnaḥ | hastinoktam-sakhe śṛgāla ! kim adhunā vidheyam ? mahā-paṅke patito 'haṃ mriye | parāvṛtya paśya !
body.translated_text: Therefore, act swiftly so that the auspicious moment does not pass, and let Your Lordship come.' So saying, he rose and departed. Then that <s>Karpūratilaka</s>, drawn by the prospect of gaining a kingdom, running along the path shown by the jackal, sank into a great swamp. The elephant said: 'Friend jackal! What is to be done now? I have fallen into a great swamp and am dying! Turn back and look!'

body.text: śṛgālena vihasyoktam-deva ! mama pucchāgre hastaṃ dattvā uttiṣṭha | yasmāt mad-vidhasya vacasi tvayā viśvāsaḥ kṛtaḥ, tasya phalam etat | tad anubhūyatām aśaraṇaṃ duḥkham | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: The jackal said with a laugh: 'Lord! Rise up by placing your trunk on the tip of my tail! Since you placed your trust in the words of one such as me, this is the fruit of that. So experience this helpless suffering! And as it is said —'

children.text: yadāsat-saṅga-rahito bhaviṣyasi bhaviṣyasi |
children.translated_text: When you will be free from the company of the wicked, you will [truly] prosper;

children.text: yadāsajjana-goṣṭhīṣu patiṣyasi patiṣyasi // Hit_1.192 //
children.translated_text: when you fall into the assemblies of the vile, you will [surely] fall. // Hit 1.192 //

body.text: tato mahā-paṅke nimagno hastī śṛgālair bhakṣitaḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-upāyena hi yac chakyam ity ādi |
body.translated_text: Then the elephant, sunk in the great swamp, was devoured by the jackals. Therefore I say: 'What can be accomplished by stratagem...' and so on.

body.text: tatas tad-dhita-vacanam avadhīrya mahatā bhayena vimugdha iva mantharass taj-jalāśayam utsṛjya pracalitaḥ | te'pi hiraṇyakādayaḥ snehād aniṣṭaṃ śaṅkamānās tam anujagmuḥ | tataḥ sthale gacchan kenāpi vyādhena vane paryaṭatā sa mantharaḥ prāptaḥ | sa ca taṃ gṛhītvā utthāya dhanuṣi baddhvā dhanyo 'smīty abhidhāya bhramaṇa-kleśāt kṣut-pipāsākulaḥ sva-gṛhābhimukhaṃ prayātaḥ | atha te mṛga-vāyasa-mūṣikāḥ paraṃ viṣādam upagatāḥ tam anugacchanti sma | tato hiraṇyako vilapati-
body.translated_text: Then, disregarding that well-meaning counsel, <s>Manthara</s>, bewildered as it were by great fear, abandoned that lake and set out. <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> and the others too, fearing misfortune out of affection, followed him. Then, as he was going on land, <s>Manthara</s> was caught by a certain hunter who was roaming in the forest. That [hunter], having seized him and lifted [him] up, tied [him] to his bow, and saying 'I am fortunate,' exhausted from wandering and distressed by hunger and thirst, set out toward his own home. Then the deer, crow, and mouse, having arrived at the utmost despair, followed him. Then <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> lamented:

children.text: ekasya duḥkhasya na yāvad antaṃ gacchāmy ahaṃ pāram ivārṇavasya |
children.translated_text: Before I reach the end of one sorrow — as [one reaches] the far shore of the ocean —

children.text: tāvad dvitīyaṃ samupasthitaṃ me chidreṣv anarthā bahulī-bhavanti // Hit_1.193 //
children.translated_text: a second one has presented itself to me; in [life's] weak spots, misfortunes multiply. // Hit 1.193 //

children.text: svabhāvajaṃ tu yan mitraṃ bhāgyenaivābhijāyate |
children.translated_text: A friend that is born of one's own nature arises only through destiny;

children.text: tad-akṛtrima-sauhārdam āpatsv api na muñcati // Hit_1.194 //
children.translated_text: such unfeigned goodwill does not abandon [one] even in calamities. // Hit 1.194 //

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: na mātari na dāreṣu na sodarye na cātmaje |
children.translated_text: Not in one's mother, not in one's wife, not in one's brother, not in one's son —

children.text: viśvāsas tādṛśaḥ puṃsāṃ yādṛṅ mitre svabhāvaje // Hit_1.195 //
children.translated_text: do men have such trust as in a friend born of [one's own] nature. // Hit 1.195 //

body.text: iti muhuḥ vicintya prāha-aho me durdaivam | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Thus, having reflected again and again, he said: 'Alas, my ill fortune! For —'

children.text: sva-karma-santāna-viceṣṭitāni
children.translated_text: The workings of the continuous stream of one's own <s>karma</s>,

children.text: kālāntarāvarti-śubhāśubhāni |
children.translated_text: recurring in the course of time as good and evil,

children.text: ihaiva dṛṣṭāni mayaiva tāni
children.translated_text: are seen by me right here, those very [karmic fruits] —

children.text: janmāntarāṇīva daśāntarāṇi // Hit_1.196 //
children.translated_text: as if [they were] different life-conditions from different births. // Hit 1.196 //

children.text: athavā ittham evaitat |
children.translated_text: Or rather, it is exactly thus:

children.text: kāyaḥ saṃnihitāpāyaḥ sampadaḥ padam āpadām |
children.translated_text: The body is [always] near destruction; prosperities are the abode of calamities;

children.text: samāgamāḥ sāpagamāḥ sarvam utpādi bhaṅguram // Hit_1.197 //
children.translated_text: meetings [end in] partings; everything that has arisen is perishable. // Hit 1.197 //

children.text: punar vimṛśyāha-
children.translated_text: Having reflected again, he said —

children.text: śokārāti-bhaya-trāṇaṃ prīti-viśrambha-bhājanam |
children.translated_text: A protection from grief, enmity, and fear; a vessel of affection and trust —

children.text: kena ratnam idaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ mitram ity akṣara-dvayam // Hit_1.198 //
children.translated_text: by whom was this jewel created: the two syllables 'mi-tra' (friend)? // Hit 1.198 //

body.text: kiṃ ca-

children.text: mitraṃ prīti-rasāyanaṃ nayanayor ānandanaṃ cetasaḥ
children.translated_text: A friend is an elixir of affection, a delight to the eyes, a joy to the heart;

children.text: pātraṃ yat sukha-duḥkhayoḥ samam idaṃ puṇyātmanā labhyate |
children.translated_text: it is this [friend] who is an equal vessel for happiness and sorrow — obtained [only] by one of meritorious soul.

children.text: ye cānye suhṛdaḥ samṛddhi-samaye dravyābhilāṣākulās
children.translated_text: Those other so-called friends who, in times of prosperity, are agitated by desire for wealth —

children.text: te sarvatra milanti tattva-nikaṣa-grāvā tu teṣāṃ vipat // Hit_1.199 //
children.translated_text: they are found everywhere; but the touchstone that tests them is adversity. // Hit 1.199 //

body.translated_text: Moreover —

body.text: iti bahu vilapya hiraṇyakaś citrāṅga-laghupatanakāv āha-yāvad ayaṃ vyādho vanān na niḥsarati, tāvan mantharaṃ mocayituṃ yatnaḥ kriyatām |
body.translated_text: Thus having lamented much, <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said to <s>Citrāṅga</s> (the deer) and <s>Laghupatanaka</s> (the crow): 'Before this hunter exits the forest, let an effort be made to free <s>Manthara</s>!'

body.text: tāv ūcatuḥ-satvaraṃ yathā-kāryam upadiśa |
body.translated_text: The two said: 'Quickly instruct us as to what should be done!'

body.text: hiraṇyako brūte-citrāṅgo jala-samīpaṃ gatvā mṛtam ivātmānaṃ niśceṣṭaṃ darśayatu | kākaś ca tasyopari sthitvā cañcvā kim api vilikhatu | nūnam anena lubdhakena mṛga-māṃsārthinā tatra kacchapaṃ parityajya sarvaraṃ gantavyam | tato 'haṃ mantharasya bandhanaṃ chetsyāmi | sannihite lubdhake bhavadbhyāṃ palāyitavyam |
body.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said: 'Let <s>Citrāṅga</s> go near the water and show himself as if dead, motionless. And let the crow, standing on top of him, scratch at [him] a bit with his beak. Surely this greedy hunter, desiring deer-meat, will abandon the tortoise there and go swiftly. Then I shall cut <s>Manthara</s>'s bonds. When the hunter comes near, you two must flee.'

body.text: tataś citrāṅga-laghupatanakābhyāṃ śīghraṃ gatvā tathānuṣṭhite sati sa vyādhaḥ pariśrāntaḥ pānīyaṃ pītvā taror adhastād upaviṣṭaḥ san tathāvidhaṃ mṛgam apaśyat | tataḥ kacchapaṃ jala-samīpe nidhāya kartarikām ādāya prahṛṣṭa-manā mṛgāntikaṃ calitaḥ | atrāntare hiraṇyakena āgatya mantharasya bandhanaṃ chinnam | chinna-bandhanaḥ kūrmaḥ satvaraṃ jalāśayaṃ praviṣṭaḥ | sa ca mṛga āsannaṃ taṃ vyādhaṃ vilokyotthāya drutaṃ palāyitaḥ | pratyāvṛttya lubdhako yāvat taru-talam āyāti tāvat kūrmam apaśyann acintayat-ucitam evaitat mamāsamīkṣya-kāriṇaḥ | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Then, when <s>Citrāṅga</s> and <s>Laghupatanaka</s> had quickly gone and done exactly so, that hunter, exhausted, having drunk water and sitting down at the foot of a tree, saw the deer in that state. Then, placing the tortoise near the water and taking up his knife, he set out with delighted heart toward the deer. In the meanwhile, <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> came and cut <s>Manthara</s>'s bonds. The tortoise, his bonds severed, quickly entered the lake. And the deer, seeing that hunter approach near, sprang up and fled swiftly.
