The hunter, returning and coming to the foot of the tree, not seeing the tortoise, thought: 'This is exactly what befits one like me who acts without deliberation. For —'

children.text: yo dhruvāṇi parityajya adhruvāṇi niṣevate |
children.translated_text: He who abandons what is certain and pursues what is uncertain —

children.text: dhruvāṇi tasya naśyanti adhruvaṃ naṣṭam eva hi // Hit_1.200 //
children.translated_text: what is certain perishes for him, and what is uncertain is already lost. // Hit 1.200 //

body.text: tato 'sau sva-karma-vaśān nirāśaḥ kaṭakaṃ praviṣṭaḥ | mantharādayaś ca sarve muktāpadaḥ sva-sthānaṃ gatvā yathā-sukham āsthitāḥ |
body.translated_text: Then that [hunter], hopeless due to his own <s>karma</s>, entered the camp. And <s>Manthara</s> and the others, all freed from danger, going to their own place, abode in comfort.

body.text: atha rāja-putraiḥ sānandam uktam-sarve śrutavantaḥ sukhino vayam | siddhaṃ naḥ samīhitam |
body.translated_text: Then the princes said with joy: 'We have all heard and are happy. Our desire has been accomplished.'

body.text: viṣṇu-śarmovāca-etad bhavatām abhilaṣitam api sampannam | aparam apīdam astu-
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s> said: 'This, which was your desire, has also been fulfilled. And let there be this further [blessing] —'

children.text: mitraṃ yāntu ca sajjanā janapadair lakṣmīḥ samālabhyatāṃ
children.translated_text: May friends go [well]; may good people be [blessed] by their countryfolk; may <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity) be attained;

children.text: bhūpālāḥ paripālayantu vasudhāṃ śaśvat sva-dharme sthitāḥ |
children.translated_text: may kings protect the earth, ever established in their own <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: āstāṃ mānasa-tuṣṭaye sukṛtināṃ nītir navoḍheva vaḥ
children.translated_text: may statecraft (<s>nīti</s>), like a newly-wed bride, abide for the satisfaction of the minds of the meritorious;

children.text: kalyāṇaṃ kurutāṃ janasya bhagavāṃś candrārdha-cūḍāmaṇiḥ // Hit_1.201 //
children.translated_text: may the blessed <s>Candrārdhacūḍāmaṇi</s> (<s>Śiva</s>, whose crest-jewel is the crescent moon) bring welfare to the people. // Hit 1.201 //

body.text:
ii.
suhṛd-bhedaḥ
body.translated_text:
II.
<s>Suhṛdbheda</s> (The Separation of Friends)

body.text: atha rāja-putrā ūcuḥ-ārya ! mitralābhaḥ śrutas tāvad asmābhiḥ | idānīṃ suhṛd-bhedaṃ śrotum icchāmaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then the princes said: 'Sir! We have heard the <s>Mitralābha</s> (Gaining of Friends). Now we wish to hear the <s>Suhṛdbheda</s> (Separation of Friends).'

body.text: viṣṇuśarmovāca-suhṛd-bhedaṃ tāvac chṛṇuta, yasyāyam ādyaḥ ślokaḥ-
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s> said: 'Hear then the <s>Suhṛdbheda</s>, whose opening verse is this —'

children.text: vardhamāno mahān sneho mṛgendra-vṛṣayor vane |
children.translated_text: The great and growing affection between a lion and a bull in the forest

children.text: piśunenātilubdhena jambukena vināśitaḥ // Hit_2.1 //
children.translated_text: was destroyed by a wicked and exceedingly greedy jackal. // Hit 2.1 //

body.text: rāja-putrair uktam-katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The princes said: 'How was that?'

body.text: viṣṇuśarmā kathayati-asti dakṣiṇā-pathe suvarṇavatī nāma nagarī | tatra vardhamāno nāma vaṇig nivasati | tasya pracure'pi vitte' parān bandhūn atisamṛddhān samīkṣya punar artha-vṛddhiḥ karaṇīyeti matir babhūva | yataḥ,
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s> narrates: 'In the southern region, there is a city called <s>Suvarṇavatī</s>. There dwelt a merchant named <s>Vardhamāna</s>. Though he had abundant wealth, seeing other relatives exceedingly prosperous, the thought arose in his mind that further increase of wealth should be undertaken. For —'

children.text: adho 'dhaḥ paśyataḥ kasya mahimā nopacīyate |
children.translated_text: Of one who always looks downward, whose greatness ever increases?

children.text: upary upari paśyantaḥ sarva eva daridrati // Hit_2.2 //
children.translated_text: Those who always look upward — everyone [among them] becomes poor. // Hit 2.2 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: brahmahāpi naraḥ pūjyo yasyāsti vipulaṃ dhanam |
children.translated_text: Even a man who has killed a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is honored if he has abundant wealth;

children.text: śaśinas tulya-vaṃśo 'pi nirdhanaḥ paribhūyate // Hit_2.3 //
children.translated_text: one who is of a lineage equal to the moon, if destitute, is despised. // Hit 2.3 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: avyavasāyinam alasaṃ daiva-paraṃ sahasāc ca parihīṇam |
children.translated_text: One who is without enterprise, lazy, dependent on fate, and who has suddenly fallen —

children.text: pramadeva hi vṛddha-patiṃ necchaty avagūhituṃ lakṣmīḥ // Hit_2.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s> (fortune), like a young woman, does not wish to embrace [him as] an aged husband. // Hit 2.4 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: ālasyaṃ strī-sevā sa-rogatā janma-bhūmi-vātsalyam |
children.translated_text: Laziness, devotion to women, illness, attachment to one's birthplace,

children.text: santoṣo bhīrutvaṃ ṣaḍ vyāghātā mahattvasya // Hit_2.5 //
children.translated_text: contentment, and cowardice — these are the six obstacles to greatness. // Hit 2.5 //

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: For —

children.text: sampadā susthiraṃ-manyo bhavati svalpayāpi yaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, even with a small fortune, considers himself firmly established —

children.text: kṛtakṛtyo vidhir manye na vardhayati tasya tām // Hit_2.6 //
children.translated_text: fate, I think, being satisfied [with him as he is], does not increase that [fortune] for him. // Hit 2.6 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: nirutsāhaṃ nirānandaṃ nirvīryam ari-nandanam |
children.translated_text: Without enthusiasm, without joy, without vigor, a delight to enemies —

children.text: mā sma sīmantinī kācij janayet putram īdṛśam // Hit_2.7 //
children.translated_text: may no woman ever give birth to such a son! // Hit 2.7 //

children.text: tathā coktam-
children.translated_text: And as it is said —

children.text: alabdhaṃ caiva lipseta labdhaṃ rakṣet prayatnataḥ |
children.translated_text: One should seek to obtain what has not been obtained, and diligently protect what has been obtained;

children.text: rakṣitaṃ vardhayec caiva vṛddhaṃ pātreṣu nikṣipet // Hit_2.8 //
children.translated_text: what has been protected should be increased, and what has been increased should be bestowed upon worthy recipients. // Hit 2.8 //

body.text: yato 'labdham icchato 'rtha-yogād arthasya prāptir eva | labdhasyāpy arakṣitasya nidher api svayaṃ vināśaḥ | api ca, avardhamānaś cārthaḥ kāle svalpa-vyayo 'py añjanavat kṣayam eti | naupabhujyamānaś ca niṣprayojana eva saḥ | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: For one who desires what has not been obtained, from the employment of means, there is acquisition of wealth. And even of what has been obtained, if unprotected, even of a treasure, there is self-destruction. Moreover, wealth that is not increasing, even if the expenditure is small, goes to diminution over time, like collyrium. And wealth that is not enjoyed is simply purposeless. And as it is said —

children.text: dhanena kiṃ yo na dadāti nāśnute
children.translated_text: What use is wealth for one who neither gives nor eats?

children.text: balena kiṃ yaś ca ripūn na bādhate |
children.translated_text: What use is strength for one who does not subdue enemies?

children.text: śrutena kiṃ yo na ca dharmam ācaret
children.translated_text: What use is learning for one who does not practice <s>dharma</s>?

children.text: kim ātmanā yo na jitendriyo bhavet // Hit_2.9 //
children.translated_text: What use is a self for one who has not conquered the senses? // Hit 2.9 //

children.text: yataḥ,
children.translated_text: For —

children.text: jala-bindu-nipātena kramaśaḥ pūryate ghaṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: By the falling of water drops, gradually a pot is filled;

children.text: sa hetuḥ sarva-vidyānāṃ dharmasya ca dhanasya ca // Hit_2.10 //
children.translated_text: He is the cause of all knowledge, of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), and of wealth. // Hit_2.10 //

children.text: dānopabhoga-rahitā divasā yasya yānti vai |
children.translated_text: One whose days pass without giving or enjoying,

children.text: sa karma-kāra-bhastreva śvasann api na jīvati // Hit_2.11 //
children.translated_text: he, like the bellows of a blacksmith, though breathing, does not truly live. // Hit_2.11 //

body.text: iti saṃcintya nandaka-sajīvaka-nāmānau vṛṣabhau dhuri niyojya śakaṭaṃ nānāvidha-dravya-pūrṇaṃ kṛtvā vāṇijyena gataḥ kaśmīraṃ prati | anyac ca-
body.translated_text: Having reflected thus, he yoked two bulls named <s>Nandaka</s> and <s>Sañjīvaka</s> to the cart, filled it with various kinds of goods, and set out for trade toward <s>Kaśmīra</s>. And further—

children.text: añjanasya kṣayaṃ dṛṣṭvā valmīkasya ca sañcayam |
children.translated_text: Seeing the diminution of collyrium and the accumulation of an anthill,

children.text: avandhyaṃ divasaṃ kuryād dānādhyayana-karmabhiḥ // Hit_2.12 //
children.translated_text: one should make each day fruitful through charity, study, and ritual action. // Hit_2.12 //

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: For—

children.text: ko 'tibhāraḥ samarthānāṃ kiṃ dūraṃ vyavasāyinām |
children.translated_text: What burden is too heavy for the capable? What is far for the industrious?

children.text: ko videśaḥ savidyānāṃ kaḥ paraḥ priya-vādinām // Hit_2.13 //
children.translated_text: What land is foreign to the learned? Who is a stranger to those who speak kindly? // Hit_2.13 //

body.text: atha gacchatas tasya sudurga-nāmni mahāraṇye sañjīvako bhagna-jānur nipatitaḥ | tam ālokya vardhamāno 'cintayat-
body.translated_text: Now, as he was traveling, in a great forest called <s>Sudurga</s>, <s>Sañjīvaka</s> fell with a broken knee. Seeing him, <s>Vardhamāna</s> thought—

children.text: karotu nāma nīti-jño vyavasāyam itas tataḥ |
children.translated_text: Let the wise man make effort here and there,

children.text: phalaṃ punas tad eva syād yad vidher manasi sthitam // Hit_2.14 //
children.translated_text: yet the result will only be what is fixed in the mind of <s>Vidhi</s> (Fate). // Hit_2.14 //

children.text: kintu-
children.translated_text: However—

children.text: vismayaḥ sarvathā heyaḥ pratyūhaḥ sarva-karmaṇām |
children.translated_text: Despair is to be entirely abandoned, for it is an obstacle to all undertakings;

children.text: tasmād vismayam utsṛjya sādhye siddhir vidhīyatām // Hit_2.15 //
children.translated_text: therefore, casting off despair, let accomplishment be directed toward the goal. // Hit_2.15 //

body.text: iti saṃcintya saṃjīvakaṃ tatra parityajya vardhamānaḥ punaḥ svayaṃ dharmapuraṃ nāma nagaraṃ gatvā mahākāyam anyaṃ vṛṣabham ekaṃ samānīya dhuri niyojya calitaḥ | tataḥ saṃjīvako 'pi kathaṃ katham api khura-traye bharaṃ kṛtvotthitaḥ | yataḥ-

children.text: nimagnasya payo-rāśau parvatāt patitasya ca |
children.translated_text: For one who has sunk in the ocean, or fallen from a mountain,

children.text: takṣakeṇāpi daṣṭasya āyur marmāṇi rakṣati // Hit_2.16 //
children.translated_text: or been bitten by <s>Takṣaka</s> (the serpent), if his life-span endures, his vital points are protected. // Hit_2.16 //

body.translated_text: Having reflected thus and abandoning <s>Sañjīvaka</s> there, <s>Vardhamāna</s> himself went to a city called <s>Dharmapura</s>, procured another large bull, yoked it, and set off. Then <s>Sañjīvaka</s> too, somehow or other, placing his weight on three hooves, managed to rise. For—

children.text: nākāle miryate jantur viddhaḥ śara-śatair api |
children.translated_text: A creature does not die before its time, even if pierced by hundreds of arrows;

children.text: kuśāgreṇaiva saṃspṛṣṭaḥ prāpta-kālo na jīvati // Hit_2.17 //
children.translated_text: but when the appointed time has come, one does not survive even if touched by the tip of a blade of <s>kuśa</s> grass. // Hit_2.17 //

children.text: arakṣitaṃ tiṣṭhati daiva-rakṣitaṃ
children.translated_text: That which is unprotected stands safe if guarded by fate;

children.text: surakṣitaṃ daiva-hataṃ vinaśyati |
children.translated_text: that which is well-protected perishes if fate strikes it down;

children.text: jīvaty anātho 'pi vane visarjitaḥ
children.translated_text: one without a guardian lives even when abandoned in the forest;

children.text: kṛta-prayatno 'pi gṛhe na jīvati // Hit_2.18 //
children.translated_text: one who has made every effort does not survive even at home. // Hit_2.18 //

body.text: tato dineṣu gacchatsu saṃjīvakaḥ svecchāhāra-vihāraṃ kṛtvāraṇyaṃ bhrāmyan hṛṣṭa-puṣṭāṅgo balavan nanāda | tasmin vane piṅgalaka-nāmā siṃhaḥ sva-bhujopārjita-rājya-sukham anubhavan nivasati | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: Then, as the days passed, <s>Sañjīvaka</s>, roaming the forest freely eating and sporting as he pleased, became strong and stout of limb, and bellowed mightily. In that forest dwelt a lion named <s>Piṅgalaka</s>, enjoying the pleasure of a kingdom won by the strength of his own arms. As it is said—

children.text: nābhiṣeko na saṃskāraḥ siṃhasya kriyate mṛgaiḥ |
children.translated_text: No consecration and no investiture is performed by the animals for the lion;

children.text: vikramārjita-rājyasya svayam eva mṛgendratā // Hit_2.19 //
children.translated_text: sovereignty over beasts comes of itself to one whose kingdom is won by valor. // Hit_2.19 //

body.text: sa caikadā pipāsākulitaḥ pānīyaṃ pātuṃ yamunā-kaccham agacchat | tena ca tatra siṃhenānanubhūta-pūrvakam akāla-ghana-garjitam iva saṃjīvaka-narditam aśrāvi | tac chrutvā pānīyam apītvā sa-cakitaḥ parivṛtya sva-sthānam āgatya kim idam ity ālocayaṃs tūṣṇīṃ sthitaḥ | sa ca tathāvidhaḥ karaṭa-kadamanakābhyām asya mantri-putrābhyāṃ dṛṣṭaḥ | taṃ tathāvidhaṃ dṛṣṭvā damanakaḥ karaṭakam āha-sakhe karaṭaka ! kim ity ayam udakārthī svāmī pānīyam apītvā sacakito mandaṃ mandam avatiṣṭhate |
body.translated_text: One day, afflicted by thirst, he went to the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s> to drink water. There, the lion heard the bellowing of <s>Sañjīvaka</s>, which was like the rumbling of thunder out of season, never heard by him before. Hearing it, without even drinking the water, he turned back startled, came to his own place, and stood there silently wondering, 'What was that?' And he in that state was seen by <s>Karaṭaka</s> and <s>Damanaka</s>, his two ministers' sons. Seeing him thus, <s>Damanaka</s> said to <s>Karaṭaka</s>: 'Friend <s>Karaṭaka</s>! Why does our master, who came for water, stand here hesitantly, moving slowly, without having drunk the water, and looking frightened?'

body.text: karaṭako brūte-mitra damanaka ! asman-matenāsya sevaiva na kriyate | yadi tathā bhavati tarhi kim anena svāmi-ceṣṭānirūpeṇāsmākam | yato 'nena rājñā vināparādhena ciram avadhīritābhyām āvābhyāṃ mahad-duḥkham anubhūtam |
body.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> says: 'Friend <s>Damanaka</s>! In my opinion, we should not serve him at all. If that is the case, then what concern is it of ours to observe the master's behavior? For we two, long disregarded by this king without any offense on our part, have endured great suffering.'

children.text: sevayā dhanam icchadbhiḥ sevakaiḥ paśya yat kṛtam |
children.translated_text: See what has been done by servants who desire wealth through service:

children.text: svātantryaṃ yac charīrasya mūḍhais tad api hāritam // Hit_2.20 //
children.translated_text: the very freedom of their own bodies has been surrendered by those fools. // Hit_2.20 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And further—

children.text: śīta-vātātapa-kleśān sahante yān parāśritāḥ |
children.translated_text: The sufferings of cold, wind, and heat that dependents endure—

children.text: tad-aṃśenāpi medhāvī tapas taptvā mukhī bhavet // Hit_2.21 //
children.translated_text: with even a fraction of that effort, an intelligent man, performing <s>tapas</s> (austerities), could become a leader. // Hit_2.21 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And also—

children.text: etāvaj janmasāphalyaṃ dehinām iha dehiṣu |
children.translated_text: This much is the fruit of birth for embodied beings among the embodied:

children.text: prāṇair arthair dhiyā vācā śreya evācaret sadā // Hit_2.22 //
children.translated_text: with one's life, wealth, intellect, and speech, one should always pursue what is good. // Hit_2.22 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And further—

children.text: ehi gaccha patottiṣṭha vada maunaṃ samācara |
children.translated_text: 'Come, go, fall down, stand up, speak, observe silence'—

children.text: iti vitrasta-sāraṅga-netrayā ko na vañcitaḥ // Hit_2.23 //
children.translated_text: who has not been deceived by the roving-deer-like eyes (of Fortune)? // Hit_2.23 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover—

children.text: abudhair artha-lābhāya paṇya-strībhir iva svayam |
children.translated_text: By the foolish, for the sake of gaining wealth, like courtesans,

children.text: ātmā saṃskṛtya saṃskṛtya paropakaraṇī-kṛtaḥ // Hit_2.24 //
children.translated_text: the self has been adorned again and again and made into an instrument for others' use. // Hit_2.24 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover—

children.text: yā prakṛtyaiva capalā nipataty aśucāv api |
children.translated_text: That glance which is fickle by nature and falls even on the unclean—

children.text: svāmino bahu manyante dṛṣṭiṃ tām api sevakāḥ // Hit_2.25 //
children.translated_text: even that, servants regard highly as their master's (favor). // Hit_2.25 //

body.text: aparaṃ ca-

children.text: maunān mūrkhaḥ pravacana-paṭur bātulo jalpako vā
children.translated_text: If silent, he is a fool; if skilled in speech, he is a madman or a chatterer;

children.text: kṣāntyā bhīrur yadi na sahate prāyaśo nābhijātaḥ |
children.translated_text: if patient, he is a coward; if he does not endure, he is usually ignoble;

children.text: dhṛṣṭaḥ pārśve vasati niyataṃ dūrataś cāpragalbhaḥ
children.translated_text: if he stays near, he is bold; if at a distance, he is timid—

children.text: sevā-dharmaḥ parama-gahano yoginām apy agamyaḥ // Hit_2.26 //
children.translated_text: the code of service is supremely profound, impenetrable even to <s>yogins</s>. // Hit_2.26 //

body.translated_text: And further—

children.text: viśeṣataś ca-
children.translated_text: Especially—

children.text: praṇamaty unnati-hetor jīvita-hetor vimuñcati prāṇān |
children.translated_text: He bows down for the sake of advancement; he gives up his life for the sake of living;

children.text: duḥkhīyati sukha-hetoḥ ko mūḍhaḥ sevakād anyaḥ // Hit_2.27 //
children.translated_text: he suffers misery for the sake of happiness — what fool is there other than a servant? // Hit_2.27 //

body.text: damanako brūte-mitra sarvathā manasāpi naitat kartavyam, yataḥ-
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> says: 'Friend, such a thing should never be thought even in the mind, for—

children.text: kathaṃ nāma na sevyante yatnataḥ parameśvarāḥ |
children.translated_text: Why should great lords not be served diligently?

children.text: acireṇaiva ye tuṣṭāḥ pūrayanti manorathān // Hit_2.28 //
children.translated_text: When pleased, even quickly, they fulfill one's desires. // Hit_2.28 //'

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And also—

children.text: kutaḥ sevā-vihīnānāṃ cāmaroddhūta-sampadaḥ |
children.translated_text: How can those devoid of service attain the fortune of being fanned by <s>cāmaras</s> (fly-whisks),

children.text: uddaṇḍa-dhavala-cchatraṃ vāji-vāraṇa-vāhinī // Hit_2.29 //
children.translated_text: the upraised white umbrella, and armies of horses and elephants? // Hit_2.29 //

body.text: karaṭako brūte-tathāpi kim anenāsmākaṃ vyāpāreṇa | yato 'vyāpāreṣu vyāpāraḥ sarvathā pariharaṇīyaḥ | paśya-
body.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> says: 'Even so, what business is this of ours? For meddling in others' affairs is to be entirely avoided. Look—

children.text: avyāpareṣu vyāpāraṃ yo naraḥ kartum icchati |
children.translated_text: The man who wishes to meddle in matters that are not his concern,

children.text: sa eva nidhanaṃ yāti kīlotpaṭīva vānaraḥ // Hit_2.30 //
children.translated_text: he alone meets destruction, like the monkey pulling out the wedge. // Hit_2.30 //'

body.text: damanakaḥ pṛcchati--katham etat ?
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> asks: 'How is that?'

body.text: karakaṭaḥ kathayati-
body.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> narrates—

body.text: kathā 1
body.translated_text: Story 1

body.text: asti magadha-deśe dharmāraṇya-saṃnihita-vasudhāyāṃ śubhadatta-nāmnā kāyasthena vihāraḥ kartum ārabdhaḥ | tatra karapatradārya-māṇaika-stambhasya kiyad dūrasphāṭitasya kāṣṭha-khaṇḍa-dvaya-madhye kīlakaḥ sūtra-dhāreṇa nihitaḥ | tatra balavān vānara-yūthaḥ krīḍann āgataḥ | eko vānaraḥ kāla-prerita iva taṃ kīlakaṃ hastābhyāṃ dhṛtvopaviṣṭam | anantaraṃ sa ca sahaja-capalatayā mahatā prayatnena taṃ kīlakam ākṛṣṭavān | ākṛṣṭe ca kīlake cūrṇitāṇḍa-dvayaḥ pañcatvaṃ gataḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-avyāpareṣu vyāpāram ity ādi |
body.translated_text: In the land of <s>Magadha</s>, on the ground near the <s>Dharmāraṇya</s> (Forest of Righteousness), a monastery was being built by a scribe named <s>Śubhadatta</s>. There, in the middle of two pieces of a single pillar that had been partly split by a saw to some distance, a wedge had been placed by a carpenter. A strong troop of monkeys came there playing. One monkey, as if impelled by fate, sat down grasping that wedge with both hands. Then, with his innate restlessness, with great effort he pulled out the wedge. And when the wedge was pulled out, his two testicles were crushed, and he died. Therefore I say: 'The man who wishes to meddle in matters that are not his concern...' and so forth.

body.text: damanako brūte-tathāpi svāmi-ceṣṭā-nirūpaṇaṃ sevakenāvaśyaṃ karaṇīyam |
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> says: 'Even so, a servant must necessarily observe the master's behavior.'

body.text: karaṭako brūte-sarvasminn adhikāre ya eva niyuktaḥ pradhāna-mantrī sa karotu | yato 'nujīvinā parādhikāra-carcā sarvathā na kartavyā | paśya-

children.text: parādhikāra-carcā yaḥ kuryāt svāmi-hitecchayā |
children.translated_text: He who, out of desire for his master's welfare, meddles in another's jurisdiction,

children.text: sa viṣīdati cītkārād gardabhas tāḍito yathā // Hit_2.31 //
children.translated_text: he suffers, like a donkey beaten for braying. // Hit_2.31 //'

body.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> says: 'In every office, let the one who is appointed as chief minister attend to it. For a subordinate should never involve himself in another's jurisdiction. Look—

body.text: damanakaḥ pṛcchati--katham etat ?
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> asks: 'How is that?'

body.text: karaṭako brūte-
body.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> says—

body.text: kathā 2
body.translated_text: Story 2

body.text: asti vārāṇasyāṃ karpūra-paṭako nāma rajakaḥ | sa rātrau gāḍha-nidrāyāṃ prasuptaḥ | tad-anantaraṃ tad-gṛha-dravyāṇi hartuṃ cauraḥ praviṣṭaḥ | tasya prāṅgaṇe gardabho baddhas tiṣṭhati | kukkuraś copaviṣṭo 'sti | atha gardabhaḥ śvānam āha-sakhe ! bhavatas tāvad ayaṃ vyāpāraḥ | tat kim iti tvam uccaiḥ śabdaṃ kṛtvā svāminaṃ na jāgarayasi |
body.translated_text: In <s>Vārāṇasī</s> there was a washerman named <s>Karpūra-paṭaka</s>. He was fast asleep at night in deep slumber. Then a thief entered to steal the goods of his house. In his courtyard, a donkey stood tied up, and a dog was sitting nearby. Then the donkey said to the dog: 'Friend! This is your duty. Why do you not bark loudly and wake up the master?'

body.text: kukkuro brūte-bhadra ! mama niyogasya carcā tvayā na kartavyā | tvam eva kiṃ na jānāsi yathā tasyāharniśaṃ gṛha-rakṣāṃ karomi | yato 'yaṃ cirān nirvṛto mamopayogaṃ na jānāti | tenādhunāpi mamāhāra-dāne mandādaraḥ | yato vinā vidhura-darśanaṃ svāmina upajīviṣu mandādarā bhavanti |
body.translated_text: The dog says: 'Good sir! You should not meddle with my duty. Do you yourself not know that I guard his house day and night? But this master, having long been at ease, does not recognize my usefulness. Therefore he is now negligent even in giving me food. For without seeing adversity, masters become indifferent toward their dependents.'

body.text:
gardabho brūte-śṛṇu re barbara !
yācate kārya-kāle yaḥ sa kiṃ-bhṛtyaḥ sa kiṃ-suhṛt |
body.translated_text: The donkey says: 'Listen, you wretch! He who begs to be employed only at the time of need — what kind of servant is he? What kind of friend is he?'

body.text: kukkuro brūte-

children.text: bhṛtyān sambhāṣayed yas tu kārya-kāle sa kiṃ-prabhuḥ // Hit_2.32 //
children.translated_text: 'And he who addresses his servants only at the time of need — what kind of master is he? // Hit_2.32 //'

body.translated_text: The dog says:

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: For—

children.text: āśritānāṃ bhṛtau svāmi-sevāyāṃ dharma-sevane |
children.translated_text: In the maintenance of dependents, in the service of a master, in the service of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: putrasyotpādane caiva na santi pratihastakāḥ // Hit_2.33 //
children.translated_text: and in the begetting of a son — there are no substitutes. // Hit_2.33 //

body.text: tato gardabhaḥ sa-kopam āha-are duṣṭa-mate ! pāpīyāṃs tvaṃ yad vipattau svāmi-kārye upekṣāṃ karoṣi | bhavatu tāvat | yathā svāmī jāgariṣyati, tan mayā kartavyam | yataḥ-

children.text: pṛṣṭhataḥ sevayed arkaṃ jaṭhareṇa hutāśanam |
children.translated_text: One should serve the sun from behind, the fire with one's belly,

children.text: svāminaṃ sarva-bhāvena paralokam amāyayā // Hit_2.34 //
children.translated_text: one's master with one's whole being, and the next world without deceit. // Hit_2.34 //'

body.translated_text: Then the donkey said angrily: 'You wicked-minded wretch! You are sinful in that you show indifference to the master's cause in times of danger. Very well then. I shall do what will wake the master. For—

body.text: ity uktvātīva cītkāra-śabdaṃ kṛtavān | tataḥ sa rajakas tena cītkāreṇa prabuddho nidrā-bhaṅga-kopād utthāya gardabhaṃ laguḍena tādayāmāsa | tenāsau pañcatvam agamat | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-parādhikāra-carcām ity ādi | paśya, paśūnām anveṣaṇam evāsman-niyogaḥ | sva-niyoga-carcā kriyatām | kintv adya tayā carcayā na prayojanam | yata āvayor bhakṣita-śeṣāhāraḥ pracuro 'sti |
body.translated_text: Having said this, he brayed extremely loudly. Then the washerman, awakened by that braying, rose up in anger at having his sleep disturbed and beat the donkey with a club. From that, the donkey died. Therefore I say: 'He who meddles in another's jurisdiction...' and so forth. Look, searching for animals is our appointed duty. Let us attend to our own duty. But today there is no need for even that discussion, for we two have an abundance of leftover food.

body.text: damanakaḥ saroṣam āha-katham āhārārthī bhavān kevalaṃ rājānaṃ sevate ? etad ayuktam uktaṃ tvayā | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said angrily: 'What! Does your honor serve the king merely for the sake of food? That is unworthy of you. For—

children.text: suhṛdām upakāra-kāraṇād
children.translated_text: For the sake of benefiting friends,

children.text: dviṣatām apy apakāra-kāraṇāt |
children.translated_text: and for the sake of thwarting enemies,

children.text: nṛpa-saṃśraya iṣyate budhair
children.translated_text: the wise seek the shelter of a king—

children.text: jaṭharaṃ ko na bibharti kevalam // Hit_2.35 //
children.translated_text: who does not fill his belly by himself alone? // Hit_2.35 //

children.text: jīvite yasya jīvanti viprā mitrāṇi bāndhavāḥ |
children.translated_text: He by whose living <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, friends, and kinsmen live—

children.text: saphalaṃ jīvitaṃ tasya ātmārthe ko na jīvati // Hit_2.36 //
children.translated_text: his life is fruitful; who does not live merely for himself? // Hit_2.36 //'

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover—

children.text: yasmin jīvati jīvanti bahavaḥ sa tu jīvatu |
children.translated_text: Let him live by whose living many others live;

children.text: kāko 'pi kiṃ na kurute cañcvā svodara-pūraṇam // Hit_2.37 //
children.translated_text: does not even a crow fill its own belly with its beak? // Hit_2.37 //

children.text: paśya-
children.translated_text: Look—

children.text: pañcabhir yāti dāsatvaṃ purāṇaiḥ ko 'pi mānavaḥ |
children.translated_text: Some man becomes a slave for five <s>purāṇas</s> (ancient coins);

children.text: ko 'pi lakṣaiḥ kṛtī ko 'pi lakṣair api na labhyate // Hit_2.38 //
children.translated_text: some man is valued for lakhs; and some man is not to be had even for lakhs. // Hit_2.38 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And also—

children.text: manuṣya-jātau tulyāyāṃ bhṛtyatvam ati-garhitam |
children.translated_text: In the human species, which is equal (by birth), servitude is most contemptible;

children.text: prathamo yo na tan nāpi sa kiṃ jīvatsu gaṇyate // Hit_2.39 //
children.translated_text: he who is not foremost — is he even counted among the living? // Hit_2.39 //

children.text: tathā coktaṃ-
children.translated_text: And as it is said—

children.text: vāji-vāraṇa-lohānāṃ kāṣṭha-pāṣāṇa-vāsasām |
children.translated_text: Among horses, elephants, and metals, among wood, stone, and garments,

children.text: nārī-puruṣa-toyānām antaraṃ hada-hantaram // Hit_2.40 //
children.translated_text: among women, men, and waters — the difference is vast indeed. // Hit_2.40 //

body.text: tathā hi svalpam apy atiricyate-

children.text: svalpa-snāyu-vasāvaśeṣa-malinaṃ nirmāṃsam apy asthikaṃ
children.translated_text: A dog, having obtained a bone with little sinew, fat, and flesh remaining, soiled,

children.text: śvā labdhvā paritoṣam eti na bhavet tasya kṣudhaḥ śāntaye |
children.translated_text: is satisfied, yet it would not suffice to appease its hunger;

children.text: siṃho jambukam aṅkam āgatam api tyaktvā nihanti dvipaṃ
children.translated_text: a lion, disregarding a jackal that has come within reach, slays an elephant—

children.text: sarvaḥ kṛcchra-gato 'pi vāñchati janaḥ sattvānurūpaṃ phalam // Hit_2.41 //
children.translated_text: everyone, even in difficulty, desires a reward befitting their nature. // Hit_2.41 //

body.translated_text: For even a small amount is surpassed—

body.text: aparaṃ ca, sevya-sevakayor antaraṃ paśya-
body.translated_text: And further, observe the difference between the served and the servant—

children.text: lāṅgūla-cālanam adhaś caraṇāvapātaṃ
children.translated_text: Wagging the tail, falling at the feet,

children.text: bhūmau nipatya vadanodara-darśanaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: dropping to the ground and showing the mouth and belly—

children.text: śvā piṇḍadasya kurute gaja-puṅgavas tu
children.translated_text: a dog does this for one who gives it a morsel, but a lordly elephant

children.text: dhīraṃ vilokayati cāṭu-śataiś ca bhuṅkte // Hit_2.42 //
children.translated_text: gazes calmly and eats only after a hundred coaxing words. // Hit_2.42 //

body.text: kiṃ ca-

children.text: yaj jīvyate kṣaṇam api prathitaṃ manuṣyair
children.translated_text: That life which, even if lived for but a moment, is made famous among men

children.text: vijñāna-vikrama-yaśobhir abhajyamānam |
children.translated_text: through knowledge, valor, and glory, unbroken—

children.text: tan nāma jīvitam iha pravadanti taj-jñāḥ
children.translated_text: that alone the wise call true life here;

children.text: kāko 'pi jīvati cirāya baliṃ ca bhuṅkte // Hit_2.43 //
children.translated_text: a crow too lives long and eats offerings. // Hit_2.43 //

body.translated_text: Moreover—

body.text: aparaṃ ca-

children.text: yo nātmaje na ca gurau na ca bhṛtya-varge
children.translated_text: He who neither toward his offspring, nor toward his teacher, nor toward his servants

children.text: dīne dayāṃ na kurute na ca bandhu-varge |
children.translated_text: shows no compassion toward the wretched, nor toward his own kinsmen —

children.text: kiṃ tasya jīvita-phalena manuṣya-loke
children.translated_text: what is the fruit of that person's life in the world of men?

children.text: kāko 'pi jīvati cirāya baliṃ ca bhuṅkte // Hit_2.44 //
children.translated_text: Even a crow lives long and eats offerings. // Hit_2.44 //

body.translated_text: And further—

body.text: aparam api-

children.text: ahita-hita-vicāra-śūnya-buddheḥ
children.translated_text: For one whose intellect is devoid of discrimination between harmful and beneficial,

children.text: śruti-samayair bahubhir bahiṣkṛtasya |
children.translated_text: who has been ostracized by the many precepts of scripture,

children.text: udara-bharaṇa-mātra-kevalecchoḥ
children.translated_text: whose sole desire is merely filling the belly —

children.text: puruṣa-paśoś ca paśoś ca ko viśeṣaḥ // Hit_2.45 //
children.translated_text: what is the difference between a person-animal and an (actual) animal? // Hit_2.45 //

body.translated_text: And moreover:

body.text: karaṭako brūte-āvāṃ tāvad apradhānau | tadāpy āvayoḥ kim anayā vicāraṇayā |
body.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> says: "We two are, after all, of minor rank. Why then should we concern ourselves with this deliberation?"

body.text: damanako brūte-kiyatā kālenāmātyāḥ pradhānatām apradhānatāṃ vā labhante, yataḥ-
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> says: "In how short a time do ministers attain prominence or fall into insignificance! For —

children.text: na kasyacit kaścid iha svabhāvād
children.translated_text: No one in this world by nature

children.text: bhavaty udāro 'bhimataḥ khalo vā |
children.translated_text: becomes noble, esteemed, or villainous;

children.text: loke gurutvaṃ viparītatāṃ vā
children.translated_text: it is eminence or the opposite in the world —

children.text: sva-ceṣṭitāny eva naraṃ nayanti // Hit_2.46 //
children.translated_text: a man's own deeds alone lead him (to either). // Hit_2.46 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: āropyate śilā śaile yatnena mahatā yathā |
children.translated_text: Just as a boulder is raised to a mountain-top with great effort,

children.text: nipātyate kṣaṇenādhas tathātmā guṇa-doṣayoḥ // Hit_2.47 //
children.translated_text: but is hurled down in an instant — so is the self, through virtues and faults. // Hit_2.47 //

children.text: yāty adho 'dhaḥ vrajaty uccair naraḥ svair eva karmabhiḥ |
children.translated_text: A person sinks lower and lower, or rises high, by his own deeds alone —

children.text: kūpasya khanitā yadvat prākārasyeva kārakaḥ // Hit_2.48 //
children.translated_text: just like the digger of a well and the builder of a rampart. // Hit_2.48 //

body.text: tad bhadram | svayatnāyatto hy ātmā sarvasya |
body.translated_text: So, good sir — the self of everyone depends on one's own effort."

body.text: karaṭako brūte-atha bhavān kiṃ bravīti ?
body.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> says: "So what does your lordship propose?"

body.text: sa āha-ayaṃ tāvat svāmī piṅgalakaḥ kuto 'pi kāraṇāt sa-cakitaḥ parivṛtyopaviṣṭaḥ |
body.translated_text: He (<s>Damanaka</s>) says: "This master of ours, <s>Piṅgalaka</s>, for some reason has turned back in alarm and is sitting (idle)."

children.text: karaṭako brūte-
children.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> says:

children.text: udīrito 'rthaḥ paśunāpi gṛhyate hayāś ca nāgāś ca vahanti coditāḥ |
children.translated_text: "An expressed meaning is grasped even by an animal; horses and elephants carry loads when urged;

children.text: anuktam apy ūhati paṇḍito janaḥ pareṅgita-jñāna-phalā hi buddhayaḥ // Hit_2.49 //
children.translated_text: but a wise person understands even what is left unspoken — for intelligent minds bear the fruit of knowing others' gestures. // Hit_2.49 //

children.text: ākāra-riṅgatair gatyā ceṣṭayā bhāṣaṇena ca |
children.translated_text: By the involuntary movements of the body, by gait, by gestures, by speech,

children.text: netra-vaktra-vikāreṇa lakṣyate'ntargataṃ manaḥ // Hit_2.50 //
children.translated_text: and by the changes of the eyes and face — the inner mind is perceived. // Hit_2.50 //"

body.text: atra bhaya-prastāve prajñā-balenāham enaṃ svāminam ātmīyaṃ kariṣyāmi | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: "On this occasion of fear, I shall, by the power of my intellect, make this master my own man. For —

children.text: prastāva-sadṛśaṃ vākyaṃ sad-bhāva-sadṛśaṃ priyam |
children.translated_text: Words suited to the occasion, affection suited to one's true feelings,

children.text: ātma-śakti-samaṃ kopaṃ yo jānāti sa paṇḍitaḥ // Hit_2.51 //
children.translated_text: anger proportionate to one's own strength — he who knows these is a wise man. // Hit_2.51 //"

body.text: karaṭako brūte-sakhe tvaṃ sevānabhijñaḥ | paśya-
body.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> says: "Friend, you are inexperienced in service. Look —

children.text: anāhūto viśed yas tu apṛṣṭo bahu bhāṣate |
children.translated_text: He who enters uninvited, who speaks much when unasked,

children.text: ātmānaṃ manyate prītaṃ bhū-pālasya sa durmatiḥ // Hit_2.52 //
children.translated_text: who considers himself beloved (by the king) — that fool (is doomed) before the sovereign. // Hit_2.52 //"

body.text: damanako brūte-bhadra ! katham ahaṃ sevānabhijñaḥ ? paśya-
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> says: "Good sir! How am I inexperienced in service? Look —

children.text: kim apy asti svabhāvena sundaraṃ vāpy asundaram |
children.translated_text: Is anything by nature beautiful or ugly?

children.text: yad eva rocate yasmai bhavet tat tasya sundaram // Hit_2.53 //
children.translated_text: Whatever pleases whomever — that is beautiful for that person. // Hit_2.53 //

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: For —

children.text: yasya yasya hi yo bhāvas tena tena hi taṃ naram |
children.translated_text: Whatever disposition a person has — by entering into that very disposition,

children.text: anupraviśya medhāvī kṣipram ātma-vaśaṃ nayet // Hit_2.54 //
children.translated_text: a clever man may quickly bring that person under his control. // Hit_2.54 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And furthermore:

children.text: ko 'trety aham iti brūyāt samyag ādeśayeti ca |
children.translated_text: 'Who is there?' — he should answer 'I am here'; and (when told) 'give proper directions,' (he should obey);

children.text: ājñām avitathāṃ kuryād yathā-śakti mahīpateḥ // Hit_2.55 //
children.translated_text: he should carry out the king's commands faithfully, to the best of his ability. // Hit_2.55 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: alpecchur dhṛtimān prājñaś chāyevānugataḥ sadā |
children.translated_text: Of few desires, steadfast, wise, always following like a shadow,

children.text: ādiṣṭo na vikalpeta sa rāja-vasatiṃ vaset // Hit_2.56 //
children.translated_text: when commanded, he should not waver — such a person may dwell in the king's court. // Hit_2.56 //"

body.text: karaṭako brūte-kadācit tvām anavasara-praveśād avagamyate svāmī |
body.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> says: "Perhaps the master will discover you through your untimely entry."

body.text: sa cāha-astv evam | tathāpy anujīvinā svāmi-sāṃnidhyam avaśyaṃ karaṇīyam |

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: For —

children.text: doṣa-bhīter anārambhas tat kāpuruṣa-lakṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: Not undertaking action out of fear of failure — that is the mark of a coward.

children.text: kair ajīrṇa-bhayād bhrātar bhojanaṃ parihīyate // Hit_2.57 //
children.translated_text: Brother, who gives up eating out of fear of indigestion? // Hit_2.57 //

body.translated_text: He (<s>Damanaka</s>) says: "Let it be so. Still, a dependent must always be in the presence of the master.

children.text: paśya-
children.translated_text: Look —

children.text: āsannam eva nṛpatir bhajate manuṣyaṃ vidyā-vihīnam akulīnam asaṃstutaṃ vā |
children.translated_text: The king favors the person who is near him — even one devoid of learning, of low birth, or unintroduced;

children.text: prāyeṇa bhūmi-patayaḥ pramadā-latāś ca yaḥ pārśvato vasati taṃ pariveṣṭayanti // Hit_2.58 //
children.translated_text: for kings and creeper-like women generally embrace whoever dwells at their side. // Hit_2.58 //"

body.text: karaṭako brūte-atha tatra gatvā kiṃ vakṣyati bhavān |
body.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> says: "And having gone there, what will your lordship say?"

body.text: sa āha-śṛṇu ! kim anurakto virakto vā mayi svāmīti jñāsyāmi |
body.translated_text: He says: "Listen! I shall find out whether the master is attached to me or detached from me."

body.text: karaṭako brūte-kiṃ taj jñāna-lakṣaṇam |
body.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> says: "What is the mark of that knowledge?"

children.text: damanako brūte-śṛṇu-
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> says: "Listen —

children.text: dūrād avekṣaṇaṃ hāsaḥ sampraśneṣv ādaro bhṛśam |
children.translated_text: Looking from afar, smiling, showing great attentiveness in inquiries,

children.text: parokṣe'pi guṇa-ślāghā smaraṇaṃ priya-vastuṣu // Hit_2.59 //
children.translated_text: praising qualities even in one's absence, remembering with regard to cherished things, // Hit_2.59 //

children.text: asevake cānuraktir dānaṃ sa-priya-bhāṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: affection toward one who is not (currently) in service, giving accompanied by kind words —

children.text: anuraktasya cihnāni doṣe'pi guṇa-saṅgrahaḥ // Hit_2.60 //
children.translated_text: these are the signs of attachment; (and) seeing merit even in faults. // Hit_2.60 //

children.text: anyac ca--
children.translated_text: And further:

children.text: kāla-yāpanam āśānāṃ vardhanaṃ phala-khaṇḍanam |
children.translated_text: Wasting time, raising hopes, thwarting results —

children.text: virakteśvara-cihnāni jānīyān matimān naraḥ // Hit_2.61 //
children.translated_text: a wise person should recognize these as the signs of a detached master. // Hit_2.61 //"

body.text: etaj jñātvā yathā cāyaṃ mamāyatto bhaviṣyati | tathā vadiṣyāmi |
body.translated_text: "Having ascertained this, I shall speak in such a way that he will be in my power."

children.text: apāyasaṃ darśanajāṃ vipattim
children.translated_text: "The ruin arising from hazards and the success arising from

children.text: upāya-sandarśana-jāṃ ca siddhim |
children.translated_text: the demonstration of remedies —

children.text: medhāvino nīti-vidhi-prayuktāṃ
children.translated_text: the wise, skilled in the methods of statecraft,

children.text: puraḥ sphurantīm iva darśayanti // Hit_2.62 //
children.translated_text: display these as if they were shining before them. // Hit_2.62 //"

body.text: karaṭako brūte-tathāpy aprāpte prastāve na vaktum arhasi, yataḥ-
body.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> says: "Still, you should not speak when the occasion has not arrived. For —

children.text: aprāpta-kālaṃ vacanaṃ bṛhaspatir api bruvan |
children.translated_text: Even <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, if he speaks words at an inopportune time,

children.text: labhate buddhy-avajñānam avamānaṃ ca bhārata // Hit_2.63 //
children.translated_text: receives contempt and disrespect for his intellect, O <s>Bhārata</s>. // Hit_2.63 //"

body.text: damanako brūte-mitra ! mā bhaiṣīḥ ! nāham aprāptāvasaraṃ vacanaṃ vadiṣyāmi | yataḥ-

children.text: āpady unmārga-gamane kārya-kālātyayeṣu ca |
children.translated_text: In times of calamity, when (the king) takes the wrong path, when the proper time for action is passing —

children.text: apṛṣṭo 'pi hitānveṣī brūyāt kalyāṇa-bhāṣitam // Hit_2.64 //
children.translated_text: even unasked, one who seeks the good should speak words of welfare. // Hit_2.64 //

body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> says: "Friend! Fear not! I shall not speak at an inopportune time. For —

body.text: yadi ca prāptāvasareṇāpi mayā mantro na vaktavyas tadā mantritvam eva mamānupapannam | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: And if even at the right time I am not to offer counsel, then my very status as a counselor is untenable. For —

children.text: kalpayati yena vṛttiṃ yena ca loke praśasyate |
children.translated_text: The quality by which one earns one's livelihood and by which one is praised in the world —

children.text: sa guṇas tena guṇinā rakṣyaḥ saṃvardhanīyaś ca // Hit_2.65 //
children.translated_text: that quality should be protected and nurtured by the person who possesses it. // Hit_2.65 //"

body.text: tad bhadra ! anujānīhi mām | gacchāmi |
body.translated_text: "So, good sir! Give me leave. I am going."

body.text: karaṭako brūte-śubham astu | śivās te panthānaḥ | yathābhilaṣitam anuṣṭhīyatām iti |
body.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> says: "May there be auspiciousness! May your paths be blessed! Let your desire be accomplished."

body.text: tato damanako vismita iva piṅgalaka-samīpaṃ gataḥ | atha dūrād eva sādaraṃ rājñā praveśitaḥ sāṣṭāṅga-praṇipātaṃ praṇipatyopaviṣṭaḥ | rājāha-cirād dṛṣṭo 'si |
body.translated_text: Then <s>Damanaka</s>, assuming an air of wonder, went to the presence of <s>Piṅgalaka</s>. And from afar, the king respectfully admitted him. Having made a full prostration, he sat down. The king said: "It has been long since you were seen."

body.text: damanako brūte-yadyapi mayā sevakena śrīmad-devapādānāṃ na kiṃcit prayojanam asti, tathāpi prāpta-kālam anujīvinā sāṃnidhyam avaśyaṃ kartavyam ity āgato 'smi | kiṃ ca-
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> says: "Although I, a servant, am of no use to the glorious royal feet, still, a dependent must always present himself at the proper time — hence I have come. Moreover —

children.text: dantasya nirgharṣaṇakena rājan
children.translated_text: O king, even with a stick for cleaning the teeth,

children.text: karṇasya kaṇḍūyanakena vāpi |
children.translated_text: or with a (stick) for scratching the ear,

children.text: tṛṇena kāryaṃ bhavatīśvarāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: a blade of grass serves the needs of the mighty —

children.text: kim aṅga-vāk-pāṇi-matā nareṇa // Hit_2.66 //
children.translated_text: how much more, then, a man endowed with limbs, speech, and hands! // Hit_2.66 //

body.text: yadyapi cireṇāvadhīritasya deva-pādair me buddhi-nāśaḥ śakyate, tad api na śaṅkanīyam | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Although my intellect may have been destroyed by long neglect by the royal feet, still it should not be doubted. For —

children.text: kadarthitasyāpi ca dhairya-vṛtter
children.translated_text: Even for one who has been despised, if he is endowed with steadfastness of character,

children.text: buddher vināśo nahi śaṅkanīyaḥ |
children.translated_text: the destruction of his intellect should not be suspected;

children.text: adhaḥ-kṛtasyāpi tanūnapāto
children.translated_text: for fire, even when turned upside down,

children.text: nādhaḥ śikhā yāti kadācid eva // Hit_2.67 //
children.translated_text: never lets its flame go downward. // Hit_2.67 //

body.text: deva ! tat sarvathā viśeṣajñena svāminā bhavitavyam | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: O lord! Therefore, the master must in all ways be a discerner of merit. For —

children.text: maṇir luṭhati pādeṣu kācaḥ śirasi dhāryate |
children.translated_text: A gem rolls at the feet while glass is worn on the head;

children.text: yathaivāste tathaivāstāṃ kācaḥ kāco maṇir maṇiḥ // Hit_2.68 //
children.translated_text: let each remain as it is — glass is glass and a gem is a gem. // Hit_2.68 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And further:

children.text: nirviśeṣo yadā rājā samaṃ sarveṣu vartate |
children.translated_text: When the king makes no distinction and treats everyone equally,

children.text: tadodyama-samarthānām utsāhaḥ parihīyate // Hit_2.69 //
children.translated_text: then the enthusiasm of those capable of great effort is diminished. // Hit_2.69 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: trividhāḥ puruṣā rājann uttamādhama-madhyamāḥ |
children.translated_text: O king, there are three kinds of men — superior, inferior, and middling;

children.text: niyojayet tathaivaitāṃs trividheṣv eva karmasu // Hit_2.70 //
children.translated_text: one should employ them accordingly in three kinds of tasks. // Hit_2.70 //

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: For:

children.text: sthāna eva nijyojyante bhṛtyāś cābharaṇāni ca |
children.translated_text: Servants and ornaments should be placed in their proper positions;

children.text: nahi cūḍāmaṇiḥ pāde nūpuraṃ śirasā kṛtam // Hit_2.71 //
children.translated_text: for the crest-jewel is not placed on the foot, nor the anklet on the head. // Hit_2.71 //

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: Furthermore:

children.text: kanaka-bhūṣaṇa-saṅgrahaṇocito yadi maṇis trapuṇi praṇidhīyate |
children.translated_text: If a gem worthy of being set in a collection of gold ornaments is set in tin,

children.text: na sa virauti na cāpi na śobhate bhavati yojayitur vacanīyatā // Hit_2.72 //
children.translated_text: it neither shines nor sparkles nor is beautiful — the fault lies with the one who placed it. // Hit_2.72 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: mukuṭe ropitā kācaś caraṇābharaṇe maṇiḥ |
children.translated_text: Glass set in the crown, a gem in the foot-ornament —

children.text: nahi doṣo maṇer asti kintu sādhor avijñatā // Hit_2.73 //
children.translated_text: the fault does not lie with the gem, but rather with the ignorance of the jeweler. // Hit_2.73 //

children.text: paśya-
children.translated_text: Look —

children.text: buddhimān anurakto 'yam ayaṃ śūra ito bhayam |
children.translated_text: 'This one is intelligent and loyal,' 'this one is brave,' 'from this quarter comes danger' —

children.text: iti bhṛtya-vicārajño bhṛtyair āpūryate nṛpaḥ // Hit_2.74 //
children.translated_text: a king who knows how to assess his servants is surrounded by (good) servants. // Hit_2.74 //

children.text: tathā hi-
children.translated_text: For thus it is:

children.text: aśvaḥ śastraṃ śāstraṃ vīṇā vāṇī naraś ca nārī ca |
children.translated_text: A horse, a weapon, a treatise, a lute, speech, a man, and a woman —

children.text: puruṣa-viśeṣaṃ prāptā bhavanty ayogyāś ca yogyāś ca // Hit_2.75 //
children.translated_text: when they come under the charge of the right person, they become either unfit or fit. // Hit_2.75 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And further:

children.text: kiṃ bhaktenāsamarthena kiṃ śaktenāpakāriṇā |
children.translated_text: What use is a devotee who is incapable? What use is a capable person who does harm?

children.text: bhaktaṃ śaktaṃ ca māṃ rājan nāvajñātuṃ tvam arhasi // Hit_2.76 //
children.translated_text: O king, you should not disdain me — one who is both devoted and capable. // Hit_2.76 //

body.text: yataḥ-

children.text: avajñānād rājño bhavati mati-hīnaḥ parijanas
children.translated_text: When the king shows contempt, the retinue becomes demoralized;

children.text: tatas tat-prāmāṇyād bhavati na samīpe budha-janaḥ |
children.translated_text: consequently, because of this precedent, wise men no longer come near (the court);

children.text: budhais tyakte rājye na hi bhavati nītir guṇavatī
children.translated_text: when wise men have abandoned the kingdom, there is no virtuous statecraft;

children.text: vipannāyāṃ nītau sakalam avaśaṃ sīdati jagat // Hit_2.77 //
children.translated_text: and when statecraft has failed, the entire world sinks helplessly. // Hit_2.77 //

body.translated_text: For:

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: janaṃ janapadā nityam arcayanti nṛpārcitam |
children.translated_text: The people of a country always honor a person who is honored by the king;

children.text: nṛpeṇāvamato yas tu sa sarvair avamanyate // Hit_2.78 //
children.translated_text: but one who is disrespected by the king is disrespected by all. // Hit_2.78 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: bālād api gṛhītavyaṃ yuktam uktaṃ manīṣibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: The wise have said that even from a child, a well-reasoned statement should be accepted;

children.text: raver aviṣaye kiṃ na pradīpasya prakāśanam // Hit_2.79 //
children.translated_text: in a place where the sun does not reach, is a lamp's light of no use? // Hit_2.79 //"

body.text: piṅgalako 'vadat-bhadra damanaka ! kim etat ? tvam asmadīya-pradhānāmātya-putra iyantaṃ kālaṃ yāvat kuto 'pi khala-vākyān nāgato 'si | idānīṃ yathābhimataṃ brūhi |
body.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said: "Good <s>Damanaka</s>! What is this? You are the son of our chief minister, and for all this time, due to some slanderous words, you have not come. Now speak as you wish."

body.text: damanako brūte-deva ! pṛcchāmi kiṃcit | ucyatām | udakārthī svāmī pānīyam apītvā kim iti vismita iva tiṣṭhati |
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> says: "O lord! I ask something — please answer. The master came here seeking water — but without drinking the water, why does he stand as if bewildered?"

body.text: piṅgalako 'vadat-bhadram uktaṃ tvayā | kintv etad rahasyaṃ vaktuṃ kācid viśvāsa-bhūmir nāsti | tathāpi nibhṛtaṃ kṛtvā kathayāmi | śṛṇu, samprati vanam idam apūrva-sattvādhiṣṭhitam ato 'smākaṃ tyājyam | anena hetunā vismito 'smi | tathā ca śruto mayāpi mahān apūrva-śabdaḥ | śabdānurūpeṇāsya prāṇino mahatā balena bhavitavyam |
body.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said: "You have spoken well. But this is a secret, and there is no ground of trust on which to speak it. Still, having ensured secrecy, I will tell you. Listen: at present, this forest has been occupied by an unprecedented creature — therefore we must abandon it. It is for this reason that I am bewildered. I have heard a great and unprecedented sound. From the sound, this creature must possess great strength."

body.text: damanako brūte-deva ! asti tāvad ayaṃ mahān bhaya-hetuḥ | sa śabdo 'syābhir apy ākarṇitaḥ | kintu sa kiṃ mantrī yaḥ prathamaṃ bhūmi-tyāgaṃ paścād yuddhaṃ copaviśati asmin kārya-sandehe bhṛtyānām upayoga eva jñātavyaḥ | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> says: "O lord! This is indeed a great cause of fear. That sound has been heard by us too. But what sort of counselor is he who first considers abandoning the territory and then (considers) battle? In this doubtful situation, the usefulness of servants should be ascertained. For —

children.text: bandhu-strī-bhṛtya-vargasya buddheḥ sattvasya cātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: It is on the touchstone of adversity that a man knows the true worth

children.text: āpan-nikaṣa-pāṣāṇe naro jānāti sāratām // Hit_2.80 //
children.translated_text: of his kinsmen, wife, servants, intellect, and his own courage. // Hit_2.80 //"

body.text: siṃho brūte-bhadra ! mahatī śaṅkā māṃ bādhate |
body.translated_text: The lion says: "Good sir! A great apprehension troubles me."

body.text: damanakaḥ punar āha svagatam-anyathā rājya-sukhaṃ parityajya sthānāntaraṃ gantuṃ kathaṃ māṃ sambhāṣase ? prakāśaṃ brūte-deva ! yāvad ahaṃ jīvāmi tāvad bhayaṃ na kartavyam | kintu karaṭakādayo 'py āśvāsyantāṃ yasmād āpat-pratīkāra-kāle durlabhah puruṣa-samavāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> says again, to himself: "Otherwise, why would you speak to me about abandoning the comforts of the kingdom and going to another place?" Aloud he says: "O lord! As long as I am alive, there is nothing to fear. But let <s>Karaṭaka</s> and the others also be reassured, for in times of countering danger, a gathering of capable men is hard to obtain."

body.text: tatas tau damanaka-karaṭakau rājñā sarvasvenāpi pūjitau bhaya-pratīkāraṃ pratijñāya calitau | karaṭako gacchan damanakam āha-sakhe ! kiṃ śaktya-pratīkāro bhaya-hetur aśakya-pratīkāro veti na jñātvā bhayopaśamaṃ pratijñāya katham ayaṃ mahā-prasādo gṛhītaḥ ? yato 'nupakurvāṇo na kasyāpy upāyanaṃ gṛhṇīyād viśeṣato rājñaḥ | paśya-

children.text: yasya prasāde padmāste vijayaś ca parākrame |
children.translated_text: He in whose favor resides <s>Padmā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), and in whose valor resides victory,

children.text: mṛtyuś ca vasati krodhe sarva-tejomayo hi saḥ // Hit_2.81 //
children.translated_text: and in whose anger resides death — for he is entirely made of splendor. // Hit_2.81 //

body.translated_text: Then those two, <s>Damanaka</s> and <s>Karaṭaka</s>, having been honored by the king with every kind of wealth, pledged to counter the danger and set out. While walking, <s>Karaṭaka</s> said to <s>Damanaka</s>: "Friend! Without knowing whether this cause of fear can be countered or cannot be countered, how have you pledged to allay the fear and accepted this great favor? For one who renders no service should not accept a gift from anyone, especially from a king. Look —

children.text: tathā hi-
children.translated_text: For thus it is:

children.text: bālo 'pi nāvamantavyo manuṣya iti bhūmipaḥ |
children.translated_text: A king, even if young, should not be disregarded as merely a human being;

children.text: mahatī devatā hy eṣā nara-rūpeṇa tiṣṭhati // Hit_2.82 //
children.translated_text: for he is a great deity standing in human form. // Hit_2.82 //

body.text: damanako vihasyāha-mitra ! tūṣṇīm āsyatām | jñātaṃ mayā bhaya-kāraṇam | balīvarda-narditaṃ tat | vṛṣabhāś cāsmākam api bhakṣyāḥ | kiṃ punaḥ siṃhasya |
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> laughed and said—Friend! Be silent. I have understood the cause of fear. That is the bellowing of a bull. And bulls are food even for the likes of us, how much more so for a lion!

body.text: karaṭako brūte-yady evaṃ tadā kim punaḥ svāmi-trāsas tatraiva kim iti nāpanītaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> says—If so, then why was the master's fear not removed right there?

body.text: damanako brūte-yadi svāmi-trāsas tatraiva mucyate tadā katham ayaṃ mahā-prasāda-lābhaḥ syāt | aparaṃ ca-
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> says—If the master's fear is relieved right there, then how would this great favor be obtained? And moreover—

children.text: nirapekṣo na kartavyo bhṛtyai svāmī kadācana |
children.translated_text: A servant should never make the master indifferent toward him;

children.text: nirapekṣaṃ prabhuṃ kṛtvā bhṛtyaḥ syād dadhi-karṇavat // Hit_2.83 //
children.translated_text: Having made the lord indifferent, the servant would end up like <s>Dadhikarṇa</s> (Curd-Ear). // Hit_2.83 //

body.text: karaṭakaḥ pṛcchati--katham etat ?
body.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> asks—How is that?

body.text: damanakaḥ kathayati-
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> narrates—

body.text: kathā 3
body.translated_text: Story 3

body.text: asty uttara-pathe'rbudaśikhara-nāmni parvate durdānto nāma mahā-vikramaḥ siṃhaḥ | tasya parvata-kandaram adhiśayānasya kesarāgraṃ kaścin mūṣikaḥ pratyahaṃ chinatti | tataḥ kesarāgraṃ lūnaṃ dṛṣṭvā kupito vivarāntargataṃ mūṣikam alabhamāno 'cintayat-
body.translated_text: In the northern country, on a mountain called <s>Arbudaśikhara</s>, there lived a lion of great valor named <s>Durdānta</s>. A certain mouse would daily gnaw the tips of his mane as he slept in a mountain cave. Then, seeing the mane-tips cut, he became angry but unable to catch the mouse that had entered its hole, he thought—

children.text: kṣudra-śatrur bhaved yas tu vikramān naiva labhyate |
children.translated_text: When an enemy is small and cannot be caught by valor,

children.text: tam āhantuṃ puraskāryaḥ sadṛśas tasya sainikaḥ // Hit_2.84 //
children.translated_text: To strike him, one must employ a soldier equal to him. // Hit_2.84 //

body.text: ity ālocya tena grāmaṃ gatvā viśvāsaṃ kṛtvā dadhikarṇa-nāmā biḍālo yatnevānīya māṃsāhāraṃ dattvā sva-kandare sthāpitaḥ | anantaraṃ tad-bhayān mūṣiko 'pi vilān na niḥsarati | tenāsau siṃho 'kṣata-keśaraḥ sukhaṃ svapiti | mūṣika-śabdaṃ yadā yadā śṛṇoti, tadā tadā māṃsāhāra-dānena taṃ biḍālaṃ saṃvardhayati |
body.translated_text: Having thus deliberated, he went to the village, gained trust, and with effort brought a cat named <s>Dadhikarṇa</s>, gave him meat to eat, and stationed him in his own cave. Thereupon, out of fear of the cat, the mouse too did not come out of the hole; and so that lion slept comfortably with his mane unharmed. Whenever he heard the sound of the mouse, he would nourish that cat by giving him meat.

children.text: ājñā-bhaṅgo narendrāṇāṃ brāhmaṇānām anādaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Disobedience of the commands of kings, disrespect toward <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,

children.text: pṛthak śayyā ca nārīṇām aśastra-vihito vadhaḥ // Hit_2.85 //
children.translated_text: And separate beds for wives—these are death without weapons. // Hit_2.85 //

body.text: tato deśa-vyavahārānabhijñaḥ saṃjīvakaḥ sabhayam upasṛtya sāṣṭāṅga-pātaṃ karaṭakaṃ praṇatavān | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: Then <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>, unfamiliar with the customs of the land, approached fearfully and prostrated himself before <s>Karaṭaka</s> with a full prostration. As it is said—

children.text: matir eva balād garīyasī yad-abhāve kariṇām iyaṃ daśā |
children.translated_text: Intelligence is indeed greater than strength—in its absence, such is the condition of elephants;

children.text: iti ghoṣayatīva ḍiṇḍimaḥ kariṇo hastipakāhataḥ kvaṇan // Hit_2.86 //
children.translated_text: This the kettledrum seems to proclaim, resounding when struck by the elephant-driver upon the elephant. // Hit_2.86 //

body.text: atha saṃjīvakaḥ sāśaṅkam āha-senāpate ! kiṃ mayā kartavyam | tad abhidhīyatām |
body.translated_text: Then <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> said apprehensively—O general! What should I do? Let it be stated.

body.text: karaṭako brūte-vṛṣabha ! atra kānane tiṣṭhasi | asmad-deva-pādāravindaṃ praṇaya |
body.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> says—O bull! Stay in this forest. Pay homage at the lotus feet of our lord.

body.text: saṃjīvako brūte-tad-abhaya-vācaṃ me yaccha | gacchāmi |
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> says—Then give me an assurance of safety. I shall go.

body.text: karaṭako brūte-śṛṇu re balīvarda ! alam anayā śaṅkayā | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> says—Listen, O bull! Enough of this apprehension! For—

children.text: prativācam adatta keśavaḥ śapamānāya na cedi-bhūbhuje |
children.translated_text: <s>Keśava</s> did not give a reply to the <s>Cedi</s> king who was cursing him;

children.text: anuhuṅkurute ghana-dhvaniṃ na hi gomāyu-rutāni kesarī // Hit_2.87 //
children.translated_text: A lion does not echo the thunderclap—much less the howling of jackals. // Hit_2.87 //

body.text: anyac ca-

children.text: tṛṇāni nonmūlayati prabhañjano
children.translated_text: The storm does not uproot the grasses

children.text: mṛdūni nīcaiḥ praṇalāni sarvataḥ |
children.translated_text: that are soft, low, and bending on all sides;

children.text: samucchritān eva tarūn prabādhate
children.translated_text: It assails only the lofty trees—

children.text: mahān mahaty eva karoti vikramam // Hit_2.88 //
children.translated_text: the great exerts his power only against the great. // Hit_2.88 //

body.translated_text: And further—

body.text: tatas tau saṃjīvakaṃ kiyad dūre saṃsthāpya piṅgalaka-samīpaṃ gatau | tato rājā sādaram avalokitau praṇamyopaviṣṭau | rājāha-tvayā sa dṛṣṭaḥ ?
body.translated_text: Then those two stationed <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> at some distance and went to <s>Piṅgalaka</s>'s presence. The king looked at them with regard; they bowed and sat down. The king said—Did you see him?

body.text: damanako brūte-deva ! dṛṣṭaḥ | kintu yad devena jñātaṃ tat tathā | mahān evāsau devaṃ draṣṭum icchati | kintu mahābalo 'sau tataḥ sajjībhūyopaviśya dṛśyatām | śabda-mātrād eva na bhetavyam | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> says—Lord! I saw him. But what the lord surmised is indeed so. He is truly great and wishes to see the lord. But he is very powerful, so be seated with readiness and observe. One should not be afraid merely from a sound. As it is said—

children.text: śabda-mātrān na bhetavyam ajñātvā śabda-kāraṇam |
children.translated_text: One should not fear from mere sound without knowing the cause of the sound;

children.text: śabda-hetuṃ parijñāya kuṭṭanī gauravaṃ gatā // Hit_2.89 //
children.translated_text: Having ascertained the source of the sound, the procuress <s>Kuṭṭanī</s> gained great respect. // Hit_2.89 //

body.text: rājāha-katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The king said—How is that?

body.text: damanakaḥ kathayati---
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> narrates—

body.text: kathā 4
body.translated_text: Story 4

body.text:
asti śrī-parvata-madhye brahmapurākhyaṃ nagaram | tac-chikhara-pradeśe ghaṇṭākarṇo nāma rākṣasaḥ prativasatīti jana-pravādaḥ śrūyate | ekadā ghaṇṭām ādāya palāyamānaḥ kaścic cauro vyāghreṇa vyāpāditaḥ | tat-pāṇi-patitā ghaṇṭā vānaraiḥ prāptā | vānarās tāṃ ghaṇṭām anukṣaṇaṃ vādayanti | tato nagara-janaiḥ sa manuṣyaḥ khādito dṛṣṭaḥ pratikṣaṇaṃ ghaṇṭā-ravaś ca śrūyate | anantaraṃ ghaṇṭākarṇaḥ kupito manuṣyān khādati ghaṇṭāṃ ca vādayatīty uktvā sarve janā nagarāt palāyitāḥ | tataḥ karālayā nāma kuṭṭanyā vimṛśyānavaro 'yaṃ ghaṇṭā-nādaḥ | tat kiṃ markaṭā ghaṇṭāṃ vādayantīti svayaṃ vijñāya rājā vijñāpitaḥ-deva ! yadi kiyad dhanopakṣayaḥ kriyate, tadāham
enaṃ ghaṇṭākarṇaṃ sādhayāmi |
body.translated_text: In the midst of <s>Śrīparvata</s>, there is a city called <s>Brahmapura</s>. On its mountain peak, a <s>rākṣasa</s> (demon) named <s>Ghaṇṭākarṇa</s> (Bell-Ear) dwells—so goes the popular legend. Once, a certain thief who was fleeing with a bell was killed by a tiger. The bell that fell from his hand was obtained by monkeys. The monkeys kept ringing that bell incessantly. Then the townspeople saw the man eaten and constantly heard the sound of the bell. Thereafter, saying that <s>Ghaṇṭākarṇa</s> in his anger devours humans and rings the bell, all the people fled from the city. Then a procuress named <s>Karālā</s>, having reflected that this bell-sound is nothing remarkable—could it be that monkeys are ringing the bell?—ascertained this herself and informed the king: Lord! If some expenditure of wealth is made, then I shall subdue this <s>Ghaṇṭākarṇa</s>.

body.text: tato rājā tasyai dhanaṃ dattam | kuṭṭanyā maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā tatra gaṇeśādi-pūjā-gauravaṃ darśayitvā svayaṃ vānara-priya-phalāny ādāya vanaṃ praviśya phalāny ākīrṇāni | tato ghaṇṭāṃ parityajya vānarāḥ phalāsaktā babhūvuḥ | kuṭṭanī ca ghaṇṭāṃ gṛhītvā nagaram āgatā sarva-jana-pūjyābhavat | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-śabda-mātrān na bhetavyam ity ādi | tataḥ saṃjīvakam ānīya darśanaṃ kāritavantau | paścāt tatraiva parama-prītyā nivasati |
body.translated_text: Then the king gave her wealth. The procuress drew a circle, displayed the worship of <s>Gaṇeśa</s> and other deities with great ceremony, and herself entering the forest with fruits dear to monkeys, scattered them about. Then the monkeys abandoned the bell and became attached to the fruits. The procuress took the bell and returned to the city, where she became honored by all the people. Therefore I say—One should not fear from mere sound, and so on. Then they brought <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> and made him have an audience. Thereafter he dwelt there with the greatest affection.
[Section break]

body.text: atha kadācit tasya siṃhasya bhrātā stabdha-karṇa-nāmā siṃhaḥ samāgataḥ | tasyātithyaṃ kṛtvā siṃham upaveśya piṅgalakas tad-āhārāya paśuṃ hantuṃ calitaḥ | atrāntare saṃjīvako vadati-deva ! adya hata-mṛgāṇāṃ māṃsāni kva ?
body.translated_text: Now once, a lion named <s>Stabdhakarṇa</s> (Stiff-Ear), the brother of that lion, arrived. Having extended hospitality to him and seated the lion, <s>Piṅgalaka</s> set out to kill an animal for his food. In the meanwhile <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> says—Lord! Where is the meat of the animals killed today?

body.text: rājāha-damanaka-karaṭakau jānītaḥ |
body.translated_text: The king said—<s>Damanaka</s> and <s>Karaṭaka</s> know.

body.text: saṃjīvako brūte-jñāyatāṃ kim asti nāsti vā ?
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> says—Let it be found out whether there is any or not.

body.text: siṃho vimṛśyāha-nāsty eva tat |
body.translated_text: The lion, having considered, said—There is none indeed.

body.text: saṃjīvako brūte-katham etāvan māṃsaṃ tābhyāṃ khāditam ?
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> says—How was so much meat consumed by those two?

body.text: rājāha-khāditaṃ vyayitam avadhīritaṃ ca | pratyaham eṣa kramaḥ |
body.translated_text: The king said—Eaten, wasted, and squandered. This is the daily routine.

body.text: saṃjīvako brūte-kathaṃ śrīmad-deva-pādānāṃ agocareṇaiva kriyate ?
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> says—How is this done without the knowledge of the illustrious lord?

body.text: rājāha-madīyāgocareṇaiva kriyate |
body.translated_text: The king said—It is indeed done without my knowledge.

body.text: atha saṃjīvako brūte-naitad ucitam | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: Then <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> says—This is not proper. As it is said—

children.text: nānivedya prakurvīta bhartuḥ kiṃcid api svayam |
children.translated_text: A servant should not do anything on his own without reporting to the master,

children.text: kāryam āpat-pratīkārād anyatra jagatī-pate // Hit_2.90 //
children.translated_text: Except in the case of remedying an emergency, O lord of the earth. // Hit_2.90 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And further—

children.text: kamaṇḍalūpamo 'mātyas tanu-tyāgī bahu-grahaḥ |
children.translated_text: A minister who is like a water-pot—giving little, taking much—

children.text: nṛpate kiṅkṣaṇo mūrkho daridraḥ kiṃvarāṭakaḥ // Hit_2.91 //
children.translated_text: A fool dependent on the king, and a pauper who is a petty official. // Hit_2.91 //

children.text: sa hy amātyaḥ sadā śreyān kākinīṃ yaḥ pravardhayet |
children.translated_text: That minister is always beneficial who increases even a single <s>kākinī</s> (small coin);

children.text: koṣaḥ koṣavataḥ prāṇāḥ prāṇāḥ prāṇā na bhūpateḥ // Hit_2.92 //
children.translated_text: The treasury is the life-breath of one who has a treasury; the life-breath is not the life-breath of a king. // Hit_2.92 //

children.text: kiṃ cārthair na kulācāraiḥ sevatām eti pūruṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: Does a man not gain respect through wealth rather than through family customs?

children.text: dhana-hīnaḥ sva-patnyāpi tyajyate kiṃ punaḥ paraiḥ // Hit_2.93 //
children.translated_text: One bereft of wealth is abandoned even by his own wife, how much more by others! // Hit_2.93 //

body.text: etac ca rājñaḥ pradhānaṃ dūṣaṇam-
body.translated_text: And this is the chief fault of a king—

children.text: ativyayo 'napekṣā ca tathārjanam adharmataḥ |
children.translated_text: Excessive expenditure, carelessness, and acquisition through unrighteousness,

children.text: moṣaṇaṃ dūra-saṃsthānāṃ koṣa-vyasanam ucyate // Hit_2.94 //
children.translated_text: Plundering of those stationed far away—these are called the afflictions of the treasury. // Hit_2.94 //

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: For—

children.text: kṣipram āyatam anālocya vyayamānaḥ sva-vāñchayā |
children.translated_text: One who spends without considering the income that quickly arrives, driven by his own desires,

children.text: parikṣīyata evāsau dhanī vaiśravaṇopamaḥ // Hit_2.95 //
children.translated_text: Even if wealthy as <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (Kubera), surely becomes depleted. // Hit_2.95 //

body.text: stabdhakarṇo brūte-śṛṇu bhrātaḥ cirāśritād etau damanaka-karaṭakau sandhi-vigraha-kāryādhikāriṇau ca kadācid arthādhikāre na niyoktavyau | aparaṃ ca niyoga-prastāve yan mayā śrutaṃ tat kathyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Stabdhakarṇa</s> says—Listen, brother! These two, <s>Damanaka</s> and <s>Karaṭaka</s>, who are long-standing dependents and officers of peace and war, should never be appointed to the treasury. And moreover, regarding appointments, I shall relate what I have heard.

children.text: brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo bandhur nādhikāre praśasyate |
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, or a kinsman is not commendable in a position of authority;

children.text: brāhmaṇaḥ siddham apy arthaṃ kṛcchreṇāpi na yacchati // Hit_2.96 //
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> will not release even an accomplished fund except with great difficulty. // Hit_2.96 //

children.text: niyuktaḥ kṣatriyo dravye khaḍgaṃ darśayate dhruvam |
children.translated_text: A <s>Kṣatriya</s> appointed over wealth will surely brandish his sword;

children.text: sarvasvaṃ grasate bandhur ākramya jñāti-bhāvataḥ // Hit_2.97 //
children.translated_text: A kinsman devours everything, seizing it on the pretext of family ties. // Hit_2.97 //

children.text: aparādhe'pi niḥśaṅko niyogī cira-sevakaḥ |
children.translated_text: A long-serving appointee is fearless even in wrongdoing;

children.text: sa svāminam avajñāya carec ca niravagrahaḥ // Hit_2.98 //
children.translated_text: He disregards his master and acts without restraint. // Hit_2.98 //

children.text: upakartādhikāra-sthaḥ svāparādhaṃ na manyate |
children.translated_text: One who has done a favor, when placed in authority, does not consider his own faults;

children.text: upakāraṃ dhvajī-kṛtya sarvam eva vilumpati // Hit_2.99 //
children.translated_text: Brandishing his past service as a banner, he plunders everything. // Hit_2.99 //

children.text: upaṃśu-krīḍito 'mātyaḥ svayaṃ rājāyate yataḥ |
children.translated_text: A minister who is a secret confidant himself becomes like a king;

children.text: avajñā kriyate tena sadā paricayād dhruvam // Hit_2.100 //
children.translated_text: He invariably shows disrespect due to excessive familiarity. // Hit_2.100 //

children.text: antar-duṣṭaḥ kṣamā-yuktaḥ sarvānartha-karaḥ kila |
children.translated_text: One who is inwardly corrupt but outwardly patient is truly the cause of all misfortune;

children.text: śakuniḥ śakaṭāraś ca dṛṣṭāntāv atra bhūpate // Hit_2.101 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śakuni</s> and <s>Śakaṭāra</s> are examples of this, O king. // Hit_2.101 //

children.text: sadāmatyo na sādhyaḥ syāt samṛddhaḥ sarva eva hi |
children.translated_text: An ever-present minister cannot be controlled, for everyone who is prosperous becomes so;

children.text: siddhānām ayam ādeśaḥ ṛddhiś citta-vikāriṇī // Hit_2.102 //
children.translated_text: This is the teaching of the wise—prosperity alters the mind. // Hit_2.102 //

children.text: prāptārtha-grahaṇaṃ dravya-parīvarto 'nurodhanam |
children.translated_text: Accepting what comes to hand, misappropriating goods, indulging favorites,

children.text: upekṣā buddhi-hīnatvaṃ bhogo 'mātyasya dūṣaṇam // Hit_2.103 //
children.translated_text: Negligence, lack of judgment, and self-indulgence—these are the faults of a minister. // Hit_2.103 //

children.text: niyogy artha-grahopāyo rājñā nitya-parīkṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: The means to recover wealth from an appointee is constant examination by the king,

children.text: pratipatti-pradānaṃ ca tathā karma-viparyayaḥ // Hit_2.104 //
children.translated_text: Bestowing recognition, and also reversal of duties. // Hit_2.104 //

children.text: nipīḍitā vamanty uccair antaḥ-sāraṃ mahīpateḥ |
children.translated_text: When squeezed, they discharge their inner substance to the king,

children.text: duṣṭa-vraṇā iva prāyo bhavanti hi niyoginaḥ // Hit_2.105 //
children.translated_text: For appointees are generally like festering wounds. // Hit_2.105 //

children.text: muhur niyoginī bādhyā vasudhārā mahīpate |
children.translated_text: The stream of appointees must be wrung repeatedly, O king;

children.text: sakṛt kiṃ pīḍitaṃ snāna-vastraṃ muñced dhṛtaṃ payaḥ // Hit_2.106 //
children.translated_text: Does a cloth soaked once in the bath release all the water it has absorbed? // Hit_2.106 //

body.text: etat sarvaṃ yathāvasaraṃ jñātvā vyavahartavyam |
body.translated_text: All this should be understood and applied according to the occasion.

body.text: siṃho brūte-asti tāvad evam | kintv etau sarvathā na mama vacana-kāriṇau |
body.translated_text: The lion says—This is indeed so. But these two do not obey my word in any way.

body.text: stabdhakarṇo brūte-etat sarvam anucitaṃ sarvathā | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: <s>Stabdhakarṇa</s> says—All of this is entirely improper. For—

children.text: ājñā-bhaṅga-karān rājā na kṣameta sutān api |
children.translated_text: A king should not tolerate those who violate his commands, even if they be his sons;

children.text: viśeṣaḥ ko nu rājñaś ca rājñaś citra-gatasya ca // Hit_2.107 //
children.translated_text: What difference is there between a king and a king in a painting? // Hit_2.107 //

children.text: stabdhasya naśyati yaśo viṣam asya maitrī
children.translated_text: The fame of one who is rigid perishes; the friendship of one who is deceitful is poison;

children.text: naṣṭendriyasya kulam artha-parasya dharmaḥ |
children.translated_text: The family of one who has lost self-control, and the <s>dharma</s> of one devoted to wealth are destroyed;

children.text: vidyā-phalaṃ vyasaninaḥ kṛpaṇasya saukhyaṃ
children.translated_text: The fruit of learning of one addicted to vice, the happiness of a miser,

children.text: rājyaṃ pramatta-sacivasya narādhipasya // Hit_2.108 //
children.translated_text: And the kingdom of a king whose minister is negligent—all perish. // Hit_2.108 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And further—

children.text: taskarebhyo niyuktebhyaḥ śatrubhyo nṛpa-vallabhāt |
children.translated_text: From thieves, from appointees, from enemies, from the king's favorite,

children.text: nṛpatir nija-lobhāc ca prajā rakṣet piteva hi // Hit_2.109 //
children.translated_text: And from his own greed—a king should protect his subjects like a father. // Hit_2.109 //

body.text: bhrātaḥ ! sarvathāsmad-vacanaṃ kriyatām | vyavahāro 'py asmābhiḥ kṛta eva | ayaṃ saṃjīvakaḥ sasya-bhakṣako 'rthādhikāre niyujyatām |
body.translated_text: Brother! Let my counsel be followed in every way. We have already examined the matter. Let this <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>, who eats grass, be appointed to the treasury.

body.text: etad-vacanāt tathānuṣṭhite sati tad ārabhya piṅgalaka-saṃjīvakayoḥ sarva-bandhu-parityāgena mahatā snehena kālo 'tivartate | tato 'nujīvinām apyāhāra-dāne śaithilya-darśanād damanaka-karaṭakāv anyonyaṃ cintayataḥ | tad āha damanakaḥ karaṭakam-mitra ! kiṃ kartavyam ? ātma-kṛto 'yaṃ doṣaḥ | svayaṃ kṛte'pi doṣe paridevanam apy anucitam | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: When this was accordingly done at his suggestion, from that time on, <s>Piṅgalaka</s> and <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> passed time with great affection, abandoning all other companions. Then, seeing the slackness in providing food even to their dependents, <s>Damanaka</s> and <s>Karaṭaka</s> reflected together. <s>Damanaka</s> said to <s>Karaṭaka</s>—Friend! What is to be done? This fault is self-created. Even when the fault is self-made, lamenting is also improper. As it is said—

children.text: svarṇa-rekhām ahaṃ spṛṣṭvā baddhvātmānaṃ ca dūtikā |
children.translated_text: She who touched the golden line, the messenger who bound herself,

children.text: āditsuś ca maṇiṃ sādhuḥ sva-doṣād duḥkhitā ime // Hit_2.110 //
children.translated_text: And the monk who desired the jewel—these three suffered due to their own faults. // Hit_2.110 //

body.text: karaṭako brūte--katham etat ?
body.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> says—How is that?

body.text: damanakaḥ kathayati-
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> narrates—

body.text: kathā 5
body.translated_text: Story 5
