body.text: asti kāñcanapura-nāmni nagare vīravikramo rājā | tasya dharmādhikāriṇā kaścin nāpito vadhya-bhūmiṃ nīyamānaḥ kandarpaketu-nāmnā parivrājakena sādhu-dvitīyakena nāyaṃ hantavyaḥ ity uktvā vastrāñcalena dhṛtaḥ | rāja-puruṣā ūcuḥ-kim iti nāyaṃ vadhyaḥ |
body.translated_text: In a city called <s>Kāñcanapura</s>, there was a king named <s>Vīravikrama</s>. A certain barber, being led to the execution ground by the king's officer of justice, was seized by the hem of his garment by an ascetic named <s>Kandarpaketu</s>, accompanied by a monk, saying 'This man should not be killed!' The king's men said—Why should he not be executed?

body.text: sa āha-śrūyatām | svarṇa-rekhām ahaṃ spṛṣṭvā ity ādi paṭhati |
body.translated_text: He said—Listen! He recites: 'She who touched the golden line...' and so forth.

body.text: ta āhuḥ--katham etat ?
body.translated_text: They said—How is that?

body.text:
parivrājakaḥ kathayati-ahaṃ siṃhala-dvīpasya bhūpater jīmūtaketaḥ putraḥ dandarpaketur nāma | madhye caturdaśyām āvirbhūta-kalpataru-tale ratnāvalī-kiraṇa-kabūtara-paryaṅka-sthitā sarvālaṅkāra-bhūṣitā lakṣmīr iva vīnāṃ vādayantī kanyā kācid dṛśyate iti | tato 'haṃ pota-vṇijam ādāya potam āruhya tatra gataḥ | anantaraṃ tatra gatvā paryaṅke'dhamagrā tathaiva sāvalokitā | tatas tal-lāvaṇya-guṇākṛṣṭena mayāpi tat-paścāj jhampo dattaḥ | tad-anantaraṃ kanakapattanaṃ prāpya suvarṇa-prāsāde tathaiva paryaṅke sthitā vidyādharībhir upāsyamānā mayālokitā | tathāpy ahaṃ dūrād eva dṛṣṭvā sakhīṃ prasthāpya sādaraṃ sambhāṣitaḥ | tat-sakhyā ca mayā pṛṣṭayā samākhyātam-eṣā kandarpakeli-nāmno vidyādhara-cakravartinaḥ
putrī ratnamañjarī nāma pratijñāpitā vidyate | yaḥ kanakavartanaṃ sva-cakṣuṣāgatya paśyati, sa eva pitur agocaro 'pi māṃ pariṇeṣyatīti manasaḥ saṅkalpaḥ | tad enāṃ gāndharva-vivāhena pariṇayatu bhavān |
atha tatra vṛtte gandharva-vivāhe tathā saha ramamāṇas tatrāhaṃ tiṣṭhāmi | tata ekadā rahasi tayoktam-svāmin ! svecchayā sarvam idam upabhoktavyam | eṣā citra-gatā svarṇa-rekhā nāma vidyādharī na kadācit spraṣṭavyā | paścād upajāta-kautukena mayā svarṇarekhā sva-hastena spṛṣṭā | tathā citratayāpy ahaṃ caraṇa-padmena tāḍita āgatya sva-rāṣṭre patitaḥ |
body.translated_text: The wandering ascetic narrates: 'I am the son of the king of <s>Siṃhala-dvīpa</s> (the island of Ceylon), <s>Jīmūtaketu</s>, named <s>Dandarpaketu</s>. In the middle, on the fourteenth day of the lunar fortnight, beneath a wish-fulfilling tree that had appeared, seated on a couch made of rays of jeweled garlands like a pigeon, adorned with all ornaments, like <s>Lakṣmī</s> herself, some maiden was seen playing a <s>vīṇā</s>.' Thereupon I, taking a ship-merchant, boarded a ship and went there. Then, having gone there, I saw her in the same way, seated forward-leaning on the couch. Then, drawn by her beauty and virtues, I too leaped after her. Thereafter, reaching <s>Kanakapattana</s> (the Golden City), I beheld her seated in the same manner on a couch in a golden palace, attended by <s>Vidyādharī</s> goddesses. Even so, having seen her only from a distance, I sent a female companion, and was addressed with respect. And when I asked her companion, she told me: 'This is the daughter of the <s>Vidyādhara</s> emperor named <s>Kandarpakeli</s>, named <s>Ratnamañjarī</s>. She has made a vow: he who comes to <s>Kanakavarttana</s> (the Golden City) and sees it with his own eyes — he alone, even unseen by my father, shall marry me — such is her heart's resolve. So let your honor marry her by the <s>Gāndharva</s> rite of marriage.' Then, when the <s>Gāndharva</s> marriage had taken place there, I remained there, sporting with her in pleasure. Then one day, in private, she said: 'My lord! All this may be enjoyed at your will. But this <s>Vidyādharī</s> named <s>Svarṇarekhā</s> (Golden Line), depicted in a painting, should never be touched.' Afterwards, curiosity having arisen in me, I touched <s>Svarṇarekhā</s> with my own hand. Thereupon, even though she was [merely] a painting, she struck me with her lotus-foot, and I came flying back and fell in my own kingdom.'

body.text: atha duḥkhito 'haṃ parivrajitaḥ pṛthivīṃ paribhrāmyann imāṃ ngarīm anuprāptaḥ | atra cātikānte divase gopa-gṛhe suptaḥ sann apaśyam | pradoṣa-samaye paśūnāṃ pālanaṃ kṛtvā sva-geham āgato gopaḥ sva-vadhūṃ dūtyā saha kim api mantrayantīm apaśyat | tatas tāṃ gopīṃ tāḍayitvā stambhe baddhvā suptaḥ | tato 'rdha-rātre etasya nāpitasya vadhūr dūtī punas tāṃ gopīm upetyāvadat-tava virahānala-dagdho 'sau smara-śara-jarjarito mumūrṣur iva vartate | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: Then, grieving, I became a wandering ascetic and, roaming the earth, arrived at this city. And here, on a certain past day, while sleeping in a cowherd's house, I observed [the following]. At dusk, having tended the cattle and returned home, the cowherd saw his wife plotting something with a go-between. Then, having beaten that cowherd-woman and tied her to a post, he fell asleep. Then, at midnight, the wife of this barber — the go-between — came again to that cowherd-woman and said: 'That one, scorched by the fire of separation from you, pierced by the arrows of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love), is on the verge of death.' And thus it is said —

children.text: rajanī-cara-nāthena khaṇḍite timire niśi |
children.translated_text: When the lord of the night-wanderers (the moon) has destroyed the darkness of night,

children.text: yūnāṃ manāṃsi vivyādha dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭvā manobhavaḥ // Hit_2.111 //
children.translated_text: <s>Manobhava</s> (the god of love) pierces the minds of the young, again and again, upon seeing [the moonlight]. // Hit 2.111 //

body.text: tasya tādṛśīm avasthām avalokya parikliṣṭa-manās tvām anuvartitum āgatā | tad aham atrātmānaṃ baddhvā tiṣṭhāmi | tvaṃ tatra gatvā taṃ santoṣya satvaram āgamiṣyasi | tathānuṣṭhite sati sa gopaḥ prabuddho 'vadat-idānīṃ tvāṃ pāpiṣṭhāṃ jārāntikaṃ nayāmi | tato yadāsau na kiṃcid api brūte tadā kruddho gopaḥ-darpān mama vacasi pratyuttaram api na dadāsi ity uktvā kopena tena kartarikāmādāyāsyā nāsikā chinnā | tathā kṛtvā punaḥ supto gopo nidrām upagataḥ | athāgatya gopī dūtīm apṛcchat-kā vārtā ?
body.translated_text: Seeing his such condition, with an afflicted heart, she has come to attend upon you. So I shall tie myself here in your place and stay. You, having gone there and satisfied him, will quickly return.' When this was carried out accordingly, the cowherd woke up and said: 'Now I shall take you, wicked woman, to your lover!' Then, when she said nothing at all, the angry cowherd said: 'Out of arrogance you do not even give a reply to my words!' — and saying this, seizing a pair of scissors in anger, he cut off her nose. Having done so, the cowherd fell asleep again. Then the cowherd-woman returned and asked the go-between: 'What news?'

body.text: dūtyoktam-paśya mām | mukham eva vārtāṃ kathayati |
body.translated_text: The go-between said: 'Look at me! My face alone tells the story!'

body.text: anantaraṃ sā gopī tathā kṛtvātmānaṃ baddhvā sthitā | iyaṃ ca dūtī tāṃ chinna-nāsikāṃ gṛhītvā sva-gṛhaṃ praviśya sthitā | tataḥ prātar evānena nāpitena sva-vadhūḥ kṣura-bhāṇḍaṃ yācitā satī kṣuram ekaṃ prādāt | tato 'samagra-bhāṇḍe prāpte samupajāta-kopo 'yaṃ nāpitas taṃ kṣuraṃ dūrād eva gṛhe kṣiptavān | atha kṛtārtarāyeyaṃ me nāsikānena chinnety uktvā dharmādhikāri-samīpam etam ānītavatī | sā ca gopī tena gopena punaḥ pṛṣṭovāca-are pāpa ! ko māṃ mahāsatī virūpayituṃ samarthaḥ | mama vyavahāram akalmaṣam aṣṭau lokapālā eva jānanti, yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Then that cowherd-woman, having done thus (tied herself), stood bound. And this go-between, taking her severed nose, entered her own house and stayed there. Then, in the morning, when this barber asked his wife for the razor-case, she gave him only one razor. Then, angry at receiving the incomplete kit, this barber flung that razor from a distance into the house. Thereupon, having found her opportunity, she said: 'My nose has been cut off by this man!' — and saying so, she brought him before the officer of justice. And that cowherd-woman, when questioned again by the cowherd, said: 'O wicked one! Who is capable of disfiguring me, a woman of great virtue? The eight <s>Lokapālas</s> (guardians of the world) themselves know my conduct to be spotless, for —'

children.text: āditya-candrāvanilānalaś ca
children.translated_text: The sun, the moon, the wind, and fire,

children.text: dyaur bhūmir āpo hṛdayaṃ yamaś ca |
children.translated_text: the sky, the earth, water, the heart, and <s>Yama</s>,

children.text: ahaś ca rātriś ca ubhe ca sandhye
children.translated_text: day, night, and both twilights,

children.text: dharmaś ca jānāti narasya vṛttam // Hit_2.112 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Dharma</s> itself — these know a man's conduct. // Hit 2.112 //

children.text: atathyāny api tathyāni darśayanti hi peśalāḥ |
children.translated_text: The clever indeed make even untrue things appear true,

children.text: same nimnonnatānīva citra-karma-vido janāḥ // Hit_2.113 //
children.translated_text: like those skilled in painting who show unevenness on a flat surface. // Hit 2.113 //

children.text: utpanneṣu ca kāryeṣu matir yasya na hīyate |
children.translated_text: He whose wits do not fail him when difficulties arise,

children.text: sa nistarati durgāṇi gopī jāra-dvayaṃ yathā // Hit_2.114 //
children.translated_text: he overcomes all dangers — as the cowherd-woman did with her two lovers. // Hit 2.114 //

body.text: karaṭakaḥ pṛcchati-katham etat ?
body.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> asks: 'How is that?'

body.text: kathā 6
body.translated_text: Story 6

body.text: damanakaḥ kathayati-asti dvāravatyāṃ puryāṃ kasyacid gopasya vadhūr bandhakī | sā grāmasya daṇḍa-nāyakena tat-putreṇa ca samaṃ ramate | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> narrates: 'In the city of <s>Dvāravatī</s>, the wife of a certain cowherd was unchaste. She sported with the <s>Daṇḍanāyaka</s> (village chief) and his son together. And thus it is said —'

children.text: nāgnis tṛpyati kāṣṭhānāṃ nāpagānāṃ mahodadhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Fire is not sated with firewood, nor is the great ocean with rivers,

children.text: nāntakaḥ sarva-bhūtānāṃ na puṃsāṃ vāma-locanā // Hit_2.115 //
children.translated_text: nor <s>Antaka</s> (Death) with all beings, nor the dark-eyed woman with men. // Hit 2.115 //

children.text: na dānena na mānena nārjavena na sevayā |
children.translated_text: Neither by gifts, nor by honor, nor by straightforwardness, nor by service,

children.text: na śastreṇa na śāstreṇa sarvathā viṣamāḥ striyaḥ // Hit_2.116 //
children.translated_text: neither by weapons nor by scriptures — women are utterly inscrutable. // Hit 2.116 //

body.text: yataḥ-

children.text: guṇāśrayaṃ kīrti-yutaṃ ca kāntaṃ
children.translated_text: A husband who is a refuge of virtues, endowed with fame, handsome,

children.text: patiṃ ratijñaṃ sadhanaṃ yuvānam |
children.translated_text: skilled in love-making, wealthy, and youthful —

children.text: vihāya śīghraṃ vanitā vrajanti
children.translated_text: quickly abandoning him, women go

children.text: narāntaraṃ śīla-guṇādi-hīnam // Hit_2.117 //
children.translated_text: to another man, devoid of character and virtues. // Hit 2.117 //

body.translated_text: For —

body.text: aparaṃ ca-

children.text: na tādṛśīṃ prītim upaiti nārī
children.translated_text: A woman does not experience such pleasure

children.text: vicitra-śayyā śayitāpi kāmam |
children.translated_text: even when lying on an elaborate bed, however much she may desire it,

children.text: yathā hi dūrvādi-vikīrṇa-bhūmau
children.translated_text: as the happiness she obtains on ground strewn with <s>dūrvā</s> grass and the like,

children.text: prayāti saukhyaṃ para-kānti-saṅgāt // Hit_2.118 //
children.translated_text: from the embrace of another's beloved. // Hit 2.118 //

body.translated_text: And furthermore —

body.text: atha kadācit sā daṇḍa-nāyaka-putreṇa saha ramamāṇā tiṣṭhati | atha daṇḍa-nāyako 'pi rantuṃ tatrāgataḥ | tam āyāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā tat-putraṃ kusūle nikṣipya daṇḍanāyakena saha tathaiva krīḍati | anantaraṃ tasya bhartā gopo goṣṭhāt samāgataḥ | tam avalokya gopyoktam-daṇḍanāyaka ! tvaṃ laguḍaṃ gṛhītvā kopaṃ darśayan satvaraṃ gaccha | tathā tenānuṣṭhite gopena gṛham āgatya pṛṣṭhā-kena kāryeṇa daṇḍanāyakaḥ samāgatyātra sthitaḥ ?
body.translated_text: Now, once she was sporting with the son of the <s>Daṇḍanāyaka</s>. Then the <s>Daṇḍanāyaka</s> also came there to enjoy himself. Seeing him approaching, she hid his son in a grain-bin and continued to sport with the <s>Daṇḍanāyaka</s> in the same manner. Then her husband, the cowherd, returned from the cattle-pen. Seeing him, the cowherd-woman said: '<s>Daṇḍanāyaka</s>! Take up your staff, display anger, and leave quickly!' When he did so accordingly, the cowherd, having entered the house, asked: 'For what purpose did the <s>Daṇḍanāyaka</s> come and stand here?'

body.text: sā brūte-anyaṃ kenāpi kāryeṇa putrasyopari kruddhaḥ | sa ca māryamāṇo 'py atrāgatya praviṣṭo mayā kusūle nikṣipya rakṣitaḥ | tat-pitrā cānviṣyātra na dṛṣṭaḥ | ata evāyaṃ daṇḍanāyakaḥ kruddha eva gacchati |
body.translated_text: She said: 'For some other reason, he was angry at his son. And that son, though being beaten, entered here, and I hid him in the grain-bin and protected him. His father, searching, did not find him here. That is precisely why the <s>Daṇḍanāyaka</s> left still angry.'

body.text: tataḥ sā tat-putraṃ kuṣulād bahiṣkṛtya darśitavatī | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: Then she brought the son out of the grain-bin and showed him. And thus it is said —

children.text: āhāro dviguṇaḥ strīṇāṃ buddhis tāsāṃ catur-guṇā |
children.translated_text: Women's appetite is twice (that of men), their intelligence fourfold,

children.text: ṣaḍ-guṇo vyavasāyaś ca kāmāś cāṣṭaguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ // Hit_2.119 //
children.translated_text: their determination sixfold, and their desire is said to be eightfold. // Hit 2.119 //

body.text:
ato 'haṃ bravīmi-utapanneṣv api kāryeṣu ity ādi |
karaṭako brūte-astv evam | kintv anayor mahānanyognya-nisargopajāta-sneha kathaṃ bhedayituṃ śakyaḥ ?
body.translated_text:
Therefore I say: 'He whose wits do not fail him when difficulties arise' — and so on.
<s>Karaṭaka</s> says: 'Let it be so. But how can the friendship born of natural affinity between these two, who are great companions, be broken?'

body.text: damanako brūte-upāyaḥ kriyatām | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> says: 'Let a stratagem be devised. And thus it is said —'

children.text: upāyena jayo yādṛg ripos tādṛṅ na hetibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: The victory that is won by stratagem against an enemy, that cannot be won by weapons.

children.text: upāya-jño 'lpa-kāyo 'pi na śūraiḥ paribhūyate // Hit_2.120 //
children.translated_text: One skilled in stratagems, even if small-bodied, is not humiliated by warriors. // Hit 2.120 //

body.text: karaṭakaḥ pṛcchati-katham etat ?
body.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> asks: 'How is that?'

body.text:
damanakaḥ kathayati--
kathā 7
body.translated_text:
<s>Damanaka</s> narrates —
Story 7

body.text: kasmiṃścit tarau vāyasa-dampatī nivasataḥ | tayoś cāpṛtyāni tat-koṭarāvasthitena kṛṣṇa-sarpeṇa khāditāni | tataḥ punar garbhavatī vāyasī vāyasm āha-nātha ! tyajyatām ayaṃ vṛkṣaḥ | atrāvasthita-kṛṣṇa-sarpeṇāvayoḥ santatiḥ satataṃ bhakṣyate | yataḥ-

children.text: duṣṭā bhāryā śaṭhaṃ mitraṃ bhṛtyaś cottara-dāyakaḥ |
children.translated_text: A wicked wife, a deceitful friend, a servant who talks back,

children.text: sa-sarpe ca gṛhe vāso mṛtyur eva na saṃśayaḥ // Hit_2.121 //
children.translated_text: and dwelling in a house with a serpent — these are death itself, without doubt. // Hit 2.121 //

body.translated_text: On a certain tree dwelt a crow-couple. And their not-yet-hatched eggs were repeatedly eaten by a black serpent dwelling in the hollow of that tree. Then the pregnant crow-wife said to the crow: 'My lord! Let us abandon this tree. The offspring of us both is constantly devoured by the black serpent living here. For —'

body.text: vāyaso brūte-priye ! na bhetavyam | vāraṃ vāraṃ mavaitasya soḍhaḥ | idānīṃ punar na kṣantavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: The crow says: 'Dear one! There is nothing to fear. I have endured this again and again. Now it shall be tolerated no more.'

body.text: vāyasy āha-katham etena balavatā sārdhe bhavān vigrahītuṃ samarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: The crow-wife says: 'How can you be capable of contending with this powerful one?'

body.text: vāyaso brūte-alam anayā śaṅkayā | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: The crow says: 'Enough of this apprehension! For —'

children.text: buddhir yasya balaṃ tasya nirbuddhes tu kuto balam |
children.translated_text: He who has intelligence has strength; whence strength for the witless?

children.text: paśya siṃho madonmattaḥ śaśakena nipātitaḥ // Hit_2.122 //
children.translated_text: See — the proud, intoxicated lion was brought down by a hare! // Hit 2.122 //

body.text: vāyasī vihasyāha--katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The crow-wife laughed and said: 'How is that?'

body.text:
vāyasaḥ kathayati-
kathā 8
asti mandara-nāmni parvate durdānto nāma siṃhaḥ | sa ca sarvadā paśūnāṃ vadhaṃ kurvann āste | tataḥ sarvaiḥ paśubhir militvā sa siṃho vijñaptaḥ-mṛgendra ! kim artham ekadā bahu-paśu-ghātaḥ kriyate | yadi prasādo bhavati tadā vayam eva bhavad-āhārāya pratyaham ekaikaṃ paśum upaḍhaukayāmaḥ |
body.translated_text:
The crow narrates:
Story 8
On a mountain named <s>Mandara</s>, there lived a lion called <s>Durdānta</s> (the Untamable). He was constantly killing the animals. Then all the animals, having gathered together, petitioned the lion: 'O lord of beasts! Why is such mass slaughter of animals carried out at once? If you are pleased, we ourselves will present one animal each day for your food.'

body.text: tataḥ siṃhenoktam-yady etad abhimataṃ bhavatāṃ tarhi bhavatu tat |
body.translated_text: Then the lion said: 'If this is agreeable to you all, then so be it.'

body.text: tataḥ-prabhṛty ekaikaṃ paśum upakalpitaṃ bhakṣayann āste | atha kadācid vṛddha-śaśakasya vāraḥ samāyātaḥ | so 'cintayat-
body.translated_text: From then on, he continued eating one animal that was offered each day. Now, once the turn of an old hare arrived. He thought —

children.text: trāsa-hetor vinītis tu kriyate jīvitāśayā |
children.translated_text: Submission is made to a fearsome one out of the desire to live;

children.text: pañcatvaṃ ced gamiṣyāmi kiṃ siṃhānunayena me // Hit_2.123 //
children.translated_text: if I am going to die anyway, what use to me is appeasing the lion? // Hit 2.123 //

body.text: tan mandaṃ mandaṃ gacchāmi | tataḥ siṃho 'pi kṣudhā-pīḍitaḥ kopāt tam uvāca-kutas tvaṃ vilambya samāgato 'si |
body.translated_text: So, I shall go very slowly.' Then the lion too, tormented by hunger, angrily said to him: 'Why have you come so late?'

body.text: śaśako 'bravīt-deva ! nāham aparādhī | āgacchan pathi siṃhāntareṇa balād dhṛtaḥ | tasyāgre punar āgamanāya śapathaṃ kṛtvā svāminaṃ nivedayitum atrāgato 'sim |
body.translated_text: The hare said: 'Your Majesty! I am not at fault. While coming, I was forcibly seized on the path by another lion. Having sworn before him to return again, I have come here to inform my master.'

body.text: siṃhaḥ sakopam āha-satvaraṃ gatvā durātmānaṃ darśaya | kva sa durātmā tiṣṭhati |
body.translated_text: The lion said angrily: 'Go quickly and show me the villain! Where does that scoundrel stand?'

body.text: tataḥ śaśakas taṃ gṛhītvā gabhīra-kūpaṃ darśayituṃ gataḥ | tatrāgatya svayam eva paśyatu svāmīty uktvā tasmin kūpa-jale tasya siṃhasyaiva pratibimbaṃ darśitavān | tato 'sau krodhādhmāto darpāt tasyopary ātmānaṃ nikṣipya pañcatvaṃ gataḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi buddhir yasya ity ādi |
body.translated_text: Then the hare took him and went to show him a deep well. Having arrived there, he said 'Let my lord himself see!' — and in the water of that well, he showed the lion his own reflection. Thereupon, that lion, swollen with rage and pride, hurled himself upon it and perished. Therefore I say: 'He who has intelligence has strength' — and so on.

body.text: vāyasy āha-śrutaṃ mayā sarvam | samprati yathā kartavyaṃ brūhi |
body.translated_text: The crow-wife said: 'I have heard everything. Now tell me what should be done.'

body.text: vāyaso 'vadat-atrāsanne sarasi rāja-putraḥ pratyaham āgatya snāti | snāna-samaye mad-aṅgād avatāritaṃ tīrtha-śilā-nihitaṃ kanaka-sūtraṃ cañcvā vidhṛtyānīyāsmin koṭare dhārayiṣyasi |
body.translated_text: The crow said: 'In the lake nearby, a prince comes to bathe every day. At bathing time, you shall take in your beak the golden chain that is removed from my body and placed on the stone by the bathing-steps, bring it here, and keep it in this hollow of the tree.'

body.text: atha kadācit snātuṃ jalaṃ praviṣṭe rāja-putre vāyasyā tad-anuṣṭhitam | atha kanaka-sūtrānusaraṇa-pravṛttai rāja-puruṣais tatra taru-koṭare kṛṣṇa-sarpo dṛṣṭo vyāpāditaś ca | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-upāyena hi yac chakyam itena hi yac chakyam ity ādi |
body.translated_text: Then one day, when the prince had entered the water to bathe, the crow-wife carried this out. Then the royal servants, pursuing the golden chain, discovered the black serpent in that hollow of the tree and killed it. Therefore I say: 'The victory that is won by stratagem' — and so on.

body.text: karaṭako brūte-yady evaṃ tarhi gaccha | śivās te santu panthānaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> says: 'If so, then go. May your paths be auspicious!'

body.text: tato damanakaḥ piṅgalaka-samīpaṃ gatvā praṇamyovāca-deva ! ātyantikaṃ kim api mahā-bhaya-kāri kāryaṃ manyamānaḥ samāgato 'smi | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Then <s>Damanaka</s>, having gone to the presence of <s>Piṅgalaka</s> and bowed, said: 'Your Majesty! Thinking of something extremely fear-inducing and critical, I have come. For —'

children.text: āpady unmārga-gamane kārya-kālātyayeṣu ca |
children.translated_text: In times of calamity, when going astray, and when the time for action is passing,

children.text: kalyāṇa-vacanaṃ brūyād apṛṣṭo 'pi hito naraḥ // Hit_2.124 //
children.translated_text: a well-wishing person should speak beneficial words even when unasked. // Hit 2.124 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: bhogasya bhājanaṃ rājā na rājā kārya-bhājanam |
children.translated_text: A king is a vessel for enjoyment, not a vessel for (executing) affairs of state;

children.text: rāja-kārya-paridhvaṃsī mantrī doṣeṇa lipyate // Hit_2.125 //
children.translated_text: it is the minister who is tainted with blame when the king's affairs are ruined. // Hit 2.125 //

body.text: tathā hi paśya | amātyānām eṣa kramaḥ |
body.translated_text: Consider this: This is the way of ministers —

children.text: varaṃ prāṇa-parityāgaḥ śirasā vāpi kartanam |
children.translated_text: Better to give up one's life or even have one's head cut off,

children.text: na tu svāmi-padāvāpti-pātakecchor upekṣaṇam // Hit_2.126 //
children.translated_text: than to tolerate one who desires the sinful attainment of the master's position. // <s>Hit</s> 2.126 //

body.text: piṅgalakaḥ sādaram āha-atha bhavān kiṃ vaktum icchati |
body.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said with respect: 'Well, what does your honor wish to say?'

body.text: damanako brūte-deva ! saṃjīvakas tavopaya-sadṛśa-vyavahārīva lakṣyate | tathā cāsmat sannidhāne śrīmad-deva-pādānāṃ śakti-traya-nindāṃ kṛtvā rājyam evābhilaṣati |
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'Your Majesty! <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> appears to be behaving as though he were your equal in strategy. Moreover, in our very presence, having disparaged the three powers of His Majesty, he desires the kingdom itself.'

body.text: etac chrutvā, piṅgalakaḥ sabhayaṃ sāścaryaṃ matvā tūṣṇīṃ sthitaḥ | damanakaḥ punar āha-deva ! sarvāmātya-parityāgaṃ kṛtvaika evāyaṃ yat tvāṃ sarvādhikārī kṛtaḥ | sa eva doṣaḥ | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Piṅgalaka</s>, feeling both fearful and astonished, remained silent. <s>Damanaka</s> said again: 'Your Majesty! Having dismissed all other ministers, you have made this one alone the controller of all affairs. That itself is the fault. For —

children.text: atyucchrite mantriṇi pārthive ca
children.translated_text: When the minister is greatly exalted, and so too the king,

children.text: viṣṭabhya pādāv upatiṣṭhate śrīḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> (Prosperity), propping her two feet [on both], stands [between them];

children.text: sā strī-svabhāvād asahā bharasya
children.translated_text: she, being of a woman's nature, unable to bear the burden,

children.text: tayor dvayor ekataraṃ jahāti // Hit_2.127 //
children.translated_text: abandons one of the two. // <s>Hit</s> 2.127 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And furthermore —

children.text: ekaṃ bhūmi-patiḥ karoti sacivaṃ rājye pramāṇaṃ yadā taṃ mohāt śrayate madaḥ sa ca madālasyena nirvidyate |
children.translated_text: When a king makes one person his sole minister and authority in the kingdom, intoxication seizes that man through delusion, and he becomes bored by the lethargy of that intoxication;

children.text: nirviṇṇasya padaṃ karoti hṛdaye tasya svatantra-spṛhā- svātantrya-spṛhayā tataḥ sa nṛpateḥ prāṇān abhidruhyati // Hit_2.128 //
children.translated_text: the desire for independence takes its place in the heart of the discontented one — and through the craving for independence, he then plots against the king's life. // <s>Hit</s> 2.128 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: viṣa-dagdhasya bhaktasya dantasya calitasya ca |
children.translated_text: A poison-burnt [tooth], a corrupted [servant], a loose tooth,

children.text: amātyasya ca duṣṭasya mūlād uddharaṇaṃ sukham // Hit_2.129 //
children.translated_text: and a wicked minister — it is pleasant to uproot them from the base. // <s>Hit</s> 2.129 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: yaḥ kuryāt sacivāyattāṃ śriyaṃ tad-vyasane sati |
children.translated_text: A king who makes his prosperity dependent on a minister, when misfortune befalls [that minister],

children.text: so 'ndhavaj jagatī-pālaḥ sīdet sañcārakair vinā // Hit_2.130 //
children.translated_text: sinks like a blind ruler of the earth without guides. // <s>Hit</s> 2.130 //

body.text: sarva-kāryeṣu svecchātaḥ pravartate | tad atra pramāṇaṃ svāmī | etaṃ ca jānāti |
body.translated_text: He acts in all affairs according to his own will. In this matter, the master is the authority — and he knows this.'

children.text: na so 'sti puruṣo loke yo na kāmayate śriyam |
children.translated_text: There is no man in the world who does not desire wealth;

children.text: parasya yuvatiṃ ramyāṃ sādaraṃ nekṣate'tra kaḥ // Hit_2.131 //
children.translated_text: who does not gaze with admiration at another's beautiful young wife? // <s>Hit</s> 2.131 //

body.text: siṃho vimṛśyāha-bhadra ! yadyapy evaṃ tathāpi saṃjīvakena saha mama mahān snehaḥ | paśya-
body.translated_text: The lion reflected and said: 'My good fellow! Even though it is so, I have great affection for <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>. Consider —

children.text: kurvann api vyalīkāni yaḥ priyaḥ priya eva saḥ |
children.translated_text: One who is dear remains dear even though he commits offenses;

children.text: aśeṣa-doṣa-duṣṭo 'pi kāyaḥ kasya na vallabhaḥ // Hit_2.132 //
children.translated_text: the body, though full of every kind of fault, is it not cherished by all? // <s>Hit</s> 2.132 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: apriyāṇy api kurvāṇo yaḥ priyaḥ priya eva saḥ |
children.translated_text: One who is dear remains dear even while doing unpleasant things;

children.text: dagdha-mandira-sāre'pi kasya vahnāv anādaraḥ // Hit_2.133 //
children.translated_text: who shows disregard for fire, even when it has burnt the essence of one's house? // <s>Hit</s> 2.133 //

body.text: damanakaḥ punare evāha-deva ! sa evātidoṣaḥ, yataḥ-
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said again: 'Your Majesty! That itself is the great fault, for —

children.text: yasminn evādhikaṃ cakṣur ārohayati pārthivaḥ |
children.translated_text: The person upon whom the king casts his excessive eye,

children.text: sute'mātye'py udāsīne sa lakṣmyāśrīyate janaḥ // Hit_2.134 //
children.translated_text: whether a son or a minister, when he becomes indifferent — that person is seized by <s>Lakṣmī</s> (fortune). // <s>Hit</s> 2.134 //

children.text: śṛṇu deva !
children.translated_text: Hear, Your Majesty!

children.text: apriyasyāpi pathyasya pariṇāmaḥ sukhāvahaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even of what is unpleasant but wholesome, the result brings happiness;

children.text: vaktā śrotā ca yatrāsti ramante tatra sampadaḥ // Hit_2.135 //
children.translated_text: where both a speaker and a listener of such counsel exist, there prosperities delight. // <s>Hit</s> 2.135 //

body.text: tvayā ca mūla-bhṛtyānapāsyāyam āgantukaḥ puraskṛtaḥ | etac cānucitaṃ kṛtam | yataḥ-

children.text: mūla-bhṛtyān parityajya nāgantūn pratimānayet |
children.translated_text: One should not honor newcomers while abandoning hereditary servants;

children.text: nātaḥ parataro doṣo rājya-bheda-karo yataḥ // Hit_2.136 //
children.translated_text: there is no greater fault than this, for it causes the splitting of the kingdom. // <s>Hit</s> 2.136 //

body.translated_text: And you, having set aside your hereditary servants, have favored this newcomer — this too was improperly done. For —

body.text: siṃho brūte-kim āścaryam | mayā yad abhaya-vācaṃ dattvānītaḥ saṃvardhitaś ca tat kathaṃ mahyaṃ druhyati |
body.translated_text: The lion said: 'What is so surprising? I gave him a promise of safety, brought him here, and nurtured him — how then can he betray me?'

body.text: damanako brūte-deva !
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'Your Majesty!

children.text: durjano nārjavaṃ yāti sevyamāno 'pi nityaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: A wicked person does not become straight even when constantly served;

children.text: sveda-nābhyañjanopāyaiḥ śvapuccham iva nāmitam // Hit_2.137 //
children.translated_text: like a dog's tail, it does not become straight even by sweating, oiling, and other methods. // <s>Hit</s> 2.137 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And furthermore —

children.text: svedito marditaś caiva rañjubhiḥ pariveṣṭitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Heated, massaged, and bound with ropes,

children.text: mukto dvādaśabhir varṣaiḥ śva-pucchaḥ prakṛtiṃ gataḥ // Hit_2.138 //
children.translated_text: after twelve years, when released, the dog's tail returned to its natural state. // <s>Hit</s> 2.138 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: vardhanaṃ vā sammānaṃ khalānāṃ prītaye kutaḥ |
children.translated_text: How can nurturing or honoring ever bring satisfaction to the wicked?

children.text: phalanty amṛta-seke'pi na pathyāni viṣa-drumāḥ // Hit_2.139 //
children.translated_text: Poisonous trees do not yield wholesome fruits, even when watered with nectar. // <s>Hit</s> 2.139 //

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-
children.translated_text: Therefore I say —

children.text: apṛṣṭas tasya na brūyād yaś ca necchet parābhavam |
children.translated_text: One should not speak unasked to him who does not wish to face his own downfall;

children.text: eṣa eva satāṃ dharmo viparīto 'satāṃ mataḥ // Hit_2.140 //
children.translated_text: this indeed is the duty of the good — the opposite is the view of the wicked. // <s>Hit</s> 2.140 //

body.text: tathā coktam-

children.text: snigdho 'kuśalān nivārayati yas tat karma yan nirmalaṃ
children.translated_text: One who is affectionate restrains from the unwholesome — that is the action which is pure;

children.text: sā strī yātu-vidhāyinī sa matimān yaḥ sadbhir abhyarcyate |
children.translated_text: that is a [true] wife who provides for one's departure [to the next world]; he is [truly] wise who is honored by the good;

children.text: sā śrīr yā na madaṃ karoti sa sukhī yas tṛṣṇayā mucyate
children.translated_text: that is [true] prosperity which does not produce intoxication; he is [truly] happy who is freed from desire;

children.text: tan mitraṃ yat kṛtrimaṃ sa puruṣo yaḥ khidyate nendriyaiḥ // Hit_2.141 //
children.translated_text: that is [true] friendship which is not artificial; he is [truly] a man who is not overpowered by his senses. // <s>Hit</s> 2.141 //

body.translated_text: And thus it is said —

body.text: yadi sañjīvaka-vyasanādito 'vijñāpito 'pi svāmī na nivartate, tad īdṛśe bhṛtye na doṣaḥ | tathā ca-
body.translated_text: If the master does not desist from [favoring] <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> even after being informed of the danger, then the fault does not lie with such a servant. And accordingly —

children.text: nṛpaḥ kāmāsakto gaṇayati na kārye na ca hitaṃ
children.translated_text: A king attached to pleasures takes no account of duty or welfare;

children.text: yatheṣṭaṃ svacchandaḥ pravicarati matto gaja iva |
children.translated_text: he roams about as he pleases, willfully, like an intoxicated elephant;

children.text: tato māna-dhmātaḥ sa patati yadā śoka-gahane
children.translated_text: then, swollen with pride, when he falls into the abyss of sorrow,

children.text: tadā bhṛtye doṣān kṣipati na nijaṃ vetty avinayam // Hit_2.142 //
children.translated_text: he casts blame upon his servants without recognizing his own lack of discipline. // <s>Hit</s> 2.142 //

body.text: piṅgalakaḥ svagatam-
body.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalaka</s> [said] to himself:

children.text: na parasyāparādhena pareṣāṃ daṇḍam ācaret |
children.translated_text: One should not impose punishment on others for another's offense;

children.text: ātmanāvagataṃ kṛtvā badhnīyāt pūjayec ca vā // Hit_2.143 //
children.translated_text: having ascertained it oneself, one should either imprison or honor [accordingly]. // <s>Hit</s> 2.143 //

children.text: tathā coktam-
children.translated_text: And thus it is said —

children.text: guṇa-doṣāv aniścitya vidhinaṃ graha-nigrahe |
children.translated_text: Without ascertaining merits and faults, the procedure for seizing or releasing —

children.text: sva-nāśāya yathā nyasto darpāt sarpa-mukhe karaḥ // Hit_2.144 //
children.translated_text: [is like] a hand thrust from pride into the mouth of a serpent, leading to one's own destruction. // <s>Hit</s> 2.144 //

body.text: prakāśaṃ brūte-tadā saṃjīvakaḥ kiṃ pratyādiśyatām |
body.translated_text: He said openly: 'Then what should be the directive regarding <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>?'

body.text: damanakaḥ sa-sambhramam āha-deva ! mā maivam | etāvatā mantra-bhedo jāyate | tathā hy uktam-
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said hastily: 'Your Majesty! No, no, not like this! By this much, the breach of counsel occurs. For it is said —

children.text: mantra-bījam idaṃ guptaṃ rakṣaṇīyaṃ yathā tathā |
children.translated_text: This seed of counsel must be kept secret, guarded by all means;

children.text: manāg api na bhidyeta tad bhinnaṃ na prarohati // Hit_2.145 //
children.translated_text: it should not be breached even slightly, for once breached, it does not sprout again. // <s>Hit</s> 2.145 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: ādeyasya pradeyasya kartavyasya ca karmaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Of what is to be received, what is to be given, and of the task to be done —

children.text: kṣipram akriyamāṇasya kālaḥ pibati tad-rasam // Hit_2.146 //
children.translated_text: time drinks away its essence when it is not carried out swiftly. // <s>Hit</s> 2.146 //

body.text: tad avaśyaṃ samārabdhaṃ mahatā prayatnena sampādanīyam | kiṃ ca-
body.translated_text: What has been necessarily undertaken must be accomplished with great effort. Moreover —

children.text: mantro yodhaḥ ivādhīraḥ sarvāṅgaiḥ saṃvṛtair api |
children.translated_text: A secret counsel, like a timid warrior, even though covered in all limbs,

children.text: ciraṃ na sahate sthātuṃ parebhyo bheda-śaṅkayā // Hit_2.147 //
children.translated_text: cannot endure standing long, from the suspicion of being breached by others. // <s>Hit</s> 2.147 //

body.text: yady asau dṛṣṭa-doṣo 'pi doṣān nivatyaṃ sandhātavyas tad atīvānucitam | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: If, even though his faults are evident, you wish to reconcile with him despite his faults — that is most improper. For —

children.text: sakṛd duṣṭaṃ tu yo mitraṃ punaḥ sandhātum icchati |
children.translated_text: One who wishes to reconcile again with a friend once proven wicked,

children.text: sa mṛtyur eva gṛhṇāti garbham aśvatarī yathā // Hit_2.148 //
children.translated_text: seizes death itself, like a she-mule [that dies] conceiving a foetus. // <s>Hit</s> 2.148 //

children.text: aṅgāṅgi-bhāvam ajñātvā kathaṃ sāmarthya-nirṇayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Without knowing the relationship of the principal and the subordinate, how can one determine capability?

children.text: paśya ṭiṭṭibha-mātreṇa samudro vyākulīkṛtaḥ // Hit_2.149 //
children.translated_text: See — by a mere <s>ṭiṭṭibha</s> (sandpiper), the ocean was thrown into confusion. // <s>Hit</s> 2.149 //

body.text: siṃhaḥ pṛcchati--katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The lion asked: 'How is that?'

body.text: damanakaḥ kathayati-
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> narrated:

body.text: kathā 9
body.translated_text: Story 9

body.text: dakṣiṇa-samudra-tīre ṭiṭṭibha-dampatī nivasataḥ | tatra cāsanna-prasadā ṭiṭṭibhī bhartāram āha-nātha ! prasava-yogya-sthānaṃ nibhṛtam anusandhīyatām |
body.translated_text: On the shore of the southern ocean, a <s>ṭiṭṭibha</s> (sandpiper) couple dwelled. When the time of delivery was near, the <s>ṭiṭṭibha</s> wife said to her husband: 'My lord! Please find a secluded place suitable for giving birth.'

body.text: ṭiṭṭibho 'vadat-bhārye, nanv idam eva sthānaṃ prasūti-yogyam |
body.translated_text: The <s>ṭiṭṭibha</s> said: 'Wife! This very place is suitable for delivery.'

body.text: sā brūte-samudra-velayā vyāpyate sthānam etam |
body.translated_text: She said: 'This place is covered by the ocean waves.'

body.text: ṭiṭṭibho 'vadat-kim ahaṃ tvayā nirbalaḥ samudreṇa nigrahītavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: The <s>ṭiṭṭibha</s> said: 'Am I so powerless that I must be overcome by the ocean, as you suggest?'

body.text: ṭiṭṭibhī vihasyāha-svāmin ! tvayā samudreṇa ca mahad antaram | athavā-
body.translated_text: The <s>ṭiṭṭibha</s> wife said with a laugh: 'My lord! There is a great difference between you and the ocean. Or rather —

children.text: parābhavaṃ paricchettuṃ yogyāyogyaṃ ca vetti yaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who knows what is fitting and unfitting for assessing [the possibility of] defeat,

children.text: astīha yasya vijñānaṃ kṛcchreṇāpi na sīdati // Hit_2.150 //
children.translated_text: who possesses discernment — he does not sink even in adversity. // <s>Hit</s> 2.150 //

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: anucita-kāryārambhaḥ svajana-virodho balīyasā spardhā |
children.translated_text: Undertaking improper tasks, quarrel with one's own people, rivalry with the powerful,

children.text: pramadā-jana-viśvāso mṛtyor dvārāṇi catvāri // Hit_2.151 //
children.translated_text: and trust in women — these are the four gates of death. // <s>Hit</s> 2.151 //

body.text: tataḥ kṛcchreṇa svāmi-vacanātmā tatraiva prasūtā | etat sarvaṃ śrutvā samudreṇāpi yac chakti-jñānārthaṃ tad-aṇḍāny avahṛtāni | tataṣ ṭiṭṭibhī śokārtā bhartāram āha-nātha ! kaṣṭam āpatitam | tāny aṇḍāni me naṣṭāni |
body.translated_text: Then, with difficulty, persuaded by her husband's words, she gave birth right there. Having heard all this, the ocean carried away her eggs to test their power. Thereupon the grief-stricken <s>ṭiṭṭibha</s> wife said to her husband: 'My lord! A calamity has befallen us! Those eggs of mine are lost!'

body.text: ṭiṭṭibho 'vadat-priye ! mā bhaiṣīḥ ity uktvā pakṣiṇāṃ melakaṃ kṛtvā pakṣi-svāmino garuḍasya samīpaṃ gataḥ | tatra gatvā sakala-vṛttāntaṃ ṭiṭṭibhena bhagavato garuḍasya purato niveditam-deva, samudreṇāhaṃ sva-gṛhāvasthito vināparādhanenaiva nigṛhītaḥ |
body.translated_text: The <s>ṭiṭṭibha</s> said: 'Dear one! Do not fear!' Having said this, he convened an assembly of birds and went to the presence of <s>Garuḍa</s>, the lord of birds. Having gone there, the <s>ṭiṭṭibha</s> reported the entire incident before <s>Bhagavān Garuḍa</s>: 'Lord, while I was residing in my own home, I was oppressed by the ocean without any offense on my part.'

body.text: tatas tad-vacanam ākarṇya garutmanā prabhur bhagavān nārāyaṇaḥ sṛṣṭi-sthiti-pralaya-hetur vijñaptaḥ | sa samudram aṇḍa-dānāyādideśa | tato bhagavad-ājñāṃ maulau nidhāya samudreṇa tāny aṇḍāni ṭiṭṭibhāya samarpitāni | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-aṅgāṅgi-bhāvam ajñātvā ity ādi |
body.translated_text: Then, having heard his words, <s>Garutmān</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) petitioned the lord <s>Bhagavān Nārāyaṇa</s>, the cause of creation, preservation, and dissolution. He commanded the ocean to return the eggs. Then, placing the lord's command upon his head, the ocean returned those eggs to the <s>ṭiṭṭibha</s>. Therefore I say: 'Without knowing the relationship of the principal and the subordinate...' and so on.

body.text: rājāha-katham asau jñātavyo droha-buddhir iti |
body.translated_text: The king said: 'How is he to be recognized as having a treacherous mind?'

body.text: damanako brūte-yadāsau sa-darpaḥ śṛṅgāgra-praharaṇābhimukhaś cakitam ivāgacchati tadā jñāsyati svāmī | evam uktvā saṃjīvaka-samīpaṃ gataḥ | tatra gataś ca mandaṃ mandam upasarpan vismitam ivātmānam adarśayat | saṃjīvakena sādaram uktam-bhadra ! kuśalaṃ te |
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'When he comes, arrogant, approaching as if ready to strike with the tips of his horns, looking startled — then the master will know.' Having said this, he went to the presence of <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>. Having gone there, approaching slowly and gradually, he displayed himself as if bewildered. <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> said respectfully: 'My good friend! Is all well with you?'

body.text: damanako brūte-anujīvināṃ kutaḥ kuśalam | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'How can all be well with dependents? For —

children.text: sampattayaḥ parādhīnāḥ sadā cittam anirvṛttam |
children.translated_text: Fortunes are dependent on others, the mind is forever restless,

children.text: sva-jīivite'py aviśvāsas teṣāṃ ye rāja-sevakāḥ // Hit_2.152 //
children.translated_text: and they have no confidence even in their own life — such are those who serve kings. // <s>Hit</s> 2.152 //

body.text: anyac ca-

children.text: ko 'rthān prāpya na garvito viṣayiṇaḥ kasyāpado 'staṃ gatāḥ
children.translated_text: Who, having obtained wealth, is not proud? Whose misfortunes have come to an end?

children.text: strībhiḥ kasya na khaṇḍitaṃ bhuvi manaḥ ko vāsti rājñāṃ priyā |
children.translated_text: Whose mind has not been broken by women on this earth? Who is [always] dear to kings?

children.text: kaḥ kālasya bhujāntaraṃ na ca gataḥ ko 'rthī gato gauravaṃ
children.translated_text: Who has not come into the embrace of Death? What supplicant has attained dignity?

children.text: ko vā durjana-vāgurāsu patitaḥ kṣemeṇa yātaḥ pumān // Hit_2.153 //
children.translated_text: What man, fallen into the snares of the wicked, has gone forth safely? // <s>Hit</s> 2.153 //

body.translated_text: And also —

body.text: saṃjīvakenoktam-sakhe ! brūhi kim etat ?
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> said: 'Friend! Tell me, what is this about?'

body.text: damanaka āha-kiṃ bravīmi manda-bhāgyaḥ | paśya-
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'What can this unfortunate one say? See —

children.text: majjann api payorāśau labdhvā sarpāvalambanam |
children.translated_text: Even while drowning in the ocean, having found a serpent as support,

children.text: na muñcati na cādatte tathā mugdho 'smi samprati // Hit_2.154 //
children.translated_text: one neither lets go nor takes hold — so bewildered am I now. // <s>Hit</s> 2.154 //

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: For —

children.text: ekatra rāja-viśvāso naśyaty anyatra bāndhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: On one side, trust in the king is lost; on the other, a kinsman [is endangered];

children.text: kiṃ karomi kva gacchāmi patit o duḥkha-sāgare // Hit_2.155 //
children.translated_text: what shall I do? Where shall I go? I have fallen into an ocean of sorrow. // <s>Hit</s> 2.155 //

body.text: ity uktvā dīrghaḥ niḥśvasyopaviṣṭaḥ | saṃjīvako brūte-mitra ! tathāpi sa-vistaraṃ manogatam ucyatām |
body.translated_text: Having said this, he sighed deeply and sat down. <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> said: 'Friend! Even so, please tell me in detail what is on your mind.'

body.text: damanakaḥ sunibhṛtam āha-yadyapi rāja-viśvāso na kathanīyas tathāpi bhavān asmadīya-pratyayād āgataḥ | mayā paralokārthināvaśyaṃ tava hitam ākhyeyam | śṛṇu, ayaṃ svāmī tavopari vikṛta-buddhī rahasy uktavān -saṃjīvakam eva hatvā sva-parivāraṃ tarpayāmi |
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said very secretly: 'Although one should not divulge a royal confidence, yet since you have come trusting in our [friendship], I, being one who desires the welfare of the next world, must necessarily tell you what is for your benefit. Listen — this master of ours has developed a hostile intent toward you and has said in private: "I shall kill <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> and feed my retinue."'

body.text: etac chrutvā saṃjīvakaḥ paraṃ viṣādam agamat | damanakaḥ punar āha-alaṃ viṣādena | prāpta-kālakāyam anuṣṭhīyatām | saṃjīvakaḥ kṣaṇaṃ vimṛśyāha sva-gatam-suṣṭhu khalv idam ucyate | kiṃ vā durjana-ceṣṭitaṃ na vety etad vyavahārān nirṇetuṃ na śakyate | yataḥ-

children.text: durjana-gamyā nāryaḥ prāyeṇāpātra-bhṛd bhavati rājā |
children.translated_text: Women are generally accessible to the wicked; a king is often a supporter of unworthy persons;

children.text: kṛpaṇānusāri ca dhanaṃ devo giri-jaladhi-varṣī ca // Hit_2.156 //
children.translated_text: wealth follows the miserly; and the god rains on mountains and oceans. // <s>Hit</s> 2.156 //

body.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> fell into extreme despair. <s>Damanaka</s> said again: 'Enough of despair! What is appropriate to the moment should be carried out.' <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>, after reflecting for a moment, said to himself: 'This is indeed well said. But whether it is the machination of a wicked person or not — this cannot be determined from conduct. For —

children.text: kaścid āśraya-saundaryād dhatte śobhām asajjanaḥ |
children.translated_text: Some wicked person shines merely from the beauty of his refuge,

children.text: pramadālocana-nyastaṃ malīmasam ivāñjanam // Hit_2.157 //
children.translated_text: like impure collyrium placed on the eye of a beautiful woman. // <s>Hit</s> 2.157 //

children.text: ārādhyamāno nṛpatiḥ prayatnān na toṣam āyāti kim atra citram |
children.translated_text: A king, even when served with effort, does not become satisfied — what is surprising in this?

children.text: ayaṃ tv apūrva-pratimā-viśeṣo yaḥ sevyamāno riputām upaiti // Hit_2.158 //
children.translated_text: But this is a unique and extraordinary wonder: that one who is served becomes an enemy. // <s>Hit</s> 2.158 //

body.text: tad ayam aśakyarthaḥ prameyaḥ, yataḥ-
body.translated_text: This matter, impossible to achieve, should be examined. For —

children.text: nimittam uddiśya hi yaḥ prakupyati
children.translated_text: One who becomes angry pointing to a specific cause

children.text: dhruvaṃ sa tasyāpagame prasīdati |
children.translated_text: will surely be appeased when that [cause] is removed;

children.text: akāraṇa-dveṣi manas tu yasya vai
children.translated_text: but one whose mind harbors causeless hatred —

children.text: kathaṃ janas taṃ paritoṣayiṣyati // Hit_2.159 //
children.translated_text: how can anyone satisfy him? // <s>Hit</s> 2.159 //

body.text: kiṃ mayāpakṛtaṃ rājñaḥ | athavā nirnimittāpakāriṇaś ca bhavanti rājānaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'What wrong have I done to the king? Or rather, kings are indeed those who harm without cause.'

body.text: damanako brūte-evam etat | śṛṇu-
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> says: 'That is so. Listen —'

children.text: vijñaiḥ snigdhair upakṛtam api dveṣyatām eti kaiścit
children.translated_text: Even what has been done as a favor by the wise and affectionate becomes hateful to some,

children.text: sākṣād anyair apakṛtam api prītim evopayāti |
children.translated_text: while harm done by others is received with delight.

children.text: citraṃ citraṃ kim atha caritaṃ naikabhāvāśrayāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: Wonderful, wonderful! What can be said of the conduct of those whose nature is manifold?

children.text: sevā-dharmaḥ parama-gahano yoginām apy agamyaḥ // Hit_2.160 //
children.translated_text: The duty of service is supremely difficult to fathom, inaccessible even to <s>yogins</s>. // Hit 2.160 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: kṛta-śatam asatsu naṣṭaṃ subhāṣita-śataṃ ca naṣṭam abudheṣu |
children.translated_text: A hundred favors done for the wicked are lost; a hundred wise sayings are lost on fools;

children.text: vacana-śatam avacana-kare buddhi-śatam acetane naṣṭam // Hit_2.161 //
children.translated_text: a hundred counsels are lost on the disobedient; a hundred (strokes of) wisdom are lost on the senseless. // Hit 2.161 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: candana-taruṣu bhujaṅgā jaleṣu kamalāni tatra ca grāhāḥ |
children.translated_text: On sandalwood trees there are serpents; in waters there are lotuses and there too are crocodiles;

children.text: guṇa-ghātinaś ca bhoge khalā na ca sukhāny avighnāni // Hit_2.162 //
children.translated_text: destroyers of merit accompany enjoyment; the wicked (are everywhere) — and pleasures are never without obstacles. // Hit 2.162 //

children.text: mūlaṃ bhujaṅgaiḥ kusumāni bhṛṅgaiḥ
children.translated_text: The roots (are beset) by serpents, the flowers by bees,

children.text: śākhāḥ plavaṅgaiḥ śikharāṇi bhallaiḥ |
children.translated_text: the branches by monkeys, and the tops by bears —

children.text: nāsty eva tac-candana-pādapasya
children.translated_text: there is no part of the sandalwood tree

children.text: yan nāśritaṃ duṣṭataraiś ca hiṃsraiḥ // Hit_2.163 //
children.translated_text: that is not infested by the most vicious and harmful creatures. // Hit 2.163 //

body.text: ayaṃ tāvat svāmī vāci madhuro viṣa-hṛdayo jñātaḥ | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: 'This master of ours has been found to be sweet in speech but with poison in his heart. For —'

children.text: dūrād ucchrita-pāṇir ādra-nayanaḥ protsāritārdhāsano
children.translated_text: With hand raised from afar, with moist eyes, with seat half-offered,

children.text: gāḍhāliṅgana-tat-paraḥ priya-kathā-praśneṣu dattādaraḥ |
children.translated_text: intent upon tight embrace, showing deference in questions about pleasant news,

children.text: antarbhūta-viṣo bahir madhumayaś cātīva māyā-paṭuḥ
children.translated_text: inwardly poisonous but outwardly honey-sweet, and exceedingly skilled in deception —

children.text: ko nāmāyam apūrva-nāṭaka-vidhir yaḥ śikṣito durjanaiḥ // Hit_2.164 //
children.translated_text: what is this unprecedented theatrical performance that has been taught by the wicked? // Hit 2.164 //

body.text: tathā hi-

children.text: poto dustara-vāri-rāśitaraṇe dīpo 'ndhakārāgame
children.translated_text: A boat for crossing an impassable mass of water, a lamp at the onset of darkness,

children.text: nirvāte vyajanaṃ madāndha-kariṇāṃ darpopaśāntyai sṛṇiḥ |
children.translated_text: a fan in the absence of wind, a goad for subduing the pride of intoxicated elephants —

children.text: itthaṃ tad bhuvi nāsti yasya vidhinā nopāya-cintā kṛtā
children.translated_text: thus there is nothing on earth for which the Creator has not devised a remedy;

children.text: manye durjana-citta-vṛtti-haraṇe dhātāpi bhagnodyamaḥ // Hit_2.165 //
children.translated_text: I think even the Creator has given up the effort to alter the ways of the wicked mind. // Hit 2.165 //

body.translated_text: For indeed —

body.text: saṃjīvakaḥ punar niḥśvasya-kaṣṭaṃ bhoḥ ! katham ahaṃ sasya-bhakṣakaḥ siṃhena nipātayitavyaḥ ? yataḥ-
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> then sighed: 'Alas! How can I, a mere grass-eater, be killed by a lion? For —'

children.text: yayor eva samaṃ vittaṃ yayor eva samaṃ balam |
children.translated_text: A dispute should be considered (possible) only between those whose wealth is equal

children.text: tayor vivādo mantavyo nottamādhamayoḥ kvacit // Hit_2.166 //
children.translated_text: and whose strength is equal — never between a superior and an inferior. // Hit 2.166 //

children.text: ayuddhe hi yadā paśyen na kāñcid hitam ātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: When one sees no benefit to oneself in not fighting,

children.text: yudhyamānas tadā prājño mriyate ripuṇā saha // Hit_2.170 //
children.translated_text: then the wise man, fighting, dies together with the enemy. // Hit 2.170 //

body.text: aparaṃ ca-

children.text: bhūmy-eka-deśasya guṇānvitasya
children.translated_text: The destruction of a single portion of territory that possesses merit,

children.text: bhṛtyasya vā buddhimataḥ praṇāśaḥ |
children.translated_text: or of a wise servant —

children.text: bhṛtya-praṇāśo maraṇaṃ nṛpāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: the destruction of a servant is the death of kings;

children.text: naṣṭāpi bhūmiḥ sulabhā na bhṛtyāḥ // Hit_2.177 //
children.translated_text: lost territory is easily regained, but not servants. // Hit 2.177 //

body.translated_text: And furthermore —

body.text: damanako brūte-svāmin ! ko 'yaṃ nūtano nyāyo yad arātiṃ hatvā santāpaḥ kriyate ? tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> says: 'O master! What is this novel principle that one should grieve after killing an enemy? As it is said —'

children.text: pitā vā yadi vā bhrātā putrī vā yadi vā suhṛt |
children.translated_text: Whether it be a father, or a brother, a son, or a friend —

children.text: prāṇa-ccheda-karā rājñā hantavyā bhūtim icchatā // Hit_2.178 //
children.translated_text: one who threatens life must be killed by a king who desires prosperity. // Hit 2.178 //

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: dharmārtha-kāma-tattvajño naikānta-karuṇo bhavet |
children.translated_text: One who knows the truth of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>artha</s> (wealth), and <s>kāma</s> (desire) should not be exclusively compassionate,

children.text: nahi hastastham apy annaṃ kṣamāvān bhakṣituṃ kṣamaḥ // Hit_2.179 //
children.translated_text: for even a forbearing man is unable to eat the food already in his hand (if overly lenient). // Hit 2.179 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: kṣamā śatrau ca mitre ca yatīnām eva bhūṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: Forbearance toward both enemy and friend is an ornament only for ascetics;

children.text: aparādhiṣu sattveṣu nṛpāṇāṃ saiva dūṣaṇam // Hit_2.180 //
children.translated_text: but for kings, that same (forbearance) toward offending creatures is a blemish. // Hit 2.180 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: rājya-lobhād ahaṅkārād icchataḥ svāminaḥ padam |
children.translated_text: For one who, out of greed for the kingdom and arrogance, desires the position of the master,

children.text: prāyaścittaṃ tu tasyaikaṃ jīvotsargo na cāparam // Hit_2.181 //
children.translated_text: the only atonement is the forfeit of his life — there is no other. // Hit 2.181 //

body.text: anyac ca-

children.text: rājā ghṛṇī brāhmaṇaḥ sarva-bhakṣī
children.translated_text: A king who is (overly) compassionate, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who eats everything,

children.text: strī cāvajñā duṣprakṛtiḥ sahāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: a wife who is disrespectful, an associate of evil disposition,

children.text: preṣyaḥ pratīpo 'dhikṛtaḥ pramādī
children.translated_text: a servant who is hostile, and an officer who is negligent —

children.text: tyājyā ime yaś ca kṛtaṃ na vetti // Hit_2.182 //
children.translated_text: these are to be abandoned, as well as one who does not acknowledge a favor done. // Hit 2.182 //

body.translated_text: And further —

body.text: viśeṣataś ca-

children.text: satyānṛtā ca paruṣā priya-vādinī ca
children.translated_text: Truthful and false, harsh and sweet-speaking,

children.text: hiṃsrā dayālur api cārtha-parā vadānyā |
children.translated_text: violent and compassionate, wealth-seeking and generous,

children.text: nitya-vyayā pracura-ratna-dhanāgamā ca
children.translated_text: constantly spending and with an influx of abundant jewels and wealth —

children.text: vārāṅganeva nṛpa-nītir aneka-rūpā // Hit_2.183 //
children.translated_text: royal policy, like a courtesan, is of many forms. // Hit 2.183 //

body.translated_text: And especially —

body.text: iti damanakena santoṣitaḥ piṅgalakaḥ svāṃ prakṛtim āpannaḥ siṃhāsane samupaviṣṭaḥ | damanakaḥ prahṛṣṭa-manāḥ vijayatāṃ mahārājaḥ śubham astu sarva-jagatām ity uktvā yathā-sukham avasthitaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus, having been pacified by <s>Damanaka</s>, <s>Piṅgalaka</s> returned to his natural state and sat upon his throne. <s>Damanaka</s>, with a joyful heart, said 'Victory to the great king! May all beings prosper!' and remained in comfort.

body.text: viṣṇu-śarmovāca-suhṛd-bhedaḥ śrutas tāvad bhavadbhiḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s> said: 'You have now heard the Separation of Friends (<s>Suhṛdbheda</s>).'

body.text: rāja-putrā ūcuḥ-bhavat-prasādāc chrutaḥ | sukhino bhūtā vayam |
body.translated_text: The princes said: 'We have heard it by your grace. We are delighted.'

body.text: viṣṇuśarmābravīt-aparam apīdam astu-
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s> said: 'May this also be so —'

children.text: suhṛd-bhedas tāvad bhavatu bhavatāṃ śatru-nilaye
children.translated_text: May the Separation of Friends take place in the abode of your enemies;

children.text: khalaḥ kālākṛṣṭaḥ pralayam upasarpatv ahar-ahaḥ |
children.translated_text: may the wicked, dragged by Time, approach destruction day by day;

children.text: jano nityaṃ bhūyāt sakala-sukha-sampatti-vasatiḥ
children.translated_text: may people always be the abode of all happiness and prosperity;

children.text: kathārambhe rambhye satatam iha bālo 'pi ramatām // Hit_2.184 //
children.translated_text: and may even a child always delight in the commencement of this charming tale. // Hit 2.184 //

body.text:
iti hitopadeśe suhṛd-bhedo nāma dvitīyaḥ
kathā-saṅgrahaḥ samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second collection of tales in the <s>Hitopadeśa</s>, called 'The Separation of Friends' (<s>Suhṛdbheda</s>).

body.text:
iii.
vigrahaḥ
body.translated_text:
III.
War (<s>Vigraha</s>)

body.text: atha punaḥ kathārambha-kāle rāja-putrā ūcuḥ-ārya ! rājaputrā vayam | tad vigrahaṃ śrotuṃ naḥ kutūhalam asti | viṣṇuśarmaṇoktam-yad evaṃ bhavadbhyo rocate tat kathayāmi | vigrahaḥ śrūyatāṃ, yasyāyam ādyaḥ ślokaḥ-
body.translated_text: Then, at the time of commencing the tale, the princes said: 'Sir! We are princes. Therefore we are curious to hear about War (<s>Vigraha</s>).' <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s> said: 'Since this pleases you, I shall tell it. Listen to War, whose opening verse is —'

children.text: haṃsaiḥ saha mayūrāṇāṃ vigrahe tulya-vikrame |
children.translated_text: In the war between swans and peacocks, which were equally matched in valor,

children.text: viśvāsya vañcitā haṃsāḥ kākaiḥ sthitvāri-mandire // Hit_3.1 //
children.translated_text: the swans were betrayed by crows who dwelt in the enemy's fortress while being trusted. // Hit 3.1 //

body.text: rāja-putrā ūcuḥ-katham etat ? viṣṇuśarmā kathayati-
body.translated_text: The princes said: 'How is that?' <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s> narrates:

body.text: asti karpūradvīpe padmakeli-nāmadheyaṃ saraḥ | tatra hiraṇyagarbho nāma rājahaṃsaḥ prativasati | sa ca sarvair jalacaraiḥ pakṣibhir militvā pakṣi-rājye'bhiṣiktaḥ | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: On <s>Karpūradvīpa</s> (Camphor Island) there is a lake called <s>Padmakelī</s>. There dwells a royal swan named <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>. He was anointed as king of birds by all the aquatic birds together. For —

children.text: yadi na syān narapatiḥ samyaṅ-netā tataḥ prajā |
children.translated_text: If there were no king, a proper leader, then the people

children.text: akarṇa-dhārā jaladhau viplaveteha naur iva // Hit_3.2 //
children.translated_text: would be swept away like a rudderless ship on the ocean. // Hit 3.2 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: prajāṃ saṃrakṣati nṛpaḥ sā vardhayati pārthivam |
children.translated_text: A king protects the people; they (in turn) increase the king's (prosperity);

children.text: vardhanād rakṣaṇaṃ śreyas tad-abhāve sad apy asat // Hit_3.3 //
children.translated_text: increasing is better than (mere) protecting — in its absence, even what exists becomes as if non-existent. // Hit 3.3 //

body.text: ekadāsau rājahaṃsaiḥ suvistīrṇa-kamala-paryaṅke sukhāsīnaḥ parivāra-parivṛtas tiṣṭhati | tataḥ kutaścid deśād āgatya dīrgha-mukho nāma bakaḥ praṇamyopaviṣṭaḥ | rājovāca-dīrghamukha ! daśāntarād āgato 'si | vārtāṃ kathaya |
body.translated_text: One day, that royal swan was seated comfortably on a very wide lotus-couch, surrounded by his retinue. Then, from some (distant) land, a crane named <s>Dīrghamukha</s> (Long-beak) arrived, bowed, and sat down. The king said: 'O <s>Dīrghamukha</s>! You have come from another region. Tell the news.'

body.text: sa brūte-deva ! asti mahatī vārtā | tām ākhyātukāma eva satvaram āgato 'ham | śrūyatām-
body.translated_text: He says: 'O lord! There is great news. Having come in haste, wishing to report it, here I am. Listen —'

body.text: asti jambūdvīpe vindhyo nāma giriḥ | tatra citravarṇo nāma mayūraḥ pakṣirājo nivasati | tasyānucaraiś caradbhiḥ pakṣibhir ahaṃ dagdhāracya-madhye carann avalokitaḥ | pṛṣṭaś ca-kas tvam ? kutaḥ samāgato 'si ?
body.translated_text: 'On <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> (Rose-apple Island) there is a mountain called <s>Vindhya</s>. There dwells a peacock named <s>Citravarṇa</s> (Many-colored), who is the king of birds. His attendant birds, while roaming about, spotted me wandering in the midst of a burnt forest. They asked: "Who are you? Where have you come from?"'

body.text: tadā mayoktam-karpūradvīpasya rājacakravartino hiraṇyagarbhasya rjahaṃsasyānucaro 'haṃ, kautukād deśāntaraṃ draṣṭum āgato 'smi | etac chrutvā pakṣibhir uktam-anayor deśayoḥ ko deśo bhadrataro rājā ca ?
body.translated_text: 'Then I said: "I am a follower of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, the royal swan, the sovereign of <s>Karpūradvīpa</s>. I have come out of curiosity to see other lands." Hearing this, the birds said: "Of these two lands, which is the better, and which king?"'

body.text: tato mayoktam-āḥ kim evam ucyate mahad antaram | yataḥ karpūradvīpaḥ svarga eva | rājahaṃsaś ca dvitīyaḥ svargapatiḥ kathaṃ varṇayituṃ śakyate | atra marusthale patitā yūyaṃ kiṃ kurutha | asmad-deśe gamyatām |
body.translated_text: 'Then I said: "Ah! How can you say such a thing? There is a vast difference! <s>Karpūradvīpa</s> is heaven itself! And the royal swan is a second lord of heaven — how can he be described? Here in this desert you have fallen — what do you do? Come to our land!"'

body.text: tato 'smad-vacanam ākarṇya sarva-pakṣiṇaḥ sakopā babhūvuḥ | tathā coktam-

children.text: payaḥ-pānaṃ bhujaṅgānāṃ kevalaṃ viṣa-vardhanam |
children.translated_text: The drinking of milk by serpents only increases their venom;

children.text: upadeśo hi mūrkhāṇāṃ prakopāya na śāntaye // Hit_3.4 //
children.translated_text: advice to fools leads to anger, not to peace. // Hit 3.4 //

body.translated_text: 'Then, hearing my words, all the birds became angry. As it is said —'

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: vidvān evopadeṣṭavyo nāvidvāṃs tu kadācana |
children.translated_text: One should give advice only to the wise, never to the unwise;

children.text: vānarānupadiśyātha sthāna-bhraṣṭā yayuḥ khagāḥ // Hit_3.5 //
children.translated_text: for having advised monkeys, the birds were displaced from their dwelling. // Hit 3.5 //

body.text: rājovāca-katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The king said: 'How is that?'

body.text:
dīrghamukhaḥ kathayati-
kathā 1
body.translated_text:
<s>Dīrghamukha</s> narrates:
Tale 1

body.text: asti narmadā-tīre parvatopatyakāyāṃ viśālaḥ śālmalī-taruḥ | tatra nirmita-nīḍa-koḍe pakṣiṇaḥ sukhena nivasanti | athaikadā varṣāsu nīlapaṭair iva jaladhara-paṭalair āvṛte nabhas-tale | dhārā-sārair mahatī vṛṣṭir babhūva | tato vānarāṃś ca taru-tale'vasthitān śītākulān kampamānān avalokya, kṛpayā pakṣibhir uktam-bho bho vānarāḥ ! śṛṇuta--

children.text: asmābhir nirmitā nīḍāś cañcu-mātrāhṛtais tṛṇaiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'We have built nests with mere blades of grass carried in our beaks;

children.text: hasta-pādādi-saṃyuktā yūyaṃ kim avasīdatha // Hit_3.6 //
children.translated_text: you, who are endowed with hands, feet, and other limbs — why do you suffer so?' // Hit 3.6 //

body.translated_text: On the bank of the <s>Narmadā</s>, on the slope of a mountain, stands a great <s>śālmalī</s> (silk-cotton) tree. There, birds dwell happily in nests built in its hollows. Now one day, during the rains, when the sky was covered with masses of clouds like blue garments, a great downpour occurred. Then, seeing monkeys huddled at the base of the tree, trembling with cold, the birds said with compassion: 'O monkeys! Listen —'

body.text: tac chrutvā vānarair jātāmarṣair ālocitam-aho ! nirvāta-nīḍa-garbhāvasthitāḥ sukhinaḥ pakṣiṇo 'smān nindanti | tad bhavatu tāvad vṛṣṭer upaśamaḥ |
body.translated_text: Hearing that, the monkeys, filled with indignation, deliberated: 'Ah! These birds, comfortably seated in their windproof nests, mock us! Well then, let the rain stop first.'

body.text: anantaraṃ śānte pānīya-varṣe tair vānarair vṛkṣam āruhya, sarve nīḍā bhagnāḥ, teṣām aṇḍāni cādhaḥ pātitāni | ato 'haṃ bravīmi vidvān evopadeṣṭavyaḥ ity ādi |
body.translated_text: Afterwards, when the rain had ceased, those monkeys climbed the tree, broke all the nests, and dashed their eggs to the ground. Therefore I say: 'One should give advice only to the wise' and so forth.

body.text: rājovāca-tatas taiḥ pakṣibhiḥ kiṃ kṛtam ?
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Then what did those birds do?'

body.text: bakaḥ kathayati-tatas taiḥ pakṣibhiḥ kopād uktam-kenāsau rājahaṃso rājā kṛtaḥ ?
body.translated_text: The crane narrates: 'Then those birds angrily said: "Who made that royal swan a king?"'

body.text: tato mayopajāta-kopenoktam-ayaṃ yuṣmadīyo mayūraḥ kena rājā kṛtaḥ ?
body.translated_text: 'Then I, aroused to anger, said: "Who made this peacock of yours a king?"'

body.text: etac chrutvā te pakṣiṇo māṃ hantum udyatāḥ | tato mayāpi sva-vikramo darśitaḥ | yataḥ-

children.text: anyadā bhūṣaṇaṃ puṃsaḥ kṣamā lajjeva yoṣitaḥ |
children.translated_text: At other times, forbearance adorns a man, as modesty adorns a woman;

children.text: parākramaḥ paribhave vaiyātyaṃ surateṣv iva // Hit_3.7 //
children.translated_text: but valor (adorns) when insulted, as boldness (adorns) in love-making. // Hit 3.7 //

body.translated_text: 'Hearing this, those birds prepared to kill me. So I too displayed my own valor. For —'

children.text: rājā vihasyāha-
children.translated_text: The king laughed and said:

children.text: ātmanaś ca pareṣāṃ ca yaḥ samīkṣya balābalam |
children.translated_text: 'One who, having weighed the strength and weakness

children.text: antaraṃ naiva jānāti sa tiraskriyate'ribhiḥ // Hit_3.8 //
children.translated_text: of himself and of his enemies, does not perceive the difference — he is humiliated by his foes.' // Hit 3.8 //

children.text: suciraṃ hi caran nityaṃ kṣetre satyam abuddhimān |
children.translated_text: 'Though it wandered for a long time, always in the field, the witless one,

children.text: dvīpi-carma-paricchanno vāg-doṣād gardabho hataḥ // Hit_3.9 //
children.translated_text: disguised in a leopard's skin, was killed — the donkey — because of a fault in its voice.' // Hit 3.9 //

body.text: bakaḥ pṛcchati-katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The crane asks: 'How is that?'

body.text:
rājā kathayati-
kathā 2
body.translated_text:
The king narrates:
Tale 2

body.text: asti hastināpure vilāso nāma rajakaḥ | tasya gardabho 'tibhāra-vahanād durbalo mumūrṣur ivābhavat | tatas tena rajakenāsau vyāghracarmaṇā pracchādyāraṇyaka-samīpe sasya-kṣetre vimuktaḥ | tato dūrāt tam avalokya vyāghra-buddhyā kṣetra-patayaḥ satvaraṃ palāyante |
body.translated_text: In <s>Hastināpura</s> there was a washerman named <s>Vilāsa</s>. His donkey had become weak from carrying excessive loads, nearly dying. So the washerman covered it with a tiger's skin and released it in a crop-field near the forest. From afar, seeing it, the field-owners, thinking it was a tiger, fled in haste.

body.text: athaikadā kenāpi sasya-rakṣakeṇa dhūsara-kambala-kṛta-tanu-trāṇena dhanuṣkāṇḍaṃ sajjīkṛtyānata-kāyenaikānte sthitam | taṃ ca dūrād dṛṣṭvā gardabhaḥ puṣṭāṅgo yetheṣṭa-sasya-bhakṣaṇa-jāta-balo gardabho 'yam iti matvoccaiḥ śabdaṃ kurvāṇas tad-abhimukhaṃ dhāvitaḥ | tatas tena sasya-rakṣakeṇa cītkāra-śabdād gardabho 'yam iti niścitya, līlayaiva vyāpāditaḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-suciraṃ hi caran nityam ity ādi |
body.translated_text: Then one day, a certain crop-guard, having covered his body with a grey blanket as armor, having readied his bow and arrows, stood concealed in a corner, bent low. The donkey, seeing him from afar — now robust and strong from eating crops at will — thinking 'this is a donkey,' brayed loudly and ran toward him. Then that crop-guard, having determined from the braying that 'this is a donkey,' killed it effortlessly. Therefore I say: 'Though it wandered for a long time, always in the field' and so forth.

body.text: dīrghamukho brūte-tataḥ paścāt taiḥ pakṣibhir uktam-are pāpā duṣṭa-baka ! asmākaṃ bhūmau carann asmākaṃ svāminam adhikṣipasi | tan na kṣantavyam idānīm | ity uktvā sarve māṃ cañcubhir hatvā, sa-kopā ūcuḥ-paśya re mūrkha ! sa haṃsas tava rājā sarvathā mṛduḥ | tasya rājyādhikāro nāsti | yata ekānta-mṛduḥ karatalastham apy arthaṃ rakṣitum akṣamaḥ | sa kathaṃ pṛthivīṃ śāsti ? rājyaṃ vā tasya kim ? tvaṃ ca kūpa-maṇḍūkaḥ | tena tad-āśrayam upadiśasi | śṛṇu-
body.translated_text: <s>Dīrghamukha</s> says: 'Then those birds said: "O wretched, evil crane! Roaming in our territory, you insult our master! This cannot be tolerated now!" Having said this, they all struck me with their beaks, and angrily said: "Look, O fool! That swan-king of yours is altogether soft. He has no qualification for kingship. For one who is exclusively soft is unable to protect even what is already in his hand. How then does he rule the earth? What is his kingdom worth? And you are a frog in a well. That is why you recommend taking refuge with him. Listen —"'

children.text: sevitavyo mahā-vṛkṣaḥ phala-cchāyā-samanvitaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'One should serve a great tree that is endowed with fruit and shade;

children.text: yadi daivāt phalaṃ nāsti cchāyā kena nivāryate // Hit_3.10 //
children.translated_text: even if by fate there is no fruit, who can prevent the shade?' // Hit 3.10 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: hīna-sevā na kartavyā kartavyo mahad āśrayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Service of the inferior should not be rendered; one should seek the shelter of the great;'

children.text: payo 'pi śauṇḍikī-haste vāruṇĪty abhidhīyate // Hit_3.11 //
children.translated_text: Even milk in the hands of a liquor-seller is called liquor. // Hit_3.11 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: mahān apy alpatāṃ yāti nirguṇe guṇa-vistaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Even a great display of virtues becomes diminished when bestowed upon a worthless person,

children.text: ādhārādheya-bhāvena gajendra iva darpaṇe // Hit_3.12 //
children.translated_text: by the relation of container and contained — like a great elephant reflected in a mirror. // Hit_3.12 //

children.text: kintu-
children.translated_text: However —

children.text: ajā siṃha-prasādena vane carati nirbhayam |
children.translated_text: A goat roams fearlessly in the forest by the favor of a lion;

children.text: rāmam āsādya laṅkāyāṃ lebhe rājyaṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ // Hit_3.13 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> obtained the kingdom of <s>Laṅkā</s> by taking refuge with <s>Rāma</s>. // Hit_3.13 //

children.text: viśeṣataś ca-
children.translated_text: And especially —

children.text: vyapadeśe'pi siddhiḥ syād atiśakte narādhipe |
children.translated_text: Success may come even through mere pretense, when the king is exceedingly powerful;

children.text: śaśino vyapadeśena śaśakāḥ sukham āsate // Hit_3.14 //
children.translated_text: by the pretense of the moon, the hares live happily. // Hit_3.14 //

body.text: mayoktam-katham etat ?
body.translated_text: I (the crane) said: "How is that?"

body.text:
pakṣiṇaḥ kathayanti-
kathā 3
body.translated_text:
The birds narrate:
Story 3

body.text: kadācid varṣāsv api vṛṣṭer abhāvāt tṛṣārto gaja-yūtho yūthapatim āha-nātha ! ko 'bhyupāyo 'smākaṃ jīvanāya ? nāsti kṣudra-jantūnāṃ api nimajjana-sthānam | vayaṃ ca nimajjana-sthānābhāvān mṛtāḥ | andhā iva kiṃ kurmaḥ ? kva yāmaḥ ?
body.translated_text: Once during the rainy season, due to lack of rain, a herd of elephants, tormented by thirst, said to the herd-leader: "Lord! What recourse is there for our survival? There is no pool deep enough even for small creatures to immerse in. We shall die for want of a bathing place. Blind as we are, what shall we do? Where shall we go?"

body.text: tato hastirājo nātidūraṃ gatvā nirmalaṃ hradaṃ darśitavān | tato dineṣu gacchatsu tat-tīrāvasthitāḥ kṣudra-śaśakā gaja-pādāhatibhiś cūrṇitāḥ | anantaraṃ śilīmukho nāma śaśakaś cintayāmāsa-anena gajayūthena pipāsākulitena pratyaham atrāgantavyam | tato vinaṣṭam asmat-kulam |
body.translated_text: Then the elephant king, having gone not too far, showed them a clear lake. As the days passed, the small hares dwelling on its banks were crushed by the elephants' footsteps. Thereupon a hare named <s>Śilīmukha</s> (Arrow-face) reflected: "This elephant herd, driven by thirst, will come here daily. Our race will be destroyed."

body.text: tato vijayo nāma vṛddha-śaśako 'vadat-mā viṣīdata | mayātra pratīkāraḥ kartavyaḥ | tato 'sau pratijñāya calitaḥ | gacchatā ca tenālocitam-kathaṃ mayā gaja-yūtha-nātha-samīpe sthitvā vaktavyam | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Then an old hare named <s>Vijaya</s> (Victor) said: "Do not despair! I shall devise a remedy." Having made this pledge, he set out. While going, he considered: "How should I stand and speak before the leader of the elephant herd? For —

children.text: spṛśann api gajo hanti jighrann api bhujaṅgamaḥ |
children.translated_text: An elephant kills even by touching, a serpent even by smelling,

children.text: pālayann api bhūpālaḥ prahasann api durjanaḥ // Hit_3.15 //
children.translated_text: a king even while protecting, and a wicked person even while laughing. // Hit_3.15 //

body.text: ato 'haṃ parvata-śikharam āruhya yūthanāthaṃ saṃvādayāmi | tathānuṣṭhite sati yūthanātha uvāca-kas tvam ? kutaḥ samāyātaḥ ?
body.translated_text: Therefore I shall climb a mountain peak and address the herd-leader." Having done so, the herd-leader asked: "Who are you? Where have you come from?"

body.text: sa brūte-śaśako 'ham | bhagavatā candreṇa bhavad-antikaṃ preṣitaḥ |
body.translated_text: He said: "I am a hare. I have been sent to your presence by the blessed <s>Candra</s> (Moon)."

body.text: yūthapatir āha-kāryam ucyatām |
body.translated_text: The herd-leader said: "State your business."

children.text: vijayo brūte-
children.translated_text: <s>Vijaya</s> said:

children.text: udyateṣv api śastreṣu dūto vadati nānyathā |
children.translated_text: "Even when weapons are raised, a messenger speaks the truth and nothing else,

children.text: sadaivāvadhya-bhāvena yathārthasya hi vācakaḥ // Hit_3.16 //
children.translated_text: for he is always inviolable, being a speaker of what is true. // Hit_3.16 //

body.text: tad ahaṃ tad-ājñayā bravīmi, śṛṇu | yad ete candrasaro-rakṣakāḥ śaśakās tvayā niḥsāritās tad anucitaṃ kṛtam | te śaśakāś ciram asmākaṃ rakṣitāḥ | ata eva me śaśāṅka iti prasiddhiḥ |
body.translated_text: Therefore, by his command I speak — listen. You have driven out the hares who guard <s>Candrasaras</s> (Moon Lake) — that was improper. Those hares have been under my protection for a long time. It is for this very reason that I am renowned as <s>Śaśāṅka</s> (Hare-marked, i.e., the Moon)."

body.text: evam uktavati dūte yūthapatir bhayād idam āha-praṇidhe ! idam ajñānataḥ kṛtam | punar na tatra gamiṣyāmi |
body.translated_text: When the messenger had spoken thus, the herd-leader said in fear: "Emissary! This was done in ignorance. I shall not go there again."

body.text: dūta uvāca-yady evaṃ tad atra sarasi kopāt kampamānaṃ bhagavantaṃ śaśāṅkaṃ praṇamya, prasādya ca gaccha |
body.translated_text: The messenger said: "If so, then come to the lake, bow before the blessed <s>Śaśāṅka</s> (Moon) who is trembling with anger, propitiate him, and then go."

body.text: tatas tena rātrau yūthapatiṃ nītvā, tatra jale cañcalaṃ candra-bimbaṃ darśayitvā sa yūthaptiḥ praṇāmaṃ kāritaḥ | uktaṃ ca tena-deva ! ajñānād anenāparādhaḥ kṛtaḥ | tataḥ kṣamyatām | naivaṃ vārāntaraṃ vidhāsyate | ity uktvā prasthāpitaḥ | ato vayaṃ brūmaḥ-vyapadeśe'pi siddhiḥ syāt iti |
body.translated_text: Then, having led the herd-leader there at night, he showed him the trembling reflection of the moon in the water, and made the herd-leader bow. The herd-leader said: "Lord! This offense was committed in ignorance. Please forgive. It shall not happen again." Having said this, he was sent away. Therefore we say: "Success may come even through mere pretense."

body.text: tato mayoktam-sa evāsmat-prabhū rājahaṃso mahā-pratāpo 'tismarthaḥ | trailokyasyāpi prabhutvaṃ tatra yujyate, kiṃ punā rājyam iti | tadāhaṃ taiḥ pakṣibhiḥ-duṣṭa ! katham asmad-bhūmau carasi ity abhidhāya rājñaś citravarṇasya samīpaṃ nītaḥ | tato rājñaḥ puro māṃ pradarśya taiḥ praṇamyoktam-deva ! avadhīyatām | eṣa duṣṭo 'smad-deśe carann api deva-pādān adhikṣipati |
body.translated_text: Then I (the crane) said: "That very one, our lord the royal swan <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, is of great might and exceedingly powerful. Sovereignty over the three worlds would befit him, let alone a mere kingdom." Then those birds seized me, saying: "Villain! How dare you roam on our territory!" and brought me before King <s>Citravarṇa</s>. Presenting me before the king, they bowed and said: "Your Majesty! Let him be punished. This villain, while roaming in our territory, insults Your Majesty's feet."

body.text: rājāha-ko 'yam ? kutaḥ samāyātaḥ ?
body.translated_text: The king asked: "Who is this? Where has he come from?"

body.text: te ūcuḥ-hiraṇyagarbha-nāmno rājahaṃsasyānucaraḥ karpūradvīpād āgataḥ |
body.translated_text: They said: "He is a follower of the royal swan named <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, come from <s>Karpūradvīpa</s> (Camphor Island)."

body.text: athāhaṃ gṛdhreṇa mantriṇā pṛṣṭaḥ-kas tatra mukhyo mantrī ? iti |
body.translated_text: Then I was questioned by the vulture who was the minister: "Who is the chief minister there?"

body.text: mayoktam-sarva-śāstrārtha-pāragaḥ śarvajño nāma cakravākaḥ |
body.translated_text: I said: "A <s>cakravāka</s> (ruddy goose) named <s>Sarvajña</s> (All-knowing), who has mastered the meaning of all <s>śāstras</s>."
