body.text: gṛdhro brūte-yujyate | sva-deśajo 'sau | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: The vulture said: "That is fitting. He is a native of the land. For —

children.text: svadeśajaṃ kulācāra-viśuddham upadhāśucim |
children.translated_text: A minister should be native-born, of pure family conduct, free from treachery,

children.text: mantrajñam avasaninaṃ vyabhicāra-vivarjitam // Hit_3.17 //
children.translated_text: knowledgeable in counsel, steadfast, and free from transgression; // Hit_3.17 //

children.text: adhīta-vyavahārārthaṃ maulaṃ khyātaṃ vipaścitam |
children.translated_text: learned in the principles of administration, hereditary, renowned, wise,

children.text: arthasyotpādakaṃ caiva vidadhyān mantriṇaṃ nṛpaḥ // Hit_3.18 //
children.translated_text: and a generator of wealth — such a minister should the king appoint. // Hit_3.18 //

body.text: atrāntare śukenoktam-deva ! karpūra-dvīpādayo laghudvīpā jambūdvīpāntargatā eva | tatrāpi deva-pādānām evādhipatyam | tato rājñāpy uktam-evam eva | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: At that point, the parrot said: "Your Majesty! <s>Karpūradvīpa</s> and such small islands are contained within <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> itself. Over that too, Your Majesty alone holds sovereignty." The king also said: "Indeed so. For —

children.text: rājā mattaḥ śiśuś caiva pramadā dhana-garvitaḥ |
children.translated_text: A king who is intoxicated, a child, a woman, and one proud of wealth

children.text: aprāpyam api vāñchanti kiṃ punar labhyate'pi yat // Hit_3.19 //
children.translated_text: desire even the unattainable — how much more what can actually be obtained! // Hit_3.19 //

body.text:
tato mayoktam-yadi vacanam-mātreṇaivādhipatyaṃ siddhyati | tadā jambūdvīpe'py asmat-prabhor hiraṇyagarbhasya svāmyam asti |
śuko brūte-katham atra nirṇayaḥ ?
body.translated_text: Then I said: "If sovereignty is established by mere words, then our lord <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> also has dominion over <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>." The parrot said: "How is this to be decided?"

body.text: mayoktaṃ-saṅgrāma eva |
body.translated_text: I said: "By war itself."

body.text: rājñā vihasyoktam-sva-svāminaṃ gatvā sajjīkuru |
body.translated_text: The king said with a laugh: "Go to your master and prepare him."

body.text: tadā mayoktam-sva-dūto 'pi prasthāpyatām |
body.translated_text: Then I said: "Let your own messenger also be dispatched."

body.text: rājovāca-kaḥ prayāsyati dautyena ? yata evambhūto dūtaḥ kāryaḥ-
body.translated_text: The king said: "Who will go as ambassador? For a messenger should be of this sort —

children.text: bhakto guṇī śucir dakṣaḥ pragalbho 'vyasanī kṣamī |
children.translated_text: Devoted, virtuous, pure, skilled, bold, free from vice, patient,

children.text: brāhmaṇaḥ paramarmajño dūtaḥ syāt pratibhānavān // Hit_3.20 //
children.translated_text: a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a knower of vulnerabilities, and possessed of ready wit — such should be the messenger. // Hit_3.20 //

body.text: gṛdhro vadati-santy eva dūtā bahavaḥ, kintu brāhmaṇa eva kartavyaḥ | yataḥ,
body.translated_text: The vulture said: "There are many messengers, but a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should be employed. For —

children.text: prasādaṃ kurute patyuḥ sampattiṃ nābhivāñchati |
children.translated_text: He wins the lord's favor but does not covet his prosperity;

children.text: kālimā kālakūṭasya nāpaitīśvara-saṅgamāt // Hit_3.21 //
children.translated_text: the blackness of <s>kālakūṭa</s> (deadly poison) does not depart through contact with the Lord. // Hit_3.21 //

body.text: rājāha-tataḥ śuka eva vrajatu | śuka ! tvam evānena saha tatra gatvāsmad-abhilaṣitaṃ brūhi |
body.translated_text: The king said: "Then let the parrot go. O Parrot! You yourself go there with this one and convey my desire."

body.text: śuko brūte-yathājñāpayati devaḥ | kintv ayaṃ durjano bakaḥ | tad anena saha na gacchāmi | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: The parrot said: "As Your Majesty commands. But this is a wicked crane. I will not go with him. And thus it is said —

children.text: khalaḥ karoti durvṛttaṃ nūnaṃ phalati sādhuṣu |
children.translated_text: A villain commits an evil deed, but the punishment surely falls upon the virtuous;

children.text: daśānano 'harat sītāṃ bandhanaṃ syān mahodadheḥ // Hit_3.22 //
children.translated_text: the ten-headed <s>Rāvaṇa</s> abducted <s>Sītā</s>, but it was the ocean that was bound. // Hit_3.22 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: na sthātavyaṃ na gantavyaṃ durjanena samaṃ kvacit |
children.translated_text: One should neither stay nor go anywhere in the company of a wicked person;

children.text: kāka-saṅgād dhato haṃsas tiṣṭhan gachaṃś ca vartakaḥ // Hit_3.23 //
children.translated_text: by association with a crow, the swan was killed while staying, and the quail while going. // Hit_3.23 //

body.text: rājovāca-katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The king asked: "How is that?"

body.text:
śukaḥ kathayati-
kathā 4
body.translated_text:
The parrot narrates:
Story 4

body.text: asty ujjayinī-vartma-prāntare plakṣa-taruḥ | tatra haṃsa-kākau nivasataḥ | kadācit grīṣma-samaye pariśrāntaḥ kaścit pathikas tatra taru-tale dhanuṣkāṇḍaṃ saṃnidhāya suptaḥ | tatra kṣaṇāntare tan-mukhād vṛkṣa-cchāyāpagatā | tataḥ sūrya-tejasā tan-mukhaṃ vyāptam avalokya, tad-vṛkṣa-sthitena puṇya-śīlena śucinā rājahaṃsena kṛpayā pakṣau prasārya punas tan-mukhe chāyā kṛtā | tato nirbhara-nidrā-śukhinā pathi-bhramaṇa-pariśrāntena pānthena mukha-vyādānaṃ kṛtam |
body.translated_text: On the outskirts of the road to <s>Ujjayinī</s> there stood a <s>plakṣa</s> (fig) tree. A swan and a crow lived there. Once in the summer season, a weary traveler placed his bow and quiver there, lay down at the foot of the tree, and fell asleep. After a while, the tree's shade moved away from his face. Then, seeing his face engulfed by the sun's heat, the virtuous and pure royal swan dwelling in that tree, out of compassion, spread its wings and created shade over his face again. Thereupon the traveler, exhausted from wandering on the road, fell into a deep and comfortable sleep, and yawned with his mouth open.

body.text: atha para-sukham asahiṣṇuḥ svabhāva-daurjanyena sa kākas tasya mukhe purīṣotsargaṃ kṛtvā palāyitaḥ | tato yāvad asau pāntha utthāyordhvaṃ nirīkṣate, tāvat tenāvalokito haṃsaḥ kāṇḍena hato vyāpāditaḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-na sthātavyam iti |
body.translated_text: Then the crow, unable to bear another's happiness, by his naturally wicked nature defecated into the traveler's mouth and fled. The traveler, upon rising and looking up, saw the swan, and killed it with an arrow. Therefore I say: "One should neither stay" and so forth.

body.text:
deva ! vartaka-kathām api kathayāmi | śrūyatām-
kathā 5
body.translated_text:
"Your Majesty! I shall also tell the story of the quail. Listen —
Story 5

body.text: ekatra vṛkṣe kāka-vartukau sukhaṃ nivasataḥ | ekadā bhagavato garuḍasya yātrā-prasaṅgena sarve pakṣiṇaḥ samudra-tīraṃ gatāḥ | tataḥ kākena saha vartakaś calitaḥ | atha gacchato gopālasya mastakāvasthita-dadhi-bhāṇḍād vāraṃ vāraṃ tena kākena dadhi khādyate | tato yāvad asau dadhi-bhāṇḍaṃ bhūmau nidhāyordhvam avalokate, tāvat tena kāka-vartakau dṛṣṭau | tatas tena dṛṣṭaḥ kākaḥ palāyitaḥ | vartakaḥ svabhāva-niraparādho manda-gatis tena prāpto vyāpāditaḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-na gantavyam ity ādi |
body.translated_text: A crow and a quail lived happily on a certain tree. One day, on the occasion of a pilgrimage festival of the blessed <s>Garuḍa</s>, all the birds went to the seashore. The quail set out together with the crow. Now, as they were traveling, the crow repeatedly ate curds from the yogurt pot on the head of a passing cowherd. When the cowherd set the pot on the ground and looked up, he saw the crow and the quail. The crow, upon being spotted, fled. The quail, naturally innocent and slow-moving, was caught by the cowherd and killed. Therefore I say: "One should not go" and so forth.

body.text: tato mayoktam-bhrātaḥ śuka ! kim evaṃ bravīṣi ? māṃ prati yathā śrīmad-deva-pādās tathā bhavān api | śukenoktam-astv evam | kintu,
body.translated_text: Then I (the crane) said: "Brother parrot! Why do you speak thus? His Majesty's feet are to me the same as you are." The parrot said: "Be that as it may. But —

children.text: durjanair ucyamānāni saṃmatāni priyāṇy api |
children.translated_text: Even agreeable and pleasing words, when spoken by the wicked,

children.text: akāla-kusumānīva bhayaṃ saṃjanayanti hi // Hit_3.24 //
children.translated_text: generate fear, like flowers blooming out of season. // Hit_3.24 //

body.text: durjanatvaṃ ca bhavato vākyād eva jñātam | yad anayor bhūpālayor vigrahe bhavad-vacanam eva nidānam | paśya-
body.translated_text: And your wickedness is known from your very words. For your speech alone was the cause of this war between the two kings. Look —

children.text: pratyakṣe'pi kṛte doṣe mūrkhaḥ sāntvena tuṣyati |
children.translated_text: Even when the fault is committed in plain sight, a fool is satisfied with flattery;

children.text: ratha-kāro nijāṃ bhāryāṃ sajārāṃ śirasākarot // Hit_3.25 //
children.translated_text: the cartwright carried his own wife, with her lover, on his head. // Hit_3.25 //

body.text: rājñoktam--katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The king asked: "How is that?"

body.text:
śukaḥ kathayati-
kathā 6
body.translated_text:
The parrot narrates:
Story 6

body.text: asti yauvana-śrī-nagare manda-matir nāma rathakāraḥ | sa ca sva-bhāryāṃ bandhakīṃ jānāti | kintu jāreṇa samaṃ sva-cakṣuṣā naika-sthāne paśyati | tato 'sau rathakāraḥ aham anyaṃ grāmaṃ gacchāmīty uktvā calitaḥ | sa kiyad dūraṃ gatvā punar āgatya paryaṅka-tale sva-gṛhe nibhṛtaṃ sthitaḥ | atha rathakāro grāmāntaraṃ gata ity upajāta-viśvāsaḥ sa jāraḥ sandhyā-kāla evāgataḥ | paxcāt tena jāreṇa samaṃ tasmin paryaṅke nirbharaṃ krīḍantī, paryaṅka-tala-sthitasya bhartuḥ kiñcid aṅga-sparśāt svāminaṃ māyāvinaṃ vijñāya, manasi sā viṣaṇṇābhavat |
body.translated_text: In a city called <s>Yauvanaśrī</s> there lived a cartwright named <s>Mandamati</s> (Dull-witted). He knew his wife to be unfaithful. But he saw her with her lover in person at more than one place. Then the cartwright said: "I am going to another village," and departed. Having gone some distance, he returned and hid himself quietly under the bed in his own house. Then the lover, trusting that the cartwright had gone to another village, came at twilight. Afterward, while she was sporting freely with the lover on that very bed, she felt a touch of her husband hiding beneath the bed, and recognizing the schemer as her master, she became distressed at heart.

body.text: tato jāreṇoktam-kim iti tvam adya mayā saha nirbharaṃ na ramase ? vismiteva pratibhāsi me tvam |
body.translated_text: The lover said: "Why do you not sport with me freely today? You seem to me as if astonished."

body.text: atha tayoktam-anabhijño 'si | yo 'sau mama prāṇeśvaro, yena mamākaumāraṃ sakhyaṃ so 'dya grāmāntaraṃ gataḥ | tena vinā sakala-jana-pūrṇo 'pi grāmo māṃ praty araṇyavat pratibhāti | kiṃ bhāvi ? tatra para-sthāne kiṃ khāditavān ? kathaṃ vā prasuptaḥ ? ity asmad-dhṛdayaṃ vidīryate |
body.translated_text: She replied: "You do not understand. My lord, my very life, with whom I have had friendship since childhood, has today gone to another village. Without him, even this village full of people seems to me like a wilderness. What will happen? What has he eaten in that distant place? How has he slept? My heart is breaking with worry."

body.text: jāro brūte-tava kim evaṃvidhā sneha-bhūmī rathakāraḥ ?
body.translated_text: The lover said: "Is the cartwright truly such an object of your love?"

body.text: bandhaky avadat-re barbara ! kiṃ vadasi ? śṛṇu-
body.translated_text: The unfaithful woman said: "Barbarian! What are you saying? Listen —

children.text: paruṣāṇy api yā proktā dṛṣṭā yā krodha-cakṣuṣā |
children.translated_text: She who endures harsh words and is seen with angry eyes,

children.text: suprasanna-mukhī bhartuḥ sā nārī dharma-bhājanam // Hit_3.26 //
children.translated_text: yet remains with a serene face toward her husband — such a woman is a vessel of <s>dharma</s>. // Hit_3.26 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: nagarastho vanastho vā pāpo vā yadi vā śuciḥ |
children.translated_text: Whether he be in the city or in the forest, sinful or pure,

children.text: yāsāṃ strīṇāṃ priyo bhartā tāsāṃ lokā mahodayāḥ // Hit_3.27 //
children.translated_text: those women whose husband is dear to them — their worlds are of the highest glory. // Hit_3.27 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: bhartā hi paramaṃ nāryā bhūṣaṇaṃ bhūṣaṇair vinā |
children.translated_text: A husband is indeed a woman's supreme ornament, without any other ornaments;

children.text: eṣā virahitā tena śobhanāpi na śobhate // Hit_3.28 //
children.translated_text: she who is bereft of him does not shine, even though she be beautiful. // Hit_3.28 //

body.text: tvaṃ ca jāraḥ pāpa-matiḥ, mano-laulyāt puṣpa-tāmbūla-sadṛśaḥ kadācit sevyase, kadācin na sevyase ca | sa ca punar me svāmī , māṃ vikretuṃ, devebhyo, brāhmaṇebhyo vā dātum īśvaraḥ | kiṃ bahunā ? tasmin jīvati jīvāmi | tan-maraṇe cānumaraṇaṃ kariṣyāmīti pratijñā vartate | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: You are a lover, of sinful mind — due to mental fickleness, like flowers and betel, you are sometimes enjoyed and sometimes not. But he is my lord, who has the power to sell me, or to give me to the gods or to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. In brief — if he lives, I live. Upon his death, I shall follow him in death. Such is my vow. For —

children.text: tisraḥ koṭyo 'rdha-koṭī ca yāni lomāni mānave |
children.translated_text: Three and a half crores — that is the number of hairs on a human body.

children.text: tāvat kālaṃ vaset svarge bhartāraṃ yo 'nugacchati // Hit_3.29 //
children.translated_text: She who follows her husband dwells in heaven for that long a time. // Hit_3.29 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: vyāla-grāhī yathā vyālaṃ balād uddharate bilāt |
children.translated_text: Just as a snake-catcher forcibly extracts a snake from its hole,

children.text: tadvad bhartāram ādāya svarga-loke mahīyate // Hit_3.30 //
children.translated_text: so, taking her husband, she is honored in the celestial realm. // Hit_3.30 //

body.text: aparaṃ ca-

children.text: citau pariṣvajya vicetanaṃ patiṃ
children.translated_text: The beloved wife who, embracing her unconscious husband on the funeral pyre,

children.text: priyā hi yā muñcati deham ātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: gives up her own body —

children.text: kṛtvāpi pāpaṃ śata-lakṣam apy asau
children.translated_text: even if she has committed sins numbering a hundred <s>lakṣa</s> (hundreds of thousands),

children.text: patiṃ gṛhītvā sura-lokam āpnuyāt // Hit_3.31 //
children.translated_text: taking her husband, she attains the world of the gods. // Hit_3.31 //

body.translated_text: And further —

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Because —

children.text: yasmai dadyāt pitā tv enāṃ bhrātā vānumate pituḥ |
children.translated_text: To whomever a father gives her, or a brother with the father's consent,

children.text: taṃ śuśrūṣeta jīvantaṃ saṃsthitaṃ ca na laṅghayet // Hit_3.32 //
children.translated_text: she should serve him while he lives, and should not transgress him when he is dead. // Hit_3.32 //

body.text: etat sarvaṃ śrutvā manda-matiḥ sa rathakāraḥ-dhanyo 'haṃ yasyedṛśī priya-vādinī, svāmi-vatsalā ca bhāryā iti manasi nidhāya, tāṃ khaṭvāṃ strī-puruṣa-sahitāṃ mūrdhni kṛtvā sānandaṃ nanarta | ato 'haṃ bravīmi prayakṣe'pi kṛte doṣe ity ādi |
body.translated_text: Having heard all this, that dull-witted carpenter thought, 'Blessed am I, who has such a sweet-speaking, devoted wife,' and placing that cot on his head with the woman and the man on it, he danced with joy. Therefore I say: 'Even when a fault is committed in plain sight...' and so on.

body.text: ato 'haṃ tena rājñā yathā-vyavahāraṃ sampūjya prasthāpitaḥ | śuko 'pi mama paścād āgacchann āste | etat sarvaṃ parijñāya yathā-kartavyam anusandhīyatām |
body.translated_text: Therefore I was honored and sent off by that king in the customary manner. The parrot too has come following after me. Having understood all this, let the proper course of action be deliberated upon.

body.text: cakravāko vihasyāha-deva ! bakena tāvad deśāntaram api gatvā yathā-śakti rāja-kāryam anuṣṭhitam | kintu deva svabhāva eṣa mūrkhānām | yataḥ,
body.translated_text: <s>Cakravāka</s> laughed and said: 'Your Majesty! The crane has indeed gone to another country and performed the royal duty to the best of his ability. But, Your Majesty, such is the nature of fools. For —

children.text: śataṃ dadyān na vivaded iti vijñasya saṃmatam |
children.translated_text: One should give a hundred rather than quarrel — this is the view of the wise;

children.text: vinā hetum api dvandvam etan mūrkhasya lakṣaṇam // Hit_3.33 //
children.translated_text: to engage in conflict without cause — this is the mark of a fool. // Hit_3.33 //

body.text: rājāha-alam anenātītopālambhanena | prastutam anusandhīyatām |
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Enough of this reproach regarding the past. Let the matter at hand be deliberated upon.'

body.text: cakravāko brūte-deva ! vijane bravīmi | yataḥ,
body.translated_text: <s>Cakravāka</s> said: 'Your Majesty! I shall speak in private. For —

children.text: varṇākāra-pratidhvānair netra-vaktra-vikārataḥ |
children.translated_text: From the colors, forms, echoes, and from changes in the eyes and face,

children.text: apy ūhanti mano dhīrās tasmād rahasi mantrayet // Hit_3.34 //
children.translated_text: the wise can divine one's thoughts — therefore one should deliberate in secret. // Hit_3.34 //

body.text: tato rājā mantrī ca tatra sthitau anye'nyatra gatāḥ | cakravāko brūte-deva ! aham evaṃ jānām-kasyāpy asman-niyoginaḥ preraṇayā bakenedam anuṣṭhitam | yataḥ,
body.translated_text: Then the king and the minister remained there while the others went elsewhere. <s>Cakravāka</s> said: 'Your Majesty! I know this much — this was done by the crane at the instigation of some agent of ours. For —

children.text: vedyānām āturaḥ śreyān vyasanī yo niyoginām |
children.translated_text: Among those who need to be known, one who is sick is best; among officials, one who is addicted to vice;

children.text: viduṣāṃ jīvanaṃ mūrkhaḥ sad-varṇo jīvanaṃ satām // Hit_3.35 //
children.translated_text: among the learned, a fool is the livelihood; among the good, one of good repute is the livelihood. // Hit_3.35 //

body.text: rājābravīt-bhavatu, kāraṇam atra paścān nirūpaṇīyam | samprati yat kartavyaṃ tan nirūpyatām |
body.translated_text: The king said: 'So be it, the cause of this shall be investigated later. For now, let the course of action be determined.'

body.text: cakravāko brūte-deva ! praṇidhis tāvat tatra prahīyatām | tatas tad-anuṣṭhānaṃ balābalaṃ ca jānīmaḥ | tathā hi-
body.translated_text: <s>Cakravāka</s> said: 'Your Majesty! First let a spy be sent there. Then we shall know the situation and the balance of strength. For —

children.text: bhavet sva-para-rāṣṭrāṇāṃ kāryākāryāvalokane |
children.translated_text: For observing what should and should not be done in one's own and the enemy's kingdoms,

children.text: cāraś cakṣur mahībhartur yasya nāsty andha eva saḥ // Hit_3.36 //
children.translated_text: spies are the eyes of a king — he who lacks them is indeed blind. // Hit_3.36 //

body.text: sa ca dvitīyaṃ viśvāsa-pātraṃ gṛhītvā yātu | tenāsau svayaṃ tatrāvasthāya, dvitīyaṃ tatratya-mantra-kāryaṃ sunibhṛtaṃ niścitya nigadya prasthāpayati | tathā coktaṃ-
body.translated_text: And let him go taking a second trusted person. Thus, he himself will stay there, and send the second person back after carefully ascertaining the secret deliberations of that place. And it is said —

children.text: tīrthāśrama-sura-sthāne śāstara-vijñāna-hetunā |
children.translated_text: At holy places, hermitages, and temples, under the pretext of scriptural knowledge,

children.text: tapasvi-vyañjanopetaiḥ sva-caraiḥ saha saṃvaset // Hit_3.37 //
children.translated_text: one should employ one's own spies disguised as ascetics. // Hit_3.37 //

body.text: gūḍha-cāraś ca-yo jale sthale ca carati | tato 'sāv eva bako niyujyatām | etādṛśa eva kaścid bako dvitīyatvena prayātu | tad-gṛha-lokāś ca rāja-dvāre tiṣṭhantu | kintu etad api suguptam anuṣṭhātavyam | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: And as for a secret spy — one who moves on water and on land — therefore let that same crane be appointed. Let some other crane of similar nature go as a second. And let his household members remain at the royal court. But this too must be carried out with utmost secrecy. For —

children.text: ṣaṭ-karṇo bhidyate mantras tathā prāptaś ca vārtayā |
children.translated_text: A counsel heard by six ears is betrayed, and likewise one that is discovered through rumor;

children.text: ity ātmanā dvitīyena mantraḥ kāryo mahī-bhṛtā // Hit_3.38 //
children.translated_text: therefore a king should deliberate with only one other person. // Hit_3.38 //

children.text: paśya-
children.translated_text: Consider —

children.text: mantra-bhede hi ye doṣā bhavanti pṛthivī-pateḥ |
children.translated_text: The disasters that befall a king when counsel is betrayed

children.text: na śakyās te samādhātum iti nīti-vidāṃ matam // Hit_3.39 //
children.translated_text: cannot be remedied — this is the opinion of those versed in statecraft. // Hit_3.39 //

body.text: rājā vimṛśyovāca-prāptas tāvan mayottamaḥ pratinidhiḥ |
body.translated_text: The king, having reflected, said: 'I have indeed obtained an excellent envoy.'

body.text: mantrī brūte-deva ! saṅgrāme vijayo 'pi prāptaḥ |
body.translated_text: The minister said: 'Your Majesty! Victory in war has also been achieved.'

body.text: atrāntare pratīhāraḥ praviśya praṇamyovāca-deva ! jambūdvīpād āgato dvāri śukas tiṣṭhati |
body.translated_text: At that moment, the doorkeeper entered, bowed, and said: 'Your Majesty! A parrot named <s>Śuka</s>, arrived from <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, stands at the door.'

body.text: rājā cakravākam ālokate | cakravākenoktam-kṛtāvāse tāvad gatvā tiṣṭhatu, paścād ānīya draṣṭavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: The king looked at <s>Cakravāka</s>. <s>Cakravāka</s> said: 'Let him go and stay in his appointed quarters for now; he shall be brought and seen later.'

body.text: yathājñāpayati devaḥ ity abhidhāya pratīhāraḥ śukaṃ gṛhītvā tam āvāsa-sthānaṃ gataḥ | rājāha-vigrahas tāvat samupasthitaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'As Your Majesty commands,' saying this, the doorkeeper took the parrot and went to those quarters. The king said: 'War is now upon us.'

body.text: cakravāko brūte-deva ! tathāpi prāg eva vigraho na vidhiḥ | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: <s>Cakravāka</s> said: 'Your Majesty! Even so, war should not be the first course of action. For —

children.text: sa kiṃ bhṛtyaḥ sa kiṃ mantrī ya ādāv eva bhūpatim |
children.translated_text: What kind of servant is he, what kind of minister, who from the very beginning

children.text: yuddhodyogaṃ sva-bhū-tyāgaṃ nirdiśaty avicāritam // Hit_3.40 //
children.translated_text: advises the king to undertake war and abandon his own territory without due deliberation? // Hit_3.40 //

body.text:
aparaṃ ca-
vijetuṃ prayatetārīn na yuddhena kadācana |

children.text: anityo vijayo yasmād dṛśyate yudhyamānayoḥ // Hit_3.41|
children.translated_text: for victory is uncertain, as can be seen between two combatants. // Hit_3.41 //

body.translated_text:
And moreover —
one should strive to conquer enemies, but never through war,

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: sāmnā dānena bhedena samastair athavā pṛthak |
children.translated_text: Through conciliation, through gifts, through creating dissension — either all together or separately —

children.text: sādhituṃ prayatetārīn na yuddhena kadācana // Hit_3.42 //
children.translated_text: one should strive to subdue enemies, but never through war. // Hit_3.42 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: sarva eva janaḥ śūro hy anāsādita-vigrahaḥ |
children.translated_text: Everyone indeed is a hero who has not yet encountered battle;

children.text: adṛṣṭa-para-sāmarthyaḥ sa-darpaḥ ko bhaven na hi // Hit_3.43 //
children.translated_text: who would not be proud, having not seen the prowess of the enemy? // Hit_3.43 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Furthermore —

children.text: na tathotthāpyate grāvā prāṇibhir dāruṇā yathā |
children.translated_text: A stone cannot be lifted by living beings as violently as wood can;

children.text: alpopāyān mahā-siddhir etan-mantra-phalaṃ mahat // Hit_3.44 //
children.translated_text: great success through small means — this is the supreme fruit of counsel. // Hit_3.44 //

body.text: kintu vigraham upasthitaṃ vilokya vyavahriyatām, yataḥ-
body.translated_text: However, seeing that war is upon us, let action be taken accordingly, for —

children.text: yathā kāla-kṛtodyogāt kṛṣiḥ phalavatī bhavet |
children.translated_text: Just as agriculture becomes fruitful through effort made at the proper season,

children.text: tadvan nītir iyaṃ deva cirāt phalati na kṣaṇāt // Hit_3.45 //
children.translated_text: so too this policy, O king, bears fruit over time, not in an instant. // Hit_3.45 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: dūre bhīrutvam āsanne śūratā mahato guṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Timidity from afar, valor when close — this is a great quality;

children.text: vipattau hi mahān loke dhīratvam adhigacchati // Hit_3.46 //
children.translated_text: for in adversity, the great in this world attain steadfastness. // Hit_3.46 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: pratyūhaḥ sarva-siddhīnām uttāpaḥ prathamaḥ kila |
children.translated_text: The first obstacle to all accomplishments is indeed anxiety;

children.text: atiśītalam apy ambhaḥ kiṃ bhinatti na bhūbhṛtaḥ // Hit_3.47 //
children.translated_text: does not even the coldest water break apart mountains? // Hit_3.47 //

children.text: balinā saha yoddhavyam iti nāsti nidarśanam |
children.translated_text: There is no precedent for fighting against a strong enemy;

children.text: tad yuddhaṃ hastinā sārdhaṃ narāṇāṃ mṛtyum āvahet // Hit_3.48 //
children.translated_text: such a battle with an elephant would bring death to men. // Hit_3.48 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: sa mūrkhaḥ kālam aprāpya yo 'pakartari vartate |
children.translated_text: He is a fool who acts against a wrongdoer before the proper time arrives,

children.text: kalir balavatā sārdhaṃ kīṭa-pakṣodgamo yathā // Hit_3.49 //
children.translated_text: like a quarrel with a powerful one, like an insect trying to grow wings. // Hit_3.49 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Furthermore —

children.text: kaurmaṃ saṅkocam āsthāya prahāram api marṣayet |
children.translated_text: Adopting the tortoise-like posture of withdrawal, one should endure even a blow;

children.text: prāpta-kāle tu nītijña uttiṣṭhet krūra-sarpavat // Hit_3.50 //
children.translated_text: but when the right time comes, the one skilled in policy should rise up like a fierce serpent. // Hit_3.50 //

children.text: mahaty alpe'py upāyajñaḥ samam eva bhavet kṣamaḥ |
children.translated_text: One skilled in expedients should be equally capable in great and small matters,

children.text: samunmūlayituṃ vṛkṣāṃs tṛṇānīva nadīrayaḥ // Hit_3.51 //
children.translated_text: like a river's current that can uproot trees as easily as blades of grass. // Hit_3.51 //

body.text: ato dūto 'yaṃ śuko 'trāśvāsya tāvad dhriyatāṃ yāvad durgaṃ sajjīkriyate, yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Therefore, let this envoy, the parrot, be reassured and detained here until the fortress is made ready, for —

children.text: ekaḥ śataṃ yodhayati prākāra-stho dhanurdharaḥ |
children.translated_text: A single archer stationed on a rampart can fight a hundred;

children.text: śataṃ śata-sahasrāṇi tasmād durgaṃ viśiṣyate // Hit_3.52 //
children.translated_text: a hundred can fight a hundred thousand — therefore a fortress is of supreme importance. // Hit_3.52 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Furthermore —

children.text: adurga-viṣayaḥ kasya nāreḥ paribhavāspadam |
children.translated_text: Whose territory without a fortress is not a seat of contempt for the enemy?

children.text: adurgo 'nāśrayo rājā pota-cyuta-manuṣyavat // Hit_3.53 //
children.translated_text: A king without a fortress is without refuge, like a man fallen from a ship. // Hit_3.53 //

children.text: durgaṃ kuryān mahākhātam ucca-prākāra-saṃyutam |
children.translated_text: One should build a fortress with a great moat, equipped with high ramparts,

children.text: sa-yantraṃ sa-jalaṃ śaila-sarin-maru-vanāśrayam // Hit_3.54 //
children.translated_text: with machines and water supply, situated near a mountain, river, desert, or forest. // Hit_3.54 //

children.text: vistīrṇatāti-vaiṣamyaṃ rasa-dhānyedhma-saṅgrahaḥ |
children.translated_text: Spaciousness, extreme ruggedness, stores of provisions, grain, and fuel,

children.text: praveśaś cāpa-sāraś ca saptaitā durga-sampadaḥ // Hit_3.55 //
children.translated_text: an entrance, and an interior retreat — these are the seven excellences of a fortress. // Hit_3.55 //

body.text: rājāha-durgānusandhāne ko niyujyatām ?
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Who should be appointed to oversee the fortress?'

body.text: cakravāko brūte-
body.translated_text: <s>Cakravāka</s> said —

children.text: yo yatra kuśalaḥ kārye taṃ tatra viniyojayet |
children.translated_text: One who is skilled in a particular task should be assigned to that task;

children.text: karmasv adṛṣṭa-karmā yaḥ śāstrajño 'pi vimuhyati // Hit_3.56 //
children.translated_text: one who is untested in practical work, even if learned in the <s>śāstras</s>, becomes bewildered. // Hit_3.56 //

body.text: tadāhūyatāṃ sārasaḥ | tathānuṣṭhite sati samāgataṃ sārasam avalokya rājovāca-bhoḥ sārasa ! tvaṃ satvaraṃ durgam anusandhehi |
body.translated_text: Then let the <s>Sārasa</s> (crane) be summoned.' When this was done, seeing the crane who had arrived, the king said: 'O <s>Sārasa</s>! You must prepare the fortress without delay.'

body.text: sārasaḥ praṇamyovāca-deva ! durgaṃ tāvad idam eva cirāt sunirūpitam āste mahat saraḥ | kintv etan-madhya-dvīpe dravya-saṅgrahaḥ kriyatām | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: <s>Sārasa</s> bowed and said: 'Your Majesty! This great lake itself has long been well-surveyed as a fortress. However, let stores of supplies be gathered on the island in its midst. For —

children.text: dhānyānāṃ saṅgraho rājann uttamaḥ sarva-saṅgrahāt |
children.translated_text: Among all stores, O king, the store of grain is the best;

children.text: nikṣiptaṃ hi mukhe ratnaṃ na kuryāt prāṇa-dhāraṇam // Hit_3.57 //
children.translated_text: for a jewel placed in the mouth does not sustain life. // Hit_3.57 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Furthermore —

children.text: khyātaḥ sarva-rasānāṃ hi lavaṇo rasa uttamaḥ |
children.translated_text: Among all flavors, the salt flavor is renowned as the best;

children.text: gṛhṇīyāt taṃ vinā tena vyañjanaṃ gomayāyate // Hit_3.58 //
children.translated_text: without it, food tastes like cow dung. // Hit_3.58 //

body.text: rājāha-satvaraṃ gatvā sarvam anuṣṭhīyatām |
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Go quickly and carry out everything.'

body.text: punaḥ praviśya pratīhāro brūte-deva ! siṃhala-dvīpād āgato meghavarṇo nāma vāyasaḥ saparivāro dvāri vartate | sa ca deva-pādān draṣṭum icchati |
body.translated_text: Again the doorkeeper entered and said: 'Your Majesty! A crow named <s>Meghavarṇa</s>, arrived from <s>Siṃhaladvīpa</s>, stands at the door with his retinue. He wishes to see Your Majesty.'

body.text: rājāha-kākaḥ prājño bahudṛśvā ca tad bhavati sa saṅgrāhyaḥ |
body.translated_text: The king said: 'A crow is clever and experienced — therefore he should be taken in.'

body.text: cakravāko brūte-deva ! asty evaṃ | kintu asmad-vipakṣaḥ kākaḥ sthalacaraḥ | tenāsmad-vipakṣa-pakṣe niyuktaḥ kathaṃ saṅgṛhyate ? tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: <s>Cakravāka</s> said: 'Your Majesty! That is true. But a crow is a land-dweller and thus belongs to our enemy's party. How can one employed on the enemy's side be taken in? For it is said —

children.text: ātma-pakṣaṃ parityajya para-pakṣeṣu yo rataḥ |
children.translated_text: He who abandons his own side and delights in the enemy's side,

children.text: sa parair hanyate mūḍho nīla-varṇa-śṛgālavat // Hit_3.59 //
children.translated_text: that fool is destroyed by his enemies — like the blue-colored jackal. // Hit_3.59 //

body.text: rājovāca--katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The king said: 'How is that?'

body.text: mantrī kathayati-
body.translated_text: The minister narrates —

body.text: kathā 7
body.translated_text: Story 7

body.text: asty araṇye kaścic chṛgālaḥ svecchayā nagaropānte bhrāmyan nīlībhāṇḍe nipatitaḥ | paścāt tata utthātum asamarthaḥ, prātar ātmānaṃ mṛtavat sandarśya sthitaḥ | atha nīlī-bhāṇḍa-svāminā mṛti iti jñātvā, tasmāt samutthāpya, dūre nītvāsau parityaktaḥ | tasmāt palāyitaḥ |
body.translated_text: There was a jackal in the forest who, while wandering near a town as he pleased, fell into a vat of indigo dye. Afterward, unable to climb out, in the morning he stood still pretending to be dead. Then the owner of the indigo vat, thinking him dead, lifted him out, carried him far away, and abandoned him. He then fled from there.

body.text: tato 'sau vane gatvā ātmānaṃ nīlapvarṇam avalokyācintayat-aham idānīm uttama-varṇaḥ | tad ahaṃ svakīyotkarṣaṃ kiṃ na sādhayāmi ity ālocya śṛgālān āhūya, tenoktaṃ-ahaṃ bhagavatyā vana-devatayā sva-hastenāraṇya-rājye sarvauṣadhi-rasenābhiṣiktaḥ | paśyantu mama varṇam | tad adyārabhyāsmad-ājñayāsminn araṇye vyavahāraḥ kāryaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then, going into the forest and seeing himself to be blue-colored, he thought: 'Now I am of the most excellent color. Should I not bring about my own elevation?' Having thus reflected, he summoned the jackals and said to them: 'I have been anointed by the blessed forest-goddess with her own hand, with the juice of all herbs, to be king of the forest. Behold my color! Therefore, from today onward, all affairs in this forest shall be conducted by my command.'

body.text:
śṛgālāś ca taṃ viśiṣṭa-varṇam avalokya, sāṣṭāṅga-pātaṃ praṇamyocuḥ-yathājñāpayati devaḥ iti | anenaiva krameṇa sarveṣv araṇya-vāsiṣv ādhipatyaṃ tasya babhūva | tatas tena svajñātibhir āvṛtenādhikyaṃ sādhitam | tatas tena vyāghra-siṃhādīn uttama-parijanān prāpya, sadasi śṛgālān avalokya lajjamānenāvajñayā svajñātayaḥ sarve dūrīkṛtāḥ | tato viṣaṇṇān śṛgālān avalokya kenacid vṛddha-śṛgālenaitat pratijñātaṃ-mā viṣīdata, yad anenānītijñena vayaṃ marmajñāḥ | sva-samīpāt paribhūtās tad yathāyaṃ naśyati tathā vidheyam | yato 'mī vyāghrādayo varṇa-mātra-vipralabdhāḥ śṛgālam ajñātvā rājānam imaṃ manyante | tad yathāyaṃ paricīyate tathā kuruta | tatra caivam anuṣṭheyam, yathā vadāmi-sarve sandhyā-samaye
tat-sannidhāne mahārāvam ekadaiva kariṣyatha | tatas taṃ śabdam ākarṇya jāti-svabhāvāt tenāpi śabdaḥ kartavyaḥ | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: And the jackals, seeing his extraordinary color, prostrated themselves in full obeisance and said: 'As Your Majesty commands.' In this very manner, he established sovereignty over all the forest-dwellers. Then, surrounded by his own kinsmen, he achieved supremacy. Then, having obtained tigers, lions, and other noble attendants, seeing jackals in the court and feeling ashamed, he contemptuously banished all his own kinsmen. Then, seeing the dejected jackals, an old jackal made this vow: 'Do not despair! We, who know his vulnerable points, have been insulted by this one who knows nothing of statecraft — we who were at his side. So let it be arranged that he perishes. For these tigers and others, deceived merely by his color, not knowing he is a jackal, consider him their king. Therefore do what I say so that he is exposed. Here is the plan — listen to what I say: all of you, at twilight, in his presence, will let out a great howl simultaneously. Then, hearing that sound, by his natural instinct, he too will howl. For —

children.text: yaḥ svabhāvo hi yasyāsti sa nityaṃ duratikramaḥ |
children.translated_text: Whatever is one's nature, that is always difficult to overcome;

children.text: śvā yadi kriyate rājā tat kiṃ nāśnāty upānaham // Hit_3.60 //
children.translated_text: if a dog is made king, does he not still chew a shoe? // Hit_3.60 //

body.text: tataḥ śabdād abhijñāya sa vyāghreṇa hantavyaḥ | tatas tathānuṣṭhite sati tad vṛttam | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: Then, recognized by his howl, he shall be killed by the tiger.' When this was carried out, that is exactly what happened. And it is said —

children.text: chidraṃ marma ca vīryaṃ ca sarvaṃ vetti nijo ripuḥ |
children.translated_text: One's own enemy knows one's weakness, one's vulnerable point, and one's strength entirely;

children.text: dahaty antargataś caiva śuṣkaṃ vṛkṣam ivānalaḥ // Hit_3.61 //
children.translated_text: dwelling within, he burns like fire within a dry tree. // Hit_3.61 //

body.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-ātma-pakṣaṃ parityajyety ādi |
body.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'He who abandons his own side...' and so on.

body.text: rājāha-yady evaṃ tathāpi dṛśyatāṃ tāvad ayaṃ dūrād āgataḥ | tat-saṅgrahe vicāraḥ kāryaḥ |
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Even if it be so, let this one who has come from afar be seen; deliberation should be made regarding his reception.'

body.text: cakro brūte-deva ! praṇidhis tāvat prahito, durgaṃ ca sajjīkṛtam | ataḥ śuko 'py ānīya prasthāpyatām | kintu yodha-bala-samanvito bhūtvā, dūrād eva tam avalokaya | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: <s>Cakra</s> (<s>Cakravāka</s>) says: 'Your Majesty! A spy has already been dispatched and the fortress has been made ready. Therefore let the parrot too be brought and sent off. But, being accompanied by a warrior force, observe him from a distance only. For —'

children.text: nandaṃ jaghāna cāṇakyas tīkṣṇa-dūta-prayogataḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Cāṇakya</s> slew <s>Nanda</s> through the deployment of a cunning envoy;

children.text: tad dūrāntaritaṃ dūtaṃ paśyed vīra-samanvitaḥ // Hit_3.62 //
children.translated_text: therefore one should see an envoy from a distance, accompanied by heroes. // Hit 3.62 //

body.text: tataḥ sabhāṃ kṛtvāhūtaḥ śukaḥ kākaś ca | śukaḥ kiṃcid unnata-śirā dattāsane upaviśya brūte-bho hiraṇyagarbha ! tvāṃ mahārājādhirājaḥ śrīmac-citravarṇaḥ samājñāpayati-yadi jīvitena śriyā vā prayojanam asti, tadā satvaram āgatyāsmac-caraṇau praṇama | no ced avasthātuṃ sthānāntaraṃ paricintaya |
body.translated_text: Then, having convened the assembly, the parrot and the crow were summoned. The parrot, with head slightly raised, having seated himself on the offered seat, spoke: 'O <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>! The great king of kings, the illustrious <s>Citravarṇa</s>, commands you thus — if you have need of life or prosperity, then come quickly and bow at our feet; otherwise, think of another place to stay.'

body.text: rājā sa-kopam āha-āḥ, sabhāyām asmākaṃ na ko 'pi vidyate ya enaṃ galahastayati ? tata utthāya meghavarṇo brūte-deva ! ājñāpaya, hami cainaṃ duṣṭa-śukam |
body.translated_text: The king said angrily: 'What! Is there no one in our assembly who will seize this one by the throat?' Thereupon <s>Meghavarṇa</s> (the crow) rose and said: 'Your Majesty! Give the order — I shall [deal with] this wicked parrot.'

body.text: sarvajño rājānaṃ kākaṃ ca sāntvayan brūte-bhadra ! mā maivam | śṛṇu tāvat-
body.translated_text: <s>Sarvajña</s> (the all-knowing one), pacifying both the king and the crow, said: 'Good sir! Do not do so! Listen first —'

children.text: na sā sabhā yatra na santi vṛddhā
children.translated_text: That is no assembly where there are no elders;

children.text: vṛddhā na te ye na vadanti dharmam |
children.translated_text: they are no elders who do not speak of <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: dharmaḥ sa no yatra na satyam asti
children.translated_text: that is no <s>dharma</s> where there is no truth;

children.text: satyaṃ na tad yac chalam abhyupaiti // Hit_3.63 //
children.translated_text: that is no truth which resorts to fraud. // Hit 3.63 //

children.text: yato rājadharmaś caiṣaḥ-
children.translated_text: For this is the law of kings:

children.text: dūto mleccho 'py avadhyaḥ syād rājā dūta-mukho yataḥ |
children.translated_text: An envoy, even a barbarian (<s>mleccha</s>), should not be killed, since the king speaks through the envoy's mouth;

children.text: udyateṣv api śastreṣu dūto vadati nānyathā // Hit_3.64 //
children.translated_text: even when weapons are raised, an envoy speaks [freely] — not otherwise. // Hit 3.64 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: svāpakarṣaṃ parotkarṣaṃ dūtoktair manyate tu kaḥ |
children.translated_text: Who would take self-diminishment and the other's exaltation [to heart] from the words of an envoy?

children.text: sadaivāvadhya-bhāvena dūtaḥ sarvaṃ hi jalpati // Hit_3.65 //
children.translated_text: For an envoy, being always inviolable, prattles on about everything. // Hit 3.65 //

body.text: tato rājā kākaś ca svāṃ prakṛtim āpannau | śuko 'py utthāya calitaḥ | paścāc cakravākeṇānīya prabodhya kanakālaṅkārādikaṃ datvā sampreṣitaḥ svadeśaṃ yayau | śuko 'pi vindhyācalaṃ gatvā, svasya rājānaṃ citravarṇaṃ praṇatavān |
body.translated_text: Then the king and the crow returned to their own composure. The parrot too rose and departed. Afterwards, <s>Cakravāka</s>, having brought [the parrot] back, revived him, and having given him golden ornaments and the like, dispatched him; [the parrot] went to his own country. The parrot, having gone to the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain, prostrated before his own king <s>Citravarṇa</s>.

body.text: taṃ vilokya rājovāca-śuka ! kā vārtā ? kīdṛśo 'sau deśaḥ ?
body.translated_text: Seeing him, the king said: 'Parrot! What news? What is that country like?'

body.text: śuko brūte-deva ! saṃkṣepād iyaṃ vārtā | samprati yuddhodyogaḥ kriyatām | deśaś cāsau karpūra-dvīpaḥ svargaika-deśo, rājā ca dvitīyaḥ svarga-patiḥ kathaṃ varṇayituṃ śakyate | tataḥ sarvān śiṣṭān āhūya rājā mantrayitum upaviṣṭaḥ | āha ca tān-samprati kartavye vigrahe yathā-kartavyam upadeśaṃ brūta | vigrahaḥ punar avaśyaṃ kartavyaḥ | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: The parrot says: 'Your Majesty! In brief, here is the news: now let preparations for war be made. That country, <s>Karpūra-dvīpa</s> (Camphor Island), is a portion of heaven itself; and the king is a second lord of heaven — how can it be described?' Then, having summoned all the counselors, the king sat down to deliberate. And he said to them: 'Now, regarding the war that must be undertaken, tell me the proper course of action. War must certainly be waged.' For it is said —

children.text: asantuṣṭā dvijā naṣṭāḥ santuṣṭāś ca mahībhṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: Dissatisfied <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are ruined; contented kings are ruined;

children.text: salajjā gaṇikā naṣṭā nirlajjāś ca kulāṅganā // Hit_3.66 //
children.translated_text: a modest courtesan is ruined; and a shameless woman of good family [is also ruined]. // Hit 3.66 //

body.text: dūradarśī nāma gṛdhro mantrī brūte-deva ! vyasanitayā vigraho na vidhiḥ | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: The vulture minister named <s>Dūradarśī</s> (Far-sighted) says: 'Your Majesty! War undertaken out of wantonness is not the [proper] course. For —'

children.text: mitrāmātya-suhṛd-vargā yadā syur dṛḍha-bhaktayaḥ |
children.translated_text: When friends, ministers, and allies are of firm devotion,

children.text: śatrūṇāṃ viparītāś ca kartavyo vigrahas tadā // Hit_3.67 //
children.translated_text: and the enemy's [allies] are the opposite — then war should be undertaken. // Hit 3.67 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: bhūmir mitraṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca vigrahasya phalaṃ trayam |
children.translated_text: Land, allies, and gold — these are the three fruits of war;

children.text: yadaitan niścitaṃ bhāvi kartavyo vigrahas tadā // Hit_3.68 //
children.translated_text: when these are certain to be gained, then war should be undertaken. // Hit 3.68 //

body.text: rājāha-mad-balaṃ tāvad avalokayatu mantrī | tadaiteṣām upayogo jñāyatām | evam āhūyatāṃ mauhūrtikaḥ | sa yātrārthaṃ śubha-lagnaṃ nirṇīya dadātu |
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Let the minister survey my forces! Let the use of these [forces] be ascertained. Thus, let the astrologer be summoned. Let him determine and announce an auspicious moment for the march.'

body.text: mantrī brūte-deva ! tathāpi sahasā yātrā-karaṇam anucitam | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: The minister says: 'Your Majesty! Even so, a hasty march is improper. For —'

children.text: viśanti sahasā mūḍhā ye'vicārya dviṣad-balam |
children.translated_text: Those fools who rashly advance without considering the enemy's strength

children.text: khaḍga-dhārā-pariṣvaṅgaṃ labhante te suniścitam // Hit_3.69 //
children.translated_text: surely receive the embrace of the sword's edge. // Hit 3.69 //

body.text: rājāha-mantrin ! mamotsāha-bhaṅgaṃ sarvathā mā kṛthāḥ | vijigīṣur yathā para-bhūmim ākramati tathā kathaya |
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Minister! Do not by any means break my enthusiasm! Tell me how one who desires conquest should invade the enemy's territory.'

body.text: gṛdhro brūte-deva ! tat kathayāmi | kintu tad-anuṣṭhitam eva phala-pradam | tathā coktam-

children.text: kiṃ mantreṇānanuṣṭhāne śāstravit pṛthivī-pateḥ |
children.translated_text: What use is counsel without execution to a king versed in the scriptures?

children.text: na hy auṣadha-parijñānād vyādheḥ śāntiḥ kvacid bhavet // Hit_3.70 //
children.translated_text: For merely from knowledge of medicines, no disease is ever cured. // Hit 3.70 //

body.translated_text: The vulture says: 'Your Majesty! I shall tell you. But it yields fruit only when put into practice. For it is said —'

body.text: rājādeśaś cānatikramaṇīya iti yathā-śrutaṃ nivedayāmi śṛṇu-deva !
body.translated_text: 'And the king's command must not be transgressed; therefore I report what I have learned. Listen, Your Majesty!'

children.text: nady-adri-vana-durgeṣu yatra yatra bhayaṃ nṛpa |
children.translated_text: 'At rivers, mountains, forests, and fortresses — wherever there is danger, O king,

children.text: tatra tatra ca senānīr yāyād vyūhīkṛtair balaiḥ // Hit_3.71 //
children.translated_text: there the commander should march with forces arranged in battle formation. // Hit 3.71 //'

children.text: balādhyakṣaḥ puro yāyāt pravīra-puruṣānvitaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The commander of forces should march at the front, accompanied by brave warriors;

children.text: madhye kalatraṃ svāmī ca kośaḥ phalgu ca yad balam // Hit_3.72 //
children.translated_text: in the middle [should be] the royal household, the king himself, the treasury, and whatever weaker forces there are. // Hit 3.72 //'

children.text: pārśvayor ubhayor aśvā aśvānāṃ pārśvato rathāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'On both flanks [should be] horses; beside the horses, chariots;

children.text: rathānāṃ pārśvato nāgā nāgānāṃ ca padātayaḥ // Hit_3.73 //
children.translated_text: beside the chariots, elephants; and beside the elephants, foot-soldiers. // Hit 3.73 //'

children.text: paścāt senāpatir yāyāt khinnānāśvāsayan chanaiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The general should march at the rear, slowly encouraging the weary;

children.text: mantribhiḥ subhaṭair yuktaḥ pratigṛhya balaṃ nṛpaḥ // Hit_3.74 //
children.translated_text: the king, accompanied by counselors and champions, receiving the [rear] forces, // Hit 3.74 //'

children.text: sameyād viṣamaṃ nāgair jalāḍhyaṃ samahīdharam |
children.translated_text: 'should cross rough terrain with elephants, and watery [ground] with [elephants] as well;

children.text: samam aśvair jalaṃ nīmiḥ sarvatraiva padātibhiḥ // Hit_3.75 //
children.translated_text: level ground with horses, water with boats, and everywhere with foot-soldiers. // Hit 3.75 //'

children.text: hastināṃ gamanaṃ proktaṃ praśastaṃ jaladāgame |
children.translated_text: 'The movement of elephants is said to be auspicious at the onset of the rains;

children.text: tad anyatra turaṅgāṇāṃ pattīnāṃ sarvadaiva hi // Hit_3.76 //
children.translated_text: that of horses and foot-soldiers is [auspicious] at other times, indeed always. // Hit 3.76 //'

children.text: śaileṣu durga-mārgeṣu vidheyaṃ nṛpa-rakṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: 'In mountains and on difficult roads, the king's protection should be ensured;

children.text: sva-yodhai rakṣitasyāpi śayanaṃ yoga-nidrayā // Hit_3.77 //
children.translated_text: even when guarded by his own soldiers, he should sleep in the sleep of <s>yoga</s> (light vigilance). // Hit 3.77 //'

children.text: nāśayet karṣayec chatrūn durga-kaṇṭaka-mardanaiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'One should destroy and harass enemies by crushing their fortified strongholds;

children.text: para-deśa-praveśe ca kuryād āṭavikān puraḥ // Hit_3.78 //
children.translated_text: and when entering enemy territory, one should place forest-dwellers at the front. // Hit 3.78 //'

children.text: yatra rājā tatra kośo vinā kośaṃ na rājatā |
children.translated_text: 'Where the king is, there is the treasury; without the treasury, there is no kingship;

children.text: subhaṭebhyas tato dadyāt ko hi dātur na yudhyate // Hit_3.79 //
children.translated_text: therefore one should give to brave warriors — for who does not fight for a generous giver? // Hit 3.79 //'

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: For —

children.text: na narasya naro dāso dāsas tv arthasya bhūpate |
children.translated_text: 'A man is not the servant of a man; a man is the servant of wealth, O king;

children.text: gauravaṃ lāghavaṃ vāpi dhanādhana-nibandhanam // Hit_3.80 //
children.translated_text: honor and dishonor are both dependent on wealth and lack thereof. // Hit 3.80 //'

children.text: abhedena ca yudhyeta rakṣec caiva parasparam |
children.translated_text: 'One should fight with unity and protect one another;

children.text: phalgu sainyaṃ ca yat kiṃcin madhye vyūhasya kārayet // Hit_3.81 //
children.translated_text: any weak forces should be placed in the center of the battle formation. // Hit 3.81 //'

children.text: padātīṃś ca mahīpālaḥ puro 'nīkasya yojayet |
children.translated_text: 'The king should station foot-soldiers at the front of the army;

children.text: uparudhyārim āsīta rāṣṭraṃ cāsyopapīḍayet // Hit_3.82 //
children.translated_text: besieging the enemy, he should wait and harass the enemy's territory. // Hit 3.82 //'

children.text: syandanāśvaiḥ same yudhyed anūpe nau-dvipais tathā |
children.translated_text: 'On level ground one should fight with chariots and horses; in marshy land, with boats and elephants;

children.text: vṛkṣa-gulmāvṛte cāpair asi-carmāyudhaiḥ sthale // Hit_3.83 //
children.translated_text: in [terrain] covered with trees and thickets, with bows; on [open] ground, with swords and shields. // Hit 3.83 //'

children.text: dūṣayec cāsya satataṃ yavasān nodakendhanam |
children.translated_text: 'One should constantly spoil the enemy's fodder, water, and fuel;

children.text: bhindyāc caiva taḍāgāni prakārārān parikhās tathā // Hit_3.84 //
children.translated_text: and one should breach their reservoirs, ramparts, and moats. // Hit 3.84 //'

children.text: baleṣu pramukho hastī na tathānyo mahīpateḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Among forces, the elephant is foremost for a king, unlike any other;

children.text: nijair avayavair eva mātaṅgo 'ṣṭāyudhaḥ smṛtaḥ // Hit_3.85 //
children.translated_text: for the elephant is said to be an eight-weapon [warrior] by its own limbs alone. // Hit 3.85 //'

children.text: balam aśvaś ca sainyānāṃ prākāro jaṅgamo yataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The horse is the strength of armies, for it is a moving rampart;

children.text: tasmād aśvādhiko rājā vijayī sthala-vigrahe // Hit_3.86 //
children.translated_text: therefore a king rich in horses is victorious in land warfare. // Hit 3.86 //'

children.text: tathā coktam-
children.translated_text: And it is said —

children.text: yudhyamānā hayārūḍhā devānām api durjayāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Those who fight mounted on horses are hard to conquer even for the gods;

children.text: api dūrasthitās teṣāṃ vairiṇo hastavattinaḥ // Hit_3.87 //
children.translated_text: even from afar, their enemies are within their reach. // Hit 3.87 //'

children.text: prathamaṃ yuddha-kāritvaṃ samasta-bala-pālanam |
children.translated_text: 'Initiating battle first, guarding the entire force,

children.text: diṅ-mārgāṇāṃ viśodhitvaṃ patti-karma pracakṣate // Hit_3.88 //
children.translated_text: and clearing the roads in all directions — these are described as the duties of infantry. // Hit 3.88 //'

children.text: svabhāva-śūram astrajñam aviraktaṃ jita-śramam |
children.translated_text: 'Naturally brave, skilled in weapons, not disaffected, having conquered fatigue,

children.text: prasiddha-kṣatriya-prāyaṃ balaṃ śreṣṭhatamaṃ viduḥ // Hit_3.89 //
children.translated_text: consisting mainly of proven <s>Kṣatriyas</s> — such a force is known as the very best. // Hit 3.89 //'

children.text: yathā prabhu-kṛtān mānād yudhyante bhuvi mānavāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'As men fight on earth from the honor bestowed by a master,

children.text: na tathā bahubhir dattair draviṇair api bhūpate // Hit_3.90 //
children.translated_text: they do not fight so [well] even for much wealth given [by another], O king. // Hit 3.90 //'

children.text: varam alpa-balaṃ sāraṃ na kuryān muṇḍa-maṇḍalīm |
children.translated_text: 'Better a small but excellent force — one should not make a shaved circle (a mob of useless troops);

children.text: kuryād asāra-bhaṅgo hi sāra-bhaṅgam api sphuṭam // Hit_3.91 //
children.translated_text: for the breaking of the worthless clearly causes the breaking of the worthy too. // Hit 3.91 //'

children.text: aprasādo 'nadhiṣṭhānaṃ deyāṃśa-haraṇaṃ ca yat |
children.translated_text: 'Displeasure, lack of command, seizure of what is due [to them],

children.text: kāla-yāpo 'pratīkāras tad vairāgyasya kāraṇam // Hit_3.92 //
children.translated_text: delay in payment, and lack of remedy — these are the causes of disaffection [in soldiers]. // Hit 3.92 //'

children.text: apīḍayan balaṃ śatrūñ jigīṣur abhiṣeṇayet |
children.translated_text: 'Without harassing one's own forces, the one desiring victory should march against the enemy;

children.text: sukha-sādhyaṃ dviṣāṃ sainyaṃ dīrgha-prayāṇa-pīḍitam // Hit_3.93 //
children.translated_text: the enemy's army, fatigued by a long march, is easy to overcome. // Hit 3.93 //'

children.text: dāyādād aparo yasmān nāsti bheda-karo dviṣām |
children.translated_text: 'Since there is no greater cause of division among enemies than a rival claimant,

children.text: tasmād utthāpayed yatnād dāyādaṃ tasya vidviṣaḥ // Hit_3.94 //
children.translated_text: therefore one should diligently incite the rival heir of one's adversary. // Hit 3.94 //'

children.text: sandhāya yuvarājena yadi vā mukhya-mantriṇā |
children.translated_text: 'Having made an alliance with the crown prince or the chief minister,

children.text: antaḥ-prakopaṇaṃ kuryād abhiyoktā sthirātmanaḥ // Hit_3.95 //
children.translated_text: the attacker of a resolute [enemy] should create internal insurrection. // Hit 3.95 //'

children.text: krūrāmitraṃ raṇe cāpi bhaṅgaṃ dattvā vighātayet |
children.translated_text: 'A cruel enemy should be routed in battle and destroyed;

children.text: athavā go-grahākṛṣṭyā tan-mukhyāśrita-bandhanāt // Hit_3.96 //
children.translated_text: or else, through cattle-raids and by capturing his chief dependents. // Hit 3.96 //'

children.text: svarājyaṃ vāsayed rājā para-deśāpaharaṇāt |
children.translated_text: 'A king should consolidate his own kingdom from the seizure of enemy territory;

children.text: athavā dāna-mānābhyāṃ vāsitaṃ dhanadaṃ hi tat // Hit_3.97 //
children.translated_text: or else, [the conquered land], settled by gifts and honors, yields revenue. // Hit 3.97 //'

children.text: athavā bahunoditena-
children.translated_text: Or, to say much in brief —

children.text: ātmodayaḥ para-glānir dvayaṃ nītir itīyatī |
children.translated_text: 'Self-advancement and the rival's decline — these two constitute the extent of statecraft;

children.text: tad ūrīkṛtya kṛtibhir vācaspatyaṃ pratīyate // Hit_3.98 //
children.translated_text: having accepted this, the wise attain mastery of speech (the authority of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>). // Hit 3.98 //'

body.text: rājñā vihasyoktam-sarvam etad viśeṣataś cocyate | kintu,
body.translated_text: The king said with a laugh: 'All this is stated in great detail. But —'

children.text: anyad ucchṛṅkhalaṃ sattvam anyac chāstra-niyantritam |
children.translated_text: 'One thing is unbridled courage; another is [conduct] regulated by scripture;

children.text: sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ hi tejas-timirayoḥ kutaḥ // Hit_3.99 //
children.translated_text: for how can there be co-inherence of radiance and darkness? // Hit 3.99 //'

body.text: tata utthāya rājā mauhūrtikāvedita-lagne prasthitaḥ | atha prahita-praṇidhiś caro hiraṇyagarbham āgatya praṇamyovāca-deva ! samāgata-prāyo rājā citravarṇaḥ | samprati malaya-parvatādhityakāyāṃ samāvāsita-kaṭako vartate | durga-śodhanaṃ pratikṣaṇam anusandhātavyam | yato 'sau gṛdhro mahāmantrī | kiṃ ca kenacit saha tasya viśvāsa-kathā-prasaṅgenetad iṅgitam avagataṃ mayā | yat-anena ko 'py asmad-durge prāg eva niyuktaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thereupon the king rose and set forth at the moment indicated by the astrologer. Now the dispatched spy came to <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, bowed, and said: 'Your Majesty! King <s>Citravarṇa</s> has nearly arrived. He is presently encamped on the plateau of the <s>Malaya</s> mountain. The fortress must be inspected constantly. For that vulture is a great minister. Moreover, from a conversation of trust with someone, I have gathered this indication — that some agent has already been placed by him in our fortress.'

body.text: cakravāko brūte-deva ! kāka evāsau sambhavati |
body.translated_text: <s>Cakravāka</s> says: 'Your Majesty! That must be the crow.'

body.text: rājāha-na kadācid etat | yady evaṃ tadā kathaṃ tena śukasyābhibhavodyogaḥ kṛtaḥ ? aparaṃ ca, śukasyāgamanāt tasya vigrahotsāhaḥ | sa ca cirād atrāste |
body.translated_text: The king said: 'This can never be! If so, then why did he make the effort to attack the parrot? Moreover, his enthusiasm for war [arose] from the parrot's arrival. And [the crow] has been staying here for a long time.'

body.text: mantrī brūte-tathāpy āgantukaḥ śaṅkanīyaḥ |
body.translated_text: The minister says: 'Even so, a newcomer should be suspected.'

body.text: rājāha-āgantukā api kadācid upakārakā dṛśyante | śṛṇu-
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Even newcomers are sometimes seen to be beneficial. Listen —'

children.text: paro 'pi hitavān bandhur bandhur apy ahitaḥ paraḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Even a stranger is a kinsman if he acts for one's good; even a kinsman is a stranger if he acts harmfully;

children.text: ahito dehajo vyādhir hitam āraṇyam auṣadham // Hit_3.100 //
children.translated_text: harmful is a disease born in the body; beneficial is a medicine [found] in the forest. // Hit 3.100 //'

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And furthermore —

children.text: āsīd vīra-varo nāma śūdrakasya mahībhṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'There was a hero named <s>Vīravara</s>, a servant of King <s>Śūdraka</s>;

children.text: sevakaḥ svalpa-kālena sa dadau sutam ātmanaḥ // Hit_3.101 //
children.translated_text: in a short time, he gave up his own son. // Hit 3.101 //'

body.text: cakravākaḥ pṛcchati--katham etat ?
body.translated_text: <s>Cakravāka</s> asks: 'How was that?'

body.text: rājā kathayati-
body.translated_text: The king narrates:

body.text: kathā 8
body.translated_text: Story 8

body.text: ahaṃ purā śūdrakasya rājñaḥ krīḍā-sarasi karpūrakeli-nāmno rājahaṃsasya putryā karpūramañjaryā sahānurāgavān abhavam | vīravaro nāma rājaputraḥ kutaścid deśād āgatya rāja-dvāram upagamya pratīhāram uvāca-ahaṃ tāvad vartanārthī rājaputraḥ | māṃ raja-darśanaṃ kāraya | tatas tenāsau rāja-darśanaṃ kārito brūte-deva ! yadi mayā sevakena prayojanam asti, tadāsmad-vartanaṃ kriyatām |
body.translated_text: I was once in love with <s>Karpūramañjarī</s>, the daughter of a royal swan named <s>Karpūrakeli</s>, at the pleasure-lake of King <s>Śūdraka</s>. A prince named <s>Vīravara</s>, having come from some country, approached the king's gate and said to the door-keeper: 'I am a prince seeking employment. Arrange an audience with the king for me.' Thereupon, having been given an audience by him, he said: 'Your Majesty! If you have need of a servant like me, then provide my wages.'

body.text: śūdraka uvāca-kiṃ te vartanam ?
body.translated_text: <s>Śūdraka</s> said: 'What are your wages?'

body.text: vīravaro brūte-pratyahaṃ suvarṇa-pañca-śatāni dehi |
body.translated_text: <s>Vīravara</s> says: 'Give me five hundred gold coins daily.'

body.text: rājāha-kā te sāmagrī ?
body.translated_text: The king said: 'What are your qualifications?'

body.text: vīravaro brūte-dvau bāhū | tṛtīyaś ca khaḍgaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Vīravara</s> says: 'Two arms — and a third, [my] sword.'

body.text: rājāha-naitac chakyam |
body.translated_text: The king said: 'This cannot be [granted].'

body.text: tac chrutvā vīravaraḥ praṇamya calitaḥ | atha mantribhir uktam-deva ! dina-catuṣṭayasya vartanaṃ dattvā jñāyatām asya svarūpam | kim upayukto 'yam etāvad vartanaṃ gṛhṇāti anupayukto veti |
body.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Vīravara</s>, bowing, departed. Then the ministers said — Your Majesty! Give him provisions for four days and ascertain his true nature — whether he is useful and deserving of such provisions, or not.

body.text: tato mantri-vacanād āhuhūya vīravarāya tāmbūlaṃ dattvā pañca-śatāni suvarṇāni dattāni | vartana-viniyogaś ca rājñā sunibhṛtaṃ nirūpitaḥ | tad-ardhaṃ vīravareṇa devebhyo brāhmaṇebhyo dattam | sthitasyārdhaṃ duḥkhitebhyaḥ | tad avaśiṣṭaṃ bhojya-vilāsa-vyayena | etat sarvaṃ nitya-kṛtyaṃ kṛtvā, rāja-dvāram aharniśaṃ khaḍga-pāṇiḥ sevate | yadā ca rājā svayaṃ samādiśati tadā sva-gṛham api yāti |
body.translated_text: Then, at the ministers' word, <s>Vīravara</s> was summoned and given betel-leaf along with five hundred gold coins. The king carefully observed how the provisions were spent. Half of it <s>Vīravara</s> gave to the gods and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>; half of the remainder to the suffering; and the rest was spent on food, enjoyment, and expenses. Having performed all this as his daily duty, he served at the royal gate day and night, sword in hand. Only when the king himself gave permission did he go to his own house.

body.text: athaikadā kṛṣṇa-caturdaśyāṃ rātrau sa rājā sa-karuṇa-krandana-dhvaniṃ śuśrāva | tat śrutvā rājā brūte-kaḥ ko 'tra dvāri tiṣṭhati ?
body.translated_text: Now once, on the dark fourteenth night, the king heard a sound of piteous wailing. Hearing it, the king said — Who stands here at the gate?

body.text: tadā tenoktaṃ-deva ! ahaṃ vīravaraḥ |
body.translated_text: Then he replied — Your Majesty! I am <s>Vīravara</s>.

body.text: rājovāca-krandanānusaraṇaṃ kriyatām |
body.translated_text: The king said — Go and follow the source of that weeping.

body.text: vīravaro 'pi-yathājñāpayati devaḥ, ity uktvā calitaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Vīravara</s> said — As the Lord commands, and departed.

body.text: rājñā ca cintitam-ayam ekākī rājaputro mayā sūcībhedye tamasi prahitaḥ | naitad ucitam | tad aham api gatvā kim etad iti nirūpayāmi |
body.translated_text: The king then thought — I have sent this prince alone into a darkness so thick a needle could not pierce it. This is not right. Let me also go and ascertain what this is about.

body.text: tato rājāpi khaḍgam ādāya tad-anusaraṇa-krameṇa nagarād bahir nirjagāma | gatvā ca vīravareṇa rudatī rupa-yauvana-sampannā sarvālaṅkāra-bhūṣitā kācit strī dṛṣṭā, pṛṣṭā ca-kā tvam ? kim arthaṃ rodiṣi ? iti |
body.translated_text: Then the king too, taking his sword, followed him and went outside the city. Having gone, <s>Vīravara</s> saw a certain woman weeping — endowed with beauty and youth, adorned with all ornaments — and asked her — Who are you? Why do you weep?

body.text: striyoktam-aham etasya śūdrakasya rāja-lakṣmīḥ | cirād etasya bhuja-cchāyāyāṃ mahatā sukhena viśrāntā | idānīm anyatra gamiṣyāmi |
body.translated_text: The woman said — I am <s>Rājalakṣmī</s> (Royal Fortune) of this [king] <s>Śūdraka</s>. For a long time I have rested in great comfort under the shade of his arms. Now I am about to go elsewhere.

body.text: vīravaro brūte-yatāpāyaḥ sambhavati, tatropāyo 'py asti | tat kathaṃ syāt punar ihāvāso bhavatyāḥ ?
body.translated_text: <s>Vīravara</s> said — Where there is a danger, there too lies a remedy. So what could be done so that you may dwell here again?

body.text: lakṣmīr uvāca-yadi tvam ātmanaḥ putraṃ śaktidharaṃ dvātriṃśal-lakṣaṇopetaṃ bhagavatyāḥ sarva-maṅgalāyā upahārīkaroṣi, tadāhaṃ punar atra suciraṃ nivasāmi | ity uktvādṛśyābhavat |
body.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s> said — If you offer your own son <s>Śaktidhara</s>, endowed with the thirty-two auspicious marks, as a sacrifice to the goddess <s>Sarvamaṅgalā</s>, then I shall dwell here again for a very long time. Having said this, she vanished.

body.text: tato vīravareṇa sva-gṛhaṃ gatvā nidrāyamāṇā sva-vadhūḥ prabodhitā putraś ca | tau nidrāṃ parityajyotthāyopaviṣṭau | vīravaras tat sarvaṃ lakṣmī-vacanam uktavān | tac chrutvā sānandaḥ śaktidharo brūte-dhanyo 'ham evambhūtaḥ | svāmi-rājya-rakṣārthaṃ yasyopayogaḥ | tāta ! tat ko 'dhunā vilambasya hetuḥ ? evaṃ-vidhe karmaṇi dehasya viniyogaḥ ślāghyaḥ | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vīravara</s> went to his home and woke his sleeping wife and son. They abandoned sleep and sat up. <s>Vīravara</s> told them everything that <s>Lakṣmī</s> had said. Hearing this, <s>Śaktidhara</s> said joyfully — I am blessed to be such a one whose service can protect the kingdom of the master! Father! What reason is there now for delay? In such a deed, the employment of one's body is praiseworthy. For —

children.text: dhanāni jīvitaṃ caiva parārthe prājña utsṛjet |
children.translated_text: The wise person should sacrifice wealth and even life for the sake of others;

children.text: tan-nimitto varaṃ tyāgo vināśe niyate sati // Hit_3.102 //
children.translated_text: When destruction is inevitable, it is better to give them up for a [noble] cause. // Hit_3.102 //

body.text: śaktidhara-mātovāca-yady etan na kartavyaṃ tat kenānyena karmaṇā gṛhītasya mahāvartanasya niṣkrayo bhaviṣyati | ity ālocya sarve sarvamaṅgalāyāḥ sthānaṃ gatāḥ | tatra sarvamaṅgalāṃ sampūjya vīravaro brūte-devi ! prasīda | vijayatāṃ śūdrako mahārājaḥ | gṛhyatām ayam upahāraḥ | ity uktvā putrasya śiraś ciccheda | tato vīravaraś cintayāmāsa-gṛhīta-rāja-vartanasya nistāraḥ kṛtaḥ | adhunā niṣputrasya me jīvanenālam | ity ālocyātmanaḥ śiraś ciccheda |
body.translated_text: <s>Śaktidhara</s>'s mother said — If this is not done, then by what other deed will the repayment of the great salary received be made? Having thus resolved, they all went to the temple of <s>Sarvamaṅgalā</s>. There, having worshipped <s>Sarvamaṅgalā</s>, <s>Vīravara</s> said — O Goddess! Be gracious. May King <s>Śūdraka</s> be victorious. Accept this offering. Having said this, he severed his son's head. Then <s>Vīravara</s> reflected — The debt of the royal salary has been repaid. Now, being without a son, what use is my life? Having thus resolved, he severed his own head.

body.text: tataḥ striyāpi svāmi-putra-śokārtayā tad anuṣṭhitam | tat sarvaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājā sāścaryaṃ cintayāmāsa--

children.text: jāyante ca mriyante ca mad-vidhāḥ kṣudra-jantavaḥ |
children.translated_text: Lowly creatures like me are born and die;

children.text: anena sadṛśo loke na bhūto na bhaviṣyati // Hit_3.103 //
children.translated_text: One like him has never been nor ever shall be in this world. // Hit_3.103 //

body.translated_text: Then his wife too, afflicted with grief for her husband and son, followed suit. Seeing all this, the king thought with astonishment —

body.text:
tad etat-parityaktena mama rājyenāpi kiṃ prayojanam | tataḥ śūdrakeṇāpi sva-śiraś chettuṃ khaḍgaḥ samutthāpitaḥ | atha bhagavatyā sarvamaṅgalayā pratyakṣa-bhūtayā rājā haste dhṛtaḥ | uktaṃ ca-putra ! prasanno 'smi te, etāvatā sāhasenālam | jīvanānte'pi tava rāja-bhaṅgo nāsti |
rājā ca sāṣṭāṅga-pātaṃ praṇamyovāca-devi ! kiṃ me rājyena ? jīvitena vā mama kiṃ prayojanam ? yady aham anukampanīyas tadā mamāyuḥ-śeṣeṇāpy ayaṃ sa-dāra-putro vīravaro jīvatu | anyathāhaṃ yathā-prāptāṃ gatiṃ gacchāmi |
body.translated_text: If such [people] have given up [their lives], what use is even my kingdom to me? Then <s>Śūdraka</s> too raised his sword to cut his own head. But the goddess <s>Sarvamaṅgalā</s>, appearing in person, seized the king by the hand and said — Son! I am pleased with you; enough of this heroism. Even until the end of your life, there shall be no loss of your kingship. The king, prostrating with all eight limbs, said — Goddess! What use is kingship to me? What purpose does my life serve? If I am worthy of your compassion, then let this <s>Vīravara</s>, with his wife and son, live out the remainder of my lifespan. Otherwise I shall accept whatever fate awaits me.

body.text: bhagavaty uvāca-putra ! anena te sattvotkarṣeṇa bhṛtya-vātsalyena ca sarvathā santuṣṭāsmi | gaccha vijayī bhava | ayam api sa-parivāro rāja-putro jīvatu | ity uktvā devy adṛśyābhavat | tato vīravaraḥ sa-putra-dāraḥ prāpta-jīvanaḥ sva-gṛhaṃ gataḥ | rājāpi tair alakṣitaḥ satvaram antaḥ-puraṃ praviṣṭaḥ |
body.translated_text: The goddess said — Son! By this excellence of your courage and your affection for your servant, I am thoroughly pleased. Go, be victorious. This prince too, with his family, shall live. Having said this, the goddess vanished. Then <s>Vīravara</s>, with his son and wife, having regained life, went to his home. The king too, unseen by them, swiftly entered the inner palace.

body.text: atha prabhāte vīravaro dvārasthaḥ punar bhūpālena pṛṣṭaḥ sann āha-deva ! sā rudatī mām avalokyādṛśyābhavat | na kāpy anyā vārtā vidyate |
body.translated_text: Now at dawn, <s>Vīravara</s>, standing at the gate, when asked again by the king, said — Your Majesty! That weeping woman, upon seeing me, vanished. There is no other news.

body.text: tad vacanam ākarṇya santuṣṭo rājā sāścaryaṃ cintayāmāsa-katham ayaṃ ślāghyo mahā-sattvaḥ ? yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Hearing those words, the pleased king thought with wonder — How praiseworthy is this great-souled man! For —

children.text: priyaṃ brūyād akṛpaṇaḥ śūraḥ syād avikatthanaḥ |
children.translated_text: He should speak kindly, be generous, be brave without boasting,

children.text: dātā nāpātra-varṣī ca pragalbhaḥ syād aniṣṭhuraḥ // Hit_3.104 //
children.translated_text: Be a giver who does not rain [gifts] on the unworthy, and be bold without being harsh. // Hit_3.104 //

body.text: etan mahāpuruṣa-lakṣaṇam etasmin sarvam asti | tataḥ sa rājā prātaḥ śiṣṭa-sabhāṃ kṛtvā, sarvaṃ vṛttāntaṃ prastutya prasādāt tasmai karṇāṭaka-rājyaṃ dadau | tat kim āgantuko jāti-mātrād duṣṭaḥ ? tatrāpy uttamādhama-madhyamāḥ santi |
body.translated_text: These are the marks of a great man, and all of them are present in him. Then, in the morning, the king held an assembly of the learned, and having related the entire account, graciously bestowed upon him the kingdom of <s>Karṇāṭaka</s>. So is a stranger necessarily bad merely by birth? Even among them there are superior, inferior, and middling ones.

children.text: cakravāko brūte-
children.translated_text: The <s>Cakravāka</s> (ruddy goose) said —

children.text: yo 'kāryaṃ kāryavac chāsti sa kiṃ mantrī nṛpecchayā |
children.translated_text: He who counsels what is improper as proper — is he a minister merely to please the king?

children.text: varaṃ svāmi-mano-duḥkhaṃ tan-nāśo na tv akāryataḥ // Hit_3.105 //
children.translated_text: Better that the master's mind suffer [momentary] distress than that ruin come from improper action. // Hit_3.105 //

children.text: vaidyo guruś ca mantrī ca yasya rājñaḥ priyaṃvadāḥ |
children.translated_text: When a king's physician, preceptor, and minister are all given to flattery,

children.text: śarīra-dharma-kośebhyaḥ kṣipraṃ sa parihīyate // Hit_3.106 //
children.translated_text: He is quickly deprived of body, <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), and treasury. // Hit_3.106 //

children.text: śṛṇu deva !
children.translated_text: Listen, Your Majesty!

children.text: puṇyāl labdhaṃ yad ekena tan mamāpi bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: What was obtained by one person through merit — 'that will happen to me too' —

children.text: hatvā bhikṣuṃ yato mohān nidhy-arthī nāpito hataḥ // Hit_3.107 //
children.translated_text: [thinking thus], the barber, out of delusion, killed a mendicant for the sake of a treasure and was [himself] killed. // Hit_3.107 //

body.text: rājā pṛcchati--katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The king asks — How is that?

body.text: mantrī kathayati-
body.translated_text: The minister narrates —

body.text: kathā 9
body.translated_text: Story 9

body.text: asty ayodhyāyāṃ puri cūḍāmaṇir nāma kṣatriyaḥ | tena dhanārthinā mahatā kleśena bhagavāṃś candrārdha-cūḍāmaṇiś ciram ārādhitaḥ | tataḥ kṣīṇa-pāpo 'sau svapne darśanaṃ dattvā, bhagavad-ādeśādy-akṣeśvareṇādiṣṭo yat tvam adya prātaḥ kṣauraṃ kārayitvā, laguḍa-hastaḥ san sva-gṛha-dvāri nibhṛtaṃ sthāsyasi, tato yam evāgataṃ bhikṣukaṃ prāṅgaṇe paśyasi taṃ nirdakṣaṃ laguḍa-prahāreṇa haniṣyasi | tato 'sau bhikṣukas tat-kṣaṇāt suvarṇa-kalaso bhaviṣyati | tena tvayā yāvaj-jīvaṃ sukhinā bhavitavyam | tatas tathānuṣṭhite tad vṛttam |
body.translated_text: In the city of <s>Ayodhyā</s> there lived a <s>Kṣatriya</s> named <s>Cūḍāmaṇi</s>. Seeking wealth, he worshipped the blessed Lord <s>Candrārdhacūḍāmaṇi</s> (Śiva, whose crest-jewel is the half-moon) for a long time with great effort. Then, when his sins were exhausted, [the Lord] appeared in a dream and, by the command of the blessed <s>Akṣeśvara</s>, instructed him: 'Tomorrow morning, having had your head shaved, you shall stand at the door of your house with a club in hand, concealed. Then whichever mendicant you see in the courtyard, you shall strike him mercilessly with the club. That mendicant will instantly become a golden vessel. With that, you shall live happily for the rest of your life.' When this was done accordingly, that very thing happened.

body.text: tatra kṣaura-karaṇāyānītena nāpitena tat sarvam ālokya cintitam-aye nidhi-prāpter ayam upāyaḥ | tad aham apy evaṃ kiṃ na karomi ? tataḥ prabhṛti sa nāpitaḥ pratyahaṃ tathāvidho laguḍa-hastaḥ sunibhṛtaṃ bhikṣor āgamanaṃ pratīkṣate | ekadā tena prāpto bhikṣur laguḍena vyāpāditaḥ | tasmād aparādhāt so 'pi nāpito rāja-puruṣair vyāpāditaḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-puṇyāl labdhaṃ yad ekena ity ādi |
body.translated_text: Now, the barber who had been brought there for the shaving, having observed all this, thought — Aha! This is the method for obtaining treasure. Why should I not do the same? From that day on, that barber, similarly club in hand, would carefully wait at his door for the arrival of a mendicant. One day, finding a mendicant, he killed him with the club. For that crime, the barber too was put to death by the king's men. Therefore I say — 'What was obtained by one person through merit' — and so on.

children.text: rājāha-
children.translated_text: The king said —

children.text: purāvṛtta-kathodgāraiḥ kathaṃ nirṇīyate paraḥ |
children.translated_text: How can one judge another merely by recounting tales of the past?

children.text: syān niṣkāraṇa-bandhur vā kiṃ vā viśvāsa-ghātakaḥ // Hit_3.108 //
children.translated_text: One may be a friend without cause, or perhaps a betrayer of trust. // Hit_3.108 //

body.text: yātu, prastutam anusandhīyatām | malayādhityakāyāṃ cec citravarṇas tad adhunā kiṃ vidheyam ? mantrī vadati-deva ! āgata-praṇidhi-mukhān mayā śrutaṃ, yat mahā-mantriṇo gṛdhrasyopadeśe citravarṇenānādaraḥ kṛtaḥ tato 'sau mūḍho jetuṃ śakyaḥ | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: Let it be; let us return to the matter at hand. If <s>Citravarṇa</s> is on the <s>Malaya</s> plateau, what should now be done? The minister said — Your Majesty! From the reports of arriving spies I have heard that <s>Citravarṇa</s> has shown disregard for the counsel of his great minister, the vulture. Therefore that fool can be conquered. As it is said —

children.text: lubdhaḥ krūro 'laso 'satyaḥ pramādī bhīrur asthiraḥ |
children.translated_text: Greedy, cruel, lazy, untruthful, negligent, cowardly, fickle,

children.text: mūḍho yodhāvamantā ca sukha-cchedyo ripuḥ smṛtaḥ // Hit_3.109 //
children.translated_text: Foolish, and contemptuous of soldiers — such an enemy is easily overthrown. // Hit_3.109 //

body.text: tato 'sau yāvad asmad durga-dvāra-rodhaṃ na karoti, tāvan nady-adri-vana-vartmasu tad-balāni hantuṃ sārasādayaḥ senāpatayo niyujyantām | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: Therefore, before he blocks the gates of our fortress, let commanders such as <s>Sārasa</s> (the crane) be deployed to destroy his forces on the routes through rivers, mountains, and forests. As it is said —

children.text: dīrgha-vartma-pariśrāntaṃ nady-adri-vana-saṅkulam |
children.translated_text: An [enemy army] exhausted by a long march, obstructed by rivers, mountains, and forests,

children.text: ghorāgni-bhaya-santrastaṃ kṣut-pipāsārditaṃ tathā // Hit_3.110 //
children.translated_text: Terrified by the danger of terrible fire, and afflicted by hunger and thirst,

children.text: pramattaṃ bhojana-vyagraṃ vyādhi-durbhikṣa-pīḍitam |
children.translated_text: Careless, preoccupied with eating, afflicted by disease and famine,

children.text: asaṃsthitam abhūyiṣṭhaṃ vṛṣṭi-vāta-samākulam // Hit_3.111 //
children.translated_text: Disarrayed, reduced in numbers, and confused by rain and wind,

children.text: paṅka-pāṃśu-jalācchannaṃ suvyastaṃ dasyu-vidrutam |
children.translated_text: Covered in mud, dust, and water, scattered, and routed by bandits —

children.text: evambhūtaṃ mahīpālaḥ para-sainyaṃ vighātayet // Hit_3.112 //
children.translated_text: A king should strike the enemy army when it is in such a state. // Hit_3.112 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: avaskanda-bhayād rājā prajāgara-kṛta-śramam |
children.translated_text: A king, through fear of a night attack, should always strike

children.text: divā-suptaṃ sadā hanyān nidrā-vyākula-sainikam // Hit_3.113 //
children.translated_text: An army that has slept during the day, fatigued by sleeplessness, with soldiers drowsy from sleep. // Hit_3.113 //

body.text: atas tasya pramādito balaṃ gatvā yathāvakāśaṃ divā-niśaṃ ghnantv asmat-senāpatayaḥ | tathānuṣṭhite citravarṇasya sainikāḥ senāpatayaś ca bahavo nihatāḥ | tataś citravarṇo viṣaṇṇaḥ sva-mantriṇaṃ dūra-darśinam āha-tāta ! kim ity asmad-upekṣā kriyate ? kiṃ kvāpy avinayo mamāsti ? tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: Therefore, taking advantage of his negligence, let our commanders go and strike his forces at every opportunity, by day and night. When this was done, many soldiers and commanders of <s>Citravarṇa</s> were slain. Thereupon, the dejected <s>Citravarṇa</s> said to his minister <s>Dūradarśin</s> (Far-seer) — Father!
