Why has indifference been shown toward me? Is there any misconduct on my part? As it is said —

children.text: na rājyaṃ prāptam ity eva vartitavyam asāmpratam |
children.translated_text: One should not behave improperly merely because one has obtained a kingdom;

children.text: śriyaṃ hy avinayo hanti jarā rūpam ivottamam // Hit_3.114 //
children.translated_text: For improper conduct destroys prosperity, just as old age destroys the finest beauty. // Hit_3.114 //

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: dakṣaḥ śriyam adhigacchati pathy āśī kalyatāṃ sukham arogī |
children.translated_text: The diligent one attains prosperity, the traveler finds ease and health,

children.text: udyukto viyāntaṃ dharmārtha-yaśāṃsi ca vinītaḥ // Hit_3.115 //
children.translated_text: The industrious one [gains] the end of separation, and the modest one [gains] <s>dharma</s>, wealth, and fame. // Hit_3.115 //

children.text: gṛdhro 'vadat-deva ! śṛṇu-
children.translated_text: The vulture (<s>Gṛdhra</s>) said — Your Majesty! Listen —

children.text: avidvān api bhū-pālo vidyā-vṛddhopasevayā |
children.translated_text: Even an unlearned king, through the service of those advanced in learning,

children.text: parāṃ śriyam avāpnoti jalāsanna-tarur yathā // Hit_3.116 //
children.translated_text: Attains the highest prosperity, like a tree near water. // Hit_3.116 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: pāpaṃ strī mṛgayā dyūtam artha-dūṣaṇam eva ca |
children.translated_text: Sin, women, hunting, gambling, and the squandering of wealth,

children.text: vāg-daṇḍayoś ca pāruṣyaṃ vyasanāni mahībhujām // Hit_3.117 //
children.translated_text: And harshness in speech and punishment — these are the vices of kings. // Hit_3.117 //

body.text: kiṃ ca-

children.text: na sāhasaikānta-rasānuvartinā
children.translated_text: Not by one who follows only the passion for reckless daring alone,

children.text: na cāpy upāyopahatāntarātmanā |
children.translated_text: Nor by one whose inner soul is corrupted by [mere reliance on] stratagems,

children.text: vibhūtayaḥ śakyam avāptum ūrjitā
children.translated_text: Can mighty glories be attained;

children.text: naye ca śaurye ca vasanti sampadaḥ // Hit_3.118 //
children.translated_text: Prosperity dwells in both wise policy and valor. // Hit_3.118 //

body.translated_text: Moreover —

body.text:
tvayā sva-balotsāham avalokya, sāhasaika-rasikena mayopanthas teṣv api mantreṣv anavadhānaṃ, vāk-pāruṣyaṃ ca kṛtam | ato durnīteḥ phalam idam anubhūyate | tathā coktam-
durmantriṇaṃ kam upayānti na nīti-doṣāḥ ?

children.text: santāpayanti kam apathya-bhujaṃ na rogāḥ ?
children.translated_text: What diseases do not torment one who eats unwholesome food?

children.text: kaṃ śrīr na darpayati kaṃ na nihanti mṛtyuḥ
children.translated_text: Whom does fortune not make proud? Whom does death not slay?

children.text: kaṃ strī-kṛtā na viṣayāḥ paritāpayanti // Hit_3.119 //
children.translated_text: What sensual pleasures caused by women do not bring torment? // Hit_3.119 //

body.translated_text: Having seen the enthusiasm of your own army, I, being fond only of reckless daring, showed inattention to their counsels and harshness in speech. Therefore, the fruit of bad policy is now being experienced. As it is said — What faults of policy do not befall one with a bad counselor?

body.text: aparaṃ ca-

children.text: mudaṃ viṣādaḥ śaradaṃ himāgamas
children.translated_text: Sorrow [destroys] joy, winter [destroys] autumn,

children.text: tamo vivasvān sukṛtaṃ kṛtaghnatā |
children.translated_text: The sun [destroys] darkness, ingratitude [destroys] good deeds,

children.text: priyopapattiḥ śucam āpadaṃ nayaḥ
children.translated_text: The arrival of a loved one [destroys] grief, wise policy [destroys] calamities;

children.text: śriyaḥ samṛddhā api hanti durnayaḥ // Hit_3.120 //
children.translated_text: [But] bad policy destroys even the most flourishing prosperity. // Hit_3.120 //

body.translated_text: And further —

body.text: tato mayāpy ālocitam-prajñā-hīno 'yaṃ rājā | na cet kathaṃ nīti-śāstra-kathā-kaumudīṃ vāg-ulkābhis timirayati | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Then I too reflected: 'This king is devoid of wisdom. Otherwise, how does he obscure the moonlight of <s>nīti-śāstra</s> (political science) narratives with the torches of [mere] words? For —'

body.text: yasya nāsti svayaṃ prajñā śāstraṃ tasya karoti kim ?

children.text: locanābhyāṃ vihīnasya darpaṇaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati // Hit_3.121 //
children.translated_text: What will a mirror do for one deprived of eyes?'

body.translated_text: 'Of what use is a treatise to one who has no wisdom of his own?

body.text: ity ālocyāham api tūṣṇīṃ sthitaḥ | atha rājā baddhāñjalir āha-tāta ! asty ayaṃ mamāparādhaḥ, idānīṃ yathāham avaśiṣṭa-bala-sahitaḥ pratyāvṛttya vindhyācalaṃ gacchāmi, tathopadiśa |
body.translated_text: 'Having reflected thus, I too remained silent.' Then the king, with folded hands, said: 'Father! This is indeed my fault. Now instruct me as to how I, together with my remaining forces, may return and go to the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain.'

body.text: gṛdhraḥ svagataṃ cintayati-kriyatām atra pratīkāraḥ | yataḥ,
body.translated_text: The vulture thought to himself: 'Let a remedy be devised here. For —'

children.text: devatāsu gurau goṣu rājasu brāhmaṇeṣu ca |
children.translated_text: 'Anger should always be restrained toward deities, teachers, cows, kings, and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,

children.text: niyantavyaḥ sadā kopo bāla-vṛddhātureṣu ca // Hit_3.122 //
children.translated_text: as well as toward children, the aged, and the sick.'

body.text: mantrī prahasya brūte-deva mā bhaiṣīḥ | samāśvasihi | śṛṇu deva-
body.translated_text: The minister, smiling, said: 'Your Majesty, do not fear! Take heart! Listen, Your Majesty —'

children.text: mantriṇāṃ bhinna-sandhāne bhiṣajāṃ sāṃnipātike |
children.translated_text: 'The wisdom of ministers is displayed in the breaking of alliances, and of physicians in critical fevers;

children.text: karmaṇi vyajyate prajñā susthe ko vā na paṇḍitaḥ // Hit_3.123 //
children.translated_text: when all is well, who is not a scholar?'

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'And furthermore —'

children.text: ārambhante'lpam evājñāḥ kāmaṃ vyagrā bhavanti ca |
children.translated_text: 'The ignorant undertake little and become quite agitated;

children.text: mahārambhāḥ kṛta-dhiyas tiṣṭhanti ca nirākulāḥ // Hit_3.124 //
children.translated_text: the resolute undertake great [tasks] and remain unperturbed.'

body.text: tad atra bhavat-pratāpād eva durgaṃ bhaṅktvā, kīrti-pratāpa-sahitaṃ tvām acireṇa kālena vindhyācalaṃ neṣyāmi |
body.translated_text: 'So here, by your very prowess, having broken through the fortress, I shall lead you, endowed with fame and power, to the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain in a short time.'

body.text: rājāha-katham adhunā svalpa-balena tat sampadyate ?
body.translated_text: The king said: 'How can that be accomplished now with a small force?'

body.text: gṛdhro vadati-deva ! sarvaṃ bhaviṣyati | yato vijigīṣor adīrgha-sūtratā vijaya-siddher avaśyambhāvi lakṣaṇam | tat sahasaiva durga-dvārāvarodhaḥ kriyatām |
body.translated_text: The vulture said: 'Your Majesty! All will come to pass. For the absence of procrastination in one who desires conquest is an inevitable mark of victory's attainment. So let the blockade of the fortress gates be done immediately.'

body.text: atha prahita-praṇidhinā bakenāgatya hiraṇyagarbhasya kathitam-deva ! svalpa-bala evāyaṃ rājā citravarṇo gṛdhrasya vacanopaṣṭambhād āgatya durga-dvārāvarodhaṃ kariṣyati |
body.translated_text: Then <s>Baka</s> (the crane), who had been sent as a spy, came and told <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>: 'Your Majesty! This king <s>Citravarṇa</s>, with only a small force, emboldened by the vulture's words, has come and will blockade the fortress gates.'

body.text: rājahaṃso brūte-sva-bale sārāsāra-vicāraḥ kriyatām | taj jñātvā suvarṇa-vastrādikaṃ yathārhaṃ prasāda-pradānaṃ ca kriyatām | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: The royal swan said: 'Let the strength and weakness of our own forces be assessed. Having ascertained this, let gold, garments, and the like be distributed as gifts and honors as deserved. For —'

children.text: yaḥ kākiṇīm apy apatha-prapannāṃ
children.translated_text: 'He who would rescue even a single <s>kākiṇī</s> (small coin) gone astray,

children.text: samuddharen niṣka-sahasra-tulyām |
children.translated_text: [knowing it to be] equal to a thousand gold [coins],

children.text: kāleṣu koṭiṣv api mukta-hastas
children.translated_text: who is generous at [all] millions of occasions —

children.text: taṃ rāja-siṃhaṃ na jahāti lakṣmīḥ // Hit_3.125 //
children.translated_text: prosperity does not abandon that lion among kings.'

body.text: anyac ca-

children.text: kratau vivāhe vyasane ripu-kṣaye
children.translated_text: 'In sacrifices, in weddings, in calamities, in the destruction of enemies,

children.text: yaśaskare karmaṇi mitra-saṅgrahe |
children.translated_text: in fame-bringing deeds, in gathering friends,

children.text: priyāsu nārīṣv adhaneṣu bāndhaveṣv
children.translated_text: regarding beloved women and destitute kinsmen —

children.text: ativyayo nāsti narādhipāṣṭasu // Hit_3.126 //
children.translated_text: there is no excess of expenditure in these eight [occasions] for a ruler.'

body.translated_text: 'And also —'

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: 'For —'

children.text: mūrkhaḥ svalpa-vyaya-trāsāt sarvanāśaṃ karoti hi |
children.translated_text: 'A fool, through fear of small expenditure, brings about total ruin;

children.text: kaḥ sudhīḥ santyajed bhāṇḍaṃ śuklasyaivātisādhvasāt // Hit_3.127 //
children.translated_text: what wise person would abandon his vessel merely from excessive fear of [a small] leak?'

body.text: rājāha-katham iha samaye'tivyayo yujyate ? uktaṃ ca-āpad-arthe dhanaṃ rakṣed iti |
body.translated_text: The king said: 'How is excessive expenditure appropriate at this juncture? And it is said: "Wealth should be preserved for times of adversity."'

body.text: mantrī brūte-śrīmatāṃ katham āpadaḥ ?
body.translated_text: The minister said: 'How can adversities befall the prosperous?'

body.text: rājāha-kadācic calitā lakṣmīḥ |
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Prosperity may one day depart.'

body.text: mantrī brūte-sañcitāpi vinaśyati | tad deva ! kārpaṇyaṃ vimucya sva-bhaṭā dāna-mānābhyāṃ puraskriyantām | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: The minister said: 'Even what is hoarded perishes. So, Your Majesty, abandoning miserliness, let your own warriors be rewarded with gifts and honors. And as it is said —'

children.text: parasparajñāḥ saṃhṛṣṭās tyaktuṃ prāṇān suniścitāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Those who know each other, who are delighted, who are firmly resolved to sacrifice their lives,

children.text: kulīnāḥ pūjitāḥ samyag vijayante dviṣad-balam // Hit_3.128 //
children.translated_text: who are of noble birth and are duly honored — they conquer the enemy's forces.'

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'And furthermore —'

children.text: subhaṭāḥ śīla-sampannāḥ saṃhatāḥ kṛta-niścayāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Brave warriors endowed with good character, united and firm in resolve,

children.text: api pañca-śataṃ śūrā nighnanti ripu-vāhinīm // Hit_3.129 //
children.translated_text: even [if only] five hundred heroes, can destroy the enemy's army.'

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'Moreover —'

children.text: śiṣṭair apy avaśeṣajña ugraś ca kṛta-nāśakaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'One who knows what should be left over among the faithful, yet is harsh and destructive of what has been done,

children.text: tyajyate kiṃ punar nānyair yaś cāpy ātmambharir naraḥ // Hit_3.130 //
children.translated_text: is abandoned [even] by the good — how much more by others — as is the self-seeking man.'

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: 'For —'

children.text: satyaṃ śauryaṃ dayā tyāgo nṛpasyaite mahā-guṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Truthfulness, valor, compassion, and generosity — these are the great virtues of a king;

children.text: etais tyakto mahīpālaḥ prāpnoti khalu vācyatām // Hit_3.131 //
children.translated_text: a king who is devoid of these certainly earns censure.'

body.text: īdṛśi prastāve'mātyās tāvad avaśyam eva puraskartavyāḥ | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: 'In such a situation, the ministers must certainly be honored. And as it is said —'

children.text: yo yena pratibaddhaḥ syāt saha tenodayī vyayī |
children.translated_text: 'He with whom one is connected, who prospers and declines together [with the king],

children.text: sa viśvasto niyoktavyaḥ prāṇeṣu ca dhaneṣu ca // Hit_3.132 //
children.translated_text: such a trusted person should be employed in [matters of] life and wealth.'

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: 'For —'

children.text: dhūrtaḥ strī vā śiśur yasya mantriṇaḥ syur mahīpateḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The king whose ministers are a rogue, a woman, or a child —

children.text: anīti-pavana-kṣipto 'kāryābdhau sa nimajjati // Hit_3.133 //
children.translated_text: blown by the wind of bad policy, sinks in the ocean of wrong action.'

children.text: śṛṇu deva! -
children.translated_text: 'Listen, Your Majesty —'

children.text: harṣa-krodhau yatau yasya śāstrārthe pratyayas tathā |
children.translated_text: 'He whose anger and elation are subdued, who has confidence in the meaning of the <s>śāstras</s> (treatises),

children.text: nityaṃ bhṛtyānupekṣā ca tasya syād dhanadā dharā // Hit_3.134 //
children.translated_text: and who constantly looks after his servants — to him the earth becomes a giver of wealth.'

children.text: yeṣāṃ rājñā saha syātām uccayāpacayau dhruvam |
children.translated_text: 'Those with whom the king would certainly share in rise and decline —

children.text: amātyā iti tān rājā nāvamanyet kadācana // Hit_3.135 //
children.translated_text: those are the ministers; the king should never disrespect them.'

children.text: mahībhujo madāndhasya saṅkīrṇasyeva dantinaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'For a king blinded by pride, like a maddened elephant gone astray,

children.text: skhalato hi karālambaḥ suśiṣṭair eva kīyate // Hit_3.136 //
children.translated_text: support of the arm [when stumbling] is offered only by the well-disciplined.'

body.text: athāgatya praṇamya meghavarṇo brūte-deva ! dṛṣṭi-prasādaṃ kuru | idānīṃ vipakṣo durga-dvāri vartate | tad deva-pādādeśād bahir niḥsṛtya sva-vikramaṃ darśayāmi | tena deva-pādānām ānṛṇyam upagacchāmi |
body.translated_text: Then <s>Meghavarṇa</s> (Cloud-color) came, bowed, and said: 'Your Majesty, bestow the grace of your glance! Now the enemy stands at the fortress gate. By the command of Your Majesty's feet, let me go forth and display my valor. Thereby I shall discharge my debt to Your Majesty's feet.'

body.text: cakravāko brūte-maivam | yadi bahir niḥsṛtya yoddhavyam | tadā durgāśrayaṇam eva niṣprayojanam | aparaṃ ca-
body.translated_text: The <s>Cakravāka</s> (ruddy goose) said: 'Not so! If one must go forth to fight, then taking refuge in the fortress is pointless. And furthermore —'

children.text: viṣamo 'pi yathā nakraḥ salilān nisṛto vaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Just as a crocodile, formidable [in water], becomes helpless when it leaves the water,

children.text: vanād vinirgataḥ śūraḥ siṃho 'pi syāc chagālavat // Hit_3.137 //
children.translated_text: a hero who leaves the forest, even a lion, becomes like a jackal.'

body.text: atha te sarve durga-dvāraṃ gatvā mahāhavaṃ kṛtavantaḥ | aparedyuś citravarṇo rājā gṛdhram uvāca-tāta ! sva-pratijñātam adhunā nirvāhaya |
body.translated_text: Then all of them went to the fortress gate and waged a great battle. The next day, King <s>Citravarṇa</s> said to the vulture: 'Father! Now fulfill your promise.'

body.text: vāyaso brūte-deva ! svayaṃ gatvā dṛśyatāṃ yuddham | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: The crow said: 'Your Majesty! Go yourself and observe the battle. For —'

children.text: puraskṛtya balaṃ rājā yodhayed avalokayan |
children.translated_text: 'A king should fight, placing his army before him, watching over [it];

children.text: svāminādhiṣṭhitaḥ śvāpi kiṃ na siṃhāyate dhruvam // Hit_3.138 //
children.translated_text: even a dog, when commanded by his master, surely acts like a lion.'

body.text: gṛdhro brūte-deva ! śṛṇu tāvat-
body.translated_text: The vulture said: 'Your Majesty! Listen —'

children.text: akāla-sahamaty-alpaṃ mūrkha-vyasani-nāyakam |
children.translated_text: 'A fortress that cannot withstand untimely [attack], that has few [defenders], that has a foolish, vice-ridden commander,

children.text: aguptaṃ bhīru-yodhaṃ ca durga-vyasanam ucyate // Hit_3.139 //
children.translated_text: that is unguarded and has cowardly soldiers — that is said to be a vulnerable fortress.'

body.text: tat tāvad atra nāsti-
body.translated_text: 'But none of that applies here —'

children.text: upajāpaś cirārodho 'vaskandas tīvra-pauruṣam |
children.translated_text: 'Subversion from within, prolonged siege, sudden assault, and fierce valor —

children.text: durgasya laṅghanopāyāś catvāraḥ kathitā ime // Hit_3.140 //
children.translated_text: these four are described as the means of capturing a fortress.'

body.text: atra yathāśakti kriyate yatnaḥ | karṇe kathayati-evam evam | tato 'nudita eva bhāskare caturṣv api durga-dvāreṣu pravṛtte yuddhe, durgābhyantara-gṛheṣv ekadā kākair agni-nikṣiptaḥ | tataḥ gṛhītaṃ gṛhītaṃ durgam iti kolāhalaṃ śrutvā sarvataḥ pradīptāgnim avalokya rāja-haṃsa-sainikā bahavo durga-vāsinaś ca satvaraṃ hradaṃ praviṣṭāḥ, yataḥ-
body.translated_text: 'Efforts are being made here as much as possible.' He whispered in the ear: 'Thus and thus.' Then, even before the sun had risen, when battle was being waged at all four fortress gates, crows set fire to the houses inside the fortress. Then, hearing the uproar 'The fortress is taken! The fortress is taken!' and seeing fire blazing on all sides, many soldiers of the royal swan and fortress-dwellers quickly entered the lake. For —

children.text: sumantritaṃ suvikrāntaṃ suyuddhaṃ supalāyitam |
children.translated_text: 'Well-counseled, well-fought, well-battled, well-retreated —

children.text: kārya-kāle yathā-śakti kuryān na tu vicārayet // Hit_3.141 //
children.translated_text: one should act according to one's ability at the time of action, and not deliberate.'

body.text: rājā haṃsaś ca svabhāvān manda-gatiḥ | sārasa-dvitīyaś citravarṇasya senāpatinā kukkuṭenāgatya veṣṭitaḥ | hiraṇyagarbhaḥ sārasam āha-senāpate ! sārasa ! mamānurodhād ātmānaṃ kathaṃ vyāpādayasi | adhunāhaṃ gantum asamarthaḥ | tvaṃ gantum adhunāpi samarthaḥ | tad gatvā jalaṃ praviśyātmānaṃ parirakṣa | asmat-putraṃ cūḍāmaṇi-nāmānaṃ sarvajñasya saṃmatyā rājānaṃ kariṣyasi |
body.translated_text: The royal swan, being naturally slow-moving, accompanied by the crane, was surrounded by <s>Kukkuṭa</s> (the rooster), the general of <s>Citravarṇa</s>'s army, who had come [to attack]. <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> said to the crane: 'General <s>Sārasa</s>! Out of loyalty to me, why do you sacrifice yourself? Now I am unable to go. You are still able to go. So go, enter the water, and save yourself. And with the approval of <s>Sarvajña</s>, make my son named <s>Cūḍāmaṇi</s> the king.'

body.text: sāraso brūte-deva ! na vaktavyam evaṃ duḥsahaṃ vacaḥ, yāvac candrārkau divi tiṣṭhatas tāvad vijayatāṃ devaḥ | ahaṃ deva durgādhikārī | tan mama māṃsāsṛg viliptena dvāra-vartmanā tāvat praviśatu śatruḥ | aparaṃ ca, deva--
body.translated_text: The crane said: 'Your Majesty! Do not speak such unbearable words. As long as the sun and moon stand in the sky, may Your Majesty be victorious! I am the keeper of Your Majesty's fortress. Let the enemy enter through the gateway smeared with my flesh and blood. And furthermore, Your Majesty —'

body.text: dātā kṣamī guṇa-grāhī svāmī duḥkhena labhyate |
body.translated_text: 'A lord who is generous, forgiving, and appreciative of qualities is obtained with difficulty.'

body.text: rājāha-satyam evaitat | kintu-

children.text: śucir dakṣo 'nuraktaś ca jāne bhṛtyo 'pi durlabhaḥ // Hit_3.142 //
children.translated_text: 'A servant who is pure, capable, and devoted is also rare, I know.'

body.translated_text: The king said: 'This is indeed true. But —'

body.text: sāraso brūte-śṛṇu deva!
body.translated_text: The crane said: 'Listen, Your Majesty!'

children.text: yadi samaram apāsya nāsti mṛtyor
children.translated_text: 'If, by abandoning battle, there were no fear of death,

children.text: bhayam iti yuktam ito 'nyataḥ prayātum |
children.translated_text: then it would be proper to depart elsewhere from here;

children.text: atha maraṇam avaśyam eva jantoḥ
children.translated_text: but since death is inevitable for all creatures,

children.text: kim iti mudhā malinaṃ yaśaḥ kriyate ? // Hit_3.143 //
children.translated_text: why would one pointlessly tarnish one's reputation?'

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: 'And also —'

children.text: bhave'smin pavanodbhrānta-vīci-vibhrama-bhaṅgure |
children.translated_text: 'In this existence, as fleeting as the play of waves tossed by the wind,

children.text: jāyate puṇay-yogena parārthe jīvita-vyayaḥ // Hit_3.144 //
children.translated_text: the spending of one's life for another's sake occurs only through the merit of [past] good deeds.'

children.text: svāmy-amātyaś ca rāṣṭraṃ ca durgaṃ kośo balaṃ suhṛt |
children.translated_text: 'The king, the minister, the realm, the fortress, the treasury, the army, and the ally —

children.text: rājyāṅgāni prakṛtayaḥ paurāṇāṃ śreṇayo 'pi ca // Hit_3.145 //
children.translated_text: these are the constituents of a kingdom, along with the subjects and the guilds of citizens.'

body.text: deva ! tvaṃ ca svāmī sarvathā rakṣaṇīyaḥ | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: 'Your Majesty, you are the sovereign and must be protected by all means. For —'

children.text: prakṛtiḥ svāminaṃ tyaktvā samṛddhāpi na jīvati |
children.translated_text: 'The subjects, even when prosperous, do not survive if they abandon the sovereign;

children.text: api dhanvantarir vaidyaḥ kiṃ karoti gatāyuṣi // Hit_3.146 //
children.translated_text: what can even <s>Dhanvantari</s>, the physician, do for one whose life has departed?'

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'And furthermore —'

children.text: nareśe jīva-loko 'yaṃ nimīlati nimīlati |
children.translated_text: 'This world of the living closes as the lord closes [his eyes],

children.text: udety udīyamāne ca ravāv iva saroruham // Hit_3.147 //
children.translated_text: and opens as he rises, like a lotus at the rising of the sun.'

body.text: atrāpi pradhānāṅgaṃ rājā |
body.translated_text: 'In this matter too, the king is the principal constituent.'

body.text: atha kukkuṭenāgatya rājahaṃsasya śarīre kharatara-nakhāghātaḥ kṛtaḥ | tadā satvaram upasṛtya sārasena sva-dehāntarito rājā jale kṣiptaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then <s>Kukkuṭa</s> (the rooster) came and struck the body of the royal swan with his sharp claws. Thereupon the crane quickly came forward, interposed his own body, and threw the king into the water.

body.text: atha kukkuṭa-nakha-prahāra-jarjarīkṛtenāpi sārasena kukkuṭa-senā bahuśo hatā | paścāt sāraso 'pi bahubhiḥ pakṣibhiḥ sametya cañcu-prahāreṇa vibhidya vyāpāditaḥ | atha citravarṇo durgaṃ praviśya, durgāvasthitaṃ dravyaṃ grāhayitvā vandibhir jaya-śabdair ānanditaḥ sva-skandhāvāraṃ jagāma |
body.translated_text: Then, even though the crane was shattered by the rooster's claw-blows, he slew many of the rooster's army. Afterwards, the crane too, attacked by many birds together with beak-blows, was pierced and killed. Then <s>Citravarṇa</s> entered the fortress, seized the wealth stored within, and, gladdened by the cries of victory from the bards, returned to his own encampment.

body.text: atha rāja-putrair uktaṃ-tasmin rājahaṃsa-pakṣe puṇyavān sa sārasa eva, yena sva-deha-tyāgena svāmī rakṣitaḥ | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Then the princes said: 'In that party of the royal swan, the truly meritorious one was that crane alone, who protected his master by sacrificing his own body. For —'

children.text: janayanti sutān gāvaḥ sarvā eva gavākṛtīn |
children.translated_text: 'All cows give birth to calves that look like cows,

children.text: viṣāṇollikhita-skandhaṃ kācid eva gavāṃ patim // Hit_3.148 //
children.translated_text: but only a rare one [gives birth to] a lord of cattle with shoulders marked by horns.'

body.text: viṣṇuśarmovāca-sa tāvat sattva-krītān akṣaya-lokān vidyādharī-parivṛtto 'nubhavatu mahā-sattvaḥ | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s> said: 'Let that great-souled one enjoy the imperishable worlds purchased by his valor, attended by celestial maidens. And as it is said —'

children.text: āhaveṣu ca ye śūrāḥ svāmy-arthe tyakta-jīvitāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Those who are brave in battles, who have sacrificed their lives for their master's sake,

children.text: bhartṛ-bhaktāḥ kṛtajñāś ca te narāḥ svarga-gāminaḥ // Hit_3.149 //
children.translated_text: who are devoted to their lord and grateful — such men go to heaven.'

children.text: yatra tatra hataḥ śūraḥ śatrubhiḥ pariveṣṭitaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'A hero who is slain, surrounded by enemies, wherever he may be,

children.text: akṣayān labhate lokān yadi klaibyaṃ na gacchati // Hit_3.150 //
children.translated_text: attains imperishable worlds, provided he does not succumb to cowardice.'

body.text: atha viṣṇuśarmā prāha-vigrahaḥ śruto bhavadbhiḥ |
body.translated_text: Then <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s> said: 'The [book on] War has been heard by you.'

body.text: rājaputrair uktam-śrutvā sukhino bhūtā vayam |
body.translated_text: The princes said: 'Having heard it, we are delighted.'

body.text: viṣṇuśarmābravīt-aparam apy evam astu-
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s> said: 'May this also be so —'

children.text: vigrahaḥ kari-turaṅga-pattibhir
children.translated_text: 'May war with elephants, horses, and foot-soldiers

children.text: no kadāpi bhavatān mahībhujām |
children.translated_text: never befall you, O kings;

children.text: nīti-mantra-pavanaiḥ samāhatāḥ
children.translated_text: struck by the winds of wise counsel,

children.text: saṃśrayantu giri-gahvaraṃ dviṣaḥ // Hit_3.151 //
children.translated_text: may [your] enemies take refuge in mountain caves.'

body.text:
iti śrī-nārāyaṇa-paṇḍita-kṛte hitopadeśe nīti-śāstre
vigraho nāma tṛtīyaḥ kathā-saṅgrahaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus ends the third story-collection, called 'War,' in the <s>Hitopadeśa</s>, a treatise on <s>Nīti</s> (political wisdom), composed by the illustrious <s>Nārāyaṇa Paṇḍita</s>.

body.text:
iv.
sandhiḥ
body.translated_text: IV. Peace (<s>Sandhi</s>)

body.text: punaḥ kathārambha-kāle rāja-putrair uktam-ārya ! vigrahaḥ śruto 'smābhiḥ | sandhir adhunābhidhīyatām |
body.translated_text: Again, at the time of beginning the story, the princes said: 'Sir! We have heard [the book on] War. Now let Peace be narrated.'

body.text: viṣṇuśarmeṇoktam-śrūyatām | sandhim api kathayāmi | yasyāyam ādyaḥ ślokaḥ-
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s> said: 'Listen. I shall narrate Peace as well. Its opening verse is —'

children.text: vṛtte mahati saṅgrāme rājñor nihata-senayoḥ |
children.translated_text: 'After a great battle had taken place, when the armies of both kings were slain,

children.text: stheyābhyāṃ gṛdhra-cakrābhyāṃ vācā sandhiḥ kṛtaṃ kṣaṇat // Hit_4.1 //
children.translated_text: peace was made instantly through words by the two [parties], the vulture and the crane-wheel.'

body.text: rājaputrā ūcuḥ-katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The princes said: 'How was that?'

body.text: viṣṇuśarmā kathayati-tatas tena rājahaṃsena uktam-kenāsmad-durge nikṣipto 'gniḥ ? kiṃ pārakyeṇa ? kiṃ vāsmad-durga-vāsinā kenāpi vipakṣa-prayuktena ?
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s> narrates: 'Then that royal swan said: "By whom was the fire set in our fortress? By a foreigner? Or by one of our own fortress-dwellers, employed by the enemy?"'

body.text: cakravāko brūte-deva ! bhavato niṣkāraṇa-bandhur asau meghavarṇaḥ saparivāro na dṛśyate | tan manye tasyaiva viceṣṭitam idam |
body.translated_text: <s>Cakravāka</s> said — Your Majesty! That <s>Meghavarṇa</s>, your friend without cause, is not to be seen along with his retinue. Therefore I suspect this is his doing.

body.text: rājā kṣaṇaṃ vicintyāha-asti tāvad evam | mama durdaivam etat | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: The king, after reflecting for a moment, said — It is indeed so. This is my misfortune. And so it is said —

children.text: aparādhaḥ sa daivasya na punar mantriṇām ayam |
children.translated_text: This is the fault of fate, not of the ministers;

children.text: kāryaṃ sucaritaṃ kvāpi daiva-yogād vinaśyati // Hit_4.2 //
children.translated_text: Even well-executed plans are sometimes destroyed by the workings of fate. // Hit_4.2 //

children.text: viṣamāṃ hi daśāṃ prāpya daivaṃ garhayate naraḥ |
children.translated_text: A person in adversity blames fate,

children.text: ātmanaḥ karma-doṣāṃś ca naiva jānāty apaṇḍitaḥ // Hit_4.3 //
children.translated_text: But the foolish one does not recognize the faults of his own actions. // Hit_4.3 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: suhṛdāṃ hita-kāmānāṃ yo vākyaṃ nābhinandati |
children.translated_text: He who does not welcome the words of well-wishing friends,

children.text: sa kūrma iva durbuddhiḥ kāṣṭhād bhraṣṭo vinaśyati // Hit_4.4 //
children.translated_text: That fool, like the tortoise, falls from the stick and perishes. // Hit_4.4 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: rakṣitavyaṃ sadā vākyaṃ vākyād bhavati nāśanam |
children.translated_text: One should always guard one's speech, for speech can bring destruction;

children.text: haṃsābhyāṃ nīyamānasya kūrmasya patanaṃ yathā // Hit_4.5 //
children.translated_text: Just as the tortoise, while being carried by the two swans, fell. // Hit_4.5 //

body.text: rāhāha-katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The king said — How is that?

body.text:
mantrī kathayati-
kathā 1
body.translated_text: The minister narrates — Story 1

body.text: asti magadha-deśe phullotpalābhidhānaṃ saraḥ | tatra ciraṃ saṅkaṭa-vikaṭa-nāmānau haṃsau nivasataḥ | tayor mitraṃ kambugrīva-nāmā kūrmaś ca prativasati | athaikadā dhīvarair āgatya tathoktaṃ yat-atrāsmābhir adyoṣitvā prātar matsya-kūrmādayo vyāpādayitavyāḥ |
body.translated_text: In the land of <s>Magadha</s>, there is a lake named <s>Phullotpala</s> (Full-of-Lotuses). There, two swans named <s>Saṅkaṭa</s> and <s>Vikaṭa</s> had long resided. Their friend, a tortoise named <s>Kambugrīva</s> (Conch-neck), also dwelt there. Once, fishermen came and said — Having camped here today, we shall kill the fish, tortoises and others tomorrow morning.

body.text: tad ākarṇya kūrmo haṃsāv āha-suhṛdau ! śruto 'yaṃ dhīvarālāpaḥ | adhunā kiṃ mayā kartavyam?
body.translated_text: Hearing that, the tortoise said to the swans — Dear friends! You have heard this talk of the fishermen. Now what should I do?

body.text: haṃsāv āhatuḥ-jñāyatāṃ tāvat | punas tāvat prātar yad ucitaṃ tat kartavyam |
body.translated_text: The two swans said — Let us first see. Tomorrow morning, whatever is proper shall be done.

body.text: kūrmo brūte-maivam | yato dṛṣṭa-vyatikaro 'ham atra | yathā coktam-
body.translated_text: The tortoise said — Not so! For I have witnessed the danger here firsthand. As it is said —

children.text: anāgata-vidhātā ca pratyutpanna-matis tathā |
children.translated_text: The one who plans for the future and the one who is quick-witted in the present —

children.text: dvāv eva sukham edhete yad-bhaviṣyo vinaśyati // Hit_4.6 //
children.translated_text: These two alone prosper happily; the one who says 'whatever will be' perishes. // Hit_4.6 //

body.text: tāv ūcatuḥ-katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The two asked — How is that?

body.text: kūrmaḥ kathayati-
body.translated_text: The tortoise narrates —

body.text: kathā 2
body.translated_text: Story 2

body.text: purāsminn eva sarasy evaṃvidheṣv eva dhīvareṣūpasthiteṣu matsya-trayeṇālocitam | tatrānāgata-vidhātā nāmaiko matsyaḥ | tenoktaṃ-ahaṃ tāvaj-jalāśayāntaraṃ gacchāmi | ity uktvā sa hradāntaraṃ gataḥ | apareṇa pratyutpannamati-nāmnā mastyenābhihitam-bhaviṣyad-arthe pramāṇābhāvāt kutra mayā gantavyam ? tad utpanne yathā-kāryaṃ tad anuṣṭheyam | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: Once before, in this very lake, when just such fishermen had arrived, three fish deliberated. Among them, one fish was named <s>Anāgatavidhātā</s> (Planner-for-the-Future). He said — I shall go to another body of water. Having said so, he went to another lake. Another fish, named <s>Pratyutpannamati</s> (Quick-witted), said — Since there is no certainty about the future, where should I go? When trouble arises, one should act as the situation demands. As it is said —

children.text: utpannām āpadaṃ yas tu samādhatte sa buddhimān |
children.translated_text: He who can manage a calamity when it arises is truly wise;

children.text: vaṇijo bhāryayā jāraḥ pratyakṣe nihnuto yathā // Hit_4.7 //
children.translated_text: Just as the merchant's wife concealed her lover even when caught in the act. // Hit_4.7 //

body.text: yadbhaviṣyaḥ pṛcchati-katham etat ?
body.translated_text: <s>Yadbhaviṣya</s> (Whatever-will-be) asks — How is that?

body.text: pratyutpannamatiḥ kathayati-
body.translated_text: <s>Pratyutpannamati</s> narrates —

body.text: kathā 3
body.translated_text: Story 3

body.text: purā vikramapure samudradatto nāma vaṇig asti | tasya ratnaprabhā nāma gṛhiṇī sva-sevakena saha sadā ramate | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Once, in <s>Vikramapura</s>, there was a merchant named <s>Samudradatta</s>. His wife, named <s>Ratnaprabhā</s>, always sported with her own servant. For —

children.text: na strīṇām apriyaḥ kaścit priyo vāpi na vidyate |
children.translated_text: There is no man who is truly displeasing to women, nor any who is truly dear;

children.text: gāvas tṛṇam ivāraṇye prārthayante navaṃ navam // Hit_4.8 //
children.translated_text: Like cows in the forest seeking grass, they ever desire what is new. // Hit_4.8 //

body.text: athaikadā sā ratnaprabhā tasya sevakasya mukhe cumbanaṃ dadatī samudradattenāvalokitā | tataḥ sā bandhakī satvaraṃ bhartuḥ samīpaṃ matvāha-nātha ! etasya sevakasya mahatī nikṛtiḥ | yato 'yaṃ caurikāṃ kṛtvā karpūraṃ khādatīti | mayāsya mukham āghrāya jñātam | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: Once, that <s>Ratnaprabhā</s>, while kissing the servant's mouth, was observed by <s>Samudradatta</s>. Thereupon that harlot quickly approached her husband and said — My lord! This servant has committed a great offense, for he has been stealing and eating camphor, and I smelled it on his mouth. As it is said —

children.text: āhāro dviguṇaḥ strīṇāṃ buddhis tāsāṃ catur-guṇā |
children.translated_text: Women's appetite is double, their intelligence fourfold,

children.text: ṣaḍ-guṇo vyavasāyaś ca kāmāś cāṣṭaguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ // Hit_4.9 //
children.translated_text: Their enterprise sixfold, and their desire is said to be eightfold. // Hit_4.9 //

body.text: tac chrutvā sevakenāpi prakupyoktaṃ-nātha ! yasya svāmino gṛhe etādṛśī bhāryā tatra sevakena kathaṃ sthātavyam ? yatra ca pratikṣaṇaṃ gṛhiṇī sevakasya mukhaṃ jighrati | tato 'sāv utthāya calitaḥ | sādhunā ca yatnāt prabodhya dhṛtaḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-utpannām āpadam ity ādi |
body.translated_text: Hearing this, the servant also spoke angrily — My lord! How can a servant remain in a master's house where such a wife resides? Where the mistress of the house is constantly sniffing the servant's mouth! Then he rose and began to leave. The good man had to make great effort to calm him and make him stay. Therefore I say — 'He who can manage a calamity when it arises,' and so on.

body.text: tato yadbhaviṣyeṇoktam-
body.translated_text: Then <s>Yadbhaviṣya</s> said —

children.text: yad abhāvi na tad bhāvi bhāvi cen na tad anyathā |
children.translated_text: What was not to be will not be; what is to be cannot be otherwise;

children.text: iti cintā-viṣa-ghno 'yam agadaḥ kiṃ na pīyate // Hit_4.10 //
children.translated_text: This antidote destroys the poison of anxiety — why is it not drunk? // Hit_4.10 //

body.text: tataḥ prātar jālena baddhaḥ pratyutpannamatir mṛtavad ātmānaṃ sandarśya sthitaḥ | tato jālād apasārito yathāśakty utplutya gabhīraṃ nīraṃ praviṣṭaḥ | yadbhaviṣyaś ca dhīvaraiḥ prāpto vyāpāditaḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-anāgata-vidhātā ca ity ādi | tad yathāham anyaṃ hradaṃ prāpnomi tathā kriyatām |
body.translated_text: Then in the morning, <s>Pratyutpannamati</s>, caught in the net, displayed himself as if dead and lay still. When removed from the net, he leapt with all his might and plunged into deep water. But <s>Yadbhaviṣya</s> was caught by the fishermen and killed. Therefore I say — 'The one who plans for the future,' and so on. So let it be arranged that I may reach another lake.

body.text: haṃsāv āhatuḥ-jalāśayāntare prāpte tava kuśalam | sthale gacchatas te ko vidhiḥ ?
body.translated_text: The two swans said — Once you reach another body of water, all will be well for you. But how shall you travel overland?

body.text: kūrma āha-yathāhaṃ bhavadbhyāṃ sahākāśa-vartmanā yāmi, tathā vidhīyatām |
body.translated_text: The tortoise said — Arrange it so that I may travel with you through the sky.

body.text: haṃsāv brūtaḥ-katham upāyaḥ sambhavati ?
body.translated_text: The two swans said — How is such a device possible?

body.text: kacchapo vadati-yuvābhyāṃ cañcu-dhṛtaṃ kāṣṭha-khaṇḍam ekaṃ mayā mukhenāvalambitavyam | tataś ca yuvayoḥ pakṣa-balena mayāpi sukhena gantavyam |
body.translated_text: The tortoise said — You two hold a stick in your beaks, and I shall grip it with my mouth. Then, by the power of your wings, I too shall travel comfortably.

body.text: haṃsau brūtaḥ-sambhavaty eṣa upāyaḥ | kintu-
body.translated_text: The swans said — This device is possible. However —

children.text: upāyaṃ cintayet prājño hy apāyam api cintayet |
children.translated_text: A wise person should think of the means and also think of the dangers;

children.text: paśyato baka-mūrkhasya nakulair bhakṣitāḥ sutāḥ // Hit_4.11 //
children.translated_text: While the foolish crane watched, his young ones were devoured by the mongoose. // Hit_4.11 //

body.text: kūrmaḥ pṛcchati--katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The tortoise asks — How is that?

body.text:
tau kathayataḥ-
kathā 4
body.translated_text: The two narrate — Story 4

body.text: asty uttarā-pathe gṛdhrakūṭa-nāmni parvate mahān pippala-vṛkṣaḥ | tatrāneke bakā nivasanti | tasya vṛkṣasyādhastād vivare sarpas tiṣṭhati | sa ca bakānāṃ bālāpatyāni khādati | atha śokārtānāṃ vilāpaṃ śrutvā kenacid vṛddha-bakenābhihitaṃ-bho evaṃ kuruta, yūyaṃ matsyān upādāya nakula-vivarād ārabhya sarpa-vivaraṃ yāvat-paṅkti-krameṇa ekaikaśo vikirata | tatas tad-āhāra-lubdhair nakulair āgatya sarpo draṣṭavyaḥ | svabhāva-dveṣād vyāpadayitavyaś ca | tathānuṣṭhite sati tad vṛttam |
body.translated_text: In the northern country, on a mountain named <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak), there stands a great <s>pippala</s> (fig) tree. Many cranes dwell there. In a hole beneath that tree lives a serpent, and he devours the young chicks of the cranes. Now, upon hearing the lamentations of the grief-stricken ones, a certain old crane said — Do this: take some fish and scatter them one by one in a line from the mongoose's hole all the way to the serpent's hole. Then the mongooses, lured by the food, will come and see the serpent, and out of natural enmity will kill him. When this was done, so it happened.

body.text: atha nakulair vṛkṣopari baka-śāvakānāṃ rāvaḥ śrutaḥ | paścāt tad-vṛkṣam āruhya baka-śāvakāḥ khāditāḥ | ata āvāṃ brūvaḥ-upāyaṃ cintayan ity ādi |
body.translated_text: Then the mongooses heard the cries of the crane-chicks atop the tree. Afterwards they climbed that tree and devoured the crane-chicks. Therefore we say — 'A wise person should think of the means,' and so on.

body.text: āvābhyāṃ nīyamānaṃ tvām avalokya lokaiḥ kiṃcid vaktavyam eva | yadi tvam uttaraṃ dāsyasi, tadā tvan-maraṇam | tat sarvathaiva sthīyatām |
body.translated_text: While you are being carried by us, people seeing you will surely say something. If you give a reply, it will be your death. So you must remain absolutely silent.

body.text: kūrmo vadati-kim aham aprājñaḥ ? nāham uttaraṃ dāsyāmi | na kim api mayā vaktavyam | tathānuṣṭhite tathā-vidhaṃ kūrmam ālokya sarve go-rakṣakāḥ paścād dhāvanti, vadanti ca-aho ! mahad āścaryam ! pakṣibhyāṃ kūrmo nīyate |
body.translated_text: The tortoise said — Am I not wise? I shall not give any reply. I shall say nothing at all. When it was so arranged, seeing the tortoise being carried thus, all the cowherds ran after them, saying — Oh! What a great wonder! A tortoise is being carried by two birds!

body.text: kaścid vadati-yady ayaṃ kūrmaḥ patati, tadātraiva paktvā khāditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: One said — If this tortoise falls, we shall cook and eat it right here.

body.text: kaścid vadati-sarasas tīre dagdhvā khāditavyo 'yam |
body.translated_text: Another said — We should burn and eat it on the bank of the lake.

body.text: kaścid vadati-gṛhaṃ nītvā bhakṣaṇīyaḥ | iti |
body.translated_text: Yet another said — We should take it home and eat it.

body.text: tad-vacanaṃ śrutvā sa kūrmaḥ kopāviṣṭo vismṛta-pūrva-saṃskāraḥ prāha-yuṣmābhir bhasma bhakṣitavyam iti vadann eva patitas tair vyāpāditaś ca | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-suhṛdāṃ hita-kāmānām ity ādi |
body.translated_text: Hearing their words, that tortoise, overcome with rage and forgetting his prior resolve, said — You shall eat ashes! — and as he spoke, he fell, and was killed by them. Therefore I say — 'He who does not welcome the words of well-wishing friends,' and so on.

body.text: atha praṇidhir bakas tatrāgatyovāca-deva ! prāg eva mayā nigaditaṃ durga-śodha hi pratikṣaṇaṃ kartavyam iti | tac ca yuṣmābhir na kṛtaṃ, tad-anavadhānasya phalam idam anubhūtam | durga-dāho meghavarṇena vāyasena gṛdhra-pratyuktena kṛtaḥ | rājā niḥśvasyāha-
body.translated_text: Now the spy, the crane, came there and said — Your Majesty! I had told you earlier that the fortress should be inspected constantly. That was not done by you; hence you have suffered the fruit of this negligence. The burning of the fortress was done by <s>Meghavarṇa</s> the crow, as advised by the vulture. The king sighed and said —

children.text: praṇayād upakārād vā yo viśvasiti śatruṣu |
children.translated_text: He who trusts enemies out of affection or past favors,

children.text: sa supta iva vṛkṣāgrāt patitaḥ pratibudhyate // Hit_4.12 //
children.translated_text: Awakens as if from sleep after falling from the top of a tree. // Hit_4.12 //

body.text: atha praṇidhir uvāca-ito durgadāhaṃ vidhāya, yadā yato meghavarṇas tadā citravarṇena prasāditenoktam-ayaṃ meghavarṇo 'tra karpūra-dvīpa-rājye'bhiṣicyatām | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: Then the spy said — After burning the fortress and departing, <s>Meghavarṇa</s> was addressed by <s>Citravarṇa</s>, who had been gratified, and said — Let this <s>Meghavarṇa</s> be consecrated as king in this kingdom of <s>Karpūradvīpa</s> (Camphor Island). As it is said —

children.text: kṛta-kṛtyasya bhṛtyasya kṛtaṃ naiva praṇāśayet |
children.translated_text: One should not destroy the achievement of a servant who has accomplished his task;

children.text: phalena manasā vācā dṛṣṭyā cainaṃ praharṣayet // Hit_4.13 //
children.translated_text: One should delight him with reward, with heart, with words, and with regard. // Hit_4.13 //

body.text: cakravāko brūte-deva ! śrutaṃ yat praṇidhiḥ kathayati ?
body.translated_text: <s>Cakravāka</s> said — Your Majesty! Did you hear what the spy reports?

body.text: rājā prāha--tatas tataḥ ?
body.translated_text: The king said — And then what?

body.text: praṇidhir uvāca-tataḥ pradhāna-mantriṇā gṛdhreṇābhihitam-deva ! nedam ucitam | prasādāntaraṃ kim api kriyatām | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: The spy said — Then the chief minister, the vulture, said — Your Majesty! This is not proper. Let some other favor be granted. For —

children.text: avicārayato yukti-kathanaṃ tuṣa-khaṇḍanam |
children.translated_text: Speaking reason to one who does not reflect is like pounding husks;

children.text: nīceṣūpakṛtaṃ rājan bālukāsv iva mūtritam // Hit_4.14 //
children.translated_text: A favor done to the low, O king, is like urinating on sand. // Hit_4.14 //

body.text: mahatām āspade nīcaḥ kadāpi na kartavyaḥ | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: A base person should never be placed in the position of the great. As it is said —

children.text: nīcaḥ ślāghya-padaṃ prāpya svāminaṃ hantum icchati |
children.translated_text: A base person, having attained a praiseworthy position, desires to kill his master;

children.text: mūṣiko vyāghratāṃ prāpya muniṃ hantuṃ gato yathā // Hit_4.15 //
children.translated_text: Just as the mouse, having attained the state of a tiger, went to kill the sage. // Hit_4.15 //

body.text: citravarṇaḥ pṛcchati--katham etat ?
body.translated_text: <s>Citravarṇa</s> asks — How is that?

body.text:
mantrī kathayati-
kathā 5
body.translated_text: The minister narrates — Story 5

body.text: asti gautamasya maharṣes tapovane mahātapā nāma muniḥ | tatra tena āśrama-saṃnidhāne mūṣika-śāvakaḥ kāka-mukhād bhraṣṭo dṛṣṭaḥ | tato dayā-yuktena tena muniā nīvāra-kaṇaiḥ saṃvardhitaḥ | tato biḍālas taṃ mūṣikaṃ khāditum upadhāvati | tam avalokya mūṣikas tasya muneḥ kroḍe praviveśa | tato muninoktam-mūṣika ! tvaṃ mārjāro bhava | tataḥ sa biḍālaḥ kukkuraṃ dṛṣṭvā palāyate | tato muninoktaṃ-kukkurād bibheṣi, tvam eva kukkuro bhava | sa ca kukkuro vyāghrād bibheti tatas tena muninā kukkuro vyāghraḥ kṛtaḥ |
body.translated_text: In the penance-grove of the great sage <s>Gautama</s>, there lived an ascetic named <s>Mahātapā</s> (Great-Ascetic). Near his hermitage, he saw a baby mouse that had fallen from a crow's beak. Out of compassion, the sage raised it with grains of wild rice. Then a cat would chase the mouse to eat it. Seeing this, the mouse took refuge in the sage's lap. The sage said — Mouse, become a cat! Then that cat, seeing a dog, would run away. The sage said — You fear the dog? Become a dog yourself! That dog feared a tiger; so the sage turned the dog into a tiger.

body.text: atha taṃ vyāghraṃ munir mūṣiko 'yam iti paśyati | atha taṃ muniṃ vyāghraṃ ca dṛṣṭvā sarve vadanti-anena muninā mūṣiko vyāghratāṃ nītaḥ | etac chrutvā sa-vyatho vyāghro 'cintayat-yāvad anena muninā sthīyate, tāvad idaṃ me svarūpākhyānam akīrtikaraṃ na palāyiṣyate ity ālocya mūṣikas taṃ muniṃ hantuṃ gataḥ | tato muninā taj jñātvā-punar mūṣiko bhava ity uktvā mūṣika eva kṛtaḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-nīcaḥ ślāghya-padaṃ prāpyety ādi // Hit_4.
body.translated_text: Now the sage still regarded that tiger as a mouse. And seeing both the sage and the tiger, everyone said — This sage has turned a mouse into a tiger. Hearing this, the tiger, distressed, thought — As long as this sage lives, this account of my true form, which brings me disgrace, will not cease. So thinking, the mouse-turned-tiger went to kill the sage. The sage, knowing this, said — Become a mouse again! — and made him a mouse once more. Therefore I say — 'A base person, having attained a praiseworthy position,' and so on. // Hit_4.

body.text: aparaṃ ca, deva ! sukaram idam iti na mantavyam | śṛṇu-
body.translated_text: And moreover, Your Majesty! Do not think this is easy to handle. Listen —

children.text: bhakṣayitvā bahūn matsyān uttamādhama-madhyamān |
children.translated_text: Having devoured many fish — superior, inferior, and middling —

children.text: atilobhād bakaḥ paścān mṛtaḥ karkaṭaka-grahāt // Hit_4.16 //
children.translated_text: The crane, out of excessive greed, was finally killed by the grip of a crab. // Hit_4.16 //

body.text: citravarṇaḥ pṛcchati--katham etat ?
body.translated_text: <s>Citravarṇa</s> asks — How is that?

body.text:
mantrī kathayati-
kathā 6
body.translated_text: The minister narrates — Story 6

body.text: asti mālava-viṣaye padmagarbhābhidhānaṃ saraḥ | tatraiko vṛddho bakaḥ sāmarthya-hīna udvignam ivātmānaṃ darśayitvā sthitaḥ | sa ca kenacit kulīraṇe dūrād eva dṛṣṭaḥ | pṛṣṭaś ca-kim iti bhavān atrāhāra-tyāgena tiṣṭhati ?
body.translated_text: In the <s>Mālava</s> region, there is a lake named <s>Padmagarbha</s> (Lotus-hearted). There, an old crane, devoid of strength, stood displaying himself as if distressed. He was seen from afar by a certain crab, who asked — Why are you standing here, having given up food?

body.text: bakenoktam-matsyā mama jīvana-hetavaḥ | te kaivartair āgatya vyāpādayitavyā iti vārtā nagaropānte mayā śrutā | ato vartanābhāvād evāsman maraṇam upasthitam iti jñātvāhāre'py anādaraḥ kṛtaḥ | tato matsyair ālocitam-iha samaye tāvad upakāraka evāyaṃ lakṣyate | tad ayam eva yathā-kartavyaṃ pṛcchyatām | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: <s>The crane said</s> — Fish are the means of my livelihood. I heard news near the town that fishermen will come and kill them. Therefore, knowing that my death has come due to the loss of my sustenance, I have lost all desire for food. Then the fish deliberated — At this time, he indeed appears to be a benefactor. So let him be asked what should be done. As it is said —

children.text: upakartrāriṇā sandhir na mitreṇāpakāriṇā |
children.translated_text: Alliance with an enemy who helps is preferable to a friend who harms.

children.text: upakārāpakāro hi lakṣyaṃ lakṣaṇam etayoḥ // Hit_4.17 //
children.translated_text: For benefit and harm are indeed the mark and characteristic of these two. // <s>Hit</s>_4.17 //

body.text: matsyā ūcuḥ-bho baka ! ko 'tra asmākaṃ rakṣanopāyaḥ ?
body.translated_text: The fish said — O crane! What means of protection is there for us here?

body.text: bako brūte-asti rakṣaṇopāyo jalāśayāntarāśrayaṇam | tatrāham ekaikaśo yuṣmān nayāmi |
body.translated_text: The crane said — There is a means of protection: taking refuge in another body of water. I shall carry you there one by one.

body.text: matsyā āhuḥ-evam astu | tato 'sau duṣṭa-bakas tān matsyān ekaikaśo nītvā khādati | anantaraṃ kulīras tam uvāca-bho baka ! mām api tatra naya | tato bako 'py apūrva-kulīra-māṃsārthī sādaraṃ taṃ nītvā sthale dhṛtavān | kulīro 'pi mastya-kaṇṭakākīrṇaṃ taṃ sthalam ālokyācintayat-hā hato 'smi manda-bhāgyaḥ | bhavatu idānīṃ samayocitaṃ vyavahariṣyāmi | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: The fish said — So be it! Then that wicked crane, carrying the fish one by one, devoured them. Next, a crab said to him — O crane! Take me there too! Then the crane, desiring the novel taste of crab meat, carried him respectfully and placed him on dry ground. The crab, seeing that ground strewn with fish bones, thought — Alas! I am doomed, wretched as I am. So be it — I shall now act as the occasion demands. For —

children.text: tāvad bhayena bhetavyaṃ yāvad bhayam anāgatam |
children.translated_text: One should fear danger only so long as the danger has not yet arrived;

children.text: āgataṃ tu bhayaṃ dṛṣṭvā praharatvayam abhītivat // Hit_4.18 //
children.translated_text: But seeing danger that has come, one should strike as if fearless. // <s>Hit</s>_4.18 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: abhiyukto yadā paśyen na kiñcid gatim ātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: When one under attack sees no escape for himself,

children.text: yudhyamānas tadā prājño mriyate ripuṇā saha // Hit_4.19 //
children.translated_text: Then the wise man, fighting, dies together with his enemy. // <s>Hit</s>_4.19 //

body.text: ity ālocya sa kulīrakas tasya bakasya grīvāṃ ciccheda | atha sa bakaḥ pañcatvaṃ gataḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-bhakṣayitvā bahūn matsyān ity ādi |
body.translated_text: Having reflected thus, that crab severed the crane's neck. And so the crane perished. Therefore I say — "Having devoured many fish" and so forth.
[Story break]

body.text: tataś citravarṇo 'vadat-śṛṇu tāvan mantrin ! mayaitad ālocitam | asti yad atrāvasthitenānena meghavarṇena rājñā yāvanti vastūni karpūra-dvīpasyottamāni tāvanty asmākam upanetavyāni | tenāsmābhir mahā-sukhena vindhyācale sthātavyam | dūradarśī vihasyāha-deva !
body.translated_text: Then <s>Citravarṇa</s> said — Listen, minister! I have considered this: while <s>Meghavarṇa</s>, the king, remains stationed here, however many excellent things belong to <s>Karpūra-dvīpa</s>, all those must be brought to us. Thus we shall dwell in great comfort on <s>Vindhyācala</s>. <s>Dūradarśī</s> laughed and said — Your Majesty!

children.text: anāgatavatīṃ cintāṃ kṛtvā yas tu prahṛṣyati |
children.translated_text: He who rejoices having entertained expectations about things that have not yet come to pass,

children.text: sa tiraskāram āpnoti bhagna-bhāṇḍo dvijo yathā // Hit_4.20 //
children.translated_text: He meets with humiliation, like the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> whose pots were broken. // <s>Hit</s>_4.20 //

body.text: rājāha--katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The king said — How is that?

body.text:
mantrī kathayati---
kathā 7
body.translated_text:
The minister tells —
Story 7

body.text:
asti devī-koṭa-nāmni nagare devaśarmā nāma brāhmaṇaḥ | tena mahāviṣuvat-saṅkrāntyāṃ saktupūrṇaśarāva ekaḥ prāptaḥ | tatas tam ādāyāsau kumbhakārasya bhāṇḍapūrṇa-maṇḍapaika-deśe raudreṇākulitaḥ suptaḥ | tataḥ saktu-rakṣārthaṃ haste daṇḍam ekam ādāyācintayat-adyāhaṃ saktuśarāvaṃ vikrīya daśa kapardakān prāpsyāmi, tadātraiva taiḥ kapardakair ghaṭaśarāvādikam upakrīyānekadhā vṛddhais tad-dhanaiḥ punaḥ punaḥ pūrga-vastrādim upakrīya, vikrīya lakṣa-saṅkhyāni dhanāni kṛtvā, vivāha-catuṣṭayaṃ kariṣyāmi | anantaraṃ tāsu sva-patnīṣu yā rūpa-yauvanavatī tasyām adhikānurāgaṃ kariṣyāmi | sapatnyo yadā dvandvaṃ kariṣyāmi, tadā kopākulo 'haṃ tāḥ sarvā laguḍena tāḍayiṣyāmīty
abhidhāya tena laguḍaḥ prakṣiptaḥ | tena saktuśarāvaś cūrṇito bhāṇḍāni ca bahūni bhagnāni | tatas tena śabdenāgatena kumbhakāreṇa tathā-vidhāni bhāṇḍāny avalokya, brāhmaṇas tiraskṛto maṇḍapād bahiṣkṛtaś ca | ato 'haṃ bravīmi - anāgatavatīṃ cintām ity ādi |
body.translated_text: In a city called <s>Devīkoṭa</s>, there was a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Devaśarman</s>. At the great <s>Viṣuvat-saṅkrānti</s> (equinox festival), he obtained a pot full of barley flour. Taking it, he went to a potter's pavilion full of wares and, overcome by the heat, fell asleep. Then, holding a stick in his hand to guard the barley flour, he thought — Today I shall sell this pot of barley flour and obtain ten <s>kapardakas</s> (cowrie coins); then, right here, with those <s>kapardakas</s> I shall buy pots, bowls and the like, and with the money multiplied many times over, I shall again and again buy betel, cloth and other goods, and selling them, I shall amass wealth numbering in the hundreds of thousands, and I shall perform four marriages! Then, among those wives of mine, whichever one is most beautiful and youthful, upon her I shall bestow the greatest affection. When the co-wives quarrel, then, filled with anger, I shall beat them all with this stick! — Having said this, he flung the stick. By that, the pot of barley flour was smashed and many of the potter's wares were broken. Then the potter, arriving at the sound and seeing his wares in such a state, reviled the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and expelled him from the pavilion. Therefore I say — "He who rejoices having entertained expectations" and so forth.
[Story break]

body.text: tato rājā rahasi gṛdhram uvāca-tāta ! yathā kartavyaṃ tathopadiśa |
body.translated_text: Then the king said to the vulture in private — Father! Instruct me as to what should be done.

body.text: gṛdhro brūte-
body.translated_text: The vulture said —

children.text: madoddhatasya nṛpateḥ prakīrṇasyeva dantinaḥ |
children.translated_text: The guides of a king maddened by pride, like a rogue elephant running loose,

children.text: gacchanty unmārga-yātasya netāraḥ khalu vācyatām // Hit_4.21 //
children.translated_text: Who has gone astray — they are surely reduced to mere remonstrance. // <s>Hit</s>_4.21 //

body.text: śṛṇu deva ! kim asmābhir bala-darpād durgaṃ bhagnam ? uta tava pratāpādhiṣṭhitenopāyena ?
body.translated_text: Listen, Your Majesty! Did we break the fortress by the arrogance of our strength? Or was it by a stratagem guided by your prowess?

body.text: rājāha-bhavatām upāyena |
body.translated_text: The king said — By the stratagem of you all.

body.text: gṛdhro brūte-yady asmad-vacanaṃ kriyate, tadā sva-deśe gamyatām | anyathā varṣā-kāle prāpte punas tulya-balena vigrahe saty asmākaṃ para-bhūmiṣṭhānāṃ sva-deśa-gamanam api durlabhaṃ bhaviṣyati | tat-sukha-śobhārthaṃ sandhāya gamyatām | durgaṃ bhagnaṃ, kīrtiś ca labdheva | mama saṃmataṃ tāvad etat | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: The vulture said — If our counsel is heeded, then let us return to our own land. Otherwise, when the rainy season arrives, and war resumes with an equally powerful foe, it will be difficult even for us, stationed in enemy territory, to return home. Therefore, let us make peace and depart, for the sake of ease and glory. The fortress has been broken and fame has been won. This is my considered view. For —

children.text: yo hi dharmaṃ puraskṛtya hitvā bhartuḥ priyāpriye |
children.translated_text: He who, placing <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) foremost and setting aside what pleases or displeases his master,

children.text: apriyāṇy āha pathyāni tena rājā sahāyavān // Hit_4.22 //
children.translated_text: Speaks unpleasant but salutary words — through him the king is truly well-supported. // <s>Hit</s>_4.22 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: suhṛd-balaṃ tathā rājyam ātmānaṃ kīrtim eva ca |
children.translated_text: One's allied strength, one's kingdom, one's own self, and one's fame —

children.text: yudhi sandehadolāsthaṃ ko hi kuryād abāliśaḥ // Hit_4.23 //
children.translated_text: Who but a fool would place all these on the swaying balance of battle's uncertainty? // <s>Hit</s>_4.23 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: sandhim icchet samenāpi sandigdho vijayo yudhi |
children.translated_text: One should seek peace even with an equal, for victory in war is uncertain;

children.text: nahi saṃśayitaṃ kuryād ity uvāca bṛhaspatiḥ // Hit_4.24 //
children.translated_text: One should never undertake what is doubtful — thus spoke <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. // <s>Hit</s>_4.24 //

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: yuddhe vināśo bhavati kadācid ubhayor api |
children.translated_text: In war, destruction befalls sometimes both sides;

children.text: sundopa-sundāv anyonyaṃ naṣṭau tulya-balau na kim // Hit_4.25 //
children.translated_text: Did not <s>Sunda</s> and <s>Upasunda</s>, being of equal strength, destroy each other? // <s>Hit</s>_4.25 //

body.text: rājovāca--katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The king said — How is that?

body.text: mantrī kathayati-
body.translated_text: The minister tells —

body.text: kathā 8
body.translated_text: Story 8

body.text: purā daityau sahodarau sundopasunda-nāmānau mahatā kāya-kleśena trailokya-rājya-kāmanayā cirāc candra-śekharam ārādhitavantau | tatas tayor bhagavān parituṣṭaḥ san varaṃ varayatam ity uvāca | anantaraṃ tayoḥ kaṇṭhādhiṣṭhitāyāḥ sarasvatyāḥ prabhāvāt tāv anyad vaktu-kāmāv anyad-abhihitavantau-yady āvayor bhavān parituṣṭas tadā sva-priyāṃ pārvatīṃ parameśvaro dadātu |
body.translated_text: Long ago, there were two <s>Daitya</s> (demon) brothers named <s>Sunda</s> and <s>Upasunda</s>. With great bodily austerity, desiring sovereignty over the three worlds, they worshipped <s>Candraśekhara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) for a long time. Then the Lord, well pleased with them, said — Choose your boon! Thereupon, by the power of <s>Sarasvatī</s> stationed at their throats, those two, wishing to say one thing, uttered another — If the Lord is pleased with us, then let the Supreme Lord give us his beloved <s>Pārvatī</s>!

body.text: atha bhagavatā kruddhena varadānasyāvaśyakatayā, vicāra-mūḍhayoḥ pārvatī pradattā | tatas tasyā rūpa-lāvaṇya-lubdhābhyāṃ, jagad-ghātibhyāṃ masasotsukābhyāṃ, pāpa-timirābhyām, mamety anyonyaṃ kalahāyamānābhyāṃ, pramāṇa-puruṣaḥ kaścit pṛcchyatām iti matau kṛtāyāṃ, sa eva bhaṭṭārako vṛddha-dvija-rūpaḥ samāgatya tatropasthitaḥ | anantaraṃ-āvābhyām iyaṃ sva-bala-labdhā, kasyeyam āvayor bhavati iti brāhmaṇam apṛcchatām | brāhmaṇo brūte-
body.translated_text: Then the Lord, angered yet bound by the necessity of granting the boon, gave <s>Pārvatī</s> to those two who were confused in judgment. Then those two, infatuated by her beauty and loveliness, destroyers of the world, burning with mutual longing, enveloped in the darkness of sin, quarreling with each other saying "She is mine!" — when they resolved that some arbiter should be consulted, that very Lord, having arrived in the form of an aged <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, stood before them. Then they asked the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — She was won by our own strength; to which of us does she belong?. The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> said —

children.text: jñāna-śreṣṭho dvijaḥ pūjyaḥ kṣatriyo balavān api |
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is honored for his knowledge, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> for his strength,

children.text: dhana-dhānyādhiko vaiśyaḥ śūdras tu dvija-sevayā // Hit_4.26 //
children.translated_text: A <s>Vaiśya</s> for his abundance of wealth and grain, and a <s>Śūdra</s> for his service to the twice-born. // <s>Hit</s>_4.26 //

body.text: tad yuvāṃ kṣātra-dharmānugau | yudda eva yuvayor niyama ity abhihite sati sādhūktam aneneti kṛtvānyonya-tulya-vīryau, sama-kālam anyonya-ghātena vināśam upāgatau | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-sandhim icchet samenāpi ity ādi |
body.translated_text: Since you two follow the <s>Kṣātra-dharma</s> (warrior's code), combat alone is the rule for you — when this was said, the two, thinking "He has spoken well," being of equal valor, destroyed each other by mutual slaughter at the same moment. Therefore I say — "One should seek peace even with an equal" and so forth.
[Story break]

body.text: rājāha-tat prāg eva kiṃ nedam upadiṣṭaṃ bhavadbhiḥ ?
body.translated_text: The king said — Then why was this not advised by you earlier?

body.text: mantrī brūte-tadā mad-vacanaṃ kim avasāna-paryantaṃ śrutaṃ bhavadbhiḥ ? tadāpi mama saṃmatyā nāyaṃ vigrahārambhaḥ | yataḥ-sādhu-guṇa-yukto 'yaṃ hiraṇyagarbho na vigrāhyaḥ | tathā coktaṃ-
body.translated_text: The minister said — Was my counsel then heard by you to its conclusion? Even then, this war was not begun with my approval. For — this <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, endowed with virtuous qualities, should not be warred against. And thus it is said —

children.text: satyārthau dhārmiko 'nāryo bhrātṛ-saṅhātavān balī |
children.translated_text: One who is truthful, one whose aims are righteous, one who is noble, one who has a united band of kinsmen, one who is strong,

children.text: aneka-yuddha-vijayī sandheyāḥ sapta kīrtitāḥ // Hit_4.27 //
children.translated_text: One who has won many battles — these seven are declared to be those with whom peace should be made. // <s>Hit</s>_4.27 //

children.text: satyo 'nupālayan satyaṃ sandhito naiti vikriyām |
children.translated_text: A truthful king, upholding truth, does not deviate once a treaty is made,

children.text: prāṇa-bādhe'pi suvyaktam āryo nāyāty anārthatām // Hit_4.28 //
children.translated_text: Even when his life is threatened — clearly, a noble king does not resort to dishonor. // <s>Hit</s>_4.28 //

children.text: dhārmikasyābhiyuktasya sarva eva hi yudhyate |
children.translated_text: When a righteous king is attacked, everyone indeed fights for him;

children.text: prajānurāgād dharmāc ca duḥkhocchedyo hi dhārmikaḥ // Hit_4.29 //
children.translated_text: Due to the people's devotion and his <s>dharma</s>, a righteous king is difficult to uproot. // <s>Hit</s>_4.29 //

children.text: sandhiḥ kāryo 'py anāryeṇa vināśe samupasthite |
children.translated_text: Peace may be made even with an ignoble person when destruction is imminent;

children.text: vinā tasyāśrayeṇāryo na kuryāt kāla-yāpanam // Hit_4.30 //
children.translated_text: But without his shelter, a noble king should not merely pass the time. // <s>Hit</s>_4.30 //

children.text: saṃhatatvād yathā veṇur niviḍaiḥ kaṇṭakair vṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as bamboo, being densely bound together, covered with thick thorns,

children.text: na śakyate samucchettuṃ bhrātṛ-saṅghātavāṃs tathā // Hit_4.31 //
children.translated_text: Cannot be uprooted — so too is one who has a united band of brothers. // <s>Hit</s>_4.31 //

children.text: balinā saha yoddhavyam iti nāsti nidarśanam |
children.translated_text: That one should fight against the strong — there is no precedent for this;

children.text: prativātaṃ na hi ghanaḥ kadācid upasarpati // Hit_4.32 //
children.translated_text: A cloud never advances against the wind. // <s>Hit</s>_4.32 //

children.text: jamadagneḥ sutasyeva sarvaḥ sarvatra sarvadā |
children.translated_text: As with the son of <s>Jamadagni</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>), everyone, everywhere, at all times,

children.text: aneka-yuddha-jayinaḥ pratāpād eva bhajyate // Hit_4.33 //
children.translated_text: Submits to the one who has won many battles, by his prowess alone. // <s>Hit</s>_4.33 //

children.text: aneka-yuddha-vijayī sandhānaṃ yasya gacchati |
children.translated_text: When the one who has won many battles agrees to a treaty,

children.text: tat-pratāpena tasyāśu vaśam āyānti śatravaḥ // Hit_4.34 //
children.translated_text: By his prowess, his enemies quickly come under his sway. // <s>Hit</s>_4.34 //

body.text: tatra tāvad bahubhir guṇair upetaḥ sandheyo 'yaṃ rājā | cakravāko 'vadat-praṇidhe ! sarvam avagatam | vraja | punar āgamiṣyasi |
body.translated_text: Now, this king, endowed with many virtues, is one with whom peace should be made. <s>Cakravāka</s> said — Spy! Everything is understood. Go. You shall come again.

body.text: atha rājā hiraṇyagarbhaś cakravākaṃ pṛṣṭhavān-mantrin ! asandheyāḥ kati ? tān śrotum icchāmi | mantrī brūte-deva ! kathayāmi | śṛṇu-
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> asked <s>Cakravāka</s> — Minister! How many types are unfit for alliance? I wish to hear of them. The minister said — Your Majesty! I shall tell you. Listen —

children.text: bālo vṛddho dīrgha-rogī tathājñāti-bahiṣkṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: A child, an old man, one afflicted with prolonged illness, one expelled by his kinsmen,

children.text: bhīruko bhīruka-jano lubdho lubdha-janas tathā // Hit_4.35 //
children.translated_text: A coward, one whose people are cowardly, a greedy man, and one whose people are greedy; // <s>Hit</s>_4.35 //

children.text: virakta-prakṛtiś caiva viṣayeṣv atisaktimān |
children.translated_text: One whose subjects are disaffected, one excessively attached to sensual pleasures,

children.text: aneka-citta-mantras tu deva-brāhmaṇa-nindakaḥ // Hit_4.36 //
children.translated_text: One whose counsel is shared with many minds, one who reviles the gods and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>; // <s>Hit</s>_4.36 //

children.text: daivopahatakaś caiva tathā daiva-parāyaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: One afflicted by fate, and likewise one wholly dependent on fate,

children.text: durbhikṣa-vyasanopeto bala-vyasana-saṅkulaḥ // Hit_4.37 //
children.translated_text: One beset by the calamity of famine, one plagued by the misfortune of a weakened army; // <s>Hit</s>_4.37 //

children.text: adeśastho bahu-ripur yuktaḥ kālena yaś ca na |
children.translated_text: One stationed in unfavorable territory, one with many enemies, one who is not aligned with the proper time,

children.text: satya-dharma-vyapetaś ca viṃśatiḥ puruṣā amī // Hit_4.38 //
children.translated_text: And one devoid of truth and <s>dharma</s> — these are the twenty types of men. // <s>Hit</s>_4.38 //

children.text: etaiḥ sandhiṃ na kurvīta vigṛhṇīyāt tu kevalam |
children.translated_text: With these one should never make a treaty, but only wage war against them;

children.text: ete vigṛhyamāṇā hi kṣipraṃ yānti ripor vaśam // Hit_4.39 //
children.translated_text: For when warred upon, they quickly fall under the enemy's power. // <s>Hit</s>_4.39 //

children.text: bālasyālpa-prabhāvatvān na loko yoddhum icchati |
children.translated_text: Because of a child's feeble power, no one wishes to fight for him;

children.text: yuddhāyuddha-phalaṃ yasmāj jñātuṃ śakto na bāliśaḥ // Hit_4.40 //
children.translated_text: Since a fool cannot discern the consequences of war and non-war. // <s>Hit</s>_4.40 //

children.text: utsāha-śakti-hīnatvād vṛddho dīrghāmayas tathā |
children.translated_text: Due to lack of vigor and strength, the old man and the chronically ill likewise —

children.text: svair eva paribhūyete dvāv apy etāv asaṃśayam // Hit_4.41 //
children.translated_text: Both of these are treated with contempt even by their own people, without doubt. // <s>Hit</s>_4.41 //

children.text: sukha-cchedyo hi bhavati sarva-jñāti-bahiṣkṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who is expelled by all his kinsmen is easily overthrown;

children.text: ta evainaṃ vinighnanti jñātayas tv ātma-sātkṛtāḥ // Hit_4.42 //
children.translated_text: Those very kinsmen, once won over to one's own side, destroy him. // <s>Hit</s>_4.42 //

children.text: bhīrur yuddha-parityāgāt svayam eva praṇaśyati |
children.translated_text: A coward, by abandoning battle, perishes of his own accord;

children.text: tathaiva bhīru-puruṣaḥ saṅgrāme tair vimucyate // Hit_4.43 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, one whose men are cowardly is abandoned by them in battle. // <s>Hit</s>_4.43 //

children.text: lubdhasyāsaṃvibhāgitvān na yudhyante'nujīvinaḥ |
children.translated_text: Because a greedy man does not share, his dependents will not fight for him;

children.text: lubdhānujīvī tair eva dāna-bhinnair nihanyate // Hit_4.44 //
children.translated_text: One with greedy dependents is slain by those very men, won over by gifts from the enemy. // <s>Hit</s>_4.44 //

children.text: santy ajyate prakṛtibhir virakta-prakṛtir yudhi |
children.translated_text: One whose subjects are disaffected is abandoned by his people in battle;

children.text: sukhābhiyojyo bhavati viṣayev atisaktimān // Hit_4.45 //
children.translated_text: One excessively attached to sensual pleasures is easily assailable. // <s>Hit</s>_4.45 //

children.text: aneka-citta-mantras tu dveṣyo bhavati mantriṇām |
children.translated_text: One whose counsel is shared with many minds becomes odious to his ministers;

children.text: anavasthita-cittatvāt karyataḥ sa upekṣyate // Hit_4.46 //
children.translated_text: Due to his unstable mind, he is disregarded in matters of policy. // <s>Hit</s>_4.46 //

children.text: sadādharma-balīyastvād deva brāhmaṇa-nindakaḥ |
children.translated_text: Because unrighteousness always prevails in him, the reviler of gods and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>

children.text: viśīryate svayaṃ hy eṣa daivopahatakas tathā // Hit_4.47 //
children.translated_text: Disintegrates of his own accord; so too does one afflicted by adverse fate. // <s>Hit</s>_4.47 //

children.text: sampatteś ca vipatteś ca daivam eva hi kāraṇam |
children.translated_text: Of prosperity and adversity alike, fate alone is the cause —

children.text: iti daivaparo dhyāyann ātmanā na viceṣṭate // Hit_4.48 //
children.translated_text: Thus brooding, the fatalist does not exert himself at all. // <s>Hit</s>_4.48 //

children.text: durbhikṣa-vyasanī caiva svayam eva viṣīdati |
children.translated_text: One beset by the calamity of famine sinks of his own accord;

children.text: bala-vyasana-saktasya yoddhuṃ śaktir na jāyate // Hit_4.49 //
children.translated_text: One afflicted by the misfortune of a weakened army has no strength to fight. // <s>Hit</s>_4.49 //

children.text: adeśa-stho hi ripuṇā svalpakenāpi hanyate |
children.translated_text: One stationed in unfavorable territory is slain even by a minor enemy;

children.text: grāho 'lpīyān api jale jalendram api karṣati // Hit_4.50 //
children.translated_text: A crocodile, however small, drags even the lord of elephants in water. // <s>Hit</s>_4.50 //

children.text: bahu-śatrus tu santrastaḥ śyena-madhye kapotavat |
children.translated_text: One with many enemies, terrified like a pigeon amid hawks,

children.text: yenaiva gacchati pathā tenaivāśu vipadyate // Hit_4.51 //
children.translated_text: Is destroyed swiftly along the very path he takes. // <s>Hit</s>_4.51 //

children.text: akāla-yukta-sainyas tu hanyate kāla-yodhinā |
children.translated_text: One whose army is mustered at the wrong time is slain by the one who fights at the right time,

children.text: kauśikena hata-jyotir niśītha iva vāyasaḥ // Hit_4.52 //
children.translated_text: Like a crow at midnight, its vision destroyed, by an owl. // <s>Hit</s>_4.52 //

children.text: satya-dharma-vyapetena sandadhyān na kadācana |
children.translated_text: One should never make a treaty with one devoid of truth and <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: sa sandhito 'py asādhutvād acirād yāti vikriyām // Hit_4.53 //
children.translated_text: Even if allied, due to his dishonesty, he quickly turns treacherous. // <s>Hit</s>_4.53 //

body.text: aparam api kathayāmi-sandhi-vigraha-yānāsana-saṃśraya-dvaidhī-bhāvāḥ ṣāḍguṇyam | karmaṇām ārambhopāyaḥ | puruṣa-dravya-sampat | deśa-kāa-vibhāgaḥ | vinipāta-pratīkāraḥ | kārya-siddhiś ceti pañcāṅgo mantraḥ | sāma-dāna-bheda-daṇḍāś catvāra upāyāḥ | utsāha-śaktiḥ, mantra-śaktiḥ, prabhu- śaktiś ceti śakti-trayam | etat sarvam ālocya nityaṃ vijigīṣavo bhavanti mahāntaḥ | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: I shall tell you yet more — <s>sandhi</s> (alliance), <s>vigraha</s> (war), <s>yāna</s> (marching), <s>āsana</s> (staying), <s>saṃśraya</s> (seeking refuge), and <s>dvaidhībhāva</s> (double-dealing) — these are the six aspects of policy (<s>ṣāḍguṇya</s>). The means of undertaking actions; the wealth of men and resources; the division of place and time; the remedy for calamity; and the accomplishment of the objective — these are the five limbs of counsel. <s>Sāma</s> (conciliation), <s>dāna</s> (gifts), <s>bheda</s> (division), and <s>daṇḍa</s> (punishment) — these are the four expedients. Energy-power, counsel-power, and sovereign-power — these are the three powers. Having considered all this, great men are always desirous of conquest. For —

children.text: yā hi prāṇa-parityāga-mūlyenāpi na labhyate |
children.translated_text: That prosperity which cannot be obtained even at the cost of abandoning one's life —

children.text: sā śrīr nītividaṃ paśya cañcalāpi pradhāvati // Hit_4.54 //
children.translated_text: behold, that <s>Śrī</s> (fortune) runs eagerly toward one who knows <s>nīti</s> (statecraft), even though she is fickle. // Hit_4.54 //

body.text: yathā coktaṃ-

children.text: vittaṃ sadā yasya samaṃ vibhaktaṃ
children.translated_text: He whose wealth is always equally distributed,

children.text: gūḍhaś caraḥ saṃnibhṛtaś ca mantraḥ |
children.translated_text: whose spies are concealed, and whose counsel is kept secret,

children.text: nacāpriyaṃ prāṇiṣu yo bravīti
children.translated_text: and who never speaks what is displeasing to living beings —

children.text: sa sāgarāntāṃ pṛthivīṃ praśāsti // Hit_4.55 //
children.translated_text: he rules the earth bounded by the oceans. // Hit_4.55 //

body.translated_text: And as it is said —

body.text: kintu deva yadyapi mahā-mantriṇā gṛdhreṇa sandhānam upanyastaṃ, tathāpi tena rājñā samprati bhūta-jaya-darpān na mantavyam | deva ! tad evaṃ kriyatāṃ | siṃhala-dvīpasya mahābalo nāma sāraso rājāsman-mitraṃ jambudvīpe kopaṃ janayatu | yataḥ-

children.text: suguptim ādhāya susaṃhatena
children.translated_text: Having established good protection, with a well-united

children.text: balena vīro vicarann arātim |
children.translated_text: army, the hero, ranging about, should torment the enemy,

children.text: santāpayed yena samaṃ sutaptas
children.translated_text: so that, equally scorched,

children.text: taptena sandhānam upaiti taptaḥ // Hit_4.56 //
children.translated_text: the scorched one enters into alliance with the scorched one. // Hit_4.56 //

body.translated_text: But, O lord, although the alliance was proposed by the great minister, the vulture, even so, that king should not be presumed upon now, due to his pride in having conquered the <s>Bhūtas</s> (spirits). Your Majesty! Let this be done: let <s>Mahābala</s> by name, the crane-king of <s>Siṃhala-dvīpa</s> (the island of Ceylon), our ally, generate anger against him in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. For —

body.text: rājñā evam astv iti nigadya vicitra-nāmā bakaḥ sugupta-lekhaṃ dattvā siṃhala-dvīpaṃ prahitaḥ |
body.translated_text: The king having agreed, saying 'So be it,' a crane named <s>Vicitra</s> was dispatched with a secret letter to <s>Siṃhala-dvīpa</s>.

body.text: atha praṇidhiḥ punar āgatyovāca-deva ! śrūyatāṃ tāvat tatratya-prastāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then the spy, having returned, said: 'Your Majesty! Hear first the events from there.'

body.text: evaṃ tatra gṛdhreṇoktam-deva ! meghavarṇas tatra ciram uṣitaḥ | sa vetti kiṃ sandheya-guṇa-yukto hiraṇyagarbho rājā, na vā ? iti |
body.translated_text: Thus the vulture spoke there: 'Your Majesty! <s>Meghavarṇa</s> (the crow) dwelt there for a long time. He knows whether King <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> is endowed with the qualities worthy of alliance, or not.'

body.text: tato 'sau meghavarṇaś citravarṇena rājñā samāhūya pṛṣṭaḥ-vāyasa ! kīdṛśo hiraṇyagarbho rājā ? cakravāko mantrī vā kīdṛśaḥ ?
body.translated_text: Then that <s>Meghavarṇa</s> was summoned by King <s>Citravarṇa</s> and asked: 'O crow! What kind of king is <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>? And what kind of minister is <s>Cakravāka</s>?'

body.text: vāyasa uvāca-deva ! sa hiraṇyagarbho rājā yudhiṣṭhira-samo mahāśayaḥ satya-vāk | cakravāka-samo mantrī na kvāpy avalokyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Vāyasa</s> (the crow) said: 'Your Majesty! That King <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> is noble-minded like <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, and truthful in speech. A minister equal to <s>Cakravāka</s> is not to be seen anywhere.'

body.text: rājāha-yady evaṃ tadā katham asau tvayā vañcitaḥ ?
body.translated_text: The king said: 'If so, then how was he deceived by you?'

body.text: vihasya meghavarṇaḥ prāha-deva !
body.translated_text: Laughing, <s>Meghavarṇa</s> said: 'Your Majesty!

children.text: viśvāsa-pratipannānāṃ vañcane kā vidagdhatā |
children.translated_text: What cleverness is there in deceiving those who have placed their trust?

children.text: aṅkam āruhya suptaṃ hi hatvā kiṃ nāma pauruṣam // Hit_4.57 //
children.translated_text: Having climbed into one's lap and killed one while asleep — what kind of valor is that? // Hit_4.57 //

body.text: śṛṇu deva ! tena mantriṇāhaṃ prathama-darśane evaṃ vijñātaḥ, kintu mahāśayo 'sau rājā, tena mayā vipralabdhaḥ | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: Listen, Your Majesty! I was recognized by that minister at the very first sight. But that king was noble-minded, and therefore he was deceived by me. And as it is said —

children.text: ātmaupamyena yo vetti durjanaṃ satya-vādinam |
children.translated_text: He who, judging by himself, considers a wicked person to be truthful —

children.text: sa tathā vañcyate dhūrtair brāhmaṇāś chāgato yathā // Hit_4.58 //
children.translated_text: he is thus deceived by rogues, just as the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> were deceived regarding the goat. // Hit_4.58 //

body.text: rājovāca-katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The king said: 'How is that?'

body.text:
meghavarṇaḥ kathayati-
kathā 9
body.translated_text:
<s>Meghavarṇa</s> narrates —
Story 9
