body.text: asti gautamasyāraṇye prastuta-yajñaḥ kaścid brāhmaṇaḥ | sa ca yajñārthaṃ grāmāntarāc chāgam upakrīya, skandhe nītvā, gaccha dhūrta-trayeṇāvalokitaḥ | tatas te dhūrtāḥ-yady eṣa chāgaḥ kenāpy upāyena labhyate, tadā mati-prakarṣo bhavatīti samālocya, vṛkṣa-traya-tale krośāntareṇa tasya brāhmaṇasyāgamanaṃ pratīkṣya pathi sthitāḥ |
body.translated_text: There lived in the forest of <s>Gautama</s> a certain <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who had commenced a sacrifice. Having purchased a goat from another village for the sacrifice, he was carrying it on his shoulder and walking, when he was spotted by three rogues. Then those rogues deliberated: 'If this goat can be obtained by some stratagem, it would be a triumph of wit.' Having thus resolved, they positioned themselves on the path at intervals of a <s>krośa</s> (about two miles) under three trees, awaiting the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s approach.

body.text: tatraikena dhūrtena gacchan sa brāhmaṇo 'bhihitaḥ-bho brāhmaṇa ! kim iti tvayā kukkuraḥ skandhenohyate |
body.translated_text: There, the first rogue, encountering the walking <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, said: 'Ho, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>! Why are you carrying a dog on your shoulder?'

body.text: vipreṇoktaṃ-nāyaṃ śvā, kintu yajña-cchāgaḥ |
body.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> said: 'This is not a dog, but a sacrificial goat.'

body.text: athāntara-sthitenānyena dhūrtena tathaivoktam | tad ākarṇya brāhmaṇaś chāgaṃ bhūmau nidhāya muhur nirīkṣya, punaḥ skandhe kṛtvā dolāyamāna-matiś calitaḥ | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Then another rogue, stationed further along, said the same thing. Hearing that, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> put the goat down on the ground, examined it repeatedly, then placed it back on his shoulder and proceeded with a wavering mind. For —

children.text: matir dolāyate satyaṃ satām api khaloktibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Truly, the mind of even the virtuous wavers through the words of the wicked;

children.text: tābhir viśvāsitaś cāsau mriyate citrakarṇavat // Hit_4.59 //
children.translated_text: and one who is made to trust by such words perishes, like <s>Citrakarṇa</s>. // Hit_4.59 //

body.text: rājāha--katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The king said: 'How is that?'

body.text:
sa kathayati-
kathā 10
body.translated_text:
He narrates —
Story 10

body.text: asti kasmiṃścid vanoddeśe madotkaṭo nāma siṃhaḥ | tasya sevakās trayaḥ kāko vyāghro jambukaś ca | atha tair bhramadbhiḥ sārtha-bhraṣṭaḥ kaścid uṣṭro dṛṣṭaḥ | pṛṣṭaś ca-kuto bhavān āgataḥ sārthād bhraṣṭaḥ ?
body.translated_text: In a certain forest region, there was a lion named <s>Madotkaṭa</s> (Intoxicated with Pride). He had three servants: a crow, a tiger, and a jackal. Now, while they were wandering about, they saw a camel that had strayed from a caravan. They asked him: 'Where have you come from? Have you strayed from the caravan?'

body.text: sa cātma-vṛttāntam akathayat | tatas tair nītvā siṃhāyāsau samarpitaḥ | tena cābhaya-vācaṃ dattvā, citrakarṇa iti nāma kṛtvā sthāpitaḥ |
body.translated_text: He told them his own story. Then they took him and presented him to the lion. The lion, having given him a promise of safety, named him <s>Citrakarṇa</s> (Spotted-Ear) and kept him.

body.text: atha kadācit siṃhasya śarīra-vaikalyād bhūri-vṛṣṭi-kāraṇāc cāhāram alabhamānās te vyagrā babhūvuḥ | tatas tair ālocitam | citrakarṇam eva yathā svāmī vyāpādayati tathānuṣṭhīyatām | kim anena kaṇṭaka-bhujāsmākam ?
body.translated_text: Now, once the lion, due to bodily infirmity and heavy rain, was unable to obtain food, and they all became anxious. Then they deliberated: 'Let us contrive so that the master kills <s>Citrakarṇa</s>. What use is this thorn-eater to us?'

body.text: vyāghra uvāca-svāminābhaya-vācaṃ dattvānugṛhīto 'yaṃ, tat katham evaṃ sambhavati ?
body.translated_text: The tiger said: 'The master gave him a promise of safety and took him under his protection. How then can this be?'

body.text: kāko brūte-iha samaye parikṣīṇaḥ svāmī pāpam api kariṣyati | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: The crow said: 'In times like these, the master, being weakened, will even commit a sin. For —

children.text: tyajet kṣudhārtā mahilā svaputraṃ
children.translated_text: A woman tormented by hunger would abandon her own child;

children.text: khādet kṣudhārtā bhujagī svamaṇḍam |
children.translated_text: a female serpent tormented by hunger would eat her own eggs;

children.text: bubhukṣitaḥ kiṃ na karoti pāpaṃ
children.translated_text: what sin will a starving one not commit?

children.text: kṣīṇā narā niṣkaruṇā bhavanti // Hit_4.60 //
children.translated_text: When diminished, people become merciless. // Hit_4.60 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: mattaḥ pramattaś conmattaḥ śrāntaḥ kruddho bubhukṣitaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who is intoxicated, careless, insane, exhausted, angry, hungry,

children.text: lubdho bhīrus tvarā-yuktaḥ kāmukaś ca na dharma-vit // Hit_4.61 //
children.translated_text: greedy, fearful, hasty, or lustful — none of these know <s>dharma</s> (righteousness). // Hit_4.61 //

body.text: iti sañcintya sarve siṃhāntikaṃ jagmuḥ | siṃhenoktam-āhārārthaṃ kiñcit prāptam ?
body.translated_text: Having thus deliberated, they all went to the lion. The lion asked: 'Has anything been obtained for food?'

body.text: tair uktam-deva ! yatnād api prāptaṃ kiñcit ?
body.translated_text: They said: 'Your Majesty! Has anything been obtained even with effort?'

body.text: siṃhenoktaṃ-ko 'dhunā jīvanopāyaḥ ?
body.translated_text: The lion said: 'What is the means of sustenance now?'

body.text: kāko vadati-deva ! svādhīnāhāra-parityāgāt sarva-nāśo 'yam upasthitaḥ ?
body.translated_text: The crow said: 'Your Majesty! From the abandoning of food that is within our control, this total ruin has arrived.'

body.text: siṃhenoktam-atrāhāraḥ kaḥ svādhīnaḥ ?
body.translated_text: The lion said: 'What food here is within our control?'

body.text: kākaḥ karṇe kathayati-citrakarṇa iti | siṃho bhūmiṃ spṛṣṭvā karṇau spṛśati | abravīc ca-abhaya-vācaṃ dattvā dhṛto 'yam asmābhiḥ | tat katham evaṃ sambhavati ? tathā hi-

children.text: na bhūta-dānaṃ na suvarṇa-dānaṃ
children.translated_text: Neither the gift of land, nor the gift of gold,

children.text: na go-pradānaṃ na tathānna-dānam |
children.translated_text: nor the gift of cows, nor the gift of food —

children.text: yathā vadantīha mahā-pradānaṃ
children.translated_text: none of these is as great a gift, they say,

children.text: sarveṣu dāneṣv abhaya-pradānam // Hit_4.62 //
children.translated_text: as the gift of safety among all gifts. // Hit_4.62 //

body.translated_text: The crow whispered in his ear: '<s>Citrakarṇa</s>.' The lion touched the ground and then touched his ears [in horror]. And he said: 'We have kept this one, having given a promise of safety. How then can this be? For indeed —

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: sarva-kāma-samṛddhasya aśvamedhasya yat phalam |
children.translated_text: The fruit of the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice), endowed with all desires —

children.text: tat-phalaṃ labhate samyag rakṣite śaraṇāgate // Hit_4.63 //
children.translated_text: that very fruit one rightly obtains when one protects one who has sought refuge. // Hit_4.63 //

body.text: kāko brūte-nāsau svāminā vyāpādayitavyaḥ | kintv asmābhir eva tathā kartavyaṃ, yathāsau sva-deha-dānam aṅgīkaroti |
body.translated_text: The crow said: 'The master need not kill him. But we ourselves must contrive so that he offers the gift of his own body.'

body.text: siṃhas tac chrutvā tūṣṇīṃ sthitaḥ | tato 'sau labdhāvakāśaḥ kūṭaṃ kṛtvā sarvān ādāya siṃhāntikaṃ gataḥ | atha kākenoktaṃ-deva ! yatnād apy āhāro na prāptaḥ | anekopavāsa-kliṣṭaś ca svāmī | tad idānīṃ madīya-māṃsam upabhujyatām | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: The lion, hearing that, remained silent. Then the crow, having found an opportunity, devised a plot, and taking all of them, went to the lion. The crow said: 'Your Majesty! Even with effort, no food has been obtained, and the master is tormented by many fasts. Therefore, let my flesh be consumed now. For —

children.text: svāmi-mūlā bhavanty eva sarvāḥ prakṛtayaḥ khalu |
children.translated_text: All subjects indeed have their root in the master;

children.text: samūleṣv api vṛkṣeṣu prayatnaḥ saphalo nṛṇām // Hit_4.64 //
children.translated_text: even with trees that have roots, the effort of men bears fruit. // Hit_4.64 //

body.text: siṃhenoktaṃ-bhadra ! varaṃ prāṇa-parityāgo, na punar īdṛśe karmaṇi pravṛttiḥ |
body.translated_text: The lion said: 'Good one! Better to abandon life than to engage in such an act.'

body.text: jambukenāpi tathoktam | tataḥ siṃhenoktaṃ-maivam |
body.translated_text: The jackal also spoke similarly. Then the lion said: 'Do not say such things.'

body.text: atha vyāghreṇoktaṃ-mad-dehena jīvatu svāmī |
body.translated_text: Then the tiger said: 'Let the master live by my body.'

body.text: siṃhenoktaṃ-na kadācid evam ucitam |
body.translated_text: The lion said: 'Such a thing is never proper.'

body.text: atha citrakarṇo 'pi jāta-viśvāsas tathaivātma-deha-dānam āha-tatas tad-vacanāt tena vyāghreṇāsau kukṣiṃ vidārya vyāpāditaḥ | sarvair bhakṣitaś ca | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-matir dolāyate satyam ity ādi |
body.translated_text: Then <s>Citrakarṇa</s> too, having gained confidence, likewise offered the gift of his own body. Thereupon, at those words, the tiger tore open his belly and killed him. And he was eaten by all. Therefore I say: 'Truly, the mind wavers,' and so on.

body.text: tatas tṛtīya-dhūrta-vacanaṃ śrutvā, sva-mati-bhramaṃ niścitya chāgaṃ tyaktvā, brāhmaṇaḥ snātvā gṛhaṃ yayau | chāgaś ca tair dhūrtair nītvā bhakṣitaḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-ātmaupamyena yo vettīty ādi |
body.translated_text: Then, having heard the words of the third rogue, and having ascertained the confusion of his own mind, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> abandoned the goat, bathed, and went home. And the goat was taken and eaten by those rogues. Therefore I say: 'He who, judging by himself, considers,' and so on.

body.text: rājāha-meghavarṇa ! kathaṃ śatru-madhye tvayā suciram uṣitam ? kathaṃ vā teṣām anunayaḥ kṛtaḥ ?
body.translated_text: The king said: 'O <s>Meghavarṇa</s>! How did you dwell for so long among the enemies? And how did you win their trust?'

body.text: meghavarṇa uvāca-deva ! svāmi-kāryārthitayā sva-prayojana-vaśād vā kiṃ kiṃ na kriyate ? paśya-
body.translated_text: <s>Meghavarṇa</s> said: 'Your Majesty! For the sake of the master's purpose, or driven by one's own objective, what is not done? Behold —

children.text: loko vahati kiṃ rājan na mūrdhnā dagdhum indhanam |
children.translated_text: O king, do people not carry firewood to be burned upon their own heads?

children.text: kṣālayanty api vṛkṣāṅghriṃ nadī-velā nikṛntati // Hit_4.65 //
children.translated_text: Even while washing the roots of trees, the river-flood cuts them down. // Hit_4.65 //

children.text: tathā coktam-
children.translated_text: And as it is said —

children.text: skandhenāpi vahec chatrūn kāryam āsādya buddhimān |
children.translated_text: A wise man would even carry enemies on his shoulders when purpose demands it,

children.text: yathā vṛddhena sarpeṇa maṇḍūkā vinipātitāḥ // Hit_4.66 //
children.translated_text: just as by the old serpent, the frogs were brought to their doom. // Hit_4.66 //

body.text: rājāha-katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The king said: 'How is that?'

body.text:
meghavarṇaḥ kathayati-
kathā 11
body.translated_text:
<s>Meghavarṇa</s> narrates —
Story 11

body.text: asti jīrṇodyāne manda-viṣo nāma sarpaḥ | so 'tijīrṇatayā svāhāram apy anveṣṭum akṣamaḥ saras-tīre patitvā sthitaḥ | tato dūrād eva kenacin maṇḍūkena dṛṣṭaḥ, pṛṣṭaś ca-kim iti tvām āhāraṃ nānviṣyati ?
body.translated_text: In a certain old garden, there was a serpent named <s>Mandaviṣa</s> (Feeble-Venom). Due to extreme old age, he was unable even to search for his own food, and lay fallen on the bank of a lake. Then a certain frog, seeing him from afar, asked: 'Why are you not seeking food?'

body.text: sarpo 'vadat-gaccha bhadra ! kiṃ te mama manda-bhāgyasya vṛttānta-praśnena ? tataḥ sañjāta-kautukaḥ sa ca bhekaḥ sarvathā kathyatām ity āha | sarpo 'py āha-bhadra ! pura-vāsinaḥ śrotriyasya kauṇḍinyasya putro viṃśati-varṣa-deśīyaḥ sarva-guṇa-sampanno durdaivān mayā nṛśaṃsena daṣṭaḥ | tatas taṃ suśīla-nāmānaṃ putraṃ mṛtam avalokya, śokena mūrcchitaḥ kauṇḍinyaḥ pṛthivyāṃ luloṭha | anantaraṃ brahmapura-vāsinaḥ sarve bāndhavās tatrāgatyopaviṣṭāḥ | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: The serpent said: 'Go, good one! What use is your question about the affairs of this unfortunate one like me?' Then that frog, his curiosity aroused, said: 'Tell me everything.' The serpent then said: 'Good one! A son of the town-dwelling <s>Śrotriya</s> (Vedic scholar) <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, a young man of about twenty years, endowed with all virtues, was cruelly bitten by me due to ill fate. Then, seeing his son named <s>Suśīla</s> dead, <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, overcome with grief, fell rolling on the ground. Soon after, all the kinsmen dwelling in <s>Brahmapura</s> came there and sat down. And as it is said —

children.text: utsave vyasane yuddhe durbhikṣe rāṣṭra-viplave |
children.translated_text: In festivities, in calamities, in war, in famine, in the upheaval of the kingdom,

children.text: rāja-dvāre śmaśāne ca yas tiṣṭhati sa bāndhavaḥ // Hit_4.67 //
children.translated_text: at the king's gate, and at the cremation ground — he who stands by you is a true kinsman. // Hit_4.67 //

body.text: tatra kapilo nāma snātako 'vadat-are kauṇḍinya ! mūḍho 'si yenaivaṃ vilapasi | śṛṇu-

children.text: kroḍīkaroti prathamaṃ yadā jātam anityatā |
children.translated_text: When impermanence first embraces the newly born,

children.text: dhātrīva jananī paścāt tadā śokasya kaḥ kramaḥ // Hit_4.68 //
children.translated_text: like a nurse before the mother — then what course is there for grief? // Hit_4.68 //

body.translated_text: There, a graduate named <s>Kapila</s> said: 'O <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>! You are foolish to lament thus. Listen —

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: kva gatāḥ pṛthivī-pālāḥ sa-sainya-bala-vāhanāḥ |
children.translated_text: Where have those rulers of the earth gone, with their armies, forces, and vehicles?

children.text: viyoga-sākṣiṇī yeṣāṃ bhūmir adyāpi tiṣṭhati // Hit_4.69 //
children.translated_text: The earth, witness to their separation, still remains to this day. // Hit_4.69 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyur dhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca |
children.translated_text: For one who is born, death is certain; and for one who has died, birth is certain.

children.text: adya vābda-śatānte vā mṛtyur vai prāṇināṃ dhruvaḥ // Hit_4.70 //
children.translated_text: Whether today or at the end of a hundred years, death is indeed certain for all living beings. // Hit_4.70 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: kāyaḥ saṃnihitāpāyaḥ sampadaḥ padam āpadām |
children.translated_text: The body is attended by destruction; prosperity is the seat of calamity;

children.text: samāgamāḥ sāpagamāḥ sarvam utpādi bhaṅguram // Hit_4.71 //
children.translated_text: meetings end in separation; everything that arises is perishable. // Hit_4.71 //

children.text: pratikṣaṇam ayaṃ kāyaḥ kṣīyamāṇo na lakṣyate |
children.translated_text: This body, being diminished moment by moment, is not noticed,

children.text: āmakumbha ivāmbhaḥ-stho viśīrṇaḥ san vibhāṣyate // Hit_4.72 //
children.translated_text: like an unbaked pot placed in water — when it crumbles, it is perceived. // Hit_4.72 //

children.text: āsannataratāmeti mṛtyur jantor dine dine |
children.translated_text: Death draws ever closer to a creature day by day,

children.text: āghātaṃ nīyamānasya vadhyasyeva pade pade // Hit_4.73 //
children.translated_text: like one being led to execution, step by step. // Hit_4.73 //

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: For —

children.text: anityaṃ yauvanaṃ rūpaṃ jīvitaṃ dravya-sañcayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Youth, beauty, life, accumulation of wealth,

children.text: aiśvaryaṃ priya-saṃvāso muhyet tatra na paṇḍitaḥ // Hit_4.74 //
children.translated_text: sovereignty, and the company of loved ones are all impermanent — a wise person is not deluded by these. // Hit_4.74 //

children.text: yathā kāṣṭhaṃ ca kāṣṭhaṃ ca sameyātāṃ mahodadhau |
children.translated_text: Just as two pieces of wood meet together in the great ocean

children.text: sametya ca vyapeyātāṃ tadvad bhūta-samāgamaḥ // Hit_4.75 //
children.translated_text: and, having met, drift apart again — such is the meeting of beings. // Hit_4.75 //

children.text: yathā hi pathikaḥ kaścic chāyām āśritya tiṣṭhati |
children.translated_text: Just as some traveler rests under a shade

children.text: viśramya ca punar gacched tadvad bhūta-samāgamaḥ // Hit_4.76 //
children.translated_text: and, having rested, moves on again — such is the meeting of beings. // Hit_4.76 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: pañcabhir nirmite dehe pañcatvaṃ ca punar gate |
children.translated_text: The body, created from the five (elements), when it returns again to the five elements,

children.text: svāṃ svāṃ yonim anuprāpte tatra kā paridevanā // Hit_4.77 //
children.translated_text: each element having returned to its own source — what cause is there for lamentation? // Hit_4.77 //

children.text: yāvataḥ kurute jantuḥ sambandhān manasaḥ priyān |
children.translated_text: As many pleasing attachments as a creature forms,

children.text: tāvanto 'sya nikhanyante hṛdaye śoka-śaṅkavaḥ // Hit_4.78 //
children.translated_text: so many thorns of grief and apprehension are planted in his heart. // Hit 4.78 //

children.text: nāyam atyanta-saṃvāso labhyate yena kenacit |
children.translated_text: This perpetual companionship cannot be obtained with anyone,

children.text: api svena śarīreṇa kim utānyena kenacit // Hit_4.79 //
children.translated_text: not even with one's own body — what then of another person? // Hit 4.79 //

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: saṃyogo hi viyogasya saṃsūcayati sambhavam |
children.translated_text: Union itself announces the possibility of separation,

children.text: anatikramaṇīyasya janma mṛtyor ivāgamam // Hit_4.80 //
children.translated_text: like birth announces the advent of inescapable death. // Hit 4.80 //

children.text: āpāta-ramaṇīyānāṃ saṃyogānāṃ priyaiḥ saha |
children.translated_text: Of unions with loved ones that are delightful at first encounter,

children.text: apathyānām ivānnānāṃ pariṇāmo hi dāruṇaḥ // Hit_4.81 //
children.translated_text: the consequence is terrible, like that of unwholesome foods. // Hit 4.81 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And another —

children.text: vrajanti na nivartante srotāṃsi saritāṃ yathā |
children.translated_text: Like the currents of rivers, they flow and do not return,

children.text: āyur ādāya martyānāṃ tathā rātry-ahanī sadā // Hit_4.82 //
children.translated_text: so do nights and days always carry away the life of mortals. // Hit 4.82 //

children.text: sukhāsvāda-paro yas tu saṃsāre sat-samāgamaḥ |
children.translated_text: That meeting with the good in this world which is supreme in the savoring of happiness,

children.text: sa viyogāvasānatvād duḥkhānāṃ dhuri yujyate // Hit_4.83 //
children.translated_text: since it ends in separation, is yoked to the foremost of sorrows. // Hit 4.83 //

children.text: ata eva hi necchanti sādhavaḥ sat-samāgamam |
children.translated_text: For this very reason the virtuous do not desire the company of the good,

children.text: yad-viyogāsi-lūnasya manaso nāsti bheṣajam // Hit_4.84 //
children.translated_text: for there is no remedy for a heart cut by the sword of separation from them. // Hit 4.84 //

children.text: sukṛtāny api karmāṇi rājabhiḥ sagarādibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Even meritorious deeds were performed by kings such as <s>Sagara</s> and others,

children.text: atha tāny eva karmāṇi te cāpi pralayaṃ gatāḥ // Hit_4.85 //
children.translated_text: yet those very deeds and those kings too have gone to dissolution. // Hit 4.85 //

children.text: saṃcintya saṃcintya tam ugra-daṇḍaṃ
children.translated_text: Reflecting again and again upon that fierce-staffed

children.text: mṛtyuṃ manuṣyasya vicakṣaṇasya |
children.translated_text: <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death) of the discerning man,

children.text: varṣāmbu-siktā iva carma-bandhāḥ
children.translated_text: like leather bindings soaked by rain-water,

children.text: sarve prayatnāḥ śithilībhavanti // Hit_4.86 //
children.translated_text: all efforts become slack. // Hit 4.86 //

children.text: yām eva rātriṃ prathamām upaiti
children.translated_text: From the very first night that a person enters

children.text: garbhe nivāsaṃ naravīra lokaḥ |
children.translated_text: his dwelling in the womb, O hero among men,

children.text: tataḥ prabhṛty askhalita-prayāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: from that time onward, with unfaltering journey,

children.text: sa pratyahaṃ mṛtyu-samīpam eti // Hit_4.87 //
children.translated_text: he approaches death day by day. // Hit 4.87 //

children.text: ajñānaṃ kāraṇaṃ na syād viyogo yadi kāraṇam |
children.translated_text: If separation were not the cause, ignorance would not be the cause (of grief);

children.text: śoko dineṣu gacchatsu vardhatām apayāti kim // Hit_4.88 //
children.translated_text: as the days pass, does the grief that grows (ever) depart? // Hit 4.88 //

body.text: tad bhadra ! tad ātmānam anusandhehi | śoka-carcāṃ ca parihara, yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Therefore, dear one! Examine your own self, and abandon the indulgence in grief, for —

children.text: akāṇḍa-pāta-jātānām astrāṇāṃ marma-bhedinām |
children.translated_text: Against blows of deep grief that strike at vital points

children.text: gāḍha-śoka-prahārāṇām acintaiva mahauṣadham // Hit_4.89 //
children.translated_text: like weapons falling unexpectedly, not thinking about it is the great medicine. // Hit 4.89 //

body.text: tatas tad-vacanaṃ niśamya, prabuddha iva kauṇḍinya utthāyābravīt | tad alam idānīṃ gṛha-naraka-vāsena vanam eva gacchāmi | kapilaḥ punar āha-
body.translated_text: Then, hearing those words, <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, as if awakened, rose and said: 'Enough now of dwelling in the hell of domestic life — I shall go to the forest!' <s>Kapila</s> again said —

children.text: vane'pi doṣāḥ prabhavanti rāgiṇāṃ
children.translated_text: Even in the forest, faults arise for those with attachments;

children.text: gṛhe'pi pañcendriya-nigrahas tapaḥ |
children.translated_text: even at home, restraint of the five senses is <s>tapas</s> (austerity);

children.text: akutsite karmaṇi yaḥ pravartate
children.translated_text: he who engages in blameless action —

children.text: trivṛtta-rāgasya gṛhaṃ tapovanam // Hit_4.90 //
children.translated_text: for one whose passions are thrice-bound, the home itself is a hermitage. // Hit 4.90 //

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: For —

children.text: duḥkhito 'pi cared dharmaṃ yatra kutrāśrame rataḥ |
children.translated_text: Even in distress, one should practice <s>dharma</s>, devoted to whatever <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life);

children.text: samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu na liṅgaṃ dharma-kāraṇam // Hit_4.91 //
children.translated_text: equal toward all beings — the outward mark is not the cause of <s>dharma</s>. // Hit 4.91 //

children.text: uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And it is said —

children.text: vṛtty-arthaṃ bhojanaṃ yeṣāṃ santānārthaṃ ca maithunam |
children.translated_text: Those for whom eating is only for sustenance, and sexual union only for progeny,

children.text: vāk satya-vacanārthāya durgāṇy api taranti te // Hit_4.92 //
children.translated_text: and speech only for truthful utterance — they cross over even the most difficult passages. // Hit 4.92 //

body.text: tathā hi-

children.text: ātmā nadī saṃyam apuṇya-tīrthā
children.translated_text: The self is a river, with self-restraint as its sacred <s>tīrtha</s> (ford),

children.text: satyodakā śīla-taṭā dayormiḥ |
children.translated_text: with truth as its water, good conduct as its banks, and compassion as its waves;

children.text: tatrābhiṣekaṃ kuru pāṇḍu-putra !
children.translated_text: bathe therein, O son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>!

children.text: na vāriṇā śuṣyati cāntarātmā // Hit_4.93 //
children.translated_text: For the inner self is not purified by (mere) water. // Hit 4.93 //

body.translated_text: For instance —

children.text: viśeṣataś ca-
children.translated_text: And especially —

children.text: janma-mṛtyu-jarā-vyādhi-vedanābhir upadrutam |
children.translated_text: Afflicted by the pains of birth, death, old age, and disease,

children.text: saṃsāram imam utpannam asāraṃ tyajataḥ sukham // Hit_4.94 //
children.translated_text: happiness comes from renouncing this arisen, essence-less <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence). // Hit 4.94 //

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: For —

children.text: duḥkham evāsti na sukhaṃ yasmāt tad upalakṣyate |
children.translated_text: There is only suffering, not happiness — from which that (happiness) is perceived;

children.text: duḥkhārtasya pratīkāre sukha-saṃjñā vidhīyate // Hit_4.95 //
children.translated_text: when remedying the condition of one afflicted by suffering, the designation 'happiness' is applied. // Hit 4.95 //

body.text: kauṇḍinyo brūte-evam eva | tato 'haṃ tena śokākulena brāhmaṇena śapto, yad adyārabhya maṇḍūkānāṃ vāhanaṃ bhaviṣyatīti |
body.translated_text: <s>Kauṇḍinya</s> says: 'Just so.' Then I was cursed by that grief-stricken <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, that from today onward I would become a vehicle for frogs.

body.text: kapilo brūte-sampraty upadeśāsahiṣṇur bhavān | śokāviṣṭaṃ te hṛdayam | tathāpi kāryaṃ śṛṇu-

children.text: saṅgaḥ sarvātmanā tyājyaḥ sa cet tyaktuṃ na śakyate |
children.translated_text: Attachment should be abandoned entirely; but if it cannot be given up,

children.text: sa sadbhiḥ saha kartavyaḥ satāṃ saṅgo hi bheṣajam // Hit_4.96 //
children.translated_text: it should be formed with the virtuous, for the company of the good is the remedy. // Hit 4.96 //

body.translated_text: <s>Kapila</s> says: 'At present you are unable to bear counsel. Your heart is overwhelmed by grief. Even so, hear what must be done —

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And another —

children.text: kāmaḥ sarvātmanā heyaḥ sa ced dhātuṃ na śakyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Kāma</s> (desire) should be entirely forsaken; but if it cannot be contained,

children.text: sva-bhāryāṃ prati kartavyaḥ saiva tasya hi bheṣajam // Hit_4.97 //
children.translated_text: it should be directed toward one's own wife, for she alone is its remedy. // Hit 4.97 //

body.text: etac chrutvā sa kauṇḍinyaḥ kapilopadeśāmṛta-praśānta-śokānalo yathāvidhi daṇḍa-grahaṇaṃ kṛtavān | ato brāhmaṇa-śāpān maṇḍūkān voḍhum atra tiṣṭhāmi | anantaraṃ tena maṇḍūkena gatvā maṇḍūka-nāthasya jālapāda-nāmno 'gre tat kathitam | tato 'sāv āgatya maṇḍūka-nāthas tasya sarpasya pṛṣṭham ārūḍhavān | sa ca sarpas taṃ pṛṣṭhe kṛtvā citrapada-kramaṃ babhrāma |
body.translated_text: Hearing this, that <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, his fire of grief pacified by the nectar of <s>Kapila</s>'s teaching, duly accepted the staff (of a renunciant). 'Therefore, because of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s curse, I remain here to carry frogs.' Thereupon, that frog went and told this before the frog-lord named <s>Jālapāda</s>. Then that frog-lord came and mounted the back of that serpent. And that serpent, carrying him on his back, wandered about with elegant, varied steps.

body.text: paredyuś calitum asamarthaṃ taṃ maṇḍūka-nātham avadat-kim adya bhavān manda-gatiḥ ?
body.translated_text: The next day, (the frog-lord) addressed him, who was unable to move: 'Why are you so slow today?'

body.text: sarpo brūte-deva ! āhāra-virahād asamartho 'smi |
body.translated_text: The serpent says: 'Lord! I am unable due to lack of food.'

body.text: maṇḍūka-nātho 'vadat-asmād ājñayā maṇḍūkān bhakṣaya | tataḥ gṛhīto 'yaṃ mahā-prasāda ity uktvā kramaśo maṇḍūkān khāditavān | atha nirmaṇḍūkaṃ saro vilokya maṇḍūka-nātho 'pi tena khāditaḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-skandhenāpi vahec chatrūn ity ādi | deva ! yātv idānīṃ purāvṛttākhyāna-kathanaṃ sarvathā sandheyo 'yaṃ hiraṇyagarbha-rājā sandhīyatām iti me matiḥ |
body.translated_text: The frog-lord said: 'By my command, eat frogs.' Then, saying 'This is a great favor,' he gradually devoured all the frogs. Then, seeing the pond devoid of frogs, he ate the frog-lord too. Therefore I say: 'One should carry enemies on one's shoulder' and so forth. Your Majesty! Let us now set aside the telling of tales of the past. This king <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> should be conciliated in every way — peace should be made: this is my counsel.

body.text: rājovāca-ko 'yaṃ bhavato vicāraḥ ? yato jitas tāvad ayam asmābhiḥ | tato yady asmat sevayā vasati, tad āstām | no ced vigṛhyatām |
body.translated_text: The king said: 'What is this deliberation of yours? For we have already defeated him. If he dwells in our service, so be it. Otherwise, let there be war.'

body.text: atrāntare jambūdvīpād āgatya śukenoktaṃ-deva ! siṃhala-dvīpasya sāraso rājā samprati jambūdvīpam ākramyāvatiṣṭhate |
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, <s>Śuka</s>, having come from <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, reported: 'Your Majesty! The crane king of <s>Siṃhala-dvīpa</s> (Sri Lanka) has now invaded and established himself in <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>.'

body.text: rājā sa-sambhramaṃ brūte-kiṃ kim ?
body.translated_text: The king says in alarm: 'What? What?'

body.text: śukaḥ pūrvoktaṃ kathayati | gṛdhraḥ svagatam uvāca-sādhu re cakravāka mantrin ! sādhu !
body.translated_text: <s>Śuka</s> recounts the aforementioned events. The vulture (<s>Dūradarśī</s>) said to himself: 'Well done, O minister <s>Cakravāka</s>! Well done!'

body.text: rājā sa-kopam āha-āstāṃ tāvad ayaṃ gatvā tam eva sa-mūlam unmūlayāmi |
body.translated_text: The king said angrily: 'Let that be for now — I shall go and uproot him completely!'

body.text: dūradarśī vihasyāha-
body.translated_text: <s>Dūradarśī</s> said, laughing —

children.text: na śaran-meghavat kāryaṃ vṛthaiva ghana-garjitam |
children.translated_text: One should not act like an autumn cloud, thundering loudly to no purpose;

children.text: parasyārtham anarthaṃ vā prakāśayati no mahān // Hit_4.98 //
children.translated_text: a great man does not reveal his purpose or harm to the enemy. // Hit 4.98 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: ekadā na vigṛhṇīyād bahūn rājābhighātinaḥ |
children.translated_text: A king should not wage war against many assailants at once;

children.text: sa-darpo 'py uragaḥ kīṭair bahubhir nāśyate dhruvam // Hit_4.99 //
children.translated_text: even a proud serpent is surely destroyed by many insects. // Hit 4.99 //

body.text: deva ! kim ito vinā sandhānaṃ gamanam asti ? yatas tadāsmākaṃ paścāt prakopo 'nena kartavyaḥ | aparaṃ ca-
body.translated_text: Your Majesty! Is there any option of departing from here without making peace? For then he will attack us from behind. And moreover —

children.text: yo 'rtha-tattvam avijñāya krodhasyaiva vaśaṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, without ascertaining the true nature of things, surrenders to anger alone,

children.text: sa tathā tapyate mūḍho brāhmaṇo nakulād yathā // Hit_4.100 //
children.translated_text: that fool suffers as the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> did on account of the mongoose. // Hit 4.100 //

body.text: rājāha--katham etat ?
body.translated_text: The king said: 'How is that?'

body.text:
dūradarśī kathayati-
kathā 11
body.translated_text:
<s>Dūradarśī</s> narrates —
Story 11

body.text: asty ujjayinyāṃ mādhavo nāma vipraḥ | tasya brāhmaṇī prasūtā, bālāpatyasya rakṣārthaṃ brāhmaṇam avasthāpya sthātuṃ gatā | atha brāhmaṇāya rājñaḥ pārvaṇa-śrāddhaṃ dātum āhvānam āgatam | tac chrutvā brāhmaṇo 'pi sahaja-dāridryād acintayat-yadi satvaraṃ na gacchāmi, tadānyā kaścic chrutvā śrāddhaṃ grahīṣyati | yataḥ-

children.text: ādeyasya pradeyasya kartavyasya ca karmaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Of what should be received, what should be given, and what action should be performed,

children.text: kṣipram akriyamāṇasya kālaḥ pibati tad-rasam // Hit_4.101 //
children.translated_text: if not done quickly, time drinks away its essence. // Hit 4.101 //

body.translated_text: In <s>Ujjayinī</s> there lived a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Mādhava</s>. His wife, having given birth, left the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> stationed to guard the infant and went out. Then an invitation came for the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> to attend the king's <s>pārvaṇa-śrāddha</s> (ancestral rite on the new-moon day). Hearing this, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, due to his innate poverty, thought: 'If I do not go quickly, someone else hearing of it will take the <s>śrāddha</s> offering.' For —

body.text:
kintu bālākasyātra rakṣako nāsti | tat kiṃ karomi ? yātu, cira-kāla-pālitam imaṃ nakulaṃ putra-nirviśeṣaṃ bālaka-rakṣāyāṃ vyavasthāpya gacchāmi | tathā kṛtvā gataḥ | tatas tena nakulena bālaka-samīpam āgacchan kṛṣṇa-sarpo dṛṣṭo vyāpādya kopāt khaṇḍaṃ khaṇḍaṃ kṛtvā bhakṣitaś ca | tato 'sau nakulo brāhmaṇam āyāntam avalokya rakta-vilipta-mukha-padaḥ satvaram upagamya tac-caraṇayor luloṭha | tataḥ sa vipras tathā-vidhaṃ dṛṣṭvā mama bālako 'nena khādita ity avadhārya nakulaḥ vyāpāditavān | anantaraṃ yāvad upasṛtyāpatyaṃ paśyati brāhmaṇas tāvad bālakaḥ susthaḥ svapiti sarpaś ca vyāpāditas tiṣṭhati | tatas tam upakārakaṃ nakulaṃ nirīkṣya, bhāvita-cetāḥ sa brāhmaṇaḥ paraṃ viṣādam agamat | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-yo
'rtha-tattvam avijñāya ity ādi | aparaṃ ca-
body.translated_text: But there is no one here to guard the infant. What shall I do? Well then, I shall station this mongoose, reared for a long time and regarded no differently than a son, to guard the child and go.' Having done so, he left. Then that mongoose saw a black serpent approaching the infant and killed it, angrily tearing it to pieces and devouring it. Then that mongoose, seeing the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> returning, quickly approached and rolled at his feet, its mouth and paws smeared with blood. Then the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, seeing it in that state and concluding 'My child has been devoured by this one,' killed the mongoose. Afterwards, when the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> went closer and looked at his child, the infant was sleeping safely and the serpent lay slain. Then, seeing that beneficent mongoose, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, his heart filled with remorse, fell into the deepest anguish. Therefore I say: 'He who, without ascertaining the true nature of things' and so forth. And moreover —

children.text: kāmaḥ krodhas tathā lobho harṣo māno madas tathā |
children.translated_text: Desire, anger, greed, elation, pride, and intoxication —

children.text: ṣaḍ-vargam utsṛjed enaṃ tasmiṃs tyakte sukhī nṛpaḥ // Hit_4.102 //
children.translated_text: one should abandon this group of six; when they are forsaken, a king finds happiness. // Hit 4.102 //

body.text: rājāha-mantrin ! eṣa te niścayaḥ ?
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Minister! Is this your firm conclusion?'

body.text: mantrī brūte-evam eva | yataḥ-

children.text: smṛtis tat-paratārtheṣu vitarko jñāna-niścayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Memory, concern for the meaning of things, discernment, firm resolve,

children.text: dṛḍhatā mantra-guptiś ca mantriṇaḥ paramo guṇaḥ // Hit_4.103 //
children.translated_text: and secrecy in counsel — these are the supreme qualities of a minister. // Hit 4.103 //

body.translated_text: The minister says: 'Just so. For —

body.text: tathā ca-

children.text: sahasā vidadhīta na kriyām
children.translated_text: One should not undertake action hastily;

children.text: avivekaḥ paramāpadāṃ padam |
children.translated_text: lack of discernment is the seat of the greatest calamities;

children.text: vṛṇute hi vimṛśya kāriṇaṃ
children.translated_text: for prosperity, attracted by merit,

children.text: guṇa-lubdhāḥ svayam eva sampadaḥ // Hit_4.104 //
children.translated_text: chooses of its own accord the man who acts after deliberation. // Hit 4.104 //

body.translated_text: And also —

body.text: tad deva ! yadīdānīm asmad-vacanaṃ kriyate, tadā sandhāya gamyatām | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Therefore, Your Majesty! If our counsel is now followed, then let peace be made and let us depart. For —

children.text: yadyapy upāyāś catvāro nirdiṣṭāḥ sadhya-sādhane |
children.translated_text: Although four means (<s>upāya</s>) are prescribed for accomplishing what is to be accomplished,

children.text: saṅkhyā-mātraṃ phalaṃ teṣāṃ siddhiḥ sāmni vyavasthitā // Hit_4.105 //
children.translated_text: that is merely a count; success is established in <s>sāma</s> (conciliation). // Hit 4.105 //

body.text: rājāha-katham evaṃ satvaraṃ sambhāvyate ?
body.translated_text: The king said: 'How can this be accomplished so quickly?'

body.text: mantrī brūte-deva ! satvaraṃ bhaviṣyati | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: The minister says: 'Your Majesty! It will happen quickly. For —

children.text: mṛd-ghaṭavat sukha-bhedyo
children.translated_text: A wicked person is as easily broken as a clay pot

children.text: duḥsandhānaś ca durjano bhavati |
children.translated_text: and is difficult to mend;

children.text: sujanas tu kanaka-ghaṭavad
children.translated_text: but a good person, like a golden pot,

children.text: durbhedyaś cāśu sandheyaḥ // Hit_4.106 //
children.translated_text: is hard to break and quickly reconciled. // Hit 4.106 //

children.text: ajñaḥ sukham ārādhyaḥ sukhataram ārādhyate viśeṣajñaḥ |
children.translated_text: An ignorant person is easily won over; even more easily is a man of special knowledge won over;

children.text: jñāna-lava-durvidagdhaṃ brahmāpi naraṃ na rañjayati // Hit_4.107 //
children.translated_text: but one puffed up with a little learning — even <s>Brahmā</s> cannot please such a man. // Hit 4.107 //

children.text: karmānumeyāḥ sarvatra parokṣa-guṇa-vṛttayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Those whose merits and conduct are unseen should be judged everywhere by their actions;

children.text: tasmāt parokṣa-vṛttīnāṃ phalaiḥ karma vibhāvayet // Hit_4.108 //
children.translated_text: therefore, one should infer the conduct of those whose ways are hidden by their fruits. // Hit 4.108 //

body.text: rājāha-alam uttarottareṇa, yathābhipretam anuṣṭhīyatām | etan mantrayitvā gṛdhro mahāmantrī-tatra yathārhaṃ kartavyam ity uktvā durgābhyantaraṃ calitaḥ | tataḥ praṇidhi-bakenāgatya rājñī hiraṇyagarbhasya niveditaṃ-deva ! sandhi-kartuṃ mahāmantrī gṛdhro 'smat-samīpam āgacchati |
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Enough of further deliberation — let what is intended be carried out.' Having thus deliberated, the vulture, the great minister, saying 'Let what is proper be done there,' set out toward the interior of the fortress. Then the spy-crane came and reported to king <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>: 'Your Majesty! The vulture, the great minister, is coming to our side to make peace.'

body.text: rājahaṃso brūte-mantrin ! punar abhisandhinā kenacid atrāgamanam |
body.translated_text: The royal swan (<s>Rājahaṃsa</s>) says: 'Minister! Perhaps someone is coming here again with a hidden agenda.'

body.text: sarvajño vihasyāha-deva ! na śaṅkāspadam etat | yato 'sau mahāśayo dūradarśī | athavā sthitir iyaṃ manda-matīnāṃ, kadācic chaṅkaiva na kriyate, kadācit sarvatra śaṅkā | tathā hi-
body.translated_text: <s>Sarvajña</s> said, laughing: 'Your Majesty! There is no cause for suspicion here, for that noble <s>Dūradarśī</s> is magnanimous. Or rather, this is the way of the dim-witted: sometimes they suspect nothing at all, sometimes they suspect everything. For instance —

children.text: sarasi bahuśas tārācchāyekṣaṇāt parivañcitaḥ
children.translated_text: A swan, searching for <s>kumuda</s> (night-lotus) stems, deceived many times

children.text: kumuda-viṭapānveṣī haṃso niśāsvavicakṣaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: by seeing the reflections of stars in the lake, and thus unable to discern at night,

children.text: na daśati punas tārāśaṅkī divāpi sitotpalaṃ
children.translated_text: then, suspicious of stars (even by day), does not bite the white day-lotus even in daylight;

children.text: kuhuka-cakito lokaḥ satye'py apāyam apekṣate // Hit_4.109 //
children.translated_text: the world, deceived by trickery, expects danger even in what is true. // Hit 4.109 //

children.text: durjana-dūṣita-manasaḥ sujaneṣv api nāsti viśvāsaḥ |
children.translated_text: One whose mind has been corrupted by the wicked has no trust even in the virtuous;

children.text: bālaḥ pāyasa-dagdho dadhy api phūtkṛtya bhakṣayati // Hit_4.110 //
children.translated_text: a child scalded by hot milk blows even on curds before eating. // Hit 4.110 //

body.text: tad deva ! yathā-śakti tat-pūjārthaṃ ratnopahārādi-sāmagrī susajjīkriyatām | tathānuṣṭhite sati sa gṛdhro durga-dvārāc cakravākeṇopagamya, satkṛtyānīya rāja-darśanaṃ kārito dattāsane copaviṣṭaḥ | cakravāka uvāca-mantrin ! yuṣmad-āyattaṃ sarvaṃ svecchayopabhujyatām idaṃ rājyam æ
body.translated_text: Therefore, Your Majesty! Let all provisions of gems, gifts, and the like be well prepared for his honor, to the best of our ability.' When this was carried out, that vulture was met by <s>Cakravāka</s> at the fortress gate, honorably escorted in, given an audience with the king, and seated on the seat offered to him. <s>Cakravāka</s> said: 'Minister! Everything depends on you — enjoy this kingdom as you please.'

body.text: rājahaṃso brūte-evam eva |
body.translated_text: The royal swan (<s>Rājahaṃsa</s>) says: 'Just so.'

body.text: dūradarśī kathayati-evam evaitat | kintv idānīṃ bahu-prapañca-vacanaṃ niṣparyojanam | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: <s>Dūradarśī</s> (the vulture) says: 'Indeed so. But now, verbose elaboration is pointless. For —

children.text: lubdham arthena gṛhṇīyāt stabdham añjali-karmaṇā |
children.translated_text: The greedy should be won over with wealth, the arrogant with folded hands,

children.text: mūrkhaṃ chandānurodhena yāthātathyena paṇḍitam // Hit_4.111 //
children.translated_text: the fool by humoring his wishes, and the learned with truth. // Hit 4.111 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And another —

children.text: sad-bhāvena haren mitraṃ sambhrameṇa tu bāndhavān |
children.translated_text: One should win over a friend with goodwill, kinsmen with attentiveness,

children.text: strī-bhṛtyau dāna-mānābhyāṃ dākṣiṇyenetarān janān // Hit_4.112 //
children.translated_text: wife and servants with gifts and respect, and other people with courtesy. // Hit 4.112 //

body.text: tad idānīṃ sandhātuṃ gamyatām | mahā-pratāpaś citravarṇo rājā |
body.translated_text: Therefore, now go to make the alliance. King <s>Citravarṇa</s> is of great majesty.'

body.text: cakravāko brūte-yathā sandhānaṃ kāryam | tad apy ucyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Cakravāka</s> (the sheldrake) says: 'Tell us also how the alliance should be made.'

body.text: rājahaṃso brūte-kati prakārāḥ sandhīnāṃ sambhavanti ?
body.translated_text: <s>Rājahaṃsa</s> (the royal swan) says: 'How many kinds of alliances are there?'

body.text: gṛdhro brūte-kathayāmi śrūyatām-
body.translated_text: The vulture says: 'I shall tell — listen —

children.text: balīyasābhiyuktas tu nṛpo nānya-pratikriyaḥ |
children.translated_text: A king who is attacked by a mightier one, and has no other recourse,

children.text: āpannaḥ sandhim anvicchet kurvāṇaḥ kāla-yāpanam // Hit_4.113 //
children.translated_text: being in distress, should seek an alliance, thereby gaining time. // Hit 4.113 //

children.text: kapāla upahāraś ca santānaḥ saṃgatas tathā |
children.translated_text: <s>Kapāla</s> (equal division), <s>upahāra</s> (tribute), <s>santāna</s> (marriage), <s>saṃgata</s> (friendship),

children.text: upanyāsaḥ pratīkāraḥ saṃyogaḥ puruṣāntaraḥ // Hit_4.114 //
children.translated_text: <s>upanyāsa</s> (representation), <s>pratīkāra</s> (reciprocity), <s>saṃyoga</s> (joint expedition), <s>puruṣāntara</s> (proxy), // Hit 4.114 //

children.text: adṛṣṭa-nara ādiṣṭa ātmāmiṣa upagrahaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>adṛṣṭanara</s> (unseen champion), <s>ādiṣṭa</s> (designated agent), <s>ātmāmiṣa</s> (self as bait), <s>upagraha</s> (submission),

children.text: parikrayas tathocchinnas tathā ca para-dūṣaṇaḥ // Hit_4.115 //
children.translated_text: <s>parikraya</s> (purchase of peace), <s>ucchinna</s> (cession), and <s>parabhūṣaṇa</s> (adornment of another), // Hit 4.115 //

children.text: skandhopaneyaḥ sandhiś ca ṣoḍaśaḥ parakīrtitaḥ |
children.translated_text: and <s>skandhopaneya</s> (installment-based) — thus alliance has been declared to be of sixteen kinds.

children.text: iti ṣoḍaśakaṃ prāhuḥ sandhiṃ sandhi-vicakṣaṇāḥ // Hit_4.116 //
children.translated_text: Those skilled in alliances speak of these sixteen types of alliance. // Hit 4.116 //

children.text: kapāla-sandhir vijñeyaḥ kevalaṃ sama-sandhikaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>kapāla</s> alliance should be understood as one based solely on equal terms;

children.text: sampradānād bhavati ya upahāraḥ sa ucyate // Hit_4.117 //
children.translated_text: that which comes about through a gift or offering is called <s>upahāra</s>. // Hit 4.117 //

children.text: santāna-sandhir vijñeyo dārikā-dāna-pūrvakaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>santāna</s> alliance should be understood as one preceded by the giving of a daughter;

children.text: sadbhis tu saṅgataḥ sandhir maitrī-pūrva udāhṛtaḥ // Hit_4.118 //
children.translated_text: the <s>saṃgata</s> alliance with the good is described as one preceded by friendship. // Hit 4.118 //

children.text: yāvad āyuḥ-pramāṇas tu samānārtha-prayojanaḥ |
children.translated_text: It lasts as long as life, serves a common purpose,

children.text: sampattau vā vipattau vā kāraṇair yo na bhidyate // Hit_4.119 //
children.translated_text: and is not broken by any cause, whether in prosperity or adversity. // Hit 4.119 //

children.text: saṅgataḥ sandhir evāyaṃ prakṛṣṭatvāt suvarṇavat |
children.translated_text: This is the <s>saṃgata</s> alliance itself — on account of its excellence, like gold;

children.text: tathānyaiḥ sandhi-kuśalaiḥ kāñcanaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ // Hit_4.120 //
children.translated_text: therefore, by other experts in alliance too, it is called the 'golden' (alliance). // Hit 4.120 //

children.text: ātma-kāryasya siddhiṃ tu samuddiśya kriyeta yaḥ |
children.translated_text: That which is made with the aim of accomplishing one's own purpose

children.text: sa upanyāsa-kuśalair upanyāsa udāhṛtaḥ // Hit_4.121 //
children.translated_text: is called <s>upanyāsa</s> by those skilled in representation. // Hit 4.121 //

children.text: mayāsyopakṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ mamāpy eṣa kariṣyati |
children.translated_text: 'I have previously done a favor for him, and he too will do (one) for me' —

children.text: iti yaḥ kriyate sandhiḥ pratīkāraḥ sa ucyate // Hit_4.122 //
children.translated_text: the alliance that is made thus is called <s>pratīkāra</s> (reciprocity). // Hit 4.122 //

children.text: upakāraṃ karomy asya mamāpy eṣa kariṣyati |
children.translated_text: 'I shall do a favor for him, and he too will do (one) for me' —

children.text: ayaṃ cāpi pratīkāro rāma-sugṛīvayor iva // Hit_4.123 //
children.translated_text: this too is a <s>pratīkāra</s>, like (the alliance) between <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Sugrīva</s>. // Hit 4.123 //

children.text: ekārthāṃ samyag uddiśya yātrāṃ yatra hi gacchataḥ |
children.translated_text: When two go together on a well-planned expedition, having identified a common goal,

children.text: susaṃhita-prayāṇas tu sandhiḥ saṃyoga ucyate // Hit_4.124 //
children.translated_text: that alliance with a well-coordinated march is called <s>saṃyoga</s> (joint expedition). // Hit 4.124 //

children.text: āvayor yodha-mukhyābhyāṃ mad-arthaḥ sādhyatām iti |
children.translated_text: 'Let my purpose be accomplished by a chief warrior of each of us two' —

children.text: yasmin paṇaḥ prakriyate sa sandhiḥ puruṣāntaraḥ // Hit_4.125 //
children.translated_text: the alliance in which such a wager is made is called <s>puruṣāntara</s> (proxy). // Hit 4.125 //

children.text: tvayaikena madīyo 'rthaḥ samprasādhyas tv asāv iti |
children.translated_text: 'My purpose is to be accomplished by you alone' —

children.text: yatra śatruḥ paṇaṃ kuryāt so 'dṛṣṭa-puruṣaḥ smṛtaḥ // Hit_4.126 //
children.translated_text: where the enemy makes such a wager, that is known as <s>adṛṣṭapuruṣa</s> (unseen champion). // Hit 4.126 //

children.text: yatra bhūmy-eka-deśena paṇena ripur ūrjitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Where a powerful enemy makes an alliance

children.text: sandhīyate sandhi-vidbhiḥ sa cādiṣṭa udāhṛtaḥ // Hit_4.127 //
children.translated_text: with the wager of a portion of territory, that is described by those versed in alliance as <s>ādiṣṭa</s> (designated). // Hit 4.127 //

children.text: sva-sainyena tu sandhānam ātmādiṣṭa udāhṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: Alliance through (offering) one's own army is described as <s>ātmādiṣṭa</s>;

children.text: kriyate prāṇa-rakṣārthaṃ sarva-dānād upagrahaḥ // Hit_4.128 //
children.translated_text: <s>upagraha</s> (submission) is made for the sake of protecting life by giving up everything. // Hit 4.128 //

children.text: kośāṃśenārdha-kośena sarva-kośena vā punaḥ |
children.translated_text: With a portion of the treasury, half the treasury, or the entire treasury —

children.text: śiṣṭasya pratirakṣārthaṃ parikraya udāhṛtaḥ // Hit_4.129 //
children.translated_text: for the protection of what remains, (this) is described as <s>parikraya</s> (purchase of peace). // Hit 4.129 //

children.text: bhuvāṃ sāravatīnāṃ tu dānād ucchinna ucyate |
children.translated_text: From the giving of fertile lands, (the alliance) is called <s>ucchinna</s> (cession);

children.text: bhūmy-uttha-phala-dānena sarveṇa para-bhūṣaṇaḥ // Hit_4.130 //
children.translated_text: <s>parabhūṣaṇa</s> (adornment of another) is through the giving of all produce born of the land. // Hit 4.130 //

children.text: paricchinnaṃ phalaṃ yatra pratiskandhena dīyate |
children.translated_text: Where a specified share of produce is given in installments,

children.text: skandhopaneyaṃ taṃ prāhuḥ sandhiṃ sandhi-vicakṣaṇāḥ // Hit_4.131 //
children.translated_text: those skilled in alliance call that the <s>skandhopaneya</s> alliance. // Hit 4.131 //

children.text: parasparopakāras tu maitrī sambandhakas tathā |
children.translated_text: Mutual benefit, friendship-bond,

children.text: upahāraś ca vijñeyāś catvāraś caiva sandhayaḥ // Hit_4.132 //
children.translated_text: and tribute — these four types of alliance should be known. // Hit 4.132 //

children.text: eka evopahāras tu sandhir etan mataṃ hi naḥ |
children.translated_text: Tribute alone is (the true) alliance — this is our view;

children.text: upahārasya bhedās tu sarve'nye maitra-varjitāḥ // Hit_4.133 //
children.translated_text: all the other types are (merely) subdivisions of tribute, excepting friendship. // Hit 4.133 //

children.text: abhiyoktā balī yasmād alabdhvā na nivartate |
children.translated_text: Since a mighty aggressor does not withdraw without receiving (something),

children.text: upahārād ṛte tasmāt saṃdhir anyo na vidyate // Hit_4.134 //
children.translated_text: there is no alliance other than tribute. // Hit 4.134 //

body.text: rājāha-bhavanto mahāntaḥ paṇḍitāś ca | tad atrāsmākaṃ yathā-kāryam upadiśyatām |
body.translated_text: The king says: 'You are great and learned. Therefore, advise us as to what should be done.'

body.text: dūradarśī brūte-āḥ kim evam ucyate?
body.translated_text: <s>Dūradarśī</s> says: 'Ah! Why do you say such a thing?'

children.text: ādhi-vyādhi-parītāpād adya śvo vā vināśine |
children.translated_text: For a body that will perish today or tomorrow from afflictions, diseases, and torments,

children.text: ko hi nāma śarīrāya dharmāpetaṃ samācaret // Hit_4.135 //
children.translated_text: who would perform an act that is opposed to <s>dharma</s>? // Hit 4.135 //

children.text: jalāntaś candra-capalaṃ jīvitaṃ khalu dehinām |
children.translated_text: The life of embodied beings is indeed as fleeting as a moon reflected in water.

children.text: tathā-vidham iti jñātvā śaśvat-kalyāṇam ācaret // Hit_4.136 //
children.translated_text: Knowing it to be such, one should always practice what is auspicious. // Hit 4.136 //

children.text: vātābhra-vibhramam idaṃ vasudhādhipatyam
children.translated_text: This sovereignty over the earth is as unstable as wind-driven clouds;

children.text: āpāta-mātra-madhuro viṣayopabhogaḥ |
children.translated_text: the enjoyment of sense-objects is sweet only at first contact;

children.text: prāṇās tṛṇāgra-jala-bindu-samāna-lolā
children.translated_text: life-breaths are as fickle as a drop of water on a blade of grass —

children.text: dharmaḥ sakhā param aho paraloka-yāne // Hit_4.137 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> alone is a friend, alas, in the journey to the next world! // Hit 4.137 //

children.text: mṛga-tṛṣṇā-samaṃ vīkṣya saṃsāraṃ kṣaṇa-bhaṅguram |
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) to be like a mirage, momentary and perishable,

children.text: sajjanaiḥ saṅgataṃ kuryād dharmāya ca sukhāya ca // Hit_4.138 //
children.translated_text: one should associate with the good — for <s>dharma</s> and for happiness. // Hit 4.138 //

body.text: tan mama saṃmatena tad eva kriyatām | yataḥ-
body.translated_text: Therefore, with my approval, let that very thing be done. For —

children.text: aśvamedha-sahasraṃ ca satyaṃ ca tulayā dhṛtam |
children.translated_text: When a thousand <s>Aśvamedhas</s> (horse sacrifices) and truth are weighed in the balance,

children.text: aśvamedha-sahasrād dhi satyam eva viśiṣyate // Hit_4.139 //
children.translated_text: truth alone is superior to a thousand <s>Aśvamedhas</s>. // Hit 4.139 //

body.text: ataḥ satyābhidhāna-divya-puraḥsaram anayor bhūpālayoḥ kāñcanābhidhānaḥ sandhir vidhīyatām | sarvajño brūte-evam astu | tato rājahaṃsena rājñā vastrālaṅkāropahāraiḥ sa mantrī dūradarśī pūjitaḥ | prahṛṣṭa-manāś cakravākaṃ gṛhītvā, rājño mayūrasya saṃnidhānaṃ gataḥ | tatra citravarṇena rājñā sarvajño gṛdhra-vacanād bahu-māna-dāna-puraḥ-saraṃ sambhāṣitas tathā-vidhaṃ sandhiṃ svīkṛtya rājahaṃsa-samīpaṃ prasthāpitaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therefore, preceded by a divine oath in the name of truth, let the 'golden' alliance be established between these two kings.' <s>Sarvajña</s> (the all-knowing one) says: 'So be it.' Then King <s>Rājahaṃsa</s> honored the minister <s>Dūradarśī</s> with gifts of garments and ornaments. With a delighted heart, taking <s>Cakravāka</s>, he went to the presence of King <s>Mayūra</s> (the peacock). There, King <s>Citravarṇa</s>, on the word of <s>Sarvajña</s> the vulture, preceded by much respect and gifts, held a conversation (with him); and having accepted such an alliance, he was dispatched back to the presence of <s>Rājahaṃsa</s>.

body.text: dūradarśī brūte-deva ! siddhaṃ naḥ samīhitam | idānīṃ svasthānam eva vindhyācalaṃ vyāvṛtya pratigamyatām | atha sarve sva-sthānaṃ prāpya, manābhilaṣitaṃ phalaṃ prāpnuvann iti |
body.translated_text: <s>Dūradarśī</s> says: 'Your Majesty! Our desire has been accomplished. Now let us return to our own place, turning back from the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain.' Then all, having reached their own place, obtained the fruit their minds desired.

body.text: viṣṇuśarmenoktaṃ-aparaṃ kiṃ kathayāmi, tad ucyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s> said: 'What more shall I tell? Speak!'

body.text: rāja-putrā ūcuḥ-ārya ! tava prasādāt sakala-rājya-vyavahārāṅgaṃ jātam | tataḥ sukhino bhūtā vayam |
body.translated_text: The princes said: 'Sir! By your grace, all the aspects of statecraft have been (learned). Therefore, we are happy.'

body.text: viṣṇu-śarmovāca-yadyapy evaṃ tathāpy aparam apīdam astu |
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s> said: 'Even though that is so, let there also be this further (blessing) —

children.text: sandhiḥ sarva-mahī-bhujāṃ vijayinām astu pramodaḥ sadā
children.translated_text: May there be alliance among all victorious kings of the earth; may there always be joy;

children.text: santaḥ santu nirāpadaḥ sukṛtināṃ kīrtiś ciraṃ vardhatām |
children.translated_text: may the good be free from calamity; may the fame of the meritorious long increase;

children.text: nīti-vāra-vilāsinīva satataṃ vakṣaḥ-sthale saṃsthitā
children.translated_text: may <s>Nīti</s> (statecraft), like a sporting damsel, ever resting upon the breast,

children.text: vaktraṃ cumbatu mantriṇām aharahar bhūyān mahān utsavaḥ // Hit_4.140 //
children.translated_text: kiss the face of ministers day after day; may the festival be great and perpetual! // Hit 4.140 //

body.text: anyac cāstu-

children.text: prāleyādreḥ sutāyāḥ praṇaya-nivasatiś candramauliḥ sa yāvad
children.translated_text: As long as <s>Candramauli</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) dwells as a lover of the daughter of the Snow-mountain (<s>Pārvatī</s>),

children.text: yāval lakṣmīr murārer jalada iva taḍin mānase visphurantī |
children.translated_text: as long as <s>Lakṣmī</s> of <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) flashes in his mind like lightning in a cloud,

children.text: yāvat svarṇācalo 'yaṃ dava-dahana-samo yasya sūryaḥ sphuliṅgas
children.translated_text: as long as this golden mountain (<s>Meru</s>) stands, whose spark is the sun, like a forest fire —

children.text: tāvan nārāyaṇena pracaratu racitaḥ saṅgraho 'yaṃ kathānām // Hit_4.141 //
children.translated_text: so long may this collection of stories, composed by <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, prevail! // Hit 4.141 //

body.translated_text: And further, let this be so —

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: urvīm uddāma-sasyāṃ janayatu visṛjan vāsavo vṛṣṭim iṣṭām iṣṭais traiviṣṭapānāṃ vidadhatu vidhivat prīṇanaṃ vipra-mukhyāḥ |
children.translated_text: May <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>), releasing the desired rain, make the earth abound in crops; may the foremost <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> duly perform the gratification of the gods of heaven with desired (offerings); may the association of good people endure, firm and well-established, until the end of the world-cycle; and may the unbearable words of slanderers, hard as thunderbolt-paste, all come to complete peace! // Hit 4.142 //

children.text: ākalpāntaṃ ca bhūyāt sthira-samupacitā saṅgatiḥ sajjanānāṃ niḥśeṣaṃ yāntu śāntiṃ piśuna-jana-giro duḥsahā vajra-lepāḥ // Hit_4.142 //
children.translated_text: and may the association of good people endure, firm and well-established, until the end of the world-cycle; may the unbearable words of slanderers, hard as thunderbolt-paste, all come to complete peace! // Hit 4.142 //

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: śrīmāndhavalacandro 'sau jīyān māṇḍaliko ripūn |
children.translated_text: May the glorious <s>Dhavalacandra</s>, the feudal lord, conquer his enemies,

children.text: yenāyaṃ saṅgraho yatnāl lekhayitvā pracāritaḥ // Hit_4.143 //
children.translated_text: by whom this collection was, with effort, caused to be written and disseminated. // Hit 4.143 //

body.text:
iti hitopadeśe sandhir nāma caturthaḥ kathā-saṅgrahaḥ
|| samāptaś cāyaṃ hitopadeśaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Thus ends the fourth collection of stories, named <s>Sandhi</s> (Alliance), in the <s>Hitopadeśa</s>.
|| And thus the <s>Hitopadeśa</s> is complete. //
